Tilly was shopping at the store before Father's day. She was picking up her burgers for her husband. She wanted to get him a gift but had very little money. Tilly needed some help finding something that he might like and would be willing to spend his hard earned money on. He loved anything with video games so she looked around the electronics section hoping to find a good deal on one of those game systems or maybe even accessories. "I can't believe how expensive all these things are!" said Tilly in shock, almost spouting out loud! "Just because they're electronic doesn't mean you have to buy them!" The woman behind the counter replied giving her an odd look as if there were only 2 choices; either pay retail prices or not buy it. "A lot of times department stores will do special pricing just for holidays such as today." She walked over towards where it stated on the sign that this section held electronics items. To make sure it wasn't too crowded, she went into another aisle heading right towards the back. As soon as she started walking away from the front entrance, she could hear people talking about what great sales there were throughout the whole store including places much more reasonably priced than their own! This angered her. It made her want to walk faster toward her goal knowing full well that it was making other customers mad because of her time crunch. Feeling bad for being selfish now, she slowed down so others wouldn't feel rushed also. There weren't many people in the electronics area anyway since most people go straight for toys instead. That is when she saw him sitting by himself looking very bored near the door leading outside. He looked sad and lonely. His face unshaven, dirty clothes and hair uncombed gave off the appearance of someone who didn't care anymore. The first thing Tilly noticed however was his large stature! "Wow," she thought to herself, "he has got to weigh 300 pounds easy!!!." This concerned her greatly! If dad gained 100 pounds then Mom may begin to worry. No father wants to see son become fathered by daughter! But if he didn't eat regularly...well then perhaps Walmart shouldn't sell food products? The next thing Tilly did notice was that man standing nearby staring intently at Dad. Now why would anyone stare at her overweight father?? That question floated through her head until she heard him speak. "Yo..." He began but stopped short. Why stop speaking mid sentence??? What does he know? Did he see the picture I took of my parents together? And now he is staring at me like we've never met before?! IT COULDN'T BE HE KNOWS SOMETHING!! Like Mom says: Know your enemy. This guy must work here after all. So what is going on here? Is this part of the mystery box!? Looks like I'm getting involved sooner rather than later. Who knows what else lies ahead?! Tilly turned around to leave and asked, "Excuse me sir?" Realizing that everyone knew she spoke to strangers without hesitation, she added, "Actually ma'am..about those video games...do you think I should get one for Christmas? I don't really play video games myself but dad loves them!!" Why am I telling this stranger my business again! Hmmmmm, better yet, what kind of mother am I?! All mothers probably talk to random strangers like this constantly so whatever! He replies saying, "Well, I suppose dad will appreciate any present given to him no matter what it is. Have you checked our website lately? We always try to offer good deals during holidays like last week when 3DS XL hardware was 150 dollars less!" Wow! A price reduction eh? Well nothing is stopping me from using this information against mom and dad then. "Yes Sir, I watched the ad on TV earlier while watching cartoons with my kids. I figured it'd be fun to watch it online later" Then the real plan came to mind. Maybe I'll shop elsewhere tomorrow with my family and come back to Walmart tonight. That way we won't need to put up with crowd control and lines forming long waiting lists. Yeah! Perfect! After feeling proud of her new idea, she turns around slightly planning to say goodbye and leaves smiling thinking everything worked perfectly. You know sometimes I wonder why God allows tragedies to happen especially ones hitting close to home. I guess I should thank Him though. Without allowing us to experience hardships then we are incomplete. They give meaning to life somehow. Hadn't Dad received enough hardship already? Or had I been blessed with perfect health growing up only to have someone take it away from me? Who cares! Life goes on! Whatever happens in the past or future doesn't affect me unless I allow it to. Yes, now I understand! Everything works itself out eventually so stay positive! Stay focused on your goals! Keep pushing forward regardless of obstacles! After all, adversity builds character! Nothing will ever separate you from God's love except yourself!

Quantum memories are a fundamental of any global-scale quantum Internet, high-performance quantum networking and near-term quantum computers. A main problem of quantum memories is the low retrieval efficiency of the device due to its memory effect (e.g., the lower the magnetization density, the slower the retrieval rate). Quantum integration technologies aim at minimizing this flaw by using magnetic solids that store multiple states simultaneously.[1] This technology has been applied successfully in many cases for storing data, but researchers have also tried applying it to other applications such as computing.[234] Technologies based on the magnetic solid concept include quantum digital logic circuits,[5] superconducting magnetoresistive random access memories[6], qubits and quantum integrated circuits (QICs).[78] However, they all require specialized hardware components, such as detectors, transducers or devices with special functions; thus these systems cannot be used directly as general-purpose quantum memories because their performance would not be good enough. In addition, there is no guarantee that they can scale efficiently large enough to serve as an acceptable solution for classical information processing. Furthermore, despite the claims that quantum memory will someday enable information storage and computation over a wide range of scales from large to small, the current state of the art does not provide evidence supporting this prediction yet. Hence, new solutions may still remain necessary for making further progress towards developing reliable quantum memories. One promising approach for overcoming some of the shortcomings described above was proposed by Trapnell et al. [9]. They developed a system consisting of an electronically controlled "virtual" magnetically trapped robot with different angles of incidence of two laser beams on the surface of a magnetized metal-oxide material (MOM) placed between two magnetic coils separated by a distance of approximately 1 m. The laser beam incident on one side of the MOM serves to excite the trapped magnetism while the opposite side focuses on the physical distal side of the MOM, thereby creating a potential difference between the sides of the material to generate a spin state induced polarization. These spin states were subsequently read out by scanning the MOM with successive pulses of laser light. During each reading cycle, only a portion of the MOM was excited so that no magnetization could be detected during the first half of the reading cycle. As a result, it took only 4-10 s to retrieve the entire set of stored spins when conventional techniques required hundreds of cycles to accomplish the same task. Compared to traditional systems incorporating variously shaped magnets attached to conductors, the system presented here provides significant improvements over previous approaches since it uses both lasers and magnets without employing additional external circuitry.

In December, Judge Thokozile Masipa granted permission for the prosecution to challenge Oscar Pistorius's acquittal. Previously, she convicted him of culpable homicide, equivalent to manslaughter, and handed down a five-year jail sentence. Pistorius fatally shot his partner Reeva Steenkamp in February 2013; he claimed it was an accident, whereas the prosecution contended that he killed her during a dispute within their luxurious residence in Pretoria. The renowned disabled athlete was found not guilty of premeditated and common-law murder charges by Judge Masipa. According to South African legislation, the latter implies that the defendant recognized the possibility of causing death yet proceeded regardless. Consequently, the prosecution believes that Judge Masipa misapplied the law regarding intentionality when she exonerated Pistorius from murder based on lack of evidence. Defense attorneys have recently voiced opposition to the ruling and aim to prevent reversal of the culpable homicide verdict. They plan to present relevant case precedents to argue against allowing the appeal, which is scheduled to occur before Judge Masipa on March 13th. Prior to his legal troubles, Pistorius achieved significant recognition as a pioneering Paralympic runner who competed in the 2012 Olympic Games held in London.

Various methods exist to study the evolution of language over time. For instance:

Poetry Analysis – Analyzing old English poetry, particularly from the 16th-18th centuries, reveals many instances where unconventional rhymes are employed, such as pairing "love" and "move". These peculiarities suggest phonological shifts occurred during those periods. Furthermore, examining poetic meters allows us to deduce information regarding syllabic emphasis patterns.

Historical Spelling Errors – Ancient texts also exhibit spelling mistakes, indicating linguistic transformations across eras. For example, observing multiple occurrences of "should of" instead of "should have" suggests similarities in contemporary pronunciations.

Guidelines for Pronunciation – Even in antiquity, individuals sought to correct others' improper usage of language, evident through surviving Classical Latin pronunciation manuals detailing incorrect versus proper enunciation practices.

Comparative Linguistic Techniques – Historical linguists employ various strategies to trace sound changes within languages. One notable method involves studying the transition from Vulgar Latin to modern Romance languages, exemplified by the disappearance of the letter 'H'. Observing these linguistic alterations collectively rather than independently helps establish their occurrence throughout the original speech community.

Loanwords – When a term originating in one language is adopted by another, its pronunciation remains static relative to the source language. Two prime examples include the terms "castle" and "chateau", which stemmed from the French word yet maintain distinctive phonetic attributes due to their incorporation into separate languages.

Boolean functional synthesis is the process of constructing a Boolean function from a Boolean specification that relates input and output variables. Despite significant recent developments in synthesis algorithms, Boolean functional synthesis remains a challenging problem even when state-of-the-art methods are used for decomposing the specification. In this work we bring a fresh decomposition approach, orthogonal to existing methods, that explores the decomposition of the specification into separate input and output components. We make use of an input-output decomposition of a given specification described as a CNF formula, by alternatingly analyzing the separate input and output components. We exploit well-defined properties of these components to ultimately synthesize a solution for the entire specification. We first provide a theoretical result that, for input components with specific structures, synthesis for CNF formulas via this framework can be performed more efficiently than in the general case. We then show by experimental evaluations that our algorithm performs well also in practice on instances which are challenging for existing state-of-the-art tools, serving as a good complement to modern synthesis techniques.

Apple Glasses could have the ability to transform any surface into a virtual touch interface, according to a patent that the company filed back in 2016. The patent describes using a "holographic waveguide" to bend light around the lens in front of the eye, allowing the user to see virtual buttons and controls. This is one of several patents that Apple has filed related to augmented reality (AR) glasses, but it's among the most detailed. It describes how a head-mounted device could be used to display virtual buttons and controls to the user. To the user, the virtual buttons may appear to be floating in the air in front of the user. If the user presses the virtual button, a haptic feedback mechanism in the head-mounted device would provide a physical sensation that the button was pressed. The user could be able to control the size, shape, and location of the virtual buttons, and the system could automatically adjust the lighting and brightness of the virtual buttons based on the ambient lighting in the user's surroundings. The virtual buttons could even be used to control a smart home, with a single button for turning on a light or adjusting the temperature. The user could be able to adjust the system to reduce light leakage and improve the contrast between the virtual buttons and the user's surroundings, and the headset could include a camera for facial detection. The patent was first spotted by Patently Apple.

Despite being more common in practical scenarios where user history exists without explicit ratings, the implicit feedback-based recommendation issue has received significantly less attention compared to the explicit feedback scenario. Advanced algorithms designed for explicit feedback don't seamlessly transition to the implicit case without sacrificing scalability. Implicit feedback datasets are scarce, leading researchers to test their concepts against explicit ones. This document introduces iTALS, an adaptable context-sensitive algorithm tailored for implicit feedback recommendations. Utilizing an expedited tensor factorization technique grounded in Alternating Least Squares (ALS), which grows proportionally to the amount of non-null values within the tensor, iTALS demonstrates increased speed through variations employing coordinate descent and conjugate gradient techniques during training. Furthermore, iTALS integrates diverse contextual details effectively without compromising performance. Two specialized versions of iTALS consider temporal factors such as seasonal changes and purchasing patterns over time, distinguishing between distinct consumer behaviors and product categories. Evaluated across six datasets, iTALS consistently surpasses traditional context-agnostic models and competitor approaches focused on context awareness. Additionally, it matches or exceeds Factorization Machines (FMs) in precision metrics like recall and Mean Average Precision (MAP) in numerous instances.

I know this is a hot button topic from all sides and in all different directions, but today I've tentatively cemented (yeah, there's a useful description:P) my position that religious thought is incompatible with scientific thought at its core. To begin I'll lay it out like this: 1. Religious thought encourages us to seek information in a manner that is consistent with our religious views. For many people, this is referencing their holy booksteachings. For others, this is referencing their feelings about the way the universe looks, otherwise known as that amorphous feeling of spirituality. 2. Science is a specific manner of testing what we think we know to ascertain the degree to which we can be confident in said knowledge. The whole institution is based on the idea that the individual is fallible, but the group reduces this weakness. The larger the amount of repeat testing, the more confident we can justifiably become. 3. While the two worldviews can certainly coexist in many ways at best, they inherently are incompatible because they seek the truth in differnt manners at their cores. If one values both manners of "obtaining knowledge" about the world, one inevitably has to decide which view informs the other and thus which is more reliable. In other words, if the two conflict in some way, or if there is some unknown factor that science cannot yet explain, the individual subscribing to both worldviews must decide whether to believe that science can explain the unexplained or if religion is the explanation. The former is more open to expanding one's knowledge the latter is content to stick with the current knowledge it has an ascribe "god" to it. I say all this simply because many people claim the extremes on this topic; that either science inherently refutes religion (or vice versa) or that they are compatible and can peacefully coexist. I believe that at best they can leave each other alone, but even vague deistic thought will inevitably invade into scientific thought simply because it proposes its own explanations where science has not yet been able to. Eventually, she located the diminutive brass key amidst the rest and extended it firmly using both hands. The surroundings of the key became warped and distorted due to the effects of an entire bottle of wine intended for sharing with Abby, compounded by ceaseless sobbing. Her cosmetics streaked and dripped down her face, embodying her despair as a pitiful version of herself. Internalized criticism reverberated through her thoughts: "How foolish can you get? " Within the living space she refused to allow guests to enter lay neglected plates stacked up in the sink, garbage accumulating near the bin she vowed to clear regularly, and vacant alcohol containers symbolizing every last cent she possessed. Laura flung her keys onto the ground before collapsing towards the nearest bottle, seeking a single remaining droplet, only to discover its emptiness. "Behold your abode. You're utterly degraded, equal to the squalor you inhabit." She lamented with agony, hurling the glass container at the wooden floor, which splintered into countless pieces and scattered throughout the dwelling. Noticing another bottle further away containing residual bourbon, Laura attempted to rise yet again but succumbed to the overwhelming lack of drive, settling against the adjoining wall instead. Overcome with feelings of powerlessness, she surrendered to a bout of inconsolable weeping, accompanied by nasal congestion and saliva. "Why does everything have to be this way?" she screamed at the vacant rooms. "It's because you're nothing more than a heap of refuse," the inner critic responded. "You're damaged beyond repair. You disappoint everyone. At times, you hardly seem human. " Clutching herself tightly, Laura swayed gently while seated on the ground, engulfed by her misery.

Whenever an issue relating to free speech arises it is almost guaranteed one of the responses will be "free speech means the state can't control what you say. It doesn't mean freedom from consequences from everyone else." If it's on the internet it is equally likely that this [xkcd] will be shown. This does seem at first to be a reasonable point of view. However, I believe it is flawed for several related reasons. The first reason is that underestimates the power of the public. Just because the state is not infringing your right does not mean others cannot. With other rights this is accepted as part of the system. For instance, if a company refused to serve or allow access to black people that would be considered a violation of their rights despite it not being the government. In the same way, you couldn't claim a country has gender equality if women can't be get a job, despite there being no law against hiring women. Unless freedom of speech can be distinguished from those other rights, which I believe it cannot, there can be no distinction between private agents and the state in terms of freedom of speech. Secondly, the right to free speech includes the right to unimpeded free speech, if that makes sense. It is not enough to be allowed to say what you want, you have to be allowed to communicate to who you want. It makes more tense in terms of letters. Freedom of speech is not fulfilled by allowing me to write letters, it is only fulfilled by allowing their delivery. Using the example from the comic, continually showing someone the door is the same as standing by the pillar box and shredding the letters as I post them. The final reason is that extreme reactions to someone's use of free speech can restrict it by effectively punishing them for exercising their right. If I punched someone for suggesting marmite was a valid option for toast, would I not be restricting their right to free speech? Equally, if I was sacked for making a racist reddit post, am I not being punished for exercising my right to freedom of speech? I'm not entirely convinced on this point because it might restrict someone else's freedom of speech to criticise or their freedom of association to not have to put up with me, but I would still say there is some validity to this point. Just to be clear, I don't think freedom of speech should never be restricted but I do think those restrictions should be acknowledged which the phrase "freedom of speech, not freedom from consequences" does not. Deforestation is the conversion of forested areas to non-forested areas. The main sources of deforestation in the Amazon are human settlement and development of the land. Prior to the early 1960s, access to the forest's interior was highly restricted, and the forest remained basically intact. Farms established during the 1960s were based on crop cultivation and the slash and burn method. However, the colonists were unable to manage their fields and the crops because of the loss of soil fertility and weed invasion. The soils in the Amazon are productive for just a short period of time, so farmers are constantly moving to new areas and clearing more land. These farming practices led to deforestation and caused extensive environmental damage. Deforestation is considerable, and areas cleared of forest are visible to the naked eye from outer space.

I kept my distance, not wanting to draw any attention to myself or the new kid, but I couldn't help but keep an eye on him as he made his way through the hallways. As the day went on, I began to realize what was really going on. The new kid was some kind of bodyguard for the school principal. It seems likely that Alexander himself pursued policies which led Hellenization, such as the foundations of new cities and Greek colonies. While it may have been a deliberate attempt to spread Greek culture (or as Arrian says, "to civilise the natives, it is more likely that it was a series of pragmatic measures designed to aid in the rule of his enormous empire. Cities and colonies were centers of administrative control and Macedonian power in a newly conquered region. Alexander also seems to have attempted to create a mixed Greco-Persian elite class as shown by the Susa weddings and his adoption of some forms of Persian dress and court culture. He also brought in Persian and other non-Greek peoples into his military and even the elite cavalry units of the companion cavalry. Again, it is probably better to see these policies as a pragmatic response to the demands of ruling a large empire than to any idealized attempt to bringing Greek culture to the 'barbarians'. This approach was bitterly resented by the Macedonians and discarded by most of the Diadochi after Alexander's death. These policies can also be interpreted as the result of Alexander's possible megalomania during his later years.

The normal body tissues show up as green, while the cancer comes out as intense red spots. The team, at the University of Tokyo and the RIKEN Quantitative Biology Center, says that red spots can appear in the body in different forms, including lesions, tumours, edemas or bleeding. And their size, shape, location and colour can indicate the stage of cancer. They say the method can be used to spot cancer in organs that are not easily examined by a doctor. "We can non-invasively and repeatedly track the dynamic development of tumours in hard-to-reach organs without radiation exposure," said study leader Toshikazu Aoki. "Our method can be applied to other organs that are difficult to access, such as those in the spinal cord, and it may be useful for the early diagnosis and monitoring of cancer metastasis." The team created an artificial tissue model from silicone and filled it with collagen, a protein that is found in the body. They then dripped cancer cells onto the tissue.

It follows from the Marcus-Spielman-Srivastava proof of the Kadison-Singer conjecture that if G (V , E) is a -regular dense expander then there is an edge-induced subgraph H (V , E H) of G of constant maximum degree which is also an expander. As with other consequences of the MSS theorem, it is not clear how one would explicitly construct such a subgraph. We show that such a subgraph (although with quantitatively weaker expansion and near-regularity properties than those predicted by MSS) can be constructed with high probability in linear time, via a simple algorithm. Our algorithm allows a distributed implementation that runs in O (log n) rounds and does O (n) total work with high probability. The analysis of the algorithm is complicated by the complex dependencies that arise between edges and between choices made in different rounds. We sidestep these difficulties by following the combinatorial approach of counting the number of possible random choices of the algorithm which lead to failure. We do so by a compression argument showing that such random choices can be encoded with a non-trivial compression. Our algorithm bears some similarity to the way agents construct a communication graph in a peer-to-peer network, and, in the bipartite case, to the way agents select servers in blockchain protocols.

As JerziDevil said, spontaneous human combustion is controversial and unproven. Spontaneous combustion, however, is very real. I was out of work several months due to it. Most combustion requires three things, fuel, heat, and oxygen. Fuel provides the energy, heat starts the reaction, oxygen releases the chemical energy in the fuel by combining with it. But oils are a little odd. Occasionally, an oil molecule will combust. By itself. With no additional heat source apart from being at room temperature or slightly warmer than that. Evan edible oils do this; if memory serves, this is what gives old food oils a rancid flavor. And this is what happened at a place I worked at. We typically soaked up excess deep fryer oil with large burlap rags. These rags would go into a simple cloth hamper. Wads of fabric crumpled up in a bag, creating multiple air spaces. And, here and there, a molecule of oil spontaneously combusts. 99 times out of a hundred, I guess, nothing bad happens. But once in a while, the combination of multiple air spaces and the insulating properties of the fabric means that as the occasional molecule of oil spontaneously combusts, the warmth this produces slowly builds up. As it gets warmer, more molecules of oil spontaneously combust. The increase in warmth speeds up. The bundle of rags gets warmer, and perhaps a bit of convection comes into play, bringing fresher air into the bundle as the warmer air rises. The heat continues to build, and build, and now a great many oil molecules are spontaneously combusting until the bundle of rags reaches flash point and bursts into flame. So, always store greasy rags in a sealed, fireproof container. Food oil, petroleum oil, doesn't matter.," "It's only an alleged condition. There is no empirical evidence that SHC is actually real. From what I have read, most cases that have alleged SHC were in fact simply people who most likely died from some other cause (heart attack, maybe) and their body was near a fuel source like an open flame or candle, and ended up knocking over or interfering with the fuel source and set themselves or their carcasses on fire.," "Everything I've seen and read about suggets strongly that the concept is the product of mistaken forensics. There is, to my knowledge, no evidence that living beings can spontaneously combust in the way that breathless TV shows may suggest. The flawed forensics are, however, based on very real evidence that's pretty compelling. It's generally accepted that short of a blast furnace, it's very hard to reduce human tissues to what's been found at some of these scenes, and that's where the idea arose from, because there seemed to be no good explanation. Experiments on pig carcasses eventually provided some insights that offer a likely explanation: People are usually dressed, and many fabrics can provide a wicking effect to burning matter. Human tissues won't burn aggressively in open air, but can so so under fabrics they're in contact with, achieving the much higher temperatures needed to produce the substantial reduction found in many of the documented cases of alleged SHC. What's probably happening is that someone loses consciousness in the vicinity of an open flame or other random source of combustion. Unable to react to ignition and the spreading fire, they simply burn, the way the pig carcasses did, in their clothes or whatever's on them, and that wicking effect produces these very dramatic reductions.

As more renewable energy sources like wind turbines and solar PV systems are integrated into power grids through inverters, novel dynamic behaviors emerge. These inverter-based resources differ from conventional synchronous generators because their internal workings aren't as transparent or standardized. Consequently, determining these devices' impacts within the electrical grid can be difficult without access to detailed technical data. One common method used to understand how inverters interact with the grid involves analyzing their behavior by examining measurements and deriving relationships between voltage and current in the frequency spectrum. This process results in "admittances," which reflect the inverters' characteristics under small signal conditions. To incorporate this information effectively in larger-scale grid analyses, it becomes necessary to establish a comprehensive, module-oriented analytical structure. Our pioneering study explores the latest advancements in representing and evaluating the dynamics of power networks containing such renewable technologies. It highlights the importance of developing precise and computationally effective methods for capturing inverter behavior, integrating individual elements accurrightly, summarizing them at higher levels, and conducting robust stability tests grounded in the overall network's admittance properties. Moreover, we address specific obstacles encountered during this type of modular analysis and propose strategies to overcome them.

The needle follows the grove in the record which moves left and right in the pattern of the music (in a mono recording, it's slightly more complicated for stereo although the principal is the same). The needle is connected to a device that generates an electric current from that movement. In older, cheap record players the generator was a piezoelectric crystal or ceramic, which creates electricity when distorted. High end decks generate the current by electomagnetic induction, moving a coil in a magnetic field or moving a magnet near a coil. These two types give better reproduction but need more amplification. You might also see separate MM and MC inputs on the amplifier for matching the characteristics of the two types. Edited for typo

Collaborative robots are now being utilized to assist humans in performing intricate tasks through effective communication and knowledge sharing. This study introduces a novel technique known as mutual reinforcement learning (MRL), facilitating skill acquisition via ongoing interaction and evaluation. Initially, an autonomous entity serves as a tutor for a beginner human learner within either a tangible (block construction) or virtual (Tetris game) setting. The mentor employs an MRL methodology, continuously adjusting their instructional approach based on the learner’s unique preference for rewards during training sessions. Such personalization is achieved through a balanced exploration-exploitation strategy aimed at recognizing essential human actions that could be beneficial in future scenarios. Consequently, this fosters the transmission of abilities from a proficient automated system to a less experienced human counterpart. Participants were categorized into trios, and the dynamics of skill transfer were scrutinized employing Simpson’s psychometric theory. To further comprehend the cognitive processes of individuals involved, five-tier Likert assessments were employed. Results led to the creation of a collective cognitive schema, advancing both human thought processes and the robotic system’s ability to decipher the psyche of its human colleagues, thus constructing a robust cooperative platform.

From the 16th to the 19th century, the territories of Eastern and Western Armenia experienced dominance by both the Ottoman and Iranian empires at various times. Come the 19th century, Russia took control of Eastern Armenia, whereas Western Armenia stayed under Ottoman sovereignty. The Armenian Genocide tragically occurred within the Ottoman Empire's borders during World War I, where Armenians residing on their native soil faced massacres. Post the Russian Revolution, several nations announced their secession from the Russian Empire, which led to the creation of the First Republic of Armenia in 1918. Later in 1920, it joined the Transcaucasian Socialist Federative Soviet Republic and then became one of the original members of the USSR in 1922. The formation of the Soviet Union resulted in the division of the Transcaucasian state in 1936; however, this did not alter the statuses of its component republics, such as the Armenian SSR. Finally, the contemporary Republic of Armenia emerged as an independent nation amidst the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991.

Karate is a tool that combines API test-automation, mocks, performance-testing, and UI automation into a single framework. It uses BDD syntax and has powerful JSON and XML assertions built-in. Developers can easily write a suite of automated tests in a fraction of the time and effort that it takes to write manual tests. In addition, Karate's patent-pending JSON engine allows you to write tests which are less verbose than Selenium Webdriver, and therefore more robust and readable. Karate uses the Java Platform for Java SE (JDK) 8 for running the tests. This talk is a high-level introduction to Karate and provides hands-on labs on how to use the Karate framework to write automated tests. The attendees will leave this talk with hands-on experience using Karate, as well as the ability to write automated tests for their own projects. How Karate framework is used in an automation suite Demonstration of Karate framework in action Introduction to the Karate framework Introduction to Karate-specific features and syntax Talk includes labs where attendees will learn how to create a Karate test file, import a test suite from a code repository, and write a Karate test from scratch. Software engineers who are interested in automated testing and want to try out Karate. Attendees should have programming experience, and ideally, experience with Java. Some familiarity with BDD is helpful, but not necessary. In 1707, the Kingdoms of England and Scotland merged to form the Kingdom of Great Britain. Subsequently, due to a failed republican uprising in Ireland in 1798, the Kingdoms of Ireland and Great Britain joined forces in 1801, establishing the United Kingdom. While the Isle of Man and the Channel Islands did not formally join the UK, they are still under the jurisdiction of the British Crown, which effectively means the British government is responsible for their well-being. Despite losing its North American territories that eventually became the USA during the early 19th century, the British Empire continued to grow significantly, ultimately spanning a third of the planet by the end of the century. Nonetheless, severe poverty persisted within the UK, especially amidst the harsh conditions faced by workers during England's industrialization period. Additionally, events such as the Irish Famine and Highland Clearances prompted mass emigration, altering the demographics and cultural landscape both domestically and abroad, while causing significant depopulation in Ireland throughout the latter half of the 19th century. Finally, most of Ireland gained independence from the United Kingdom through the Irish War of Independence and the resulting Anglo-Irish Treaty; however, Northern Ireland remains an autonomous region within the UK.

A keyboard is just a list of switches. There is several ways to connect those switches but basically when a switch is pressed, it allows current to flow thru and when it's not pressed, it doesn't. When a switch is pressed, the current flows from the power supply to the ground, or vice versa. When a switch is not pressed, there is no current flow. The switches are usually arranged in a matrix. That means that each row is connected to one wire and each column is connected to another wire. When a switch is pressed, it completes the circuit between the row wire and the column wire. The microcontroller reads the state of the keyboard by reading the state of the row wires. It does that by setting all the column wires to be outputs and setting them high. Then it sets all the row wires to be inputs. If a row wire is low, then at least one switch on that row is pressed. The microcontroller can figure out which switch is pressed by setting each column wire, one at a time, to be an output and setting it low. If the row wire is still low, then the switch that is connected to that row and column is pressed. You can use any kind of switch you want. The most common type is a momentary pushbutton switch. When you press it, it makes contact and when you release it, the contact is broken. Another type is a toggle switch. When you flip it one way, it makes contact and when you flip it back, the contact is broken. There are also slide switches and rotary switches. Most keyboards use membrane switches. They are made of two flexible sheets of material with a conductive layer in between. When you press on the top sheet, it presses the bottom sheet down and the two sheets make contact.

New Rochelle, located in the county of Westchester on the north shore of Long Island Sound, seemed to be the great location of the Huguenots in New York. It is difficult therefore to understand why this large community, with its numerous churches and schools, should have been so neglected; but we may perhaps credit it by a peculiar custom among Scotch-Irish Protestants who were attracted here by the wealth which was available for new settlements. The workmen, as soon as they had made their settlements, began to erect churches and monasteries, and these church buildings are still preserved. One of them is situated on the Hudson River bank opposite Fort Greene Park, and about two miles above Manhattan. This building dates from 1655, when there were about 400 families living at Evesham. Its interior is decorated with paintings, tapestries, and stained glass. From an old wall within one of the closets hangs a fine picture of the Virgin Mary, drawn by one of the monks. A similar room has a beautiful portrait of Francesco Merola. The original ceiling and walls survive intact. Nearby is another chapel dedicated to St. John; also a tower of the same name built in 1711, and lately restored and converted into apartment houses. The oldest part of this town was called Schuylerville, later changed to Little India, or New Amsterdam, because it contained several Dutch colonies. As early as 1585, the Dutch East India Company had sent out a missionary to bring converts to Christianity and established himself near the river. In 1597 it moved to the present site, where he founded several other settlements. One of his greatest achievements was the establishment of an academy for young men, now known as Van Cortlandt Institute. He also gave valuable land grants, which are still used to build magnificent homes and mansions. His son, Christopher, aided him in settling his own colony on Staten Island. Amongst those missionaries who came over in search of religious liberty were Adam Schadewick (1606), whose family settled in Schuyler's Village, on the east side of Manhattan, near where the Hudson Falls now runs through the park; William DeWitt Covington (1602), who was born at Fort Niagara, and settled in what became Frisco, on the northern shore of the Hudson Valley; Michael Innis (1590) and Vincent Gillman (1603). These three names alone will suffice to give us an idea of the number of settlers who sought opportunity and peace amid the woods and fields surrounding New York City. Some of them would not live long enough to see their herds or flocks prosper. Their bodies were taken across the straits between North America and Europe, being landed in England, France, Holland, Spain, Italy, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, Hungary, Romania, Serbia, Bulgaria, Macedonia, Greece, Egypt, Turkey, Persia, Arabia, China, Japan, Korea, India, and Africawherever there could be found speculators willing to buy English sheep or English corn or English wool. They returned home, sometimes having only a few hundred pounds' worth of merchandise with them. But the value of all that remained behind was counted in millions more than any mere money lost. In fact, the value of the goods brought back exceeded all our estimates of profit, even after the inflationary days of 1913. Of course, many obtained settlement for very little cash payment, while others went ahead without seeing the fruits of their labor. Still others never escaped poverty and squalor. Such thinking stands in direct opposition to the teachings and spirit of Christ." Nevertheless, Luther advocated for conflicts unrelated to religion under his concept of dual sovereignties; specifically, he supported defending one's nation during a legitimate war. In 1526, he articulated these views in his treatise 'Whether Soldiers Can Be in a State of Grace,' wherein he posited that self-defense constituted a valid cause for warfare. Movie special effects, crafted meticulously over several months, aim to achieve perfection within a particular scene and camera perspective. However, rendering a single frame may require extensive hours, despite utilizing top-of-the-line computers. Contrarily, video games must replicate the same effect across various camera angles simultaneously, while delivering 24 frames per second, relying soleptaonly on the capabilities of standard household PCs. A lack of sufficient processing power presents a significant challenge.

When discussing computational limitations in producing photorealistic visuals on consumer devices, we need to consider both the intricacies of mathematics involved and the balance between acceptable quality and precision. As accuracy increases, the complexity of calculations escalates, necessitating greater computing resources. There exists a substantial difference in processing demands between merely satisfactory results and highly precise outcomes. Delving into some technical aspects, Phong shading serves as our prevalent methodology in gaming applications. Essentially comprising basic mathematical equations estimating object colors on screens, it generally delivers adequate results except during extreme conditions where errors become evident, such as excessively bright reflections. To mitigate such discrepancies, additional techniques like shaders have been implemented; however, these remain mere approximations rather than true simulations of light behavior. Despite advancements in technology enhancing our ability to produce visually appealing imagery through complex algorithms, we ultimately rely on imitations based on simplified versions of reality, which inherently entail certain imperfections.

Plastid differentiation is not permanent, in fact many interconversions are possible. Chloroplasts may be converted to chromoplasts, which are pigment-filled plastids responsible for the bright colors seen in flowers and ripe fruit. Starch storing amyloplasts can also be converted to chromoplasts, and it is possible for proplastids to develop straight into chromoplasts. Chromoplasts and amyloplasts can also become chloroplasts, like what happens when a carrot or a potato is illuminated. If a plant is injured, or something else causes a plant cell to revert to a meristematic state, chloroplasts and other plastids can turn back into proplastids. Chloroplast, amyloplast, chromoplast, proplast, etc., are not absolute states - intermediate forms are common.

Women are born with about 1 - 2 million immature eggs. Those are reabsorbed into the body throughout the woman's life in a process called atresia. This happens starting at birth. By the time a woman reaches puberty, she normally only has about 400,000 eggs remaining. Hormones released during puberty cause fluid and support cells to surround the remaining eggs turning them into follicles. The release of hormones in the monthly cycle causes some of the follicles to develop further. Eventually one becomes larger than the others. That follicle will be expelled from the ovaries and will release its egg to be fertilized. For every follicle that releases an egg like this, about 1000 others die at some stage in the process. So really it's more like going through 456,000 - 910,000 eggs in 38 years.

Feature selection (FS) has become an indispensable task in dealing with today's highly complex pattern recognition problems with massive number of features. In this study, we propose a new wrapper approach for FS based on binary simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation (BSPSA). This pseudo-gradient descent stochastic algorithm starts with an initial feature vector and moves toward the optimal feature vector via successive iterations. In each iteration, the current feature vector's individual components are perturbed simultaneously by random offsets from a qualified probability distribution. We present computational experiments on datasets with numbers of features ranging from a few dozens to thousands using three widely-used classifiers as wrappers: nearest neighbor, decision tree, and linear support vector machine. We compare our methodology against the full set of features as well as a binary genetic algorithm and sequential FS methods using cross-validated classification error rate and AUC as the performance criteria. Our results indicate that features selected by BSPSA compare favorably to alternative methods in general and BSPSA can yield superior feature sets for datasets with tens of thousands of features by examining an extremely small fraction of the solution space. We are not aware of any other wrapper FS methods that are computationally feasible with good convergence properties for such large datasets. Keywords: Classification; feature selection; stochastic approximation; genetic algorithm

The Hubble Space Telescope has been instrumental in observing deep space and studying our solar system since its launch in 1990. Its recent discovery of watery plumes on Europa has opened doors for researchers to further explore the possibility of life in our solar system. The findings of the study were published in the journal Nature Astronomy and have been described as "exciting" and "promising" by experts in the field. Further studies will continue to unravel the mysteries of Europa and its potential to host life in our solar system.

The Twilight Zone Tower of Terror is the common name for a series of elevator attractions at the Disney's Hollywood Studios park in Orlando, the Disney California Adventure Park park in Anaheim, the Walt Disney Studios Park in Paris and the Tokyo DisneySea park in Tokyo. The central element of this attraction is a simulated free-fall achieved through the use of a high-speed elevator system. For safety reasons, passengers are seated and secured in their seats rather than standing. Unlike most traction elevators, the elevator car and counterweight are joined using a rail system in a continuous loop running through both the top and the bottom of the drop shaft. This allows the drive motor to pull down on the elevator car from underneath, resulting in downward acceleration greater than that of normal gravity. The high-speed drive motor is used to rapidly lift the elevator as well.

The potassium and sodium ion concentrations are what cause the neuron to fire. Or actually they allow the action potential to propagate along the nerve. A nerve cell starts off with a resting potential of -70 millivolts. The inside of the cell is 70 millivolts more negative than the outside. When the cell is stimulated, sodium ions rush into the cell. This causes the inside of the cell to become less negative. The concentration of sodium ions inside the cell is increased, and the concentration outside the cell is decreased. This makes the cell more positive. If the change in concentration is great enough, the nerve will fire. Once it has fired, then the potassium ions, which are normally inside the cell, are pushed out of the cell. This causes the cell to return to a resting potential. In this way, the cell is able to fire, and then reset itself. This allows the cell to fire repeatedly. If the potassium is not pumped out of the cell, then the cell cannot fire. A nerve cell does not normally fire for a long period of time. The sodium and potassium pumps keep the nerve cell ready to fire, but they only fire for a short period of time. This is why we can still function even though our nerve cells are constantly firing. Trees had always been Louise's safe place. She loved everything about them. How they smelled, how high up she could climb, how she could look out over the whole neighborhood..... how the leaves hid her from sight. That's why she had taken a liking to this live oak. It kept its leaves all year round, so she never had to worry about it being bare. And it's branches spread both wide and high, stretching up and out in every direction. Her skin was even the same color as the bark, and her gangly, bony limbs looked like branches from just the right angle. Even so, she had never climbed quite this high before, up into the trees upper boughs before finally straddling a thick, strong branch and sobbing, pressing her face into the trunk. She could feel the rough bark pressing lines into her forehead, and she let her face drop, hoping to hit it against the branch beneath her. But something stopped her halfway with a loud clank, briefly tangling up in her tight black braids. Confused, Louise opened her eyes, wiping the tears out of them so her sight wasn't quite so blurry. Underneath her, she saw buttons. When she wiped her eyes again, she realized that somehow, an ancient typewriter (Smith-Corona still etched clearly under its keys) had sunken halfway into the tree's wood. She knew that trees were able to grow around things, but the question of how the hell a typewriter ended up up here was still in her head. She looked down at it, running her fingers over the varnished wood and metal keys. There was even ancient, yellowed, water-stained paper inside of the cylinder, now freshly marked with carbon prints of the central letters on which she'd hit her head. That wasn't too surprising. What was was when, with a stifled clink from a bell halfway embedded in wood, the cylinder ratcheted back to the right before the hammers started moving on their own. She watched, transfixed, as the keys depressed themselves, one after the other, until a message was typed below her own keysmash: "Please do not do that again." She blinked. Then blinked again. Slowly, hands trembling, Louise pressed her fingers to the keys, ratcheting the paper down to the next level before typing her message as gently as she could: "Do you want me to stop typing?" Louise yanked her fingers back from the keyboard, scurrying and scooting away from the typewriter, still intensely focused on it. Again, the hammers started to lift and move by themselves. "No, typing is okay. Just don't hit it so hard. It feels weird." It took her a bit to inch herself forwards, but Louise managed to force herself to touch the keys again. "What are you?" "I'm the tree." The typewriter was still for a moment, but before Louise could type, it started moving again. "Well, no, that's not true. I'm part of the tree. There's lots of us in there." "So you're like..... a spirit?" "Yes, that's a good word for it! I've seen you before, from far away, but you've never come up to my branch. You're a human, right?" "Yes. Is that bad?" A few of the hammers twitched, then rested again, almost as if the tree was thinking, before it finally started clicking against the paper. "No. I don't think so. Some of the others do. They say humans are invasive. But I think they're still just part of all of us. I like humans. And I like you. You're why I can write." "What do you mean?" "I wondered what you were always doing with that little box of light and sand you play with. I recognized some of the symbols, and watched them until I understood." Louise cringed and had to think before typing her next response. "How old are you?" "What's'old'? I never understood that one." She started to type about birthdays, but changed her mind halfway through, licking her sweater sleeve and using it to smear off the ink. "It's like..... how long you've been existing. Like, I've been alive for ten years." "What's a year?" Louise smacked her forehead. This was difficult. "A year his how long it takes for the earth to go around the sun." "What? The earth doesn't move, it stays right here with me!" "No, it does!" She groaned. "Look, I'll explain more when I have my phone with me. that's the little box of glowing sand you were talking about. I can look it up and tell you how it really works. But a year is how long it takes for flowers to stop being flowers, then turn back into them again." "Ooooh." The keys trembled, doing a sort of fidgety dance before the number keys started moving. "I think I can remember six or seven of those." "You're very young then. Young is like not old." "Yeah. The shoot I came from is really thin. It's over on the edge of the branch." Louise looked over her shoulder, but she couldn't tell any of the shoots apart. She felt it was probably best not to mention this. "Do you have a name? Like, something you call yourself to set you apart from others?" "I don't think I do." "Well, we can come up with one later. We're about to run out of paper." "Is there more?" "Yeah, I'll go get it." Louise climbed down, meaning to just sneak into her house and grab her phone. But she grabbed some paper too, just in case she hadn't imagined everything that just happened. ..... By the time she was 13, Louise's parents had started telling her she was too old for tree climbing. She was careful to be the model child in every other capacity, so that they couldn't complain too much. It wasn't perfect, but the friend she had up there was worth it. She climbed every day back up to that old Smith Corona, on which she had carved a new name: Virginiana. But when she was turning 14, something was changing. "Niana?" "Yes, Louise?" "My parents are really going through with the divorce. Dad's almost certainly gon na get custody." "That's good! He's the nice one!" "Yeah, it is. But..." "But?" Louise leaned her head against the tree trunk again, crying like the first time she found the typewriter, watching her tears splash down between the keys. "Mom's gon na get the house. It's in her family." "What? But then where will you and your dad live?" "I don't know. Somewhere that isn't here." She sobbed, her whole body shuddering against the bark as she grabbed fistfuls of her coarse hair and pulled it. She could hear the typewriter moving, but it took a while before she could bear to open her eyes. "What would that mean for us?" "I don't know." "Is there anything I can do for you?" "I don't know." "Okay." The branches creaked mournfully, and a few leaves fluttered down, some brushing softly over Louise's wet cheeks. She curled herself up, sobbing and flicking through her phone for a few minutes before her eyes opened wide and she turned back to the keyboard. "Niana, do you want to stay with me?" "Yes, of course I do!" "Do you trust me?" "I do that too, Louise." "Even with your life?" The next reply came slower. But after a few minutes of uncertain key flicks, the hammers finally lifted to the paper. "Yes." "Then I might be able to do something. Give me a few days." ..... With a soft grunt of exertion, Louise put the bonsai pot on top of her desk by the window, gently straightening out the leaves and pouring some water soothingly into the mulch. Her RA looked over her shoulder, a soft, bewildered smile on his face. "Okay, I definitely understand the plant, but humor me: Why the hell is there a phone trapped inside it?" Louise glanced over at the ancient nokia, mostly swallowed by the tree's wood, except for the all important charger port, which she surreptitiously faced away from where anyone would see when it was plugged in. "That's a bit of a long story, but it's kind of why I picked it. As much as it matters, I just really liked this branch." The RA shrugged. "Alright, that makes sense. Tell me if you need anything. Your roomie will show up in a few hours." She nodded, locking the door behind him before climbing up into her bed. There, she took out her own phone, pausing to make sure next month's bill for unlimited texting was paid in full. Satisfied, she pulled up her messages and typed up to the top recipient: "You okay there, honey?" Before long, her phone hummed softly, lighting up: Message from Virginiana.

By turning on disabled users and modifying subsequent interference cancellation (SIC) patterns, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RISs) show potential as a solution to boost non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) systems. In examining downlink RIS-assisted NOMA networks through stochastic geometry, we initially present a distinct path loss model for RIS reflecting channels. Following this, we assess the angle distributions utilizing a Poisson cluster process (PCP) model, proving that the incident and reflected angles are evenly dispersed. Furthermore, we obtain precise analytical and asymptotic formulas for the coverage probabilities of paired NOMA users. Subsequently, we establish the analytical expressions for the average data transmission speeds of both paired NOMA users and compute the approximate expressions for regular users. The findings reveal that 1) the attainable data rates approach a ceiling as the size of RIS expands; 2) using RIS improves path loss intercept, thus enhancing system performance without affecting bandwidth. Conclusively, our study indicates that RIS-supported NOMA networks outperform traditional NOMA setups, and the SIC sequence in NOMA systems can be modified due to RIS's capability to adjust the channel conditions for NOMA users.

A language-independent alternative used in many countries is to hold up one's two fists with the index knuckle of the left hand against the index knuckle of the right hand. Then, starting with January from the little knuckle of the left hand, count knuckle, space, knuckle, space through the months. In contrast to other group sports, the preparatory phase before the main football season in the NFL follows a well-defined structure. Each NFL club participates in precisely four preseason showcase matches annually—two at their home ground and two on opposing turfs. However, every year, two clubs play an extra match known as the Pro Football Hall of Fame Game. Held mainly during August, these demonstration contests aid coaching staff in reducing the post-offseason player count of 90 to the standardized regular-season figure of right around fifty-three individuals. Although the schedule isn't as stringently fixed as the regular season, certain limitations and customs restrict potential preseason adversaries, alongside constraints on suitable dates and timings for these matches. Teams cannot divide themselves into separate units to engage multiple competitors simultaneously—a strategy observed in baseball and ice hockey. To broaden the reach of the sport, the NFL has hosted exhibitions abroad in countries like Europe, Japan, Canada, Australia, and even Mexico. It stopped hosting games in China owing to fiscal and operational challenges. Interaction between leagues hasn't occurred since 1972, and the final match against any entity apart from another NFL team happened in 1976. Many followers disapprove of exhibition games, especially those included in full-season ticket packages, leading to several legal disputes without success so far. Finally, the Pro Bowl, typically organized after the regular season (happening a week before the Super Bowl since 2011), is also categorized as an exhibition event.

Perhaps the first electric motors were simple electrostatic devices created by the Scottish monk Andrew Gordon in the 1740s. The theoretical principle behind production of mechanical force by the interactions of an electric current and a magnetic field, Ampere's force law, was discovered later by Andre-Marie Ampere in 1820. The conversion of electrical energy into mechanical energy by electromagnetic means was demonstrated by the British scientist Michael Faraday in 1821. A free-hanging wire was dipped into a pool of mercury, on which a permanent magnet (PM) was placed. When a current was passed through the wire, the wire rotated around the magnet, showing that the current gave rise to a close circular magnetic field around the wire. This motor is often demonstrated in physics experiments, brine substituting for toxic mercury. Though Barlow's wheel was an early refinement to this Faraday demonstration, these and similar homopolar motors were to remain unsuited to practical application until late in the century.

Criminal law pertains to offenses committed against the community and societal order, resulting in penalties such as imprisonment or monetary fines imposed by the government. On the other hand, civil law addresses grievances between individuals wherein the aggrieved party seeks recompense, without involving incarceration; instead, any awarded damages go straight to the injured party. Incidents often encompass elements from both legal domains. Consider a vehicular collision scenario - under civil law, the responsible driver must cover repair costs for the damage caused. Nevertheless, should negligent behavior like reckless driving or DUI be proven, this may also introduce criminal liabilities alongside the civil matter. Moreover, differing evidentiary standards exist within these branches: civil cases operate under the 'preponderance of evidence,' whereas criminal trials require proving guilt 'beyond a reasonable doubt.' Philosophically speaking, criminal law represents retribution from society for inflicted harm, whereas civil law resolves individual conflicts through judicial intervention based on statutes. While certain issues may impact society collectively, only those displaying significant magnitude and gravity warrant classification as crimes, prompting state involvement beyond merely adjudicating private disputes. Nonetheless, some situations might constitute breaches of both civil and criminal laws, subjecting the perpetrator to dual proceedings predicated upon corresponding legislative frameworks.

In this letter we propose the Rao test as a simpler alternative to the generalized likelihood ratio test (GLRT) for multisensor fusion. We consider sensors observing an unknown deterministic parameter and propose the Rao test statistic for multisensor fusion in a multipath environment with a non-Gaussian data distribution. The Rao test statistic is derived using the theory of optimal multisensor target detection and tracking [1] and [2]. The optimal estimator is shown to be the vectorized least squares estimator, and we show that the Rao test statistic is the maximum of this estimator over a subspace. This subspace is determined by the eigenvalues of the Fisher information matrix. The Rao test is then compared to the GLRT for the case of a simplex sensor network using an atmospheric observation in simulated radar data. V.L. Kulkarni, D.C.S. Jayaswal, and S.K. Scenario discovery is the process of finding areas of interest, commonly referred to as scenarios, in data spaces resulting from simulations. For instance, one might search for conditions - which could be related to a physical or chemical phenomenon - under which systems exhibit interesting behaviour. These scenarios can then be used to validate models or to find new areas of scientific research. The tool presented in this thesis is based on a combination of data mining and machine learning techniques. Our contribution consists of an algorithm for scenario discovery, as well as a graphical user interface that allows the user to interactively explore discovered scenarios. The algorithm takes as input a set of events (i.e. changes in some system) and outputs a number of scenarios along with a measure of how likely it is for these scenarios to occur. The rationale behind the algorithm is to first cluster together similar events, and then to find "interesting" clusters. Intuitively, a cluster of events is interesting if it is large (i.e. contains many events), but also "different" from other clusters. In other words, we are looking for areas in which the system behaves in a unique way. The main advantage of our approach is that it can be applied to any kind of data, provided that it can be represented as a set of events. This includes both simulation data and real-world data. In addition, the algorithm is unsupervised, meaning that it does not require any prior knowledge about the system under study.

In the UK, the process of selecting the Prime Minister isn't done through direct voting by citizens. Instead, individuals cast their votes for Members of Parliament (MPs), representing specific geographic areas known as constituencies. These MPs play a role in determining the Prime Minister; however, this process involves several steps. While the Queen has the authority to choose a potential Prime Minister candidate, she must consider whether this person is likely to receive parliamentary support. As members themselves, Prime Ministers participate in legislative activities alongside fellow MPs. Initially, until a change occurred in 2011, the Prime Minister could propose an unscheduled election at their discretion, after seeking permission from the monarch. However, since then, elections follow a set five-year timetable unless a two-thirds majority in Parliament deems otherwise. A party securing over half of the seats among the total 650 MPs can effectively govern without opposition. When there's no clear majority, coalition governments may form between multiple parties or when the largest party seeks alliances with minor ones to gain influence over policy matters. Prior to 2010, elections were initiated upon the Prime Minister's decision, whereas now, due to the implementation of the Fixed-term Parliaments Act, elections occur every five years barring exceptional circumstances wherein the sitting Prime Minister opts for an earlier poll.

In his latter days, Claude Monet became fixated on depicting the lilies within his Giverny garden situated in northern France through his paintings. However, had it not been for opposition from locals, particularly farmers, his body of work might have taken a completely different trajectory. Farmers penned letters expressing dissent towards Monet’s plan to expand his garden back in 1893; this information surfaced thanks to Ann Dumas, one of the curators for the upcoming Royal Academy's Painting the Modern Garden: Monet to Matisse exhibit. She elaborated on how farmers grew wary of Monet introducing exotic aquatic flora into their surroundings due to concerns over potential contamination of water sources and harm to livestock. Following Monet's relocation to Giverny in 1883, he sought to construct a water garden across the railroad tracks adjacent to his residence. This involved rerouting the River Epte, which is a branch of the Seine. Dumas noted that Monet faced considerable challenges obtaining authorization for his proposed project. Despite being perceived as distant from the community, Monet remained determined. The forthcoming exhibition at the Royal Academy delves into the significance of gardens within the masterpieces created by Monet alongside fellow artists such as Paul Klee, Emil Nolde, Gustav Klimt, and Wassily Kandinsky during the same period. Amongst its collection are numerous pieces spanning from the mid-1860s to the 1920s. Furthermore, visitors can expect to witness Monet's acclaimed 'Agapanthus Triptych' dating between 1916 and 1EEE1919, marking its inaugural appearance in the United Kingdom. According to Dumas, Monet regarded himself more proficient as a horticulturist than as a painter.

When Adidas, Gazprom, Hyundai-Kia, McDonald's, Budweiser, Coca-Cola and Visa signed their deals, they would have envisaged seeing their brands beamed into millions of households around the world. Pitch-side exposure at World Cup matches, accompanied by high-profile advertising campaigns, means that backing the World Cup guarantees getting your company promoted in all parts of the globe. However, having spent tens of millions of pounds to be associated with sporting excellence, those famous brands now find their name and products associated with the increasingly tarnished Fifa brand, arrests and allegations of "rampant, systemic, and deep-rooted corruption." A number of the sponsors - Coca-Cola, Kia, Adidas and Visa - have made known their concerns about what is happening at Fifa, with the latter particularly vociferous, warning that unless the global governing body makes "changes now," it would "reassess our sponsorship." And McDonald's said it "takes matters of ethics and corruption very seriously and the news from the US Department of Justice is extremely concerning. We are in contact with FIFA on this matter. We will continue to monitor the situation very closely." For the four years of the last "World Cup cycle," from 2011 to 2014, Fifa's six top tier Global Partners (as was - it is now five) paid a total of 177m (PS116m) annually, which would mean each partner paid roughly 30m a year for this status. Tier one sponsor Sony decided not to renew its contract last year - it had been a Fifa partner since 2007, after signing a contract in 2005 worth 38m annually. One publicity-savvy bookmaker has offered odds on which sponsor will be the first to pull out of its association with football's Swiss-based powerbrokers. It has Visa as the favourites, followed by Hyundai-Kia, although none of Fifa's backers have said yet they are ending their deals. Russian gas firm Gazprom is bottom of the betting to leave, and indeed it has put out a statement saying the current situation will have "no influence" on its agreement. But as the scandal is not likely to go away any time soon, what damage is being done to these well-known companies, some of whom have associations with Fifa stretching back decades? "This is disastrous for the main core group of big Fifa sponsors. For them, this is a major issue," says Anastasia Kourovskaia, a brands expert at agency Millward Brown. "The idea of sponsorship is to transfer the goodwill that supporters feel for the sport, to the benefit of a brand's equity." She suggests that the big seven corporations may have to position themselves at arms-length from Fifa, if they do not want to be hit by the fall-out from the sensational developments. "The solution is to emphasise that they are supporting football for the benefit of the game itself, and the pleasure and challenge of winning and playing football, rather than Fifa as an organisation," she says. "They have to differentiate themselves from Fifa's management." In addition, she points out that as this is not the first scandal to hit Fifa, it might be a good time for the sponsors to form a committee of their own "to ensure the ethical running of big global football events." One other unforeseen outcome of the furore may be that in future, potential sports sponsors may look to back smaller, grass-roots, events - which traditionally have been more complex and costly to back - rather than global blockbusters such as World Cups, which have a greater potential for scandal. "This might be the tipping point that sees sponsors move away from events which are'uniform' across the world, and towards more local events," she says. Its products are available at all matches in the finals tournament, and it also sponsors the World Cup Player Escort programme, in which children accompany the teams onto the pitch. Meanwhile, it appears that Nike, which is not an official Fifa sponsor (but does come up with clever marketing campaigns around the World Cup) has also been dragged into the furore, with the US Department of Justice questioning its deal with the Brazilian Football Association. The American indictments state that an unidentified "major US sportswear company" is alleged to have been involved in the payment and receipt of bribes. The Department of Justice did not name the firm, but Nike and the Brazilian football federation have been partners since a 400m sponsorship deal was signed back in 1996. Nike did not confirm it was the company alluded to, but said it "believes in ethical and fair play in both business and sport and strongly opposes any form of manipulation or bribery. We have been co-operating, and will continue to co-operate, with the authorities." Meanwhile, the editor-in-chief of Dutch newspaper Nederlands Dagblad says he does not want to see any adverts from Fifa sponsors in his paper until they have "converted." And the sponsorship industry's trade body in Europe is taking a dim view of the arrests and indictments. The European Sponsorship Association says that the developments "underline the critical importance of transparency and high ethical standards in sport and in business." They said that sponsors did not want to be associated with alleged "shady practices" and were "increasingly asking rights-owners tough questions on a range of compliance and corporate social responsibility (CSR) issues."

Hybrid Electric Vehicles Hybrid electric vehicles combine the best of a conventional internal combustion engine and an electric motor. An electric motor is added to the engine in order to power the vehicle at low speeds and to start the engine. At higher speeds the engine and the electric motor work in unison to provide maximum torque. A high-voltage battery powers the electric motor. A control unit determines the ratio of electric motor to engine torque and delivers it to the wheels. In this way, hybrid electric vehicles offer the best of both worlds. This makes themapplicable to a wide variety of machine learning models and methods. Deep generative modeling using flows has gained popularity owing to the tractable exact log-likelihood estimation with efficient training and synthesis process. However, flow models suffer from the challenge of having high dimensional latent space, same in dimension as the input space. An effective solution to the above challenge as proposed by is a multi-scale architecture, which is based on iterative early factorization of a part of the total dimensions at regular intervals. Prior works on generative flows involving a multi-scale architecture perform the dimension factorization based on a static masking. We propose a novel multi-scale architecture that performs data dependent factorization to decide which dimensions should pass through more flow layers. To facilitate the same, we introduce a heuristic based on the contribution of each dimension to the total log-likelihood which encodes the importance of the dimensions. Our proposed heuristic is readily obtained as part of the flow training process, enabling versatile implementation of our likelihood contribution based multi-scale architecture for generic flow models. We present such an implementation for the original flow introduced in , and demonstrate improvements in log-likelihood score and sampling quality on standard image benchmarks. We also conduct ablation studies to compare proposed method with other options for dimension factorization.

But Patrick Minford from Cardiff University's Business School said it was "not a workable scheme." Under Universal Basic Income (UBI) everyone would receive the same sum of money regardless of whether they work or not. There would be no requirements to show an individual is looking for a job either. In Scotland the policy has support from across the political spectrum, with feasibility work under way ahead of possible pilot schemes in Glasgow and Fife. Jamie Cooke, head of the RSA think tank in Scotland, told the BBC's Sunday Politics Wales programme: "Moving from a system where you aren't working to a system where you are, you won't face those penalties, you retain your consistent payment. However Prof Minford, who was an adviser to former prime minister Margaret Thatcher, told the programme: "This is not a workable scheme because it's far too expensive. Asked if he was worried by Mr Drakeford's comments, Prof Minford replied: "It's quite worrying for Wales. Automated design of neural network architectures tailored for a specific task is an extremely promising, albeit inherently difficult, avenue to explore. While most results in this domain have been achieved on image classification and language modelling problems, here we concentrate on dense per-pixel tasks, in particular, semantic image segmentation using fully convolutional networks. In contrast to the aforementioned areas, the design choices of a fully convolutional network require several changes, ranging from the sort of operations that need to be used - e.g., dilated convolutions - to a solving of a more difficult optimisation problem. In this work, we are particularly interested in searching for high-performance compact segmentation architectures, able to run in real-time using limited resources. To achieve that, we intentionally over-parameterise the architecture during the training time via a set of auxiliary cells that provide an intermediate supervisory signal and can be omitted during the evaluation phase. The design of the auxiliary cell is emitted by a controller, a neural network with the fixed structure trained using reinforcement learning. More crucially, we demonstrate how to efficiently search for these architectures within limited time and computational budgets. In particular, we rely on a progressive strategy that terminates non-promising architectures from being further trained, and on Polyak averaging coupled with knowledge distillation to speed-up the convergence. Quantitatively, in 8 GPU-days our approach discovers a set of architectures performing on-par with state-of-the-art among compact models on the semantic segmentation, pose estimation and depth prediction tasks.
