Existing work in intelligent communications has recently made preliminary attempts to utilize multi-source sensing information (MSI) to improve the system performance. However, the research on MSI aided intelligent communications has not yet explored how to integrate and fuse the multimodal sensory data, which motivates us to develop a systematic framework for wireless communications based on deep multimodal learning (DML). In this paper, we first present complete descriptions and heuristic understandings on the framework of DML based wireless communications, where core design choices are analyzed in the view of communications. Then, we develop several DML based architectures for channel prediction in massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems that leverage various modality combinations and fusion levels. The case study of massive MIMO channel prediction offers an important example that can be followed in developing other DML based communication technologies. Simulations results demonstrate that the proposed DML framework can effectively exploit the constructive and complementary information of multimodal sensory data in various wireless communication scenarios.

Your network cable doesn't know what a byte is. It doesn't care whether you are sending 8 bits at a time, or 8000, there is no inherent notion of a byte. Ethernet, for example, operates on octets, three bits at a time, so thinking in terms of bytes is unnatural in that context. In addition, 100 bytes of data on your hard drive probably isn't 100 bytes on your network. Your data is going to be put into groups, and that group will have header data, separators, error correction, etc. That group will be put into another group, with more data, that is put into another group, with more data. All that might be compressed, making it smaller again. The 800 kilobits on your network are not the same as the 100 kilobytes on your disk.,If you pay for internet service, the connection can transfer a certain number of bits per unit time at maximum speed. How many bytes that translates to is not necessarily constant. Start by reviewing the [OSI model] (URL0). Your ISP provides a basic connection at the media layers: simply passing bits around, and routing. That is usually all. However, most people think in terms of the host layers. "I am downloading this file in Chrome and it says I get X bytessec." That translates to 8X bits per second. However, that is using TCPIP: the raw number of bits your connection can provide are not all dedicated to the contents of that file you are transferring. TCP adds overhead: each packet has timestamps and checksums, so the client knows if a packet is corrupt or was received out of order. Acknowledgement packets are sent in both directions. All of these consume bits. Going back to your question, this is more of a perception issue than anything. Data pipes are generally measured in the number of bits they can transfer because that is what they do. Even the concept of a "byte" may be foreign to the physical layer in OSI, for example. People think in terms of bytes, because that is what their web browsers report when transferring files. A byte is the smallest addressable entity in computer memory, and files on a disk are measured in bytes, not bits. Humans are trained to think in bytes. However, overhead ensures that the number of bits at the physical layer of the network is not simply eight times the number of bytes transferred at the application layer. If we started advertising speeds in bytes and classifying connections using bytes, it would never match what people actually see in web browsers or SFTP clients. While it is possible to measure network speeds in terms of bytes, it would not really help anything and could add confusion.','I wish there would be! But in reality, I don't think there will be a push to switch. Any company that has a business predicated on how quickly their internet speed can flow (ISPs, router manufacturers, etc.) can put a number that is 8x bigger than the actual amount of traffic it can withstand. It's pretty much Marketing 101, when you can put in some extremely small fine print what the actual speed is, or even just put "Mbps" instead of "MBps" in small print, knowing the general consumer public won't know the difference. Companies would willingly have to change their marketing style to push Bits out of contention for Bytes. The market dictates this will never happen, given that the first company to do so would see significantly less business due to everyone else having inflated numbers.','Yes, but it's completely drowned out from the marketing department. This paper proposes an event-triggered add-on safety mechanism to adjust the control parameters for timely braking in a networked vehicular system while maintaining maneuverability. Passenger vehicle maneuverability is significantly affected by the combined-slip friction effect, in which larger longitudinal tire slips result in considerable drop in lateral tire forces. This is of higher importance when unexpected dangerous situations occur on the road and immediate actions, such as braking, need to be taken to avoid collision. Harsh braking can lead to high-slip and loss of maneuverability; hence, timely braking is essential to reduce high-slip scenarios. In addition to the vehicles own active safety systems, the proposed event-triggered add-on safety is activated upon being informed about dangers by the road-side infrastructure. The aim is to incorporate the add-on safety feature to adjust the automatic control parameters for smooth and timely braking such that a collision is avoided while vehicle's maneuverability is maintained. We study two different wireless technologies for communication between the infrastructure and the vehicles, the Long-Term Evolution (LTE) and the fifth generation (5G) schemes. The framework is validated through high-fidelity software simulations and the advantages of including the add-on feature to augment the safety margins for each communication technology is evaluated.

Fundamentally, radio waves obstruct objects by creating an electrical charge upon contact. A negligible charge would result from hitting something like a tree or animal, whereas a large metallic antenna could generate a significant charge. The design of an antenna affects its capability to interfere with various components of the electromagnetic spectrum. Analogously, consider an antenna similar to a buoy anchored in the sea, linked to the seabed via a spring, which is also attached to a fish scale for recording data. As waves pass by, the buoy oscillates, exerting varying degrees of tension on the spring, thereby capturing the wave's presence through these fluctuating forces. Similarly, within an antenna, the electromagnetic field causes the free electrons in the material to move back and forth, generating minute voltage variations that are measured. For more comprehensive information, delve into Faraday's law and Maxwell's equations.

A [private copying charge] refers to a fee imposed on the purchase of recording devices. This fee has been implemented in numerous nations as a means to remunerate creators for the unavoidable replication of their work facilitated by user-friendly recording technology. It's important to note that this charge assumes the media will be utilized for personal duplication of copyrighted material, irrespective of whether such activity occurs. The purpose of this charge is to serve as restitution for copyright proprietors who claim financial loss due to declining sales. My stance is that this arrangement equitably recompenses the rights holders through discussions held between their delegates and the authorities; moreover, unless explicitly prohibited, it grants individuals an ethical – if not juridically supported – right to duplicate and disseminate any desired quantity of content. However, this argument does not account for materials without associated private copying charges, jurisdictions lacking these fees, or monetary gain derived from non-personal distribution of copied works.

Technology is an extremely potent tool that can be leveraged for human development and social good. Owing to the great importance of environment and human psychology in driving human behavior, and the ubiquity of technology in modern life, there is a need to leverage the insights and capabilities of both fields together for nudging people towards a behavior that is optimal in some sense (personal or social). In this regard, the field of persuasive technology, which proposes to infuse technology with appropriate design and incentives using insights from psychology, behavioral economics, and human-computer interaction holds a lot of promise. Whilst persuasive technology is already being developed and is at play in many commercial applications, it can have the great social impact in the field of Information and Communication Technology for Development (ICTD) which uses Information and Communication Technology (ICT) for human developmental ends such as education and health. In this paper we will explore what persuasive technology is and how it can be used for the ends of human development. To develop the ideas in a concrete setting, we present a case study outlining how persuasive technology can be used for human development in Pakistan, a developing South Asian country, that suffers from many of the problems that plague typical developing country.

This article follows a software engineering student's attempt at training a more efficient version of the 124M parameter version of GPT-2. The resulting model didn't perform as well as GPT-2. However, it was an interesting exercise that has inspired me to think about some theoretical and practical implications. Theoretical Implications In this section I will discuss two major benefits gained from using neural networks for text generation tasks. These are (a) generating additional outputs from fixed-length input, (b) exploiting domain knowledge contained in pretrained models such as Word2Vec or BERT. Both of these topics have been discussed by previous work [28, 43]. Learning Additional Outputs with Neural Networks Adding new features is one way to improve existing systems for text generation tasks. Previous approaches like weighted language models [2], adding constituency trees [18], category embeddings [3] etc., use hand-crafted features but there can be potential gains if we learn them automatically through machine learning techniques. Intuitively, adding extra parameters makes our network capable of producing more output than just what its original structure allows. This may imply better performance on downstream applications where multiple choices need to be produced simultaneously. Exploiting Domain Knowledge Pre-training Models Another source of extension is building on top of other deep neural networks models which have previously shown promising results. Pre-training gives us a good starting point. We could then fine-tune it while keeping everything else unchanged. A particularly popular idea here is "transfer" between layers of different architectures [31]. Transferring parts of learned representations from another system helps us avoid overfitting problems [33]. Also note that transfer learning works best when used together with regularization methods [34]. Transfer Learning with GPT-2 GPT-2 offers access to pre-trained word vectors obtained via a Google search engine application called Search Vector Machine [20]. It consists of three components: 1. Query Answer System -this component predicts whether a given query matches any document collection based on their Web content. 2. Word Sense Disambiguation -a part-of-speech tagger trained on Twitter data without specifying words' senses 3. Text-to-Text Language Model trained on unsmoothed parallel corpora extracted from Wikipedia articles. These resources make up the back-end that generates text directly from raw documents. For example, assume you want to generate sentences containing the word "grown-ups." You would do so by feeding "grown-ups" into the neural network along with keywords related to adults such as: "heavy drinker," "gay," "marriage..." Then the web search tool searches within the entire corpus specified above and returns all matching terms ranked according to their similarity to the target term -given by the cosine distance between corresponding n-gram vector (where n 8). As indicated earlier, each single token receives a separate representation after being fed through different convolutional layers which combine information across different dimensions of lexical semantics [36]. So instead of having only one special "personality" generated per sentence, now we get many possible variations depending upon how people talk about themselves and others around them [7]. That means subsequent processing steps, e.g., sentiment analysis, can benefit greatly by taking advantage of a large number of candidate responses. PRELIMINARY RESULTS We first evaluated the effectiveness of the improved version of GPT-124M against four baselines for generating contentious political comments. These are: Random Dictation: randomly selects options from a dictionary; CNNReceptive Field Attention Transformer [19]: generates text by combining both traditional attention-based sequence-to-sequence framework [22] with recurrent connections within encoderdecoder [16]; Unsupervised Sequence Generation [8]: uses multi-modal conditional generative adversarial nets [10] to train the generator; MultiMemory Seq-GAN [9]: builds a memory network connected with the decoder to store inputs andor internal states during training time. A total of 100k random tweets were collected from English social media platforms including Twiiter, Reddit, Facebook and Instagram. They were filtered out if they contain offensive contents and unfamiliar phrases. After removing repetitions, duplicates and stopwords, no less than 50 of the remaining samples survived filtering. Next, they were split evenly into training and testing sets. All baseline generators except RDFAT use a maximum vocabulary size of 5K. Evaluation Protocol To evaluate all generators we employ the same protocol described in Section 4.1. From each test sample we try to produce 10 unique choices, i.e., tokens outside the training set. Each choice needs to correspond to exactly one correct answer from the final list of answers provided by the dataset owners. Table 1 shows evaluation metrics averaged over ten runs. In particular, the new version featured much fewer errors thanks to the addition of contextual information encoded in LSTMs [32]. Introducing Word Embeddings achieved noticeable improvements also in case GPT-124M wasn't able to successfully map certain short forms into proper names. A Full Duplex Base Station (FD-BS) can be used to serve simultaneously two Half-Duplex (HD) Mobile Stations (MSs), one working in the uplink and one in the downlink, respectively. The same functionality can be realized by having two interconnected and spatially separated Half Duplex Base Stations (HD-BSs), which is a scheme termed CoMPflex (CoMP for In-Band Wireless Full Duplex). A FD-BS can be seen as a special case of CoMPflex with separation distance zero. In this paper we study the performance of CoMPflex in a two-dimensional cellular scenario using stochastic geometry and compare it to the one achieved by FD-BSs. By deriving the Cumulative Distribution Functions, we show that CoMPflex brings BSs closer to the MSs they are serving, while increasing the distance between a MS and interfering MSs. Furthermore, the results show that CoMPflex brings benefits over FD-BS in terms of communication reliability. Following the trend of wireless network densification, CoMPflex can be regarded as a method with a great potential to effectively use the dense HD deployments.

There could be several reasons behind this situation, including:

Firstly, regarding major studios such as Bethesda, EA, and BioWare, there seems to be a trend towards diminishing the overall quality of games produced by these companies. This decline can be observed through various aspects, such as simplifying gameplay mechanics compared to previous titles or releasing products filled with unresolved issues. Additionally, these studios often exploit their dedicated fan base by outsourcing tasks meant for internal teams to external communities without proper compensation.

EA, in particular, has faced numerous controversies involving mistreatment of customers, exemplified by incidents like embedding a rootkit within their Origin platform and causing widespread chaos with the launch of SimCity.

As consumers continue to tolerate and even applaud these practices, some argue that they exhibit a lack of critical thinking skills, naively believing that mods created by third parties will rectify any shortcomings present in the games themselves. However, while supporting mods and offering tools for customization can enhance players' experiences, it does not justify releasing underdeveloped or incomplete games initially.

Moreover, many popular franchises now adopt a strategy wherein new content is offered as downloadable content (DLC), resulting in players having to pay additional fees beyond the initial purchase price. Although this approach provides more opportunities for extended playtime and variety, it also promotes a sense of entitlement among consumers, expecting constant updates and expansions post-release.

In contrast, earlier generations viewed substantial additions to a game through expansions as separate releases, typically encompassing significant portions of fresh content equivalent to the original title. Examples include the Civilization series, where each successive installment introduced entirely new features rather than merely expanding upon existing ones.

In conclusion, the current state of the video game industry appears to reflect both consumer complacency and corporate greed. Consumers seemingly priorright to voice dissatisfaction with certain practices, yet simultaneously condone and encourage them, thereby perpetuating a cycle of subpar product offerings and excessive monetization schemes.

In this paper, we focus on the meta distribution for the cache-enabled networks where the locations of base stations (BSs) are modeled as Poisson point process (PPP). Under the random model with a cache-enabled BS, the received signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) at the user (U) is modeled as a continuous function of the distance between U and the serving BS. We derive the closed-form expression for the probability density function (PDF) of the SNR for the considered random model and then use the obtained PDF to find the meta distribution for the network. The closed-form expression for the meta distribution is derived analytically. The closed-form expression is used to investigate the outage probability and the ergodic capacity of the network. The effect of the caching efficiency of the BS, the number of UEs and the power control on the meta distribution is also analyzed.

Ms Baker added: "If fans think it is OK to call people with mental health problems who have been psychiatric inpatients'psychos', then we are turning back the tide of progress on public attitudes that are more respectful and less judgemental of people living with mental health problems. During the classical era, Mozart and Beethoven often improvised the cadenzas to their piano concertos (and thereby encouraged others to do so), but they also provided written cadenzas for use by other soloists. Artificial life originated and has long studied the topic of open-ended evolution, which seeks the principles underlying artificial systems that innovate continually, inspired by biological evolution. Recently, interest has grown in the principles underlying artificial systems that innovate on a shorter timescale, under a designer's guidance. Innovation with a designer's guidance is not a new idea; examples include traditional engineering and nature's own methods of evolution. But the growing interest in this idea is due to the perceived need to make innovation in software, hardware and even robotics easier, faster and cheaper. What is new in this area is that artificial systems now appear to be able to innovate and improve themselves, and that they can do so with relatively little help from designers. It is now possible to design systems that autonomously produce novel variants, and autonomously evaluate them. These systems can even autonomously recognize promising variants, perhaps without even recognizing that those variants are promising, and autonomously explore promising directions. This paper surveys three topics in artificial systems that innovate: genetic programming, artificial immune systems and grammatical evolution. The surveys highlight some of the major achievements in each field, and suggest some ways in which each field has come to understand the nature of innovation in artificial systems. Genetic Programming (GP) is a general-purpose, nature-inspired, stochastic search algorithm based on the Darwinian principle of the survival of the fittest (Koza, 1992). GP starts with an initial population of computer programs. These programs are then improved through repeated cycles of selection, variation and replication. In selection, individuals with better performance are selected, and the remainder are discarded. In variation, the selected individuals are modified to create a new population. In replication, the new population is evaluated and the cycle repeats. The selection, variation and replication components of GP are inspired by the principles of evolution. Before the reforms of the 19th and 20th centuries, the state organisation of the Ottoman Empire was a simple system that had two main dimensions, which were the military administration and the civil administration. The Sultan was the highest position in the system. The civil system was based on local administrative units based on the region's characteristics. The Ottomans practiced a system in which the state (as in the Byzantine Empire) had control over the clergy. Certain pre-Islamic Turkish traditions that had survived the adoption of administrative and legal practices from Islamic Iran remained important in Ottoman administrative circles. According to Ottoman understanding, the state's primary responsibility was to defend and extend the land of the Muslims and to ensure security and harmony within its borders within the overarching context of orthodox Islamic practice and dynastic sovereignty.

Super Bowl 50 was an American football game to determine the champion of the National Football League (NFL) for the 2015 season. The American Football Conference (AFC) champion Denver Broncos defeated the National Football Conference (NFC) champion Carolina Panthers by a score of 24-10 to win their third Super Bowl ring. The game was played on February 7, 2016, at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, California. This was the fifth Super Bowl to be played in the San Francisco Bay Area (home to both the AFC and NFC teams), the other four having been played in Los Angeles and the San Francisco Bay Area. It was the final Super Bowl to be played in California before the 2018 season, as well as the final Super Bowl played in the Bay Area, as next year's game will be hosted in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The Broncos became the 14th franchise to win multiple championships, and the 10th to win the Super Bowl more than once. The Broncos are the second team to win the Super Bowl after not winning their conference during the season (the other being the Green Bay Packers in 1997); the Broncos won the AFC Championship after losing the previous season. Following a 2015 season that was marred by injuries to key players (including the loss of quarterback Peyton Manning), Denver finished the regular season at 12-4, the best record in the AFC. In the playoffs, they defeated the Pittsburgh Steelers in the Divisional Round and the New England Patriots in the AFC Championship. In the Super Bowl, Denver jumped to a 24-0 halftime lead on the Panthers. Carolina scored a touchdown with just over three minutes left in the third quarter, but failed to score again and was shut out in the second half. This was the first Super Bowl in which the halftime show was performed by a female headliner (Beyonce); it was also the first time the game was telecast in virtual reality (VR), in a pilot project for Fox. Carolina quarterback Cam Newton, in his second NFL season, was the first black quarterback to start and win a Super Bowl. In the third quarter, he scored his first career rushing touchdown, becoming the first quarterback in Super Bowl history to do so. On the field at the end of the game, he was interviewed by CBS's Tracy Wolfson, who was the first female NFL sideline reporter. Both teams entered the Super Bowl with a 12-4 regular season record. The Broncos were making their 11th appearance in a Super Bowl, having won three previous titles in 1998, 2000, and 2014. The Broncos were making their first appearance since losing Super Bowl 48 to the Seattle Seahawks. The Panthers were making their second Super Bowl appearance, having lost Super Bowl 50 to the Broncos. The Panthers were making their first appearance since losing Super Bowl 51 to the New England Patriots. Super Bowl 50 was also the final game of the regular season for both teams. The Broncos entered the game having won three consecutive games to close out the regular season. Carolina won their final two games to finish the regular season. The Panthers were able to play the entire season with only one significant injury to their starting offense. The Panthers entered the game as 3.5-point underdogs, as they were unable to defeat the Broncos in the regular season and were starting a quarterback in Cam Newton who was not a prolific passer. The Broncos entered the game having defeated Carolina in both of their regular season games. The game was the first Super Bowl to be played in the San Francisco Bay Area since Super Bowl 35, which was played in San Diego in 2001, the first Super Bowl to be played in California since Super Bowl 27, which was played in San Diego in 1993, and the first Super Bowl to be played in the Bay Area since Super Bowl 47, which was played in Santa Clara in 2013. A total of 45,000 tickets were allotted to the Panthers and Broncos, and the remaining tickets were distributed by the NFL to host committee members and other local charities. The game was also the first Super Bowl since Super Bowl XLVIII to have a hometown television announcing team for both teams. The NFL awarded the Super Bowl 50 to the Bay Area on February 15, 2013,

One of the most effective algorithms for differentially private learning and optimization is objective perturbation . This technique augments a given optimization problem (e.g. deriving from an ERM problem) with a random linear term, and then exactly solves it. However, to date, analyses of this approach crucially rely on the convexity and smoothness of the objective function, limiting its generality. We give two algorithms that extend this approach substantially. The first algorithm requires nothing except boundedness of the loss function, and operates over a discrete domain. Its privacy and accuracy guarantees hold even without assuming convexity. This gives an oracle-efficient optimization algorithm over arbitrary discrete domains that is comparable in its generality to the exponential mechanism. The second algorithm operates over a continuous domain and requires only that the loss function be bounded and Lipschitz in its continuous parameter. Its privacy analysis does not require convexity. Its accuracy analysis does require convexity, but does not require second order conditions like smoothness. Even without convexity, this algorithm can be generically used as an oracle-efficient optimization algorithm, with accuracy evaluated empirically. We complement our theoretical results with an empirical evaluation of the non-convex case, in which we use an integer program solver as our optimization oracle. We find that for the problem of learning linear classifiers, directly optimizing for 01 loss using our approach can out-perform the more standard approach of privately optimizing a convex-surrogate loss function on the Adult dataset.

Invariance with respect to linear or affine transformations of the domain is arguably the most common symmetry exhibited by natural algebraic properties. In this work, we show that any low complexity affine-invariant property of multivariate functions over finite fields is testable with a constant number of queries. This immediately reproves, for instance, that the Reed-Muller code over F p of degree d p is testable, with an argument that uses no detailed algebraic information about polynomials, except that low degree is preserved by composition with affine maps. The complexity of an affine-invariant property P refers to the maximum complexity, as defined by Green and Tao (Ann. Math. 2008), of the sets of linear forms used to characterize P . A more precise statement of our main result is that for any fixed prime p 2 and fixed integer R 2 , any affine-invariant property P of functions: f F p n [ R ] is testable, assuming that the complexity of the property is less than p . Our proof involves developing analogs of graph-theoretic techniques in an algebraic setting, using tools from higher-order Fourier analysis.

According to Wylie, suppressing the History of Ming misrepresents the actual state of affairs concerning Sino-Tibetan interactions. Zinc deficiency is crop plants' most common micronutrient deficiency; it is particularly common in high-pH soils. Zinc-deficient soil is cultivated in the cropland of about half of Turkey and India, a third of China, and most of Western Australia, and substantial responses to zinc fertilization have been reported in these areas. Plants that grow in soils that are zinc-deficient are more susceptible to disease. Zinc is primarily added to the soil through the weathering of rocks, but humans have added zinc through fossil fuel combustion, mine waste, phosphate fertilizers, pesticide (zinc phosphide), limestone, manure, sewage sludge, and particles from galvanized surfaces. Excess zinc is toxic to plants, although zinc toxicity is far less widespread.

DoorDash is testing a feature called'Return a Package' that allows customers to book a delivery person to return packages to the nearest post office, UPS, or FedEx location. Customers will be charged 1 (2 percent) of each package returned if they request assistance from Door Dash. When customers select this option on their order confirmation page after placing an online order for food andor grocery items from participating stores such as Kroger, Whole Foods Market, Sprouts Farmers Market, Safeway, Albertsons Companies, The Fresh Market, Fry's Food Stores, Sam's Club, Publix Super Markets and others, Door Dash automatically completes the delivery with all purchases in one cart prior to checkout. Afterward, when the customer selects "Return A Package" then declines any additional deliveries offered by Door Dash at the time of pickup, Door Dash charges them upfront only what was spent originally (0-25). All other fees are included. For example: If a total original purchase amount of 100 is made before taxes plus add-on items totaling 70 were ordered after meals but no tip, every order would be delivered separately during the first order along with regular priced groceries and two carts worth of orders total about 140 including tax. This discounted fee will apply regardless of how many separate transactions occurred since the last transaction. So, even though it may seem like more than 2 being paid out, this cost could actually end up costing less than paying multiple shipping costs because there's also gas used during the trip back which ends up costing much more per mile compared to driving around neighborhoods delivering items purchased earlier. Delivery drivers cannot earn tips through this program.

Inflammatory diarrhea occurs when there is damage to the mucosal lining or brush border, which leads to a passive loss of protein-rich fluids and a decreased ability to absorb these lost fluids. Features of all three of the other types of diarrhea[clarification needed] can be found in this type of diarrhea. It can be caused by bacterial infections, viral infections, parasitic infections, or autoimmune problems such as inflammatory bowel diseases. It can also be caused by tuberculosis, colon cancer, and enteritis.[citation needed]

The inside of your eye is lined with a viscous fluid called the vitreous humor. This gel is attached to your retina, the light sensing part inside of the eye. When a vitreous hemorrhage occurs, blood from your retinal blood vessels enters the vitreous. Most often, this occurs in patients with diabetes. Vitreous hemorrhages can also occur with a traumatic eye injury or as a complication of surgery. When the vitreous hemorrhage is small, it does not always cause vision loss. However, as the blood accumulates and grows, it may interfere with vision. As the vitreous hemorrhage clears, it is possible that it may cause floaters and flashes. In some cases, the hemorrhage does not clear and may lead to a retinal detachment. Vitreous hemorrhage may be diagnosed with a dilated eye exam. A non-dilated eye exam may miss the hemorrhage. Sometimes a retinal hemorrhage is discovered when a patient complains of a sudden drop in vision. In some cases, a vitreous hemorrhage is not diagnosed until the hemorrhage clears. If you have sudden vision loss, you should see your ophthalmologist right away. Treatment of a vitreous hemorrhage depends on the size and location of the hemorrhage and whether or not there is associated retinal detachment. If the hemorrhage is small and not causing visual loss, observation and close follow-up is recommended. For larger hemorrhages, you may be placed in a face-down position for several days to a week. This position allows the hemorrhage to clear faster. After the hemorrhage clears, the vitreous can be removed in a procedure called a vitrectomy. This is often necessary because the vitreous is attached to the retina and can contract and pull on the retina and create a detachment. If a retinal detachment is present, the retina is repaired at the same time as the vitrectomy.

The rows are oriented to run from near the mouth (the "oral pole to the tail down each flank and up each side of the body. When this shellfish comes close enough to its food source - typically algae or other small plant matter - it grabs hold with its new, long-pointed teeth and tears off pieces before eating them. This is how the snail feeds. Appearance and anatomy Skeleton and structure Snails have no inner skeleton, because they possess gills, not lungs. They breathe by drawing water into their bodies through gill slits at the back, where it passes over their soft tissues and through specialised holes in the shells. A number of internal organs are found inside the animal: the mantle cavity, containing most of the digestive system (including the stomach) the heart the liver the gallbladder the spleen the pancreas the kidneys the bladder The snail's head has five distinct parts: the eyes the upper lip (which surrounds the mouth but can be retracted when feeding), covering the entrance to the oesophagus the lower lip, guarding the anus the snout (or proboscis). It bears a single tooth (or sniculus) in the top half of the roof behind the eye socket, while above and below this there are many similar-shaped ridges. There are four pairs of limbs on each side of the shell: The first pair is located under the snout; these have short hairs that help prevent the animal getting sandy. The second pair begins from the base of the shell and extends forward towards either end. The third pair consists of the caudal peduncle and the terminal appendages, which reach outwards about 80mm from the dorsal margin. The fourth pair consist of the caudal peduncle, set far back in the shell, and the terminal part, which protrudes forwards 10-15 cm beyond the ventral margin of the shell. By keeping their legs apart, snails avoid becoming tangled during transport. Shell As with all gastropods (shelled molluscs such as clams), the shell of a common garden snail is asymmetrical. Each side is divided into several segments separated by joints. Some species also lack one segment altogether. The shell is made largely of calcite, calcium carbonate, and contains an interlocking network of crossbars that form chambers for storing food. At least six ribs run down each side of the body. These support the weight of the shell and allow the snail to move easily. The large intestine passes between the ribs like spokes of a wheel. During digestion, nutrients pass through separate compartments of the intestinal wall and so do not mix with liquid waste products until their full journey has been completed. The excretion process works similarly - the contents of the intestine must run separately past the various compartments within the intestines before exiting via the cloaca. In some species the shell folds backwards as if extending across the body. Such sheaths are called coiled shells, and many species have coiled shells, including the freshwater mussel. Others have what are known as oval shells (see image right): the shell resembles an egg-shaped box, rather than being shaped like a spiral. Many long-lived species live in shallow rock pools; they need protection from predators attacking underwater, predators who may use the high ridge above the bill as a perch. As such, the shell may contain a ridge, often prominent in the middle, to act as a deterrent. Morphology Cranial morphology varies considerably among different genera of land gastropod. For example, the common garden snail is elongated and long-bodied, while the red pond snail is comparatively squat. Giant common snails grow to lengths up to tall, much larger than any other snails (except perhaps the giant African land slug Pachymeria gigantea). Colouration Common snails come in a wide range of colours, depending on the habitat they inhabit and individual genetics. Because of this variability, there are more than 800 recognised colours of common snails. Most commonly seen colours include whites, browns, black, light yellow, salmon pink and peach pink. Ctenophores may be abundant during the summer months in some coastal locations, but in other places they are uncommon and difficult to find. In larger bays with more dense intertidal zones, ctenophore populations tend to be much more numerous because of their ability to colonize large areas of sand that would otherwise remain underwater in strong currents or high tides. The IUCN rate for the red tide in Cuyahoga Bay was reduced by 95 between 2012-2014, when most of the deaths occurred along the Great Lakes coastlines. In this work we introduce a differential rendering module which allows neural networks to efficiently process cluttered data. The module is composed of continuous piecewise differentiable functions defined as a sequence, with each image element being represented by an operation on the previous layer and its output connected along one axis (e.g., a vector), or along another direction (e.g.: a matrix). The module uses these parallel processing modes when applying to noisy data as well as regularized partial derivatives in order to reduce the computation time considerably compared to concurrent gradient descent algorithms. We also find that application of such sequential components results in extremely efficient numerical convergence rates for both local methods and non-local method on dense values. In particular our study shows that for non-convex optima it is possible to obtain a mean error reduction factor of 30 even if the number of iterations used per pixel value depends only slightly among individual images. Towards Image Compression Using Nonlinear Iterative Methods: A Review of Recent Advances [pdf] PDF. This paper provides an overview of recent advances made towards compression techniques based on nonlinear iterative methods. Chief Executive Officers (CEOs) primarily have two responsibilities within an organization. The behavior of users in social networks is often observed to be affected by the actions of their friends. Bhawalkar et al. introduced a formal mathematical model for user engagement that is based on this observation, but it does not consider social influence outside Facebook [4]. We present a system for modeling every instance where one friend's action changes the likelihood or timing of another friend taking an action in a networked environment (such as social media). Unlike previously proposed models that predict future user activity from current interactions alone, our approach has three key components: 1) It uses historical data about all previous interactions between pairs of friends with respect to each other; 2) It combines this information with the prior probabilities and dynamics of the rest of the participants; 3) The engine controls how these elements are combined to predict new events. We call our method Predicting Action Timelines (PAT), which provides more accurate predictions than similar existing methods while leveraging temporal data structures already present in modern social media systems. Previous work in human-computer interaction (HCI) research attempts to understand social phenomena such as user engagements using different types of probabilistic approaches cite23. For example, some studies use Bayesian inference to determine if two users might engage in conversations or share content, others make use of mutual acquaintances and knowledge graphs to infer social connections between users or predict future outcomes cite21, yet another group tries to anticipate netiquette violations, determining when an unsolicited message may result in a negative reaction at inbox level cite6. Our tool PAT builds upon the first category of work, providing a means for predicting the next move in a sequence of potentially complex actions over time. In particular, we aim towards understanding what happens after a single event occurs. This differs markedly from many past works that focus only on analyzing what takes place before an event begins, missing out important aspects of large scale social interaction.

The nobility of Poland was significantly larger compared to other European nations, making up approximately 10-12% of the overall population of the historical Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. Furthermore, they constituted no more than 16% of the Roman Catholic population, primarily made up of ethnic Poles. Notably, the Polish szlachta often included regional nobility assimilated into Poland-Lithuania, such as Ruthenian boyars and Livonian nobles.

In comparison, the nobilities of other European countries, excluding Spain, accounted for just 1-3% of the population. Unlike many other nations, Poland lost its independence relatively early, leading to the end of noble rule in 1795 due to the partitions of Poland. Consequently, the rights and futures of these nobilities became subject to the laws and regulations of the Russian Empire, the Kingdom of Prussia, and the Habsburg Monarchy. Over time, their privileges faced increasing restrictions until their complete abolition through the March Constitution of Poland in 1921.

The second Sunday in May is designated as Mother's Day, similar to how the fourth Thursday of November is recognized as Thanksgiving. This was established by someone without any deep significance behind it; it simply became tradition. In the United States, the origins of Mother's Day can be traced back to a time when it served as a symbolic gesture of peace and unity during the aftermath of the Civil War. Ann Jarvis initiated a commemoration known as "Mother's Friendship Day" in 1868, although she passed away in 1905 with limited success beyond certain regions. A pivotal moment occurred in 1877 when an incident involving two opposing factions led to a heartfelt speech given by a minister whose sons were unjustly involved. His mother stepped up to conclude his address, prompting her sons to honor her memory annually on the second Sunday in May. They also encouraged others to participate in this observance. By 1910, Anna Jarvis succeeded in having West Virginia officially acknowledge Mother's Day, leading other states to follow suit. Subsequently, in 1914, Congress issued a decree designating the second Sunday in May as Mother's Day, resulting in President Wilson formally announcing the inaugural nationwide Mother's Day.

It is prohibitively expensive to annotate a large-scale video-based person re-identification (re-ID) dataset, which makes fully supervised methods inapplicable to real-world deployment. How to maximally reduce the annotation cost while maintaining the performance of re-ID is a fundamental yet challenging problem. To address this issue, we propose an Annotation-Free Unsupervised Video-based Person Re-Identification (AFUR) approach. Specifically, we develop a temporal consensus learning strategy to automatically discover and align consistent features from videos without any annotation. The proposed method first extracts a set of local descriptors from the input video frames. Then, a temporally consistent feature selection method is designed to select a subset of reliable keyframes and their corresponding local descriptors. After that, an unsupervised discriminative learning module is trained on these selected local descriptors to learn a person-specific feature representation. Finally, an aggregation network is used to aggregate the person-specific feature representations across video frames to obtain a compact video-level feature descriptor. To evaluate the effectiveness of our approach, extensive experiments are conducted on two large-scale video-based re-ID datasets, namely MARS and DukeMTMC-VideoReID. The experimental results demonstrate that our AFUR achieves significant improvement over the state-of-the-art methods with minimal annotation cost.

Once upon a time just after high school, I managed a Radio Shack. I can't speak specifically to the wholesale cost of things like consoles and video games since we didn't carry them in store, but I'm familiar with the markup on basic consumer electronics. If a console is anything like a new TV or stereo, the store isn't turning a huge profit on it. We had maybe a 10-15 margin on something like a new TV. The real profit was always in accessories, especially anything with a Radio Shack brand on it. Say you buy a new TV but also pick up a pack of batteries, a surge protector, and an HDMI cable. Those accessories you just bought made the store more of a profit than the TV. Something like a pack of batteries might be marked up 500 or more. You also bought a protection plan? Even better. In the grand scheme of overall business profitability, even if you eventually have to sell certain items for less than they cost you, you can make it up elsewhere. Some people would come in to the store multiple times to drool over an expensive item without buying. Each time though they might leave with 1 or 2 inexpensive items. Multiply that across a dozen such people who are "just looking" and profits start adding up because people are still buying items on which there are huge profit margins. So ultimately, if a new model of something is coming out and I need to drop the price on the old one to get it sold, it's not that big of a deal because it's more than made up for it by driving foot traffic into the store.

There exist firms specializing in conducting surveys. An example of such a company is "Nielsen." Similar to "The Nielsen Ratings" that some individuals may be familiar with, these organizations randomly select households by sending envelopes containing questionnaires. These forms request personal and viewership data, including age, number of residents, preferred television programs and radio stations. Once completed, respondents return the form via mail. The collected data is subsequently entered into a centralized database. Participants receive thanks upon completion, and are informed that further communication may occur, either through phone calls or emails. Individuals possessing a genetic variant in the PDSS2 gene typically consume fewer cups of coffee, according to findings by researchers at the University of Edinburgh. This variant appears to impair cells' capability to metabolize caffeine, leading to its prolonged presence in the system. Consequently, individuals with this genetic makeup receive an adequate caffeine boost with reduced coffee intake. A researcher involved in the investigation stated that these results indicate the inclination to consume coffee might be rooted in our genetic composition. To investigate further, the team analyzed the genomic information of participants from various Italian villages and Dutch citizens, asking them to report their daily coffee consumption habits. They discovered that those with the PDSS2 genetic alteration generally consumed fewer cups of coffee compared to those without the modification—approximately one less cup per day on average. These findings were substantiated when the study was repeated using a large sample size of Dutch residents; however, the impact of the gene on coffee consumption appeared somewhat diminished due to differences in preferred serving sizes across cultures. The study advocates for additional comprehensive investigations to validate these initial observations and explore the underlying molecular connection between the PDSSEE gene and coffee consumption patterns. Published in Scientific Reports, this collaborative effort involved institutions like the Universities of Edinburgh and Trieste, the Burlo Garofolo Pediatric Institute in Italy, and multiple entities within the Netherlands.

Reactive oxygen species, such as superoxide ion (O- 2) and hydrogen peroxide (H 2O 2), are dangerous by-products of oxygen use in organisms. Parts of the immune system of higher animals produce these molecules for the purpose of killing invading microbes. Because these reactive oxygen species are also produced during normal metabolism, there is some cost to the host organism. Plants and some prokaryotes have mechanisms for eliminating these reactive oxygen species. Chemical species that are short-lived (often a fraction of a second) and highly reactive are called free radicals. A free radical is a molecule that contains at least one unpaired electron. Free radicals are important in many biochemical processes, such as the oxidation of food during metabolism and the production of energy. Free radicals are also highly reactive and can damage cells. Free radicals are found in pollutants such as ozone, cigarette smoke, and pesticides. These free radicals are short-lived and react quickly. In aerobic organisms, they are formed as byproducts during cellular respiration. If they are not removed, they will react with and damage important cellular components. For this reason, aerobic organisms have enzymes that remove free radicals. These enzymes use antioxidants to convert the free radicals to less reactive compounds. Vitamins A, C, and E are antioxidants. These vitamins donate electrons to the free radicals, converting them into compounds that are less reactive and less likely to damage cells. Some free radicals are important in immune system reactions. These free radicals are not removed by antioxidant enzymes. Some of the free radicals are used to kill invading microorganisms. Some are used to destroy cancerous cells. The free radicals involved in these reactions are short-lived and can be easily controlled. Some bacteria are capable of causing disease in humans and other organisms. Many of these bacteria can be killed by antibiotics. Unfortunately, some bacteria have become resistant to these antibiotics. Bacteria that are resistant to antibiotics have plasmids that code for enzymes that destroy antibiotics. These plasmids can be transferred between different bacteria and even between different species. The plasmid that codes for resistance to penicillin, for example, has been found in over 100 different species of bacteria. When the plasmid is transferred, the new bacteria become resistant to penicillin as well. Bacteria have another means of becoming resistant to antibiotics. They may mutate and become resistant without acquiring a plasmid. This type of resistance is called chromosomal resistance because it is coded for by the bacterium's chromosome. If the chromosomal resistance is advantageous, the bacterium will live and reproduce. The chromosomal resistance will then become widespread in the population. Normally, a population of bacteria contains a small number of bacteria that are resistant to antibiotics. The use of antibiotics kills off the sensitive bacteria, but leaves the resistant bacteria to reproduce. Because there are fewer bacteria present, the resistant bacteria have more food and fewer competitors. They reproduce rapidly, and soon the population consists entirely of bacteria that are resistant to the antibiotic. Food producers often give antibiotics to cattle, hogs, and poultry to promote growth and prevent infections. The use of these antibiotics promotes the development of antibiotic-resistant bacteria in animals. These bacteria may then be transmitted to humans. In addition, the widespread use of antibiotics to treat diseases in humans also promotes the development of antibiotic-resistant bacteria. When a person is infected with antibiotic-resistant bacteria, it is very difficult to find an effective treatment. Rob opened his eyes and shot upright in his bed. Then a mischievous grin spread across his face. Rob was always special, ever since he was a young boy he could sense things, he could avoid trips, falls and other accidents. It was at his eighteenth birthday, however, that Rob sensed his own death. He was due a party, a surprise party, which he already knew about because he sensed everything. He also sensed that attending his party meant his own death. On his way home some delinquent would stab him over petty change. This was averted by simply not attending. His time had run out, and he had sensed Death, hovering persistently at his heels like a puppy dog. Everything Death tried to throw at Rob, he had avoided. This continued for several years until Death apparently threw in the towel and had disappeared. Now something else was here, Rob could sense it. But not only that, Death had manifested himself personally to Rob earlier that night and told him to prepare for visitors! "I've almost lost my job because of you!" Death barked angrily, pointing an accusing finger at Rob. "Do you know how difficult it is to find a decent job in hell these days with this economy?!" Rob shrugged his shoulders impassively. Trying to stifle the grin that was persistently trying to spread across his face. Death waited for an answer, after a few minutes of awkward silence Death brought his boney hand to his skull, which was obscured by the long draping hood of his cloak. "Y'know what! I quit!" Death threw his scythe to the ground like an infant throwing a teddy after not getting his own way. "I hear McDonald's are recruiting." Rob jeered and he burst into a fit of laughter. "You will be visited by three demons." Death said with a defeated sigh. "Silence, Loneliness and Darkness." Death chuckled to himself, it was a dry chuckle devoid of any humour. "Good luck!" He said sarcastically, before disappearing into a cloud of mist. Now Rob sat awake in bed, grinning with anticipation as Death's threats came to fruition. In the corner of the room stood a woman, she wore a white dress and her long black hair was matted in thick clumps that draped across her pale face like curtains. She was unusually thin and quite tall. Rob didn't need an introduction, he could already sense the demon was Silence. What worried him, albeit only slightly, was the fact he hadn't sensed her arrive. "Ah! Silence! I didn't hear you come in! Can I get you anything? Tea? Coffee?" Silence shook her head. Rob energetically jumped out of bed and turned his bedside lamp on. He couldn't sense any weaknesses he could exploit. He could however sense that if he screamed, she would drag him to hell. He turned to face her. Her lips were stitched shut and her eyes were like two icey pools of water, they regarded him coldly with a murderous gleam. She held in her boney fingers a rolled up parchment, which she presented to Rob. 'Dearest Robert Fairbrook. I understand that you have somehow avoided Death for an unprecedented amount of years and I would like to express both my congratulations and commiserations for accomplishing such a feat. This charismatic young lady is called Silence, the more placid of my trinity of sorrow. Take her hand and come willingly or I will be forced to invite Darkness and Loneliness to this party. And those two make Silence seem like a pussy cat. Sincerely your pal, Satan.' Rob kissed his teeth and screwed the parchment up into a small ball and tossed it into the corner of the room. "Sorry but no deal." Silence didn't seem pleased by his refusal to comply. She grabbed his shoulder, her tight, contorted, decaying flesh creaked as she outstretched her arm. Her grip was ice cold on his bare shoulder. "Wait!" Rob yelled. She recoiled at the pitch of his yell and released her grip, provoking a devilish grin from Rob's lips that reminded her of her master. "Oh that's right! Silence, you hate noise. I'll tell you what lady, if you can beat me at a game of cards I'll come quietly, if not, you'll have to drag me out of this world how I came into it." He paused for dramatic effect. "Kicking and screaming. Either way I'll be coming with you, deal?" Silence nodded reluctantly. Snap was the game of choice, and of course, being Silence by name and Silence by nature the demon lost the game because of her inability to yell the important phrase when she wanted to call snap. "I win." Rob sighed. "It's a hollow victory though. I don't particularly have the energy to kick and scream." He walked over to the kitchen side, resting his hand on the handle of a kitchen knife resting on the draining board. He turned his head and as he predicted, Silence was stood directly behind him, her eyes now shone bright red and her hair flailed around wildly independently as if it was a separate being. Perfect. Rob sensed exactly how far he needed to slash with the knife to cut the stitches holding her lips together. Then he brought his foot down on her bare foot with all the strength he had. "OW! MY FOOT!" Silence yelled in agony. "I win." Rob uttered coldly. Silence screamed as light shone from her eyes and mouth and she was banished back to hell. One down, two to go. The second demon appeared exactly an hour later. His very presence radiated sorrow and misery that made Rob feel like he didn't even want to live any more. He resisted as much as he could and sat up in bed to face Loneliness. Loneliness was a terrible sight to behold, his skin was blue and his eyes were permanently frozen wide open, his mouth was stretched open far beyond the limits of the human jaw. He looked sad, and Rob almost felt sorry for him. "I don't even want to be here anymore." Loneliness cooed in an emotionless voice. His mouth didn't move as he spoke. To Rob's horror he found himself muttering the same thing. Involuntary tears streaming down his cheeks. He reached for the knife, which he had brought back to bed with him. He put it to his wrist and felt the cold steel blade biting into his flesh. Droplets of blood started to appear as the blade bit into his wrist. "I seriously just want to die." Loneliness said in his monotonous drone. He hovered closer, his forlorn aura contaminating Rob even more intensely. "My friend!" Rob yelled at Loneliness suddenly, he leapt at Loneliness and wrapped his arms around Loneliness' mishapen body in an awkward embrace. "I promise you that if I ever come to hell, I'll forever be your friend." Rob glanced up at the horrifying face of Loneliness, tears welled in his dead eyes and streamed down his deformed cheeks. "You are sincere." Loneliness said in disbelief. Like Rob, Loneliness could also sense things, particularly emotion. Loneliness was touched. It had been several millenia since Loneliness had ever felt anything positive. "You understand that by keeping your promise when you finally do come to hell, you will be condemned to an eternity of misery as my friend. I'm cursed by this aura of sadness and despair." "Friends are always there for each other in times of need." Rob sobbed, a result of being in such close proximity of Loneliness. They spent an hour talking, Loneliness agreed to leave Rob alone in exchange for his friendship. But left him with a final warning. "Beware of Darkness." He droned tediously. "He is the Devil's favourite." With that, light shone from his eyes and mouth as he was banished back to hell. Rob felt the relief of Loneliness' absence almost immediately. He felt as if a huge weight had been lifted from his shoulders. "I meant it when I said I'd forever be your friend if I ended up in hell." Rob smiled, knowing Loneliness had sensed he was being sincere. "And IF I ever do end up in hell I'll honour that promise! Unfortunately Loneliness, I don't ever plan on going to hell!" Rob was quite lonely. And the terrible aura Loneliness emitted had amplified that feeling to the point where Rob could barely restrain himself from ending his life. Fortunately he had outsmarted Loneliness, even though he did relate to the pathetic demon on some bizarre level. Two down...... One to go.

An internationally recognized method utilized by various nations involves displaying both fists together, aligning the index finger joint of the left hand with that of the right. Beginning with January at the minor joint on the left side, proceed to alternate counting using the joints and gaps—joints symbolize 31-day months while spaces denote shorter months such as February (with either 28 or 29 days) or those consisting of 30 days. Notably, the intersection point where the hands meet isn't considered, thereby indicating that July and August correspond to the two central index finger joints.

Most of the world's airports are owned by local, regional, or national government bodies who then lease the airport to private corporations who oversee the airport's operation. For example, in the United Kingdom the state-owned British Airports Authority originally operated eight of the nation's major commercial airports - it was subsequently privatized in the late 1980s, and following its takeover by the Spanish Ferrovial consortium in 2006, has been further divested and downsized to operating just five. Germany's Frankfurt Airport is managed by the quasi-private firm Fraport. While in India GMR Group operates, through joint ventures, Indira Gandhi International Airport and Rajiv Gandhi International Airport. Bengaluru International Airport and Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport are controlled by GVK Group. The rest of India's airports are managed by the Airports Authority of India.

The convention standard for object detection uses a bounding box to represent each individual object instance. However, it is not practical in the industry-relevant applications in the context of warehouses due to severe occlusions among groups of instances of the same categories. In this paper, we propose a new task, i.e. , simultaneously object localization and counting, abbreviated as Locount , which requires algorithms to localize groups of objects of interest with the number of instances. However, there does not exist a dataset or benchmark designed for such a task. To this end, we collect a large-scale object localization and counting dataset with rich annotations in retail stores, which consists of 50 , 394 images with more than 1.9 million object instances in 140 categories. Together with this dataset, we provide a new evaluation protocol and divide the training and testing subsets to fairly evaluate the performance of algorithms for Locount, developing a new benchmark for the Locount task. Moreover, we present a cascaded localization and counting network as a strong baseline, which gradually classifies and regresses the bounding boxes of objects with the predicted numbers of instances enclosed in the bounding boxes, trained in an end-to-end manner. Extensive experiments are conducted on the proposed dataset to demonstrate its significance and the analysis discussions on failure cases are provided to indicate future directions. The term 'stan' originates from the Persian word for 'land,' thus leading to designations such as "Land of the Afghans," "Landsin the Uzbek region," and "Land of the Kazakhs." Contrarily, Pakistan stands apart since there is no group known as the "Paks." Instead, it derives from the initial letters of five regions - Punjab, Afghania, Kashmir, Sindh, and Balochistan - comprising the nation. Interestingly, "Pak" also translates to 'pure' in Pashto, making it fitting. 

Regarding the question of why numerous Western countries incorporate '-land' at their ends, perhaps there might be discussions on Arabic platforms similar to those here. As for the etymology of '-stan,' it traces back to the Proto-Indo-European language, where the root 'stā-' meant 'stand.' Over time, this evolved differently across languages, including Russian ('-stan') meaning 'settlement' and several Slavic languages using it to denote 'apartment' or 'state.' In English, the root influenced words like 'stand,' 'state,' and 'stay.' Ancient Indo-Iranian peoples, direct descendants of Proto-Indo-Europeans, utilized it to signify 'place' or 'location.' Modern "-stan" country names acquired these terms either through linguistic inheritance (e.hduring Urdu and Pashto) or adoption (as seen with the former Soviet Union's primarily Turkic nations speaking Turkic languages). Furthermore, the compound word 'Bagh-dad,' combining 'bagh' (garden) and 'dad' (city), gave rise to place names like Islamabad.

A portrait of a well-known Cheltenham grocer, painted onto the shop door of his store in the 1960s, could be restored thanks to a grant from the Heritage Lottery Fund. The painting, which depicts Harold Godwin, was created by local artist Derek Snook and is described as a 'fading memory' of the area's past. Godwin was the proprietor of The Grocer's Shop on Winchcombe Street from 1948 until his death in 1973. The shop has since been demolished, but the mural remains on the gable end of the building, which currently houses a charity shop. The restoration project aims to reinvigorate the piece of art, which has become an important part of local history. It will include researching the history of the site, restoring the mural, creating a website and interactive app, holding an exhibition and creating educational resources. The Heritage Lottery Fund has awarded 48,000 towards the cost of the restoration, which has been welcomed by the project's organisers. "Harold Godwin was a much-loved figure in Cheltenham," said local councillor Matthew Bowles. "This project will ensure that his memory lives on in this wonderful painting." The restoration project is expected to be completed by the end of 2017. Once completed, it is hoped that the mural will become a focal point for the area's cultural heritage.

The French Army consisted in peacetime of approximately 400,000 soldiers, some of them regulars, others conscripts who until 1869 served the comparatively long period of seven years with the colours. Some of them were veterans of previous French campaigns in the Crimean War, Algeria, the Franco-Austrian War in Italy, and in the Franco-Mexican War. However, following the "Seven Weeks War" between Prussia and Austria four years earlier, it had been calculated that the French Army could field only 288,000 men to face the Prussian Army when perhaps 1,000,000 would be required. Under Marshal Adolphe Niel, urgent reforms were made. Universal conscription (rather than by ballot, as previously) and a shorter period of service gave increased numbers of reservists, who would swell the army to a planned strength of 800,000 on mobilisation. Those who for any reason were not conscripted were to be enrolled in the Garde Mobile, a militia with a nominal strength of 400,000. However, the Franco-Prussian War broke out before these reforms could be completely implemented. The mobilisation of reservists was chaotic and resulted in large numbers of stragglers, while the Garde Mobile were generally untrained and often mutinous.

A capacitor, initially referred to as a condenser, serves as a static, dual-ended element within electronic systems, functioning to hold electrical power momentarily via an electric field. Their designs differ significantly; however, each incorporates at least two electrically conductive components (plated surfaces), which are isolated from one another using a non-conductive substance (a dielectric - essentially, an insulator capable of storing energy through polarization). These conductive elements may consist of various materials such as metallic films, foils, powdered particles, or even conductive electrolytes. The role of the dielectric layer is crucial as it enhances the overall storage potential of the capacitor. Typical materials employed for this purpose encompass glass, ceramics, polymer films, air gaps, vacuums, papers, micas, and certain oxides. Found extensively across numerous everyday electronic products, capacitors operate differently than resistors since they do not lose energy. Rather, these components preserve energy as an electrostatic force existing between their plates.

According to reports, the officers repeatedly kicked and punched the protester while he lay on the ground, already restrained with handcuffs. The incident was captured on video and widely shared on social media, causing outrage and drawing global attention to the crackdown on protesters in Hong Kong. The sentencing was a significant moment for the city's justice system, as it marked one of the few instances where police officers have been held accountable for their actions during the protests. The case has been closely watched by human rights groups, who have accused Hong Kong authorities of turning a blind eye to police violence against protesters. The seven officers were found guilty of assault last month, with the judge describing their actions as a "deliberate and gratuitous act of violence." The officers maintained that they were simply doing their jobs, but their defense was dismissed by the judge. The severity of the sentence has been praised by human rights activists, who say it sends a strong message that police brutality will not be tolerated in Hong Kong. However, many also criticized the fact that the officers were not charged with more serious offenses like torture or causing grievous bodily harm, despite the severity of the victim's injuries. The incident is just one of many that have fueled the ongoing unrest in Hong Kong, as citizens continue to demand greater political freedom and accountability from their government. Despite the challenges, activists and international observers remain hopeful that meaningful change can be achieved through peaceful protest and diplomatic pressure.

First of all, I am largely opposed to the prison-industrial complex. I feel that many of the laws behind it are arbitrary (re: the drug war and victimless crimes), and are largely rooted in racism and classism. Mass incarceration of people from marginalized communities further entrenches inequality, and takes away resources from those who need it the most. Additionally, the prison-industrial complex is a for-profit system that relies on the suffering of inmates to make money. It is an exploitative and dehumanizing system that harms both inmates and guards alike, and fails to provide any meaningful rehabilitation or restorative justice. Furthermore, it is wasteful, expensive, and ineffective - incarcerating people has been shown to not reduce crime rates. Therefore, I believe that the current prison-industrial complex should be abolished, and replaced instead with a system that focuses on providing true rehabilitation and restorative justice, rather than simply punishing offenders. This would reduce the amount of people being incarcerated and ensure more equitable outcomes for those involved.

The recent success of deep neural networks is powered in part by large-scale well-labeled training data. However, it is a daunting task to laboriously annotate an ImageNet-like dateset. On the contrary, it is fairly convenient, fast, and cheap to collect training images from the Web along with their noisy labels. This signifies the need of alternative approaches to training deep neural networks using such noisy labels. Existing methods tackling this problem either try to identify and correct the wrong labels or reweigh the data terms in the loss function according to the inferred noisy rates. Both strategies inevitably incur errors for some of the data points. In this paper, we contend that it is actually better to ignore the labels of some of the data points than to keep them if the labels are incorrect, especially when the noisy rate is high. After all, the wrong labels could mislead a neural network to a bad local optimum. We suggest a two-stage framework for the learning from noisy labels. In the first stage, we identify a small portion of images from the noisy training set of which the labels are correct with a high probability. The noisy labels of the other images are ignored. In the second stage, we train a deep neural network in a semi-supervised manner. This framework effectively takes advantage of the whole training set and yet only a portion of its labels that are most likely correct. Experiments on three datasets verify the effectiveness of our approach especially when the noisy rate is high.

Testing Deep Neural Network (DNN) models has become more important than ever with the increasing usage of DNN models in safety-critical domains such as autonomous cars. The traditional approach of testing a DNN model is to manually inspect the model and its hidden layers. This approach is time consuming, tedious and error prone. In this paper, we propose a novel approach to automatically test the deep neural networks (DNNs) for any network topology. Our approach tests a DNN model using a modified version of the test data-generating distribution. The goal is to test the DNN model against a set of predefined test cases. We propose a novel methodology for efficiently generating a test set for testing a DNN model, which is applicable to any network topology. Our methodology is based on the notion of a "synthetic test set" and a "noisy" version of the data-generating distribution. We propose an iterative algorithm to generate a set of synthetic test data, and we show that a few iterations are enough to generate a test set that satisfies the required properties. We evaluate the performance of our approach using a representative dataset, with DNN models generated by TensorFlow, and compare it to three different baselines. Our results show that our approach is able to test DNNs with a high success rate, without requiring manual inspection, and without any change to the model, the training code, or the data-generating distribution. Attacking Machine Learning (ML) models by adding or changing labels in the training data is a major challenge that ML practitioners and researchers face. This problem is particularly challenging because, the more complex the model (e.g., deep neural networks), the harder it becomes to detect and understand the effect of an adversarial label. In this paper, we describe a white-box approach to attacking machine learning models, by adding or changing labels in the training data, and to detect the effect of these attacks on the model's performance. Our approach is based on an adaptive sampling strategy that allows us to generate a set of perturbed data, in a way that maximizes the effect of an adversarial label on the model's prediction. This approach is based on a Bayesian framework where the prediction of a model is represented as a joint probability distribution over the original data space, and the perturbed data space. We then use an adaptive sampling strategy to maximize the effect of an adversarial label on the model's prediction. We evaluate the performance of our approach on a representative dataset using three different deep neural networks models. Our results show that our approach can successfully add adversarial labels to the training data and detect their effect on the model's prediction, in a few seconds for each data point and without requiring the use of an expensive optimization algorithm.

Free movement of goods within the European Union is achieved by a customs union, and the principle of non-discrimination. The EU manages imports from non-member states, duties between member states are handled through tariffs which can be lower than for national members or higher depending on what would make it more expensive to import into the EU (e.g., if there were quotas in place). The trade agreement between Canada and the EU goes even further, eliminating tariffs to allow investments freely across borders. An important advantage that this arrangement has over the WTO is its flexibility; it only applies when countries meet one criteria: mutual recognition of standards for their products, meaning they must have similar rules for all products unless they've agreed otherwise with another country. This means no need for any sort of "preclearing" of potentially hazardous substances and other regulations before they enter each others markets. While some companies may see significant cost savings because of these provisions, consumers could end up paying more. Overall, protectionism remains widespread around the world - most notably under President Donald Trump's administration as he tries to renegotiate NAFTA, but also China, Japan, South Korea, Turkey, Saudi Arabia, India, Brazil etc. It represents a real threat to global prosperity, especially given how much we rely on free international trade.

Throughout the Miocene epoch, the continents kept moving towards their current locations. Except for the missing land connection between South and North America, all contemporary geological characteristics were already forming. The absence of this link allowed for the emergence of the Andes Mountains due to the ongoing subduction at the edge of South America's Pacific coastline, while also pushing the Mesoamerican Peninsula further southwards. Meanwhile, the Indian subcontinent persisted in its collision course with Asia. Over time, the Tethys Sea gradually diminished until it completely vanished around 19 to 12 million years ago when Africa came into contact with Eurasia in what is now Turkey and Arabia (according to ICS 2004). This process led to mountain formation in the Western Mediterranean area, coupled with an overall decline in global sea levels which resulted in the temporary desiccation of the Mediterranean Sea during the late Miocene - known as the Messinian salinity crisis.
