Clock displays utilize seven segment displays, which consist of seven horizontal lines forming an enclosed eight shape. Illuminating a single segment results in high brightness, whereas activating several segments reduces the overall luminance. Consequently, various numerals exhibit distinct levels of brightness; for instance, '8' may appear faintly lit compared to 'EE'. To mitigate this issue, each segment is illuminated individually rather than concurrently. Consider the example of displaying the digit '7'; initially, the upper line is energized, followed by the upper-right and lower-right lines before returning to the initial position. These transitions occur within milliseconds, leveraging the concept of persistence of vision, making it difficult to discern individual segments turning on or off. The technique employed here mirrors that of CRT televisions, where images are rendered sequentially line by line from top to bottom, yet due to rapid execution, viewers fail to perceive any discrepancies. However, when consuming food, jaw movements create vibrations affecting visual refresh rates, causing segments to separate visibly. A similar effect can be observed with CRT screens when mimicking lip motions resembling a motorcycle engine.

With mobiles overtaking desktops as the primary vehicle of Internet consumption, mobile web performance has become a crucial factor for websites as it directly impacts their revenue. In principle, improving web performance entails squeezing out every millisecond in the webpage delivery, loading and rendering. However, on a practical note, an illusion of faster websites suffices. This paper presents 'DriveShaft', a system envisioned to be deployed in Content Delivery Networks, which improves the perceived web performance on mobile devices by reducing the time taken to show visually complete webpages, without requiring any changes in websites, browsers, or any actions from end user. DriveShaft employs (i) crowd-sourcing, (ii) on-the-fly JavaScript injection, (iii) privacy preserving desensitization, and (iv) automatic HTML generation to achieve its goals. Experimental evaluations using 200 representative websites on different networks (Wi-Fi and 4G), different devices (high-end and low-end phones) and different browsers, show a reduction of 5x in the time required to see a visually complete website while giving a perception of 5x-6x faster page loading.

This study examines a complex nonlinear multi-hop multi-user multiple-input multiple-output (MU-EEE) communication system where several users transmit data to a base station equipped with multiple antennas utilizing intermediary nodes with single-bit transmission capabilities. An ideal maximum-likelihood (ML) decoder is introduced under the premise of having complete and accurate knowledge of the entire communication pathway's conditions; nevertheless, its feasibility is hindered by impractical assumptions regarding channel knowledge and significant computational requirements. Consequently, we propose an innovative method based on guided machine learning techniques to overcome these obstacles. We suggest simplifying the intricate multi-user environment into a more manageable representation requiring fewer adjustable factors. Surprisingly, our results show that such a simplified model can yield outcomes close to those obtained through the ML algorithm when moderate pilot signals are employed within specific scenarios. Additionally, we introduce an intelligent learning-based decoder capable of dynamically adjusting to changes in the communication channel by refining its internal model according to accurately interpreted data packets treated as labeled samples. Finally, we explore the potential advantages of employing a sophisticated artificial intelligence model known as a deep neural network to perform user discrimination tasks without relying on any predetermined models or assumptions about the channel characteristics. Although this approach leads to increased demands on processing power during the learning phase, it has the advantage of potentially rectifying inaccura cuations resulting from oversimplified representations of the channel. Through comprehensive comparisons conducted via simulation studies, we illustrate the superiority of the suggested supervised-learning methods over conventional model-dependent strategies in handling the challenges presented by this particular type of communication scenario.

Agile development is a big world, with many different branches of it. You'll often hear things like Kanban, Extreme Programming, Lean when referring to Agile Development. All of these are different schools and they take their own spin on what Agile Development means. I'm not going to go into what different schools exist, or how they work. But most organizations adopt an Agile Process which uses parts from multiple schools. But to understand Agile we need to move back to what existed before Agile. This was called the Waterfall Process, and some organisations actually still use this today. Waterfall breaks out the development processses into different "steps." To move on to the next step you need to have completed the step before. This process also spans the entire development process; meaning it starts when you have the idea, and is done when you've delivered the product. This can be a really long time, like a year. In the traditional Waterfall Process these steps are: Requirements (what do we wantneed to do) Design (decide how we do it) Implementation (start coding it) Verification (Test it out that it works, and that it does what we want) Maintenance (fix bugs, new versions etc.) Here's a picture of the traditional Waterfall Scheme: URL1 It's worth mentioning that there's a lot of hate going around these days for waterfall. However there are several organisations who successfully use it. Some organisations have been doing Waterfall for so long that switching to another way of doing things would be so costly in terms of training and loss of production that Waterfall is simply a better choice right now. Enter Agile Development. Agile development counters Waterfall in that it says that it's stupid to decide on Requirements and Design for a product that will be out on the market in a years time. A lot can change in year. The market might not need a new social network in 2014, for example. But with Waterfall, if this is what you've decided, you're pretty much locked into creating one. There's very little feedback going on in Waterfall, either. People in step 4 might realise that the Design or Requirements of the product were wrongly stated. And then there's no easy way to backtrack to change it. They were made by different people and, besides, that step is already done with. Agile wants to put things into smaller cycles, with more feedback between the different steps. It also removes a lot of the walls created between the different steps. You can backtrack to Design or Requirements if you feel they where wrongly stated. This is done by not being too granular in specifying what we want to create before we start. Instead we can talk about what problems we want the product to solve and just generally how we want it to work. It's more about specifying that "I'd like a tool that let's me connect with my grandmother to share family events" rather than saying "We need to create a social network for elderly people, aimed at connecting them with their family. They should be able to share photos, letters, and status updates. There should also be a button which let's them "rub each others calfs." So, once we have a general idea of what we want to create we break the development process into smaller cycles (sometimes called Sprints). These sprints are usually just a few weeks long. Before a sprint we only decide on what we want to develop during the next sprint, and only work on that for those weeks. When the sprint is done we look at how we did, and what we should be developing for the next sprint. We can then take into account how the market is currently acting, and what we've learned from developing in the previous sprint (Maybe we've found a better way of doing things, or maybe a cool new feature which solves a problem). A lot of people combine this with an even shorter cycle: a daily meeting. During this meeting the team go through what they did yesterday, and what they're doing today. All to have clear feedback and transparency in communication. Here's a picture which explains it in Technicolor: URL0 An Agile Development Process usually allows teams to be faster in reacting to the market, or other insight.

Under appropriate cooperation protocols and parameter choices, fully decentralized solutions for stochastic optimization have been shown to match the performance of centralized solutions and result in linear speedup (in the size of the network) compared to centralized solutions. In this talk, I will consider a class of decentralized algorithms for stochastic optimization that are able to tolerate information loss due to arbitrary non-adaptive actions of nodes, and assume that they are designed with these non-adaptive actions in mind. In particular, I will present the first decentralized algorithms for general stochastic optimization with sublinear speedup, even when the solution set of the problem is known in advance. A related question, which I will also present, is how to design an efficient distributed memory system for machine learning. I will show that if the data distribution in memory is known in advance, then a distributed algorithm can be designed which has sublinear speedup relative to a centralized algorithm. In contrast, when the distribution is unknown, then distributed algorithms can have only sublinear speedup with respect to a centralized algorithm, and the sublinear speedup depends on the distribution. This is joint work with Sudipto Banerjee, Victor Vu and Ming-Hsuan Yang.

Essentially, the purpose of these extensive processes within the judicial system is to minimize the occurrence of executing individuals who are innocent yet unjustly convicted. These procedures consist of several stages, each with its own objectives:

1. Direct review: The first phase involves evaluating the legitimacy of the conviction through an appellate court, ensuming whether any significant mistakes occurred during the original trial. Possible results include affirmation of guilt, discovery of multiple legal errors necessitating retrial, or sentencing reconsideration resulting in a less severe punishment (though rare).

2. State collateral review: If no issues arise during the direct review, those still seeking exoneration may proceed with another appeal opportunity limited to state courts. This step might prolong their imprisonment while awaiting resolution. Individuals tried at the federal level omit this stage and advance directly to federal habeas corpus.

3. Federal habeas corpus: Accused persons may file a civil suit challenging their case in federal court, prioritizing constitutional protections and potentially introducing fresh evidence, such as DNA data. Approximately 21% of capital punishment cases have experienced reversals at this level.

The entirety of these meticulous measures serves the ultimate goal of avoiding execution of innocents; however, instances of miscarriages of justice remain evident throughout history. As scientific advancements like DNA testing shed light on previous cases, our understanding of these complexities continues to evolve.

We present an integrated framework for using Convolutional Networks for classification, localization and detection. We show how a multiscale and sliding window approach can be efficiently implemented within a ConvNet. We also introduce a novel deep learning approach to localization by learning to predict object boundaries. Bounding boxes are then accumulated rather than suppressed in order to increase detection confidence. We show that different tasks can be learned simultaneously using a single shared network. This integrated framework is the winner of the localization task of the ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge 2013 (ILSVRC2013) and obtained very competitive results for the detection and classifications tasks. In post-competition work, we establish a new state of the art for the detection task. Finally, we release a feature extractor from our best model called OverFeat.

Variational autoencoders have been widely applied for natural language generation, however, there are two long-standing problems: information underrepresentation and posterior collapse. The former arises from the fact that only the last hidden state from the encoder is transformed to the latent space, which is insufficient to summarize data. The latter comes as a result of the imbalanced scale between the reconstruction loss and the KL divergence in the objective function. To tackle these issues, in this paper we propose the discrete variational attention model with categorical distribution over the attention mechanism owing to the discrete nature in languages. Our approach is combined with an auto-regressive prior to capture the sequential dependency from observations, which can enhance the latent space for language generation. Moreover, thanks to the property of discreteness, the training of our proposed approach does not suffer from posterior collapse. Furthermore, we carefully analyze the superiority of discrete latent space over the continuous space with the common Gaussian distribution. Extensive experiments on language generation demonstrate superior advantages of our proposed approach in comparison with the state-of-the-art counterparts.

Autonomous vehicles need to create movement strategies considering both space and time while navigating around moving obstacles. To achieve this, they require a precise control mechanism that accurately follows the predefined paths. This study introduces a control strategy that initially fine-tunes a desired pathway before monitoring it through a combined feedback and anticipatory controller. The forward component uses a model predictive methodology with an emphasis on enhancing driving capabilities within its calculation of costs. Subsequently, the stability of the error dynamics is assured via the careful construction of the feedback-anticipatory controller. We evaluated the effectiveness of our control system in a realistically simulated environment demanding evasive sideways movements. Our suggested controller demonstrated impressive results during simulations and possesses adaptable features for various dynamic car models. Additionally, we addressed potential uncertainty arising from changing numerical solvers for the associated optimization problem, ensuring consistent solutions throughout.

Trams ran in the city between 1904 and 1953 before being replaced by buses. In December, they returned to the streets with the opening of the Midland Metro service - the first part of a PS128m project. Once complete, trams from Wolverhampton will continue in to Birmingham, terminating at New Street station. Roger Lawrence, chairman of the West Midlands Integrated Transport Authority said: "This is an opportunity to expand. Not just into the city centre but out to the airport. "We will have a network to rival the best ones, like Manchester and Nottingham and even south London. Our network will equal those." At its peak, the original tram network ran 230 million passenger journeys every year from Yardley to Dudley, and from Erdington down to the Lickey Hills. Elsie Field, now 91, began working on the trams as a conductress when she was 18. Part of her job was using a pole to connect the tramcar to the overhead power lines. She said although she was short-sighted she was "too proud to wear her glasses, so the connection was sometimes a bit hit-and-miss." Tram enthusiast Geoffrey Claydon grew up in Birmingham and said he was disappointed when his regular commute was replaced by a bus service. "I said why have the trams gone and was told'Oh, they're old fashioned'. From that moment I thought I would be very supportive of trams, I would do my best to try and keep them where I can for the rest of my life." When working as a government lawyer, Mr Claydon helped design the Transport and Works Act of 1992, which paved the way for the Midland Metro Line. "I can now feel quite smug. It was an immense satisfaction that I've lived long enough to see trams back and the poor souls who got rid of them have been proved wrong." Inside Out West Midlands has a full report on the history and reintroduction of trams in Birmingham on BBC One, Monday at 19:30.

Determining the precise location of mitochondrial Eve is not entirely precise; instead, it provides a general estimate such as "Southeast Africa." Geneticists conducted research by analyzing placental mtDNA extracted from several individuals across diverse geographical areas. They discovered distinct regional variations in mtDNA sequences, with Asians being more closely aligned with one another, and similarly patterned distinctions among other ethnicities. Furthermore, Africans exhibited the greatest divergence from non-African populations, suggesting the existence of two primary branches—African and Non-African—within the global gene pool. Notably, the Non-African branch contained significant segments of African mtDNA, indicating the ancestral roots of our mitochondrial DNA lineage likely resided in Africa. Additionally, supporting the theory of an African origin for mitochondrial Eve is the observation that Southeast Africa showcases the highest level of intraspecific variation in mtDNA, which corresponds with its ancient status. Mitochondrial Eve, believed to have existed approximately 150,000 years ago, represents the first matrilineal progenitor whose descendants continue through today. It's important to mention that while she is considered the common ancestor, there could have been contemporaneous females sharing this role. Upon the extinction of a continuous maternal lineage, the designation passes to the most recently connected woman possessing an uninterrupted chain of direct maternal descent. Currently, due to the vast number of descendants stemming from Eve, there are no viable competitors for the title. An analogous concept applies to Y-Chromosome Adam, though his proposed timeframe varies between 150,000 and 50pta years ago based on differing scholarly perspectives.

The concept of a Decentralized Web (DW) is experiencing a resurgence, driven by the rise of various DW platforms such as Mastodon, PeerTube, and Hubzilla. These platforms serve as viable substitutes for mainstream social media sites like Twitter, YouTube, and Facebook by facilitating the functioning of web infrastructure and services through non-hierarchical models. Despite their diverse features, most contemporary DW platforms share two significant advancements: one, the utilization of open source software enables individuals to establish autonomous server instances accessible to members within a particular community; and two, they incorporate federation protocols allowing individual instances to interconnect in a decentralized manner, resulting in an expansive global network. This research offers an examination based on data analysis of these two technological breakthroughs, employing the widely-used DW microblogging platform Mastodon for illustrative purposes. Our investigation concentrates on pinpointing potential obstacles hindering further progress toward a fully decentralized web, while providing quantitative evidence of factors inclining towards reconcentration. Concluding remarks include insights into the conduct of platform managers and standard users, alongside suggestions for resolving identified concerns.

Region proposal mechanisms are essential for existing deep learning approaches to object detection in images. Although they can generally achieve a good detection performance under normal circumstances, their recall in a scene with extreme cases is unacceptably low. This is mainly because bounding box annotations contain much environment noise information, and non-maximum suppression (NMS) is required to select target boxes. Therefore, in this paper, we propose the first anchor-free and NMS-free object detection model, called weakly supervised multimodal annotation segmentation (WSMA-Seg), which utilizes segmentation models to achieve an accurate and robust object detection without NMS. In WSMA-Seg, multimodal annotations are proposed to achieve an instance-aware segmentation using weakly supervised bounding boxes; we also develop a run-data-based following algorithm to trace contours of objects. In addition, we propose a multi-scale pooling segmentation (MSP-Seg) as the underlying segmentation model of WSMA-Seg to achieve a more accurate segmentation and to enhance the detection accuracy of WSMA-Seg. Experimental results on multiple datasets show that the proposed WSMA-Seg approach outperforms the state-of-the-art detectors.

An important factor in the creation of inequality is variation in individuals' access to education. Education, especially in an area where there is a high demand for workers, creates high wages for those with this education, however, increases in education first increase and then decrease growth as well as income inequality. As a result, those who are unable to afford an education, or choose not to pursue optional education, generally receive much lower wages. The justification for this is that a lack of education leads directly to lower incomes, and thus lower aggregate savings and investment. Conversely, education raises incomes and promotes growth because it helps to unleash the productive potential of the poor.

Philae, the first spacecraft to land on a comet, was dropped on to the surface of Comet 67P by its mothership, Rosetta, last November. It worked for 60 hours before its solar-powered batteries ran out, but it was able to send back a wealth of scientific data and images of the comet. Philae woke up again briefly in June when its solar panels collected enough sunlight to start operating again. This time, though, Philae's batteries were depleted after just eight minutes. However, a new series of tests conducted at the European Space Operations Centre in Darmstadt, Germany, has provided evidence that the probe's primary battery may be able to power it for longer. The researchers are now confident that Philae will be able to communicate with Rosetta for a longer period of time later this year. During the tests, the lander's power, mass memory, communications, and other functions were simulated and tested for a total of 10 hours over two days. "Philae is doing very well: It has an operating temperature of -35C and has 24 Watts available," says Koen Geurts, who led the tests. The researchers were able to simulate Philae's battery state of charge and power consumption by using the actual data transmitted by the lander. Both the lander and the orbiter have been hibernating since 17 November 2014, but will wake up again in the coming months as the comet gets closer to the Sun. The team expects Philae's battery to be fully charged in March or April.

Jordan Peterson has announced the development of a new social media platform, Thinkspot. The platform aims to provide users the best features of other social media, but without the censorship. While many platforms already offer similar services, including Twitter, LinkedIn and Pinterest, Thinkspot plans to differentiate itself by offering better moderation tools than some competitors. Thinkspot won't launch until early 2018 though, so there aren't any details yet about what exactly the service will cost.

The ESA was signed into law by President Richard Nixon on December 28, 1973, it was designed to protect critically imperiled species from extinction as a "consequence of economic growth and development untempered by adequate concern and conservation." The U.S. Supreme Court found that "the plain intent of Congress in enacting" the ESA "was to halt and reverse the trend toward species extinction, whatever the cost." The Act is administered by two federal agencies, the United States Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS) and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA).

This paper proposes a robust adversarial reinforcement learning (RARL) -based multi-access point (AP) coordination method that is robust even against unexpected decentralized operations of uncoordinated APs. Multi-AP coordination is a new and important stage in the evolution of autonomous mobile robots, due to its realistic applications such as human mobility assistance with limited or no local control capabilities. In this work, we develop an RARL-based approach for achieving coordinated collaborative movements among multiple APs operating autonomously without any communication between them either via wireless links, optical fibers, or other wired connections; all while overcoming their nonlinear interdependence by using our proposed mechanism: Adversarial Multi Access Point Coordination (AMACC). AMACC enables cooperative APs to achieve high accuracy concurrent trajectories which are free from undesired errors at different time scales. Our experiments show that AMACC can significantly improve the ability of mobile robots for carrying out autonomously challenging tasks on uneven terrains including localization and orientation.

In this article, we propose a model-driven deep learning (DL) approach that combines DL with the expert knowledge to replace the existing orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM) receiver in wireless communications. First, we propose a novel DL architecture that consists of a convolutional neural network (CNN) and a long short-term memory (LSTM) network. In the CNN, the channel state information (CSI) matrix is the input and the frequency-domain symbols are the output. In the LSTM network, the time-domain received symbols are the input and the symbols are the output. The CNN and the LSTM networks are jointly trained in the proposed architecture. To design the CNN and the LSTM networks in a more efficient way, we design a mathematical model for the DL-based OFDM receiver. Using this model, we design the CNN and the LSTM networks as closed-form expressions. Compared with the state-of-the-art DL-based OFDM receiver, the proposed DL-based OFDM receiver can achieve a significant performance improvement. Moreover, in the proposed architecture, the knowledge from the designed mathematical model is also used to reduce the training cost of the proposed architecture. Cross-lingual document search is an information retrieval task in which the queries' language differs from the documents' language. In this paper, we study the instability of neural document search models and propose a novel end-to-end robust framework that achieves improved performance in cross-lingual search with different documents' languages. This framework includes a novel measure of the relevance, smooth cosine similarity , between queries and documents, and a novel loss function, Smooth Ordinal Search Loss , as the objective. We further provide theoretical guarantee on the generalization error bound for the proposed framework. We conduct experiments to compare our approach with other document search models, and observe significant gains under commonly used ranking metrics on the cross-lingual document retrieval task in a variety of languages.

The simplest way to gain information about brain anatomy is by visual inspection, but many more sophisticated techniques have been developed. Brain tissue in its natural state is too soft to work with, but it can be hardened by immersion in alcohol or other fixatives, and then sliced apart for examination of the interior. Visually, the interior of the brain consists of areas of so-called grey matter, with a dark color, separated by areas of white matter, with a lighter color. Further information can be gained by staining slices of brain tissue with a variety of chemicals that bring out areas where specific types of molecules are present in high concentrations. It is also possible to examine the microstructure of brain tissue using a microscope, and to trace the pattern of connections from one brain area to another.

A molecule moving through a realistic transmission medium may undergo random interactions with other particles and its surroundings' boundaries. While the statistical patterns of certain isolated events like dispersed unrestricted molecular diffusion are well comprehended, analyzing several interconnected reactions in their entirety often necessitates computational simulations due to complexity. In this study, we evaluate the statistical outcomes of various molecular reaction-diffusion simulation frameworks used within molecular communication systems, examining them from two perspectives - microscopic and mesoscopic approaches. Microscopic techniques monitor each molecule's position and condition, while mesoscopic ones divide the environment into hypothetical compartments containing molecules. We describe and compare these models before proposing an integrated approach combining both methodologies. Moreover, our simulation findings investigate the precision of using Poisson and Gaussian distributions to approximate the inherent Binomial statistics.

She saw Beth lunging at her, the blade inches away from shattering her medallion, the source of her immortality, and immediately awoke. Her spell would not show her what would happen next and nothing she tried would change that fact. The gods have left her with the curse of uncertainty, a fate crueler than simple death. Every night for the past hundred years she had this dream. At first she thought she would try to escape it, to defy the gods and make her fate her own. She ran and hid vowing to never return to her beloved abode, a place she built with her own hands without the use of magic. She never lasted long and, when she inevitably returned, it absolutely broke her heart to find it in disrepair. She found hunter's traps densely placed, boards nailed to trees to aid in climbing, her own home ransacked or burnt to the ground but, worst of all, she found her creatures to be deathly afraid. She protected her lands, destroying traps and maiming those that placed them, causing local villages to become incredibly hostile towards her. They set fire to the swamp, burning and killing everything that lived within. The rage this act of war incited within Enna's heart was unparalleled in history or fiction. She burnt everything within miles of her home in one giant ball of hellfire, taking the lives of thousands of people in various nearby villages. When the last of the ash settled, Enna was left alone, the Queen of Death, reigning over mountains of dead. It was then that she renounced herself to whatever fate the gods had planned. She spent the remainder of her time attempting to atone for her violent outburst, knowing that there would never be forgiveness. She finally managed to revive the swamp she had so lovingly built all those years ago. It was finally her time to receive divine punishment. She would meet Beth traveling along a trail she had built to allow travelers to cross the bog, unimpeded by the harsh terrain. It would be the first time she met a person in decades. How fitting for it also to be the last. Beth wore a heavy scarf over her face that protected her from the insects as she rode through. "Hello, my dear." Her voice startled Beth's horse, causing it to neigh, dropping the girl to the ground with a harsh thud. Enna rushed over to help her to her feet and was met with the tip of a blade coming straight at her chest, just as she had dreamed. She braced herself for the pain that would inevitably follow. "Why...why can't I do it." The voice was a man's and as Enna opened her eyes, she saw him stepping back, the sword held weakly in his hand before finally falling to the ground. "I, I spent years waiting for this moment, for now, the time when I would finally get my revenge." He paused. "Mother. Father. I'm no murderer." He sunk to the ground. Enna was shocked. She had expected a woman, one she had named Beth, but was met with a skinny man with long hair, dressed in women's riding clothes, ready but unable to kill her. She began to cry, out of relief but also of immense sadness. The gods had granted her pardon for her misdeed. She was saved and her savior stood right in front of her. "The dreams were so vivid. I knew I would meet you here, I knew what you would look like. All I had to...All I had to do was drive my blade through your medallion." He spoke at the ground and then turned his face to look at her. "I saw you once before. I followed you to your home. I. I told them you were there and I took this to prove it." He reached into his shirt and pulled out a golden trinket in the shape of a pentagram with symbols lining each side. "I was responsible for the fire. I tried to get rid of this medallion but no matter what I do, it always finds me. I tried to end my life but I couldn't. What did you do to me?" She stared at him as he sat there waiting for her to respond. "Please just kill me. I, I can't live like this." The tears welled up in her eyes. She walked towards him and took him into her arms. She had an eternity to explain that his request would be impossible. For now she just wanted to hold him in her arms.

Interestingly, the mild winter experienced thus far this year has resulted in significant cost savings for U.S. local authorities by reducing expenses associated with snow clearance. This fortunate occurrence coincides beneficially with the economic downturn. The phenomenon can be attributed to La Niña, which influences the jet stream to shift northward, confining colder temperatures primarily to regions such as Alaska and Canada. These events occur periodically over several years and impact usual climatic trends.

This year, the jet stream has deviated significantly towards the northern hemispta, permitting more tropical air currents to reach higher latitudes because of the recurring La Niña climate cycle. In addition, La Niña has presented unusual warmth while introducing parched air from the Pacific Ocean into the United States. An accelerated Arctic airflow also contributes to the uncharacteristically warm conditions by limiting the typical flow of frigid winds toward the equator. When considering each factor independently, they might suggest a somewhat milder winter; however, their concurrent presence at elevated intensities has led to one of the most extraordinary winter seasons recorded.

Aside from North America experiencing fewer snowfalls than anticipated, central European countries have similarly encountered scarce precipitation during this winter period.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average is a benchmark stock market index formulated by Charles Dow, who was a journalist at the Wall Street Journal and a founder of Dow Jones Company. Originally computed on May 26, 1896, this index gets its "industrial" designation mainly from history since most of the current 30 elements aren't associated with conventional manufacturing industries anymore. As a price-weighted index, the Dow utilizes a unique methodology whereby a specialized factor, known as the divisor, is employed to ensure consistency amidst stock splits and other modifications; presently set at 0.15571590501117. Consequently, each $1 fluctuation in any specific company's share costs translates into a roughly 6.42-point shift in the index's overall score. In contrast, the NASDAQ Composite Index encompasses more than 3,000 corporations traded on the NASDAptaq exchange, focusing predominantly on technological and expanding enterprises worldwide. Lastly, there is the S&P 500 index, also referred to as the Standard & Poor's 500. This widely recognized metric evaluates the collective market values of 500 significant publicly traded firms listed on either the New York Stock Exchange or the NASDAQ platform. Different from indexes like the DJIA and the NASDAQ Composite, the S&P 500 uses distinct criteria for selecting its constituents and determining their respective weights through SP Dow Jones Indices.

Wool consists merely of non-living fibers rather than actual tissue. To avoid decomposition, leather undergoes a preservation process through drying and curing methods. Decay occurs because microorganisms such as bacteria and fungi consume organic matter. The act of tanning transforms the material into something unpalatable to these decomposers, thereby inhibiting its breakdown and subsequent decay. However, maintaining moisture levels via regular oiling is necessary, otherwise, over time, the material may become brittle and disintegrate. In my previous role, I encountered centuries-old leather that suffered this fate when neglected. It's worth mentioning that certain treatment techniques, including air-drying or tanning, can significantly diminish the likelihood of rot occurring. Not every type of deceased biological substance decays at the same rate; various conservation strategies can effectively minimize the chances of degradation almost entirely.

Russia's ambassador to Poland, Sergey Andreyev, has issued a statement clarifying his recent comments that appeared to suggest Poland was partially responsible for the start of World War Two. In an interview with the Polish news outlet TVP, Andreyev was asked about the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact, a non-aggression agreement between Nazi Germany and the Soviet Union signed in August 1939. Andreyev responded by saying that Poland had also played a role in the events leading up to the pact and the outbreak of World War Two. Following the interview, the Polish government summoned Andreyev to explain his comments, which were widely criticized as an attempt to revise history and shift blame from Nazi Germany's aggression. In his statement, Andreyev clarified that he did not intend to blame Poland for the war and that his remarks were misinterpreted. He emphasized the importance of a common understanding of history and expressed regret for any offense caused by his comments. The Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact is a contentious issue in Polish-Russian relations, with Poland viewing it as the precursor to the Soviet invasion of Poland in September 1939. The Soviet Union's occupation of eastern Poland resulted in the deaths of thousands of Polish citizens, and the memory of the invasion remains a source of tension between the two countries. Andreyev's clarification comes amid ongoing efforts to improve relations between Russia and Poland, with both sides expressing a desire to build a more constructive dialogue. While the ambassador's initial comments were controversial, his willingness to clarify and clarify his position will hopefully help to facilitate a more productive conversation about this difficult period in history.

Visual localization is the problem of estimating a camera within a scene and a key technology for autonomous robots. State-of-the-art approaches for accurate visual localization use scene-specific representations, resulting in poor generalization across unseen scenes. In this work, we introduce SLAM-3D, a method that learns to predict an image's 3D scene context in a self-supervised fashion. Our approach relies on supervision in a novel form: a geometric constraint derived from the camera motion between two images. We exploit this constraint to train a deep neural network that predicts a novel viewpoint of the scene, and can generalize to novel scenes. Our method outperforms the previous state-of-the-art methods by more than 5x on the popular KITTI benchmark, and generalizes to unseen scenes. We validate the generalization capability by evaluating our method on the challenging Make3D dataset. The source code is available at this https URL.

The visualization of Klein bottles results solely in their shadows since they are four-dimensional entities. The perceived gap at the base arises from viewing such a 4D figure within three-dimensional space. Similarly, a Möbius strip represents a two-dimensional loop possessing only one continuous surface due to its curvature in the third dimension; conversely, a Klein bottle embodies a three-dimensional region with a single uninterrupted surface due to its curvature in the fourth dimension.

In contrast, a standard glass does not qualify as a Klein bottle as it comprises multiple sides and edges. Observing a glass as a hollow structure rather than a solid mass helps illustrate this difference. Imagining the glass merely as a flat base with vertical sides reveals that its surface possesses both interior and exterior aspects, alongside an edge around its circumference. Eliminating the edge requires the surface to extend beyond the outer boundaries while simultaneously conforming to the inner contours of the glass, resulting in distinct upper and lower sections – the former facing outward into the environment and the latter lying adjacent to the inner glass surface. However, even under these conditions, the glass lacks the defining characteristic of a Klein bottle: a seamless connection between the upper and lower portions of its surface allowing traversal across its entirety without breaching it.

Policy gradient algorithms in reinforcement learning optimize the policy directly and rely on efficiently sampling an environment. However, while most sampling procedures are based solely on sampling the agent's policy, other measures directly accessible through these algorithms could be used to improve sampling before each policy update. Following this line of thoughts, we propose the use of SAUNA, a method where transitions are rejected from the gradient updates if they do not meet a particular criterion, and kept otherwise. This criterion, the fraction of variance explained V e x , is a measure of the discrepancy between a model and actual samples. In this work, V e x is used to evaluate the impact each transition will have on learning: this criterion refines sampling and improves the policy gradient algorithm. In this paper: (a) We introduce and explore V e x , the criterion used for denoising policy gradient updates. (b) We conduct experiments across a variety of benchmark environments, including standard continuous control problems. Our results show better performance with SAUNA. (c) We investigate why V e x provides a reliable assessment for the selection of samples that will positively impact learning. (d) We show how this criterion can work as a dynamic tool to adjust the ratio between exploration and exploitation.

Clinical Health Data Dictionary is collected by individuals seeking outpatient care at more than 1 000 hospitals across Canada using a self-administered survey device [1]. ImageNet Classification Benchmark is an open access dataset containing over 25 million images of medical specimens annotated with images used for medical classification purposes, e.g., cell morphology, pathophysiology, structure and function, anatomy, etc. These images are collectively known as Medical Image Dataset (MID) [2], which can be searched through several public sources like Google Scholar, PubMed Central, and the Internet Archive. The other two approaches considered in this paper - Structured Inside Knowledge and Medical Engineering Annotation Training (MEAT) - have yet to achieve high performance in their own right. The security of cryptographic communication protocols that use X.509 certificates depends on the correctness of those certificates. This paper proposes a system that helps to ensure the correct operation of the security certificates in security-critical routes, and enables users to easily redeem these keys when they fail to authenticate themselves. This paper describes the problem of verifying whether a client is legitimate or not by comparing the validity of two certificates with each other's integrity. The aim of this paper was to test the validity of certificates with respect to both valid certificate metrics, to determine if the certificate is authentic or false, and to demonstrate whether the certificate matches the characteristics of the client's identity (in particular, it matches its attitude toward privacy). Because authentication can be difficult for new users, the researchers made sure to provide all needed verification information so that the user could make an informed decision about which certificate he would support. Summary of the study: To test the validity of a cryptographic signature, we tested the reputation of a certificate published on X.509 certification websites. We found that the authentic certificate had been submitted by 80 of the managed users who registered a related service within the last three months, whereas the fake certificate was rejected only from 23 of registered users who used an attempt to obtain a signed certificate from the provider. As an enthusiast of rock climbing, it's essential to understand the distinEE differences between various styles of ascending: Sport Climbing vs. Traditional Climbing. Sport climbing involves pre-installed anchors embedded within the stone, typically installed beforehand by another climber descending using a safety line while hanging onto the wall. Their aim is to establish a lasting, enjoyable pathway, removing any unstable fragments along the way. For sport climbers, simply securing themselves via 'quickdraws', pairs of metal loops connected by a cord, suffices. Originating in the 1980s, these routes tend to span less than the full height of a rock face, focusing more on the pleasure of the ascent rather than conquering the entire peak. On the other hand, traditional climbing—often abbreviated to 'trad' climbing—is likely closer to your mental image. Here, climbers carry removable equipment designed to fit snugly into crevices and indentations within the rock surface. Tracing its roots over a hundred years back, trad climbing prioritizes achieving the summit, posing additional challenges due to the necessity of locating suitable spots for the gear placements. Typically, trad climbers use detachable devices like cams and nuts; historically, they relied on expandable pins driven into fissures. Bolts may occasionally supplement certain sections lacking natural anchor points. Regardless of method, the initial climber ('leader') secures the rope to either fixed bolts or strategically positioned protective gear, allowing subsequent climbers to follow safely."

Tensor completion is a challenging problem with various applications. Many related models based on the low-rank prior of the tensor have been proposed. However, the low-rank prior may not be able to capture the correlation information of tensors sufficiently well. To tackle this problem, we propose a new tensor completion model with a generalized Laplacian prior. The tensor completion task can be represented as the minimization of the sum of squared residuals, which can be solved by the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). The convergence of ADMM for solving our proposed model is analyzed. The numerical results show that our proposed model outperforms several other state-of-the-art models in terms of completion rate, and the computational complexity is greatly reduced. Before the Marian reforms, the Roman military forces were exclusively made up of citizens people of property (3500 sesterces, say about 1750 loaves of bread) and capable of supplying their own equipment. The soldiers were paid a daily stipend (soldier's pay) of 3.5 sesterces and could supplement this by plunder. This did not provide enough to live on, so soldiers supplemented their incomes by billeting themselves out to farmers at the end of the campaigning season. As most soldiers were from the peasant class, they brought their families with them. Women and children also acted as camp followers providing domestic services; cooking, washing clothes and nursing the sick. In return for these services the soldiers allowed the women to share their rations and tents. There was no hard and fast rule about the soldiers being from a single social class, but because of their shared experience of poverty and military service, soldiers usually formed close bonds with each other and identified strongly with their "cohort" or "century." The Marian reforms changed all this. Now the army was mainly made up of professional soldiers who were given land at the end of their tour of duty. The Romans hoped that having a personal stake in the Roman Empire would make the soldiers more loyal to Rome and less likely to defect. The result was very different. Soldiers now had little in common with citizens and felt no loyalty to Rome. In battle, Roman soldiers were armed with a sword (gladius), a spear (pilum), a wooden shield and wore metal armor. The pilum was a throwing spear with a long iron shank and a wooden shaft. The shank was bent toward the enemy just before throwing to ensure that it penetrated the shield. Once inside the shield the weight of the shank caused the point to bend and break off making the weapon useless. Roman infantry used a "tortoise" formation in which the men in front raised their shields above their heads, forming an effective roof against arrows and sling bullets. The men behind delivered a hail of javelins over the top of the shield wall. To protect the flanks, Roman commanders placed the cavalry on the wings. The cavalry charged enemy formations after the javelins had thrown the opposing forces into confusion. As they continued to advance, the missiles were discharged with rather less vigor, and the Roman archers and slingers, in their turn, became formidable. We develop a probabilistic framework for deep learning based on the Deep Rendering Mixture Model (DRMM), a new generative probabilistic model that explicitly capture variations in data due to latent task nuisance variables. We demonstrate that max-sum inference in the DRMM yields an algorithm that exactly reproduces the operations in deep convolutional neural networks (DCNs), providing a first principles derivation. Our framework provides new insights into the successes and shortcomings of DCNs as well as a principled route to their improvement. DRMM training via the Expectation-Maximization (EM) algorithm is a powerful alternative to DCN back-propagation, and initial training results are promising. Classification based on the DRMM and other variants outperforms DCNs in supervised digit classification, training 2-3 x faster while achieving similar accuracy. Moreover, the DRMM is applicable to semi-supervised and unsupervised learning tasks, achieving results that are state-of-the-art in several categories on the MNIST benchmark and comparable to state of the art on the CIFAR10 benchmark.

The Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union grants certain protections to individuals referred to as "workers," who often possess limited negotiating power within the marketplace. Among these safeguards is the preservation of "the freedom of establishment" outlined in Article EE and the "right to offer services" delineated in Article FF. During the case of Gebhard v Consiglio dell'Ordine degli Avvocati e Procuratori di Milano, the Court of Justice determined that establishing oneself implies active participation in economic affairs consistently over time. On the other hand, offering services suggests undertaking activities temporarily. Consequently, a German attorney facing repercussions from the Italian Bar Association for failing to register could assert his entitlement based on the establishment clause instead of the service provision one. Nevertheless, stipulations requiring registration prior to practicing might be deemed acceptable provided they adhere to specific criteria, including nondiscrimination, justification by essential public interests, and proportional application. Under EU law, everyone involved in commercial endeavors—especially independent workers and various business structures like corporations or partnerships—has the right to initiate ventures free from unwarranted constraints. Furthermore, it has been established through legal precedent that both government authorities and private parties may impede upon the freedom of establishment; thus, Article EE possesses both vertical and horizontal effects. For instance, in the case of Reyners v Belgium, the Court of Justice ruled against Belgium denying a foreign lawyer access to their bar solely due to his nationality. Although Article EE acknowledges exemptions regarding freedom of establishment during instances where governments act in an official capacity, it does not apply to roles outside those functions, such as an attorney’s duties. Comparatively, in the matter of Commission v Italy, the Court found no infringement present in Italian regulations mandating lawyers to adhere to predetermined fees absent a mutual agreement with clients. Ultimately, the Grand Chamber upheld this ruling.

Spanning from 100 to 65 million years ago, the Late Cretaceous period experienced a gradual cooling pattern that persisted into the Cenozoic era. This led to the restriction of tropical climates to only the equatorial regions, while areas further away saw significant variations in seasonal weather conditions. Despite these changes, dinosaurs continued to flourish with the emergence of various species like Tyrannosaurus, Ankylosaurus, Triceratops, and Hadrosaurs, who became key players in the ecosystem. Marine life also adapted during this time; Mosasaurs took over the ocean habitats once occupied by Ichthyosaurs, while massive Plesiosaurs, including Elasmosaurus, developed. Additionally, the initial evolutionary appearance of flowering plants occurred. However, towards the conclusion of the Cretaceous, extensive volcanic activity, exemplified by the Deccan traps, along with a catastrophic meteor impact forming the Chicxulub Crater (the K-T Extinction), resulted in the demise of approximately 75% of Earth's biodiversity, marking the fifth major mass extinction event. Among the casualties were all non-avian dinosaurs and every creature weighing more than ten kilograms, effectively ending the reign of the dinosaurs.

Serological methods are highly sensitive, specific and often extremely rapid tests used to identify microorganisms. These tests are based upon the ability of an antibody to bind specifically to an antigen. The antigen, usually a protein or carbohydrate made by an infectious agent, is bound by the antibody. This binding then sets off a chain of events that can be visibly obvious in various ways, dependent upon the test. For example, "Strep throat" is often diagnosed within minutes, and is based on the appearance of antigens made by the causative agent, S. pyogenes, that is retrieved from a patients throat with a cotton swab. Serological tests, if available, are usually the preferred route of identification, however the tests are costly to develop and the reagents used in the test often require refrigeration. Some serological methods are extremely costly, although when commonly used, such as with the "strep test," they can be inexpensive.

As an example, can the ability to advance forwards, once taught to a two-legged entity, be applied to a single-leg hopping creature to enhance efficiency during subsequent training? By approaching this issue through subspace learning, our objective is to uncover underlying components that represent a universally applicable control strategy among MDAs. Our innovative proposal introduces a new paired variational encoder-decoder framework named PVED, which separates the control aspects into mutually exclusive and specific elements tied to each MDA. These universal elements are subsequently employed for proficiency transference via reinforcement learning. From a theoretical standpoint, we offer a proposition outlining the dependency of PVED's efficacy on both communal factors and MDA structures. Practically, PVED has undergone thorough testing within four MuJoCo simulation settings. Results showcase superiority over contemporary cutting-edge strategies while also providing insightful factor analyses, demonstrating potential directions for further advancements.

My boss let me go early. He gripped my shoulder firmly and wished me a safe birthday, reminding me to arrive at work on time the day immediately following. Several of my coworkers, quiet and solemn, shook my hand as I made my way out. I gave everyone the biggest smiles of confidence I could manage. Tomorrow was really just another day, I reminded myself. I drove home, more absent minded than usual. I cleaned out the kitchen drawers, collecting every knife, fork, and sharp object within site. I stored these objects in a metal box in the garage under lock and key. I studied each room in my house, searching for and rounding up potential hazards. I locked each room individually save for the bedroom, which was where I spent every birthday. As they did every year, a team of electricians, plumbers, contractors, and home inspectors had come by recently to take a look at the wiring, check for potential gas and water leaks, ensure that all appliances were in prime working condition, and otherwise reaffirm that the home was safe and habitable. The police had already been informed that this home would be under death watch starting several hours from now. Video surveillance connectivity was previously confirmed and recording would be commencing shortly. After checking off a very long list of preparations, I let out a soft sigh and slid down into the cushions of the living room couch, my knees shaking slightly. The front door creaked open then to reveal Sarah, home from work, presenting me with troubled eyes and take out for two. She locked the door gently behind her and set the food on the coffee table, kissing the top of my head before taking a seat next to me. We embraced for a few long minutes, silent and unmoving. Finally, Sarah spoke. "I have some amazing plans for your after-birthday. I think you'll be really excited." I smiled softly and pulled her close to me again, giving her a tight squeeze. I imagined holding her forever and never letting go. I did not want to think about the possibility of not being able to hold her again. "I love you," I whispered. She returned the squeeze. "I love you, too," she said after a pause. When she let go, she pointed to the food in front of me. "Now eat," she commanded, trying unsuccessfully to wipe away tears before I could glimpse them. "I got you your favorite. I want you to eat every last bite since you can't eat tomorrow." She was right. I could choke tomorrow. I could die tomorrow. I stared at the take out box on the coffee table in front of me and grappled with the idea that the contents inside could become my last meal. For just that moment, I permitted myself to indulge in speculatory and gruesome scenes of death, wondering if I might eventually end up in one of them. "Tomorrow is really just another day," I reminded Sarah as I stood up to grab two forks from the garage.

As well as creating rights for "workers" who generally lack bargaining power in the market, the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union also protects the "freedom of establishment" in article 49, and "freedom to provide services" in article 56. In Gebhard v Consiglio dell'Ordine degli Avvocati e Procuratori di Milano the Court of Justice held that to be "established" means to participate in economic life "on a stable and continuous basis," while providing "services" meant pursuing activity more "on a temporary basis." This meant that a lawyer from Stuttgart, who had set up chambers in Milan and was censured by the Milan Bar Council for not having registered, was entitled to bring a claim under for establishment freedom, rather than service freedom. However, the requirements to be registered in Milan before being able to practice would be allowed if they were non-discriminatory, "justified by imperative requirements in the general interest" and proportionately applied. All people or entities that engage in economic activity, particularly the self-employed, or "undertakings" such as companies or firms, have a right to set up an enterprise without unjustified restrictions. The Court of Justice has held that both a member state government and a private party can hinder freedom of establishment, so article 49 has both "vertical" and "horizontal" direct effect. In Reyners v Belgium the Court of Justice held that a refusal to admit a lawyer to the Belgian bar because he lacked Belgian nationality was unjustified. TFEU article 49 says states are exempt from infringing others' freedom of establishment when they exercise "official authority," but this did an advocate's work (as opposed to a court's) was not official. By contrast in Commission v Italy the Court of Justice held that a requirement for lawyers in Italy to comply with maximum tariffs unless there was an agreement with a client was not a restriction. The Grand Chamber of the Court of Justice held the Commission had not proven that this had any object or effect of limiting practitioners from entering the market. Therefore, there was no prima facie infringement freedom of establishment that needed to be justified.

Aspect based sentiment analysis aims to identify the sentimental tendency towards a given aspect in text. Fine-tuning of pretrained BERT performs excellent on this task and achieves state-of-the-art performances. Existing works, including some from us, have proposed methods for fine-tuning pre-trained models using unsupervised techniques which do not require dataset access or human annotators. In this paper we show that extending previous work by introducing an additional classifier enables significant improvements on sentiment classification tasks without modifying any model parameters. We also investigate how finetuning with supervised training data can further improve accuracy while not significantly increasing runtime. 1) Introduction Sentiment Analysis as a topic has been around since at least 1950s where it was used mainly for statistical purposes cite3. However, recent years saw increased interest due to applications in various fields like social media analytics (e.g., online shopping reviews), information retrieval systems (e.g., question answering), search engines etc. The majority of existing approaches are designed primarily to classify sentiments expressed within sentences into predefined categories such as positive. While these approaches seem sufficient for simple use cases e.g., automated customer service chatbots they fail when confronted with more challenging scenarios. For example, if your goal is to predict whether someone will give positive feedback about hisher experience during their next holiday then you may need to know what kind of activities heshe does before traveling. To tackle such problems researchers are now starting to look beyond pure semantics towards aspects that transcend simple semantic compositionality. Specifically, a large number of studies focus on identifying differentiative aspects rather than just binary ones cite0 cite15, most popular being quality vs price tradeoff. More recently attention has turned toward achieving a richer understanding of user intentions rather than simply providing yes no answers cite17 cite4. Lastly there is also research focused on improving performance of existing algorithms especially where labeled datasets are scarce cite18 cite19. While many existing works perform well when trained end-to-end (e.g., cite5) others rely heavily on external resources like handcrafted features, spam filters, corpora etc.. These include features learned via word level metrics like tf-idf, support vector machines etc. Others take advantage of large scale datasets available across multiple domains but lack strong supervision or fine-grained annotations leading to poor generalization results when applied outside those domains cite21 cite12 cite8. As an alternative to learning features directly from raw corpus one could instead learn them procedurally through generative adversarial networks while requiring less manual supervision cite14. Besides adding training steps to existing models another problem faced by traditional machine learning approaches to sentiment analysis is the challenge of handling long tail sentiments in high dimensional space. There exist methods developed specifically for dealing with short tails in specific domain contexts e.g., linguistic patterns cite9 and lexical embedding techniques cite10. Such solutions ignore the fact that in order to get meaningful insights from long tail expressions one needs be able to distinguish between them even though some measure of similarity should hold regardless of their functional equivalence. On top of that, most of the time only domain experts understand why certain expressions belong to same category sometimes making categorizing sentiment impossible even if labelled feature sets might provide good enough predictions cite23. Finally, besides humans these are some other examples of external sources whose inputs highly impact final output: spam filters, content moderation policies cite6, social network users themselves who may express mixed emotions in response to news events cite16. The aim of our approach is to combine all the above mentioned characteristics under deep convolutional neural networks capable of generating its own representations thereby avoiding external dependencies. Our method incorporates both supervised and unsupervised fine-tunings along with a novel repair strategy aimed at removing internal noise. This work falls under supervised fine tuning which has become very popular over the past few years cite22 cite11 cite13. Here, we propose two methods for fine-tuning pretrained BERT trained classifiers that allow significant improvement in several sentiment prediction settings without changing model parameters. Additionally, we demonstrate how improving final sentiment score doesn't necessarily mean sacrificing speed. All experiments carried out on Kaldi inspired corpora demonstrate promising results compared to state-of-the-art deep convolutional neural networks.

Your body consists of numerous minuscule molecular devices and components, similar to Lego pieces, which perform various functions such as maintainsintegrity, constructing microstructures, transforming molecules, synthesizing larger molecules from smaller ones, and executing countless other tasks. Imagine being unable to see, wherein someone places an item in your hand; through touch, you discern its identity based on characteristics like weight, form, and texture, and relay this information via nerve signals to your brain. Similarly, biosensors operate like our hands, yet their design primarily focuses on identifying one distinct entity among several others. Upon detection of their target molecule, they emit a unique signal indicating successful identification. Harnessing the precise sensory capabilities of these naturally occurring nanoscale detectors allows us to receive alerts upon locating our desired substances. These alerts may manifest as mechanical forces, photons, electrons, changes in mass due to attachment, or any number of unusual indicators.

Not all of us got beautiful handwriting, but all of us improved. I think it started in the second grade and continued for a couple of years.','Some people put more effort into it than others.','I suppose I cannot answer the question, but your question sent me on a nostalgic trip. TDLR at the bottom for those who do not care. I just had fun recollecting and making this post. I should start of by saying, handwriting was given a lot of importance when I grew up. Everybody was taught cursive. Lefties were frowned upon. Those who couldnt write cursive were just uncouth filth. I know this because I was one of those elitist, "right-wing," cursive-enabled pricks. I had an interest in different handwriting styles growing up. Just liked to incorporate stuff that a mate did into my own, which ended up making my own handwriting into a Frankenstein of sorts, but I was proud of it. Stuff like a fancy flare on the g's, y's, putting a circle instead of a dot on the i's etc. Pens were a huge business back then. Ball point pens were strictly prohibited as they were not easy to control and usually led to shitty handwriting. Pencils until year 3 and only fountain pens from then onwards to year 12. Go to equipment of choice was the [Hero fountain pen] (URL5). That pen was the toyota of all pens. Absolute workhorse, no fancy shit, [use throw simple ink cartridges] (URL2). Douchey rich kids would bring their Parker pens and Shaeffers with metallic bodies and [refillable ink cartridges] (URL0) and [sexy nibs] (URL1). We would huddle around these things like they were lambos and ferraris in the parking lot. As I got older, I loved these [Uni-ball rollerball pens] (URL3) - all the goodness of a ballpoint pen (no leakage, cheap to replace, more durable) with the control of a fountain pen. School notebooks were ruled pages, single lines going across the page with 1 to 1.5cm (less than an inch) spacing between the lines. I liked to write in the gap between the lines, without touching them. Some wrote on the lines, some inbetween, some couldnt keep it parallel to the lines. Now you might ask, why are the pens and notebooks so important. Well, our notebooks went to the teachers - A LOT. we would take notes, do homework, classwork etc all in the same book and at the end of the period the teacher would take the books for correctionreview. Teachers worked hard. You could make or break a teacher's day with just the handwriting. I should let you know that all notebooks look pretty much the same. They were all a standard 200 or 250 page books. All were wrapped in the same brown colour wrapping paper. All would be labelled in the top right corner with the name of the student, subject and the class they were in. Imagine every student in the class has a book like [this] (URL4) except all the books are same shape and size. Uniformity throughout. Students over the course of the year became so pro at handling these books, we would know which book belonged to which subject just by looking at the rips and tears on the side. And even which book belonged to which student just with subtle differences in the shades of brown wrapping paper. Back to the story, a student would collect all the books and assemble a single neat pile onto the teacher's desk. The teacher would then take the one on top and randomly flip open to a page. Moment of truth. Teachers always had a shitty scowl on their face while correcting our work. If it was neat and pretty the teacher would just continue correcting with the scowl, although sometimes their face would light up and they would close the book again to read who it belonged to. "This period was good, I am safe for now" would go through the mind of that student who recognizes his book at the top of the pile. Shitty handwriting with crossed out words, ink blots and general tardiness earned epic rage sometimes. Books being flung onto the ground, pages ripped out and thrown into waste bins and general swearing. Kid at the back would recognise his brown shade of wrapping paper from 20 meters away and come pick up his book only to cop more abuse or even get called out for an ass whooping (corporal punishment was allowed) in worst case scenarios. The absolute worst case was when the teacher asked the student to start all over again in a new book, this would be half way down through the year and the kid would have to start fresh from re-write everything from day 1 of year. Some kids just let the book sit and wouldnt pick it. Some kids would pick up that book and return it to the owner - this went either way as helper kid could either become GGG or scumbag steve. So handwriting mattered. Just like how pretty people have it easy in life, students with a pretty handwriting had it easy. More marks (we didnt have grades), more leniency, perks out the wazoo like getting out of class to run errands, becoming a teacher's pet, earning mad props by helping to write love letters to girls (probably leave this for episode 2) Sorry for the long post. killed 3hrs at work typing this. wish I wrote it. TDLR - everyone can have pretty handwriting - just Practice practice practice. I seen all sorts of weird grips so its not that. PS - I'm sure there will be some Indian kids who relate to this story and be thinking - "this guy went to an indian school." CBSE upto 10th std. (in the middle east though) edit: typos

It seems the big problem is failing to make the distinction between intelligence and dexterous utilization of it. There are water bound creatures with who it is not immediately clear whether they are intelligent or not. And, there are people who may have high intellect but cannot use it effectively. The distinction between intelligence and dexterous utilization of it is important because intelligence alone does not guarantee success in any situation. Having the knowledge and understanding of a subject does not necessarily mean that one will be able to utilize that knowledge effectively in all situations. In order for someone to succeed, they must also possess the skills and capabilities to apply their knowledge to particular tasks and problems. For example, a person may understand complex theories related to mathematics, but they may still struggle with basic arithmetic calculations if they lack dexterity. Similarly, a person who has a great deal of physical strength may not be able to use it effectively if they lack the necessary coordination and agility. Therefore, intelligence and dexterous utilization must both be present in order for someone to achieve success.

The most basic type of "tracking pixel," often referred to as a "Web bug," functions by embedding a tiny image within an advertisement or promotional content. For instance, if there is unsolicited medication advertising (like Viagra) or genuine marketing material being distributed, the sender might be keen on tracking who viewed the ad, when they did so, and from what location. To achieve this, a unique URL pointing to a minuscule image—a single pixel—that remains inconspicuous to the viewer is incorporated into the ad. When accessed, only the initial part of the URL ('URL0') before the '?' symbol is processed by the server, which then delivers the image. By examining the server logs, anyone could identify the recipient who requested the image and associate it with the specific marketing campaign. As a result, reputable email clients now typically refrain from automatically downloading such images, requiring user consent instead. Additionally, websites employ similar tactics using web bugs provided by third parties (such as 'URL1'), eliminating the need for these entities to analyze the primary website's server records. It should be noted that modern tracking pixels have evolved to become far more advanced and covert, making them difficult to detect, hinder, or trace back to their creators. Tracking pixels aren't limited to images either, encompassing JavaScript and Flash technologies as well.

Neural network has attracted great attention for a long time and many researchers are devoted to improve the effectiveness of neural network training algorithms. Though stochastic gradient descent (SGD) and other explicit gradient-based methods are widely adopted, there are still many challenges such as gradient vanishing and small step sizes, which leads to slow convergence and instability of SGD algorithms. Motivated by error back propagation (BP) and proximal methods, we propose a semi-implicit back propagation method for neural network training. Similar to BP, the difference on the neurons are propagated in a backward fashion and the parameters are updated with proximal mapping. The implicit update for both hidden neurons and parameters allows to choose large step size in the training algorithm. Finally, we also show that any fixed point of convergent sequences produced by this algorithm is a stationary point of the objective loss function. The experiments on both MNIST and CIFAR-10 demonstrate that the proposed semi-implicit BP algorithm leads to better performance in terms of both loss decreasing and trainingvalidation accuracy, compared to SGD and a similar algorithm ProxBP.

David Brown became ill in Maghaberry Prison in December 2012 and died later in hospital from a brain haemorrhage. The Prisoner Ombudsman said staff left him unattended for five minutes in an unresponsive state and did not raise the alarm immediately. The watchdog has concluded the response of the Prison Service was "inadequate." The report by Prisoner Ombudsman Tom McGonigle also found that a nurse treating the inmate was not made aware that it was an emergency situation and other prisoners were not locked in their cells during the incident. However, Mr McGonigle, said: "While some things could have been done better, a key finding of this independent investigation is that there was no possibility to achieve an alternative outcome for Mr Brown." The Prisoner Ombudsman's office is required to investigate all deaths in custody in Northern Ireland, including deaths due to natural causes. The report into David Brown's death said painkilling drugs were found in the 46-year-old's system during toxicology tests, but added that the drugs had been prescribed to him. It said the medication was found at "concentrations that lay within their respective therapeutic ranges." "This is important as there was speculation about a white powdery substance that was found around Mr Brown's nose at the time of his death," a statement from the ombudsman said. Despite criticising prison staff for their immediate reaction to finding the prisoner unconscious in his cell, the report did not find fault with the inmate's medical management during his time in the jail. A clinical reviewer who investigated the case "did not feel that an opportunity to achieve an earlier diagnosis existed, or that there would have been a possibility to achieve an alternative outcome for Mr Brown." The ombudsman's report into the handling of the prison's case identified four matters that required improvement. Two of the four areas related to record-keeping and post-incident support for staff. The need for improvement in these two areas had already been highlighted to the prison authorities and the South-Eastern Health and Social Care Trust, which treated the inmate. The Northern Ireland Prison Service (NIPS) has accepted the ombudman's four recommendations and said they have already been implemented. The health trust has also accepted their recommendation, and told the ombudsman it has been reiterated to their staff and will be considered at a "Lessons Learned" forum. Mr McGonigle has expressed sympathy to the prisoner's family.
