In November 2005, the Polish government opened its Warsaw Treaty archives to the Institute of National Remembrance, who published some 1,300 declassified documents in January 2006. Yet the Polish government reserved publication of 100 documents, pending their military declassification. Eventually, 30 of the reserved 100 documents were published; 70 remained secret, and unpublished. Among the documents published is the Warsaw Treaty's nuclear war plan, Seven Days to the River Rhine - a short, swift counter-attack capturing Austria, Denmark, Germany and Netherlands east of River Rhine, using nuclear weapons, in self-defense, after a NATO first strike. The plan originated as a 1979 field training exercise war game, and metamorphosed into official Warsaw Treaty battle doctrine, until the late 1980s - which is why the People's Republic of Poland was a nuclear weapons base, first, to 178, then, to 250 tactical-range rockets. Doctrinally, as a Soviet-style (offensive) battle plan, Seven Days to the River Rhine gave commanders few defensive-war strategies for fighting NATO in Warsaw Treaty territory.[citation needed]

I entered the elevator with Jim and Olli, starting a new week at Fred Norville Inc. "Hey Jim, how're the kids?" I said. "They're fine, though money is a little tight these days," Jim replied. "Yeah, we're having the same problem," Olli said. "When the bills are due, we're always a little short." "What's the matter with you guys?" I asked. "Don't you know that your problem is spiritual, not financial? If you had faith, you'd have all you need." Jim and Olli exchanged glances as we stepped off the elevator. "You're right," Olli said. "If we had faith, we'd have money." "Jim," I said, "Didn't Jesus say that if we have faith, we can say to a mountain, 'Be removed and be cast into the sea' and it will obey us?" "I'll be right back," Jim said. "I have to go to the restroom." "How long will you be?" I asked. "About 10 minutes," he said. "I'll be back in time for the meeting." I walked into the conference room and sat down at the table. I'm glad Jim and Olli are going to be here. We have a major crisis on our hands. Our new product line is not selling as well as we expected. In fact, it's not selling at all. We're going to have to do some serious rethinking. Five minutes later, Jim walked into the conference room. "Where's Olli?" I asked. "I left him by the elevator," Jim said. "He must be on his way." We waited a few more minutes, but Olli did not come. Finally Jim called his cell phone. "Hey, Olli. Where are you?" "I'm having a little trouble," Olli said. "What kind of trouble?" Jim asked. "Well, you know what you said about faith?" "Yeah. So?" "I've been standing here for five minutes and trying to get this mountain moved. It's not working." A few minutes later, I heard a loud bang as the meeting room door flew open. In walked Olli, carrying a large cardboard box. "Where'd you get that?" Jim asked. "I was standing there trying to get the mountain moved when a man came out of the elevator carrying this box. He tripped and dropped the box. The box was sealed, but I heard a rattling sound inside. I opened the box and found this." Olli pulled out a pair of scissors. "I figured that these were the answer to our problem. That's why I'm late." "Wow! You mean the scissors!" Jim said. "But you said the answer to our problem was faith." "Right. I was talking about spiritual faith. I forgot to tell you about the other kind of faith. The kind that moves mountains is supernatural faith. The kind that unseals a box is natural faith. You've got to have both." I could not believe what I was hearing. I don't know what the Bible says about faith, but I know that whatever it says, it does not say this. I tried to reason with them. "Jim, you're forgetting the context of that verse. Jesus is talking about having faith in God. He's not talking about believing that we can move mountains. Olli, you're overlooking the fact that Jesus is speaking figuratively. He's talking about the power of faith. The mountain is a metaphor for any obstacle that we encounter." "We don't care about context," Jim said. "We're just following what Jesus said. If we have faith, we can move mountains. It doesn't matter whether He meant it literally or figuratively. The important thing is that we have faith." I looked around the table and realized that none of them were listening. They were all looking up at the ceiling. "What's going on?" I asked. "Nothing," Olli said. "Jim's just having a little trouble getting this ceiling fan moved." "Oh, that's OK," I said. "I'll get the ladder. You'll have it moved in no time." "You don't understand," Olli said. "Jim is trying to move the fan by faith. He's not using a ladder." I could not believe my eyes. Environmental regulation does two main things. 1) Maintains the environment contained within a country to an acceptable standard. While this has a nice "feel good" component to it, the true value lies with protecting natural assets from costly cleanup and healthcare costs. China is the quintessential example. For years they maximized the value of their resources for export and domestic use, without many environmental restraints. While this was a major boon for them in the short run, the long term health impacts of their choices and the discouragement of foreign workers and visitors will surely result in a net negative in the long run. If your country becomes a toxic, smog filled mess, people won't want to visit or work there. (Also, I don't want to seem overly disparaging of China, I know it's a huge country and not every part is like Beijing.) It is always far easier to control pollution on the production side than it is to remediate later. Institutional controls and engineering controls put in place on the front end of design and policy making are always cheaper than trying to clean up a mess later. 2) The other charge that is usually railed against environmental regulation is that enforcement and compliance is a drain on the economy. The truth is that the regulation is a drain only on the individual companies that are required to comply with the regulations. The money spent on compliance doesn't vanish into thin air, rather it simply shifts profits from one company to environmental consulting companies and their associated infrastructure. Between construction contracts for remediation work, environmental professionals, environmental laboratories, laboratory supply companies, etc etc. The money from company A gets sent to companies B-G. So long as they are all domestic and contained within the same economy, the "net" doesn't really change. The other argument would be that the more regulations you have, the more government workers are needed for monitoring and compliance. But from working in the industry, I can assure you that the average division has a very low employeeproject ratio (meaning a few regulators monitor a ton of sites), and if anything, the govt side is understaffed. The recent high profile spills have shed light on the fact that the EPA is way way behind on toxicity characterizations of industry chemicals. This is why when the spill in West Virginia occurred, all they could say was: don't contact the water, we don't know what this chemical does to humans. But more importantly, the "bigger the industry, bigger the govt" argument is applicable to all branches of public safety. The bigger the city, the more public services. The bigger a certain food industry is, the more USDA and FDA workers you need. I'm definitely open to new ideas. In terms of discourse, if you have no business experience, environmental experience, or any sort of actual experience in the nature of these industries and their impact on economies, please avoid wanton politically charged conjecture. I'm interested in learning about actual demonstrable economic reasons why having a high level of environmental regulation is negative in the long term. For sake of clarification, lets define "long term" to mean 50-100 years. Barring a worldwide catastrophe, I don't think it's that unreasonable to expect most of the big countries that are extant today to still be clucking around in 50 years. Hello, users of CMV! Time series analysis using similarity-based strategies appears to be a fruitful field; however, numerous issues arise with parameter adjustments and limitations when dealing with multivariate time series (MTS) because of attribute interdependencies or incomplete data. This study introduces an innovative solution in the form of a resilient time series cluster kernel (TCK) via kernel methodologies. By integrating the missing data management capabilities of Gaussian mixture models (GMM) enhanced with insightful prior distributions, our methodology also incorporates an ensemble learning technique to minimize dependency on parameters through amalgamation of multiple GMM clustering outcomes into one unified kernel. A charity rugby match to raise money for the Marie Therese hospital in Hayle, which has become the former player's home since he was left paralysed in an operation last year, was organised by his sons and featured a fly-past by a helicopter from RNAS Culdrose. All three of Mr Matavesi's sons play rugby professionally and they called upon some of their illustrious colleagues to take part while others, like England international Jack Nowell, donated signed shirts that helped raise nearly PS8,000 in an auction. Ex-All Blacks player Jerry Collins, who died in a car crash earlier this month, had been due to play. The event was the latest in a story that started with less fanfare when Matavesi senior came to the UK on a rugby tour with the Fiji Barbarians, in 1985. He made such an impression during a match in Cornwall that Camborne rugby club paid for him to return to play for them. As rugby union was an amateur sport in the 1980s, the club had to find him a job and the former coconut farmer, from the remote Vanua Balavu island in eastern Fiji, was taken on as a miner at South Crofty. "The only job available was tin mining, there was a lot of banter down there and I loved it," Mr Matavesi said. "All the rugby players worked down at the mine and everybody looked after each other, apart from at the weekend when we would play against each other and try to kill each other, that was the Cornish way of life. "Rugby was completely different in Fiji, I couldn't even afford a pair of boots. I had to borrow my dad's which were size 14 and pack them with pieces of cloth and paper." He returned to play for the club for several seasons before making Cornwall his permanent home after meeting Camborne local Karen Lean, with whom he started a family after they married. When she died in 2005, Mr Matavesi was left to bring up eldest son Josh, 24, who plays for Swansea's Ospreys and features in the Fijian World Cup squad. His middle son Sam, aged 23, whose regular job is with Plymouth Albion, has also represented Fiji and his youngest son 20-year-old Joel, is up and coming at Ospreys, too. "It's so weird watching the boys on TV. I'm in the hospital with an iPad, that they had to teach me how to use - it's not like smoke signals in Fiji," Mr Matavesi quipped. "That was one proud moment for me, when I saw Josh run out and sing the national anthem, I didn't know if he could speak Fijian or not but I saw his lips moving!" The 59-year-old describes his Marie Therese home as "one of the best places that ever existed," but was moved to organise the charity match when he realised its facilities were lacking. "I suddenly found my strength here, it's the way the staff treat us, we're not treated as a number," he said. "The nurses are doing a lot of physical lifting as there are three lifts and two of them don't work. "The gym is empty, whatever we can screw, velcro or tie together, we'll use. I'm lucky enough to see this and be looked after by these dedicated staff." He approaches his life there with the same spirit Roger Moyle recognised in the 1980s. Mr Moyle was one of the men who was instrumental in bringing him to Cornwall in the first place, a decision he describes as "one of the greatest things we ever did." "He had a massive frame and he entered the clubhouse like a true south sea island warrior, he turned out to be an iconic player for us, loved wherever we went," he said. Mr Matavesi joked that it did not take long for his massive frame to be enhanced by the local delicacy. "When I came over I was about 15-16 stone and I was playing as a loose forward," he said. "Then, after so many pasties, I had to be pushed in front to prop - I was beginning to look like a pasty."

This paper addresses the issue of finding a vector alpha within the set {0,1}^n that satisfies the condition f(alpha) = 1 based on a given Boolean function's truth table vector. This task is closely related to determizinig the algebraic degree of Boolean functions quickly. Moreover, it holds significance in cryptography, specifically in S-box creation for block ciphers, pseudorandom number generators for stream ciphers, and Reed-Muller code design. To tackle this challenge effectively, our approach involves studying the ordering of n-dimensional Boolean cube vectors according to their weights. Additionally, the concept of "k-th layer" plays a role in defining and analyzing the "weight order" relationship, which is then compared to the conventional "precedence" relation. Multiple counting issues associated with these relationships have been resolved, leading to contributions made to three sequences listed in the Online Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences (OEIS). Among various possible weight orders, we focus on a specific one - the Weight-Lexicographic Order (WLO), derived through detailed analysis. Furthermore, we introduce two algorithms for producing the WLO sequence and another pair of algorithms for generating the layers' characteristic vectors. These algorithms yield two fresh sequences, A294EE88 and A305860, in the OEIS database. Finally, we present two distinct methodologies for addressing the initial problem: one operates byte-by-byte utilizing the WLO sequence while the other employs bitmasks via characteristic vectors. Extensive testing has verified the efficacy of both approaches. Additional practical applications of these algorithms include representation, generation, and sorting of other combinatorial structures.

The prevalent technique for removing caffeine from coffee is known as the Swiss Water Method. This process begins by creating an initial solution using unroasted green coffee beans; this step does not contain any caffeine since the beans are raw. Subsequently, these green beans are immersed in the solution, allowing the caffeine molecules to seep into it. After separating the beans from the liquid, they retain their coffee flavor sans the caffeine content. To reclaim the water-based solution imbued with caffeine, it undergoes filtration via activated charcoal. The purified solvent can then be reused for descaling additional lots of coffee beans.

Each time she died, she was reborn at 18; but no matter how many times she tried, she never made it past the interview stage. Finally, when Mandy was 28, she got the news she had been waiting for. She had finally been accepted as an astronaut! She was overjoyed and began preparing for her upcoming mission. On launch day, Mandy felt a strange peace come over her. She knew this was the last time she would ever be reborn. Once her mission was complete, she would die permanently, but she wouldn't be afraid. After all, she had fulfilled her unlikely life event, and that was enough.

Deep metric learning is an important area due to its applicability to many domains such as image retrieval and person re-identification. The main drawback of such models is the necessity for labeled data. In this work, we propose to generate pseudo-labels for deep metric learning directly from clustering assignment and we introduce unsupervised deep metric learning (UDML) regularized by a self-supervision (SS) task. In particular, we propose to regularize the training process by predicting image rotations. Our method (UDML-SS) jointly learns discriminative embeddings, unsupervised clustering assignments of the embeddings, as well as a self-supervised pretext task. UDML-SS iteratively cluster embeddings using traditional clustering algorithm (e.g., k-means), and sampling training pairs based on the cluster assignment for metric learning, while optimizing self-supervised pretext task in a multi-task fashion. The role of self-supervision is to stabilize the training process and encourages the model to learn meaningful feature representations that are not distorted due to unreliable clustering assignments. The proposed method performs well on standard benchmarks for metric learning, where it outperforms current state-of-the-art approaches by a large margin and it also shows competitive performance with various metric learning loss functions.

Former Manchester City manager Sven Goran Eriksson delivered a damning verdict on his old club, claiming they should be winning the Premier League rather than battling to stay in the top four. City, whose current squad cost a total of 368million, host West Ham on Sunday but a Champions League spot next year is still in doubt with just four points separating them and fifth place Liverpool with six games to play. Former England manager Sven Goran Eriksson (centre) managed City in the 2007-08 season . 'For these rich clubs whose owners invest a huge amount of money, they expect to win every year, but only one team can win the title. Following the death of Braddock, William Shirley assumed command of British forces in North America. At a meeting in Albany in December 1755, he laid out his plans for 1756. The Americans had done nothing to weaken their defenses on the Delaware River and Shirley was still convinced that they should be attacked before spring. A landing at New York City would take place first; this would allow reinforcement from England, but it would also cause trouble with the French. On January 3rd, General Thomas Gage agreed to work closely with Shirley to prepare an attack. By February 24th, approximately 200 men were ready to land near Plattsburgh after crossing Lake Champlain by barge. They had brought with them eight guns, including two brass cannons provided by the Royal Navy as well as two smaller pieces that belonged to Shirley's own troop. These guns were accompanied by 350 grenadiers who wore armor-plated jackets over homespun clothing. The plan called for the troops to march inland when they reached the Mohawk Valley while Shirley concentrated his army farther north along the Hudson River. While the main force crossed the lake without incident, a small band under Colonel Robert Rogers came ashore just south of Fort Plain (modern-day Colton) where Indian allies promised to ambush them. As fate dictated, however, the enemy never materialized leaving Rogers and 70 other soldiers stranded on a barren hillside waiting through the night. By morning, Rogers realized that there must have been some kind of mistake because no enemy could possibly have arrived so early in the campaign season. He did not hesitate to make a daring escape across country back towards Fort Plain which left 100 men behind to help hold off any attackers until reinforcements arrived. Troops finally caught up with Rogers the next day and escorted him safely back to Fort George on Lake George. It is unclear whether the raid had any real effect or if English intelligence simply interpreted its failure as having accomplished something. Regardless, a much larger invasion force led by Major John Burgoyne embarked upon a more ambitious operation aimed at seizing Quebec City. In March, Burgoyne moved 5,000 men down the St Lawrence River into Canada with orders to capture Montreal, then head west toward Quebec. Instead, he met resistance almost immediately at a battle known as the Battle of Saratoga (August 19 - 21). Despite being outnumbered about three times, Burgoyne managed to repel the American invaders as well as give himself time to build up numbers and rearm. By November 1777, the British controlled most of New York state. The war prompted many changes throughout the colonies. Many men joined the Continental Army, often leaving home to fight for independence rather than receive compensation for lost property. Not all of them returned home unscathed: roughly 10 died during service and 30 permanently injured themselves after returning home. Some fought against British sympathizers among their fellow colonists while others directly faced the new settlers such as Loyalists fleeing from Canada. Supporters of the Crown saw these people as traitors deserving punishment, although the king generally tolerated their presence within the colony and eventually allowed them to settle wherever they chose. However, those who resisted British rule were viewed with deep suspicion and often treated harshly by those loyal to England. Such attitudes sprang to life in the course of several skirmishes between Patriots and Tories within the province. And even though both sides committed atrocities, small groups of vicious murderers began roaming free while local authorities stood idly by. This atmosphere changed radically following a series of raids carried out by notorious bandits known as The Oven Rats. During the winter months of 17781779, members of the group stole livestock and food supplies belonging to Patriot families living near Kingston, New York. When word spread, mobs armed with clubs, hatchets and pitchforks descended upon suspected traitor properties and burned them to ashes, looting anything of value found inside. Fortunately for the victims, provost marshals sent out to protect the accused refused to let anyone interfere with the process and many criminals escaped justice. But the situation became worse for the survivors as the mobs continued to act indiscriminately regardless of innocence. One night around Christmas, the Oven Rats stormed the house occupied by John Greenleaf Whipple in Clinton at gunpoint. They tied up the family and set fire to everything inside. Living in nearby West Point, Patrick Butler witnessed the aftermath from the road and knew firsthand what happened because his neighbor had told him what occurred. Taken aback, Butler ordered his troopers to arrest whomever they discovered responsible since the culprits had already fled in fear for their lives. It turned out to be one of the family's slaves named David, who admitted to being afraid that the house might blow up due to the flames spreading too quickly. He made the decision to confess rather than face certain torture and execution. Still, the public outcry proved too great and Governor Dinwiddie pardoned nearly everyone involved except Dinwiddie's closest friend Samuel Parris. When it comes to the Brendan Eich controversy, there has been a lot of talk about "tolerance." People who advocated for Eich's removal are hypocrites, the argument goes, because they are themselves intolerant of Eich's difference of opinion. But in my view, this is a poorly thought out argument, and a distraction from the real issue of equal rights for gay people. Yes, it sounds nice at first to have a society where we are tolerant of everyone's views, but in reality almost no one follows this. Think back to how people lived thousands of years ago, before the development of modern systems of morality. At some point in history it was considered perfectly normal and acceptable to murder other humans for material gain, to rape women, etc. During the Middle Ages, governments engaged in gruesome acts of torture as punishments for ordinary crimes. More recently, people in the U.S. kept other humans as slaves. Today, anyone advocating these beliefs would either be shunned or laughed out of room. And this is almost certainly a good thing. We shouldn't have to waste our time debating whether murder, rape or slavery is acceptable; these things should simply be dogmatically taken for granted. By ostracizing these beliefs, we can move on to debating other, more important issues. In a similar way, I would prefer to live in a society where racism, sexism and homophobia are no longer up for debate. Just like there is nothing important lost in terms of "freedom of thought" by making advocacy of murder, slavery and rape unacceptable, I fail to see the downside if these bigoted beliefs are deemed "off limits" by society. Of course, whether being opposed to equal rights for gays is reasonable and acceptable for the CEO of an organization like Mozilla in the year 2014 can be debated, and that's where the debate should be focused. Each of these has specific organs associated with them and provides crucial information regarding our surroundings. For instance, do we detect light? Yes, because we can see. Price controls such as ceilings and floors interfere with accurately assessing a product's true market value. When a maximum price limit is imposed on a commodity, it becomes impossible to gauge who has the highest demand for it. Take, for instance, setting the cost of a medical consultation at just $10; parents might frequently take their children to see a pediatrician over minor concerns. However, if the parent needs to invest considerable time or funds for the same healthcare service, they would likely contemplate its necessity beforehand. This could result in substantial shortages, similar to what occurred during the gasoline price limits in the 1970s. Now picture this scenario playing out within hospital settings.

The source code suggestions provided by current IDEs are mostly dependent on static type learning. These suggestions often end up proposing irrelevant suggestions for a peculiar context. Recently, deep learning-based approaches have shown great potential in the modeling of source code for various software engineering tasks. However, these techniques lack adequate generalization and resistance to acclimate the use of such models in a real-world software development environment. This letter presents DeepVS, an end-to-end deep neural code completion tool that learns from existing codebases by exploiting the bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) neural net. The proposed tool is capable of providing source code suggestions instantly in an IDE by using pre-trained BiGRU neural net. The evaluation of this work is two-fold, quantitative and qualitative. Through extensive evaluation on ten real-world open-source software systems, the proposed method shows significant performance enhancement and its practicality. Moreover, the results also suggest that DeepVS tool is capable of suggesting zero-day (unseen) code tokens by learning coding patterns from real-world software systems.

I'm no professional when it comes to logic or argumentation but I have been pondering this thought lately. I am not a believer of any after life or supernatural. If you don't believe in an afterlife or supernatural, then you likely hold a naturalistic worldview. This means that you see the world as governed by natural laws and that everything can be explained through natural means. People who hold this worldview often believe that the mind is simply a product of the brain and that when the brain dies, so does the mind. From this perspective, death is seen as the end of one's existence. There is no continuation of consciousness or spirit beyond physical death. This can be a difficult concept for some to accept, as it can be comforting to believe in an afterlife or the possibility of spiritual existence beyond our physical bodies. However, others find solace in the idea that the finite nature of life gives it meaning and value. This perspective encourages individuals to make the most of their time on earth and to live with intention and purpose. Ultimately, the question of what happens after death is one that may never be fully answered. Each person must come to their own conclusion based on their beliefs and experiences.

It was a cloudy Saturday morning when a group of excited students gathered outside of their school for a museum trip. The teachers had arranged for them to visit the natural history museum, which was located across town. As they boarded the bus, everyone seemed thrilled about the prospect of seeing real-life dinosaurs and other ancient creatures. Once they arrived at the museum, the students walked into a giant hall filled with dinosaur skeletons and other fascinating exhibits. The first thing they saw was an enormous Tyrannosaurus Rex skeleton, standing tall in the center of the hall. The students were awestruck and couldn't believe that such a creature existed millions of years ago. They spent some time taking photos and learning interesting facts from their guide about the T-Rex's deadly bite and its hunting tactics. Next, they moved on to a section on prehistoric mammals, where they saw giant mammoths, saber-toothed tigers, and many other creatures that had once roamed the earth. The guide explained that these huge mammals had gone extinct thousands of years ago, but their remains taught us a lot about the history of our planet. As the students walked through the galleries, they encountered various exhibits on geology, meteorites, and fossils. The students learned about the different types of rocks, how they were formed, and their importance to human life. One particular exhibit grabbed their attention. It showed the evolution of humans from primates to Homo sapiens. It was fascinating to see how far we had come as a species over millions of years. The final exhibit was about the world's oceans and marine life. The students gazed at the extensive collection of marine species, including sharks, whales, and dolphins. They also saw some small-scale models of undersea landscapes that helped them understand more about the ecosystems that existed at the bottom of the ocean. The museum trip ended with everyone feeling incredibly inspired and amazed. They left the museum with a newfound appreciation for the diversity and richness of life on our planet. They were all excited to visit the natural history museum again, eager to deepen their knowledge of the world around them.

Nazanin Zaghari-Ratcliffe - a charity worker accused of security offences - was detained while trying to leave the country with her baby daughter after visiting relatives in April 2016. Her family denies she broke any laws. Her husband, Richard Ratcliffe, who is from London, said his wife's detention was a "stain" on Iran. Mrs Zaghari-Ratcliffe, 38, who works for the charity the Thomson Reuters Foundation, has been detained in Iran since her arrest last year. The couple's two-year-old daughter has remained in Iran after the government confiscated her passport, and is being looked after by her grandparents. Mrs Zaghari-Ratcliffe's family said in September that a Revolutionary Court had handed down the five-year term. She was accused of allegedly plotting to topple the government in Tehran, but the official charges against her were not made public. According to Mr Ratcliffe, his wife's appeal was dismissed in a secret hearing of an Iranian Revolutionary Court on 4 January but only announced on 22 January. In a statement, her husband said the precise charges against her remain secret, but that two new accusations were made at her appeal. One was that she had been head of recruitment for the BBC's Farsi service when it was launched in 2009. Her family say she worked on a BBC training project for youth in Afghanistan and Iran, but never worked for BBC Farsi. The other charge was that she was married to a British spy. Mr Ratcliffe is an accountant. Monique Villa, chief executive of Thomson Reuters Foundation said she is "outraged by this new mockery of justice," and reiterated Mrs Zaghari-Ratcliffe never worked for BBC Farsi and that her husband "is not a spy but a reputable accountant." "I am fully convinced of Nazanin's innocence," she added. Francesca Unsworth, BBC World Service Group director, said Mrs Zaghari-Ratcliffe had briefly worked for charity BBC Media Action in a "junior administrative capacity" but had never worked for BBC Persian. "In any case, to suggest that being employed by BBC Persian is tantamount to'acting against national security' is patently ludicrous," Ms Unsworth added. Mr Ratcliffe said: "The lack of justice in Nazanin's case continues to be a stain on Iran. The continued attempt to frame Nazanin behind secrets and lies brings shame. "It is a needless waste of a mother and child's life for their own political bargains and economic interests." Iran does not recognize dual nationalities, meaning those detained cannot receive consular assistance. Since her imprisonment, her family have campaigned on her behalf, highlighting her deteriorating health while in jail and her anguish at her separation from her daughter.

For the typical backbench MP, creating laws may appear like a remote opportunity. This rare occasion arises just once annually through a lottery system. Such events allow MPs to advance their favoured initiatives within the House of Commons by proposing a Private Members' Bill. These bills can enter into Parliament via one of three methods: "Ten Minute Rule" bills with brief introductory speeches; formal presentations in the Commons; or the popular "Ballot Bills," which rely on a random selection process to determine the proposer. However, many criticize this methodology, including those involved in drafting significant legislation such as the "Turing Bill". Critics argue the current approach lacks transparency and could hinder parliamentary credibility. Furthermore, even when a Private Members' Bill reaches the Commons stage, there's no assurance it will be enacted due to potential filibustering tactics used by opposing members. Accordingly, efforts are being made to revise this convoluted procedure, with suggestions aimed at providing fair opportunities for all backbench MPs seeking to contribute meaningfully to the legislative process.

Aspect Term Extraction (ATE) identifies expressions reflecting opinions within text segments, aimed at conducting sentiment analysis based on specific aspects. Review corpora accessible online are rich in expressive aspect terms across diverse sectors. This study introduces a technique utilizing these resources to develop a fresh ATE dataset. Our approach employs an attention mechanism to pinpoint sentences likely containing meaningful aspect terms, enhancing the precision of aspect extraction. Subsequently, we employ the generated dataset to instruct a model for ATE under distant supervision. Comparisons against established benchmarks reveal our strategy's superior effectiveness regarding both unsupervised and supervised methods. Additionally, we demonstrate the significance of strategic sentence selection in crafting new ATE datasets, showing marked improvements in performance by focusing on relevant sentences rather than entire collections.

Although Kenya is the biggest and most advanced economy in east and central Africa, and has an affluent urban minority, it has a Human Development Index (HDI) of 0.519, ranked 145 out of 186 in the world. Kenya has an urban population of approximately 14 million, or 30 of the total population. Nearly 40 of these people live in informal settlements (slums) on less than one dollar a day, and in conditions of poor sanitation and health. Despite its progress in social and economic development, Kenya faces a variety of development challenges. Wealth and income are concentrated in the hands of a relatively few individuals. The economic growth of the last two decades has not been able to keep up with the high population growth and the resultant demand for housing, employment, education and health care. Yet Kenya has a lot to offer the world. It has an innovative and industrious population, a dynamic civil society, and a booming economy. But Kenya's human development has been uneven, and millions of people are still living in poverty. VSO volunteers in Kenya work to address this imbalance and support the country's development by sharing skills and knowledge, and working with local communities, government and the private sector. VSO has been operating in Kenya since 1963. We work with the most vulnerable communities in the poorest counties in the country, including Turkana, Samburu, Marsabit and Wajir. Our volunteers work on projects that involve education, disability and youth. As a VSO volunteer in Kenya you can help build a fairer future for all. Browse all our current vacancies in Kenya Youth volunteering in Kenya A major aspect of Kenya's development is the empowerment of its youth. In a country where 70 of the population are under 30 years old, harnessing the energy and skills of young people is crucial to Kenya's future. We want to equip young Kenyans with the skills and knowledge that will help them to lift themselves out of poverty, and build a brighter future for their country. We do this by placing young Kenyan volunteers, who have just finished their schooling, with community projects across the country. The projects are wide-ranging, from maternal health, to education, to income generation for women. Our young volunteers gain valuable experience, which will help them in their future career or education, as well as providing much-needed support to communities across Kenya. Find out more about our youth volunteering programme Kenya education We're working to improve the quality of education in Kenya by supporting teachers with training and resources. Poor education has been a persistent problem in Kenya, particularly in disadvantaged communities. In 2011, Kenya's primary education enrolment rate was just 68.4 and the net enrolment rate for secondary school was 34.7. Children in rural communities are most at risk of receiving a poor education. Schools are often very under-resourced, with poor infrastructure and a lack of teaching staff. In these areas, VSO volunteers have been working closely with communities and teachers to improve the quality of education and raise standards. Find out more about education volunteering Kenya youth volunteering The right to education for deaf children in Kenya A major problem for deaf children in Kenya is that they are often excluded from school. Lack of awareness, understanding and resources mean that many schools are unable to support deaf children. Even schools with facilities for deaf students struggle with the challenges of teaching sign language, as well as lacking staff and resources. VSO has been working with the Kenyan Ministry of Education to find ways of improving access to education for deaf children. Find out more about our deaf education programme Deaf children in Kenya face many obstacles to accessing education Kenya disability volunteering Supporting people living with disabilities in Kenya An estimated 10 of the population of Kenya has a disability. But many people with disabilities are excluded from education and employment opportunities, as well as other social and economic activities. In many areas of Kenya, people with disabilities face stigma and are even shunned. Our disability volunteers work with disabled people and the wider community to support people with disabilities to have equal access to education, employment, and healthcare.

In a report, published in early February 2007 by the Ear Institute at the University College London, and Widex, a Danish hearing aid manufacturer, Newcastle was named as the noisiest city in the world. The report said that Newcastle had "a collective noise level of 5-6db," which is higher than any other European capital. The study also found that people living within three miles from Newcastle have to deal with an average of 1,074 ambient sounds per day, while someone who lives outside of this distance has just 160 sounds. This means they are exposed to 13 times more noise than those living on the outskirts of the city. But noise pollution isn't necessarily all bad news - it can actually help us hear better and even make life easier for some. For example, sound waves can enhance our ability to detect things like flying objects or children's voices (even if we're only able to pick them out when they make repeated loud noises). However, excessive amounts of noise can be detrimental to mental health, according to experts. In fact, keeping your bedroom quiet may reduce stress levels and help you sleep.

Looking at the new [wiki] , I saw in the philosophy section that "Nobody thinks people are inherently selfless (thus far) ." And, well, that is pretty close to what I think, so I was curious about others thoughts and if they would change my view on this topic. To be clear, by "selfless" I don't mean a perfectly good Christ-like figure who sacrifices themselves to always put all others before them. By saying someone is "inherently selfless" I mean that person has someone or something they value more highly than themselves, and which they would often put above their own well-being to support. Many people would say their "life purpose" is to make the world a better place than they left it; oftentimes in history this has resulted in people risking their lives for some ideal. Many parents would go hungry to feed their children. Countless people have or would risk themselves to save another, even a stranger. Most of us have done something as simple as giving money to a charity, even at no benefit to themselves. I don't think all people are selfless; there are of course people without empathy who care only for themselves. But I think most people, even if they can be selfish as well, do have something in them which makes them inherently selfless when it comes to what they think is important. To be inherently selfless you don't have to put everything above yourself, but you do have to put something above yourself. So what reasons do you have for me to think differently? Links to research on the topic encouraged. CMV

In connectionless mode each packet includes complete addressing information. The packets are routed individually, sometimes resulting in different paths and out-of-order delivery. Each packet is labeled with a destination address, and the network device maps source addresses to corresponding destinations (which may be unique or shared). A router receives an IP datagram from one of its interfaces as an input, then forwards it on according to some policy (such as forwarding based on MAC header fields) if no other local interface has local routing information for that packet's next hop, and finally discards it otherwise.[1] As such, routers play a central role in Internetworking. The basic distinction between Layer 3 devices and Layer 2 devices is whether they use multicast or broadcast protocols: Layer 3 switches use unicasting exclusively; while Layer 2 hubs do not implement any kind of access control lists at all (thus allowing multiple hosts to send data into the same switch port without restriction), but rather they perform per-packet filtering using hardware flow tables. This method allows them to scale more efficiently than most Layer 3 solutions.

Setting aside health concerns, I believe refraining from consuming meat, especially lamb, chicken, and pork, may complicate discussions. However, should it become necessary, let's proceed with it. In my viewpoint, avoiding meat consumption seems rather unkind. Moreover, when it comes to slaughtering these animals, we must ensure their death is as painless and dignified as possible. We ought to treat animals with reverence and prevent any form of mistreatment; this does not include supporting industrialized livestock operations.

We essentially have three options regarding animal existence: - They might never be born - They could roam freely in nature - Or, they could be reared within controlled agricultural environments

I advocate for the latter option, where animals experience a fulfilling life without inflicting significant damage upon others. Animals living on a farm receive numerous benefits such as medical care, protection from natural predators, consistent access to nourishment, and shelter from adverse weather conditions. Naturally, once they reach full maturity, they will ultimately be processed into meat products, which, in my opinion, constitutes a reasonable compromise. Additionally, raising animals under such circumstances appears more ethically sound than allowing them to perish due to harsh wilderness factors like starvation, predation, and diseases – all of which result in agonizing deaths. Therefore, summarily speaking, promoting the responsible and humane breeding and processing of animals proves advantageous for both humans and animals alike.

He felt the headache coming on in waves of throbbing pain radiating from the back of his head, forward towards his eyeballs, which in turn were having a difficult time focusing on his immediate surroundings. Squinting, he once more pulled up his bloodied sleeve, wincing as the caked blood caught and sent a jolt of pain up his arm. RUN Gaz knew the feeling, he had woken up in a similar state of drowsiness exactly ten years ago to the day, on the morning of his tenth birthday. Except back then- what seemed like centuries ago- his Awakening had been greeted by a chilled glass of water and two translucent pills. His mother had been sitting on the side of the bed, gently tilting his head forward to help him as he had tried to regain his bearings. She had kissed his clammy forehead, and then, with her sweet nurturing voice had said: " Congratulations sweetheart, I'm so very proud of you. Drink this, slowly, and don't worry honey, it will pass soon, I promise " He remembered her flipping his pillow over, fluffing it by striking it twice firmly, and setting his head back into the cool, blissfully soft cushion, just as a deep regenerating sleep had begun to take over. But that was then. There would be no glass of chilled water to help soothe away the pain today. Not unless he scrounged some credits up, and made his way two buildings over to the Automated Provisioning Machine. Something which in this state, was purely unthinkable. And certainly there would be no translucent pills. Sure, the A.P.M. probably had one or two kits in stock, but Gaz wouldn't be able to afford one, not until next month anyways- and by then this headache will have possibly killed him. He slowly swiveled his legs over the side of the bunk, and let his feet rest on the cool metal grate for a few moments. The flickering neon light outside the window was buzzing its usual monotone hum, the yellow light filtering in through the chips and dents in the otherwise closed blinds. Well, at least he had thought to shut them last night. " You'd think that with ten years to prepare for my next Awakening, I would have planned this morning slightly better " he thought to himself. But then, planning had never been Gaz's forte- isn't that why he was living in this shit hole to begin with? He carefully tried to calculate how many steps it would take for him to reach the rusty tap in the corner of his rented pad. He figured if he could at least make it within arm's reach before succumbing to the pain, he could always crawl the rest of the way. Planting his feet firmly, well as firmly as he could manage, Gaz willed himself up, staggered a few haphazard steps forwards, and face planted just short of the tap. He clearly had underestimated how incredibly off his motor skills were. Hoisting himself up awkwardly using the pedestal of the sink for support, Gaz suddenly was overcome with a wave of stomach-churning nausea. He forced his face into the sink and vomited a putrid stream of foul smelling liquid, mostly bile if he had to guess. As the waves of pain in his head increased in droves, they seemed to amplify with each pulse. Darkness begin to creep in from the sides of his vision, he yanked the tap open and managed to swallow two large gulps of tepid water before the darkness overcame him and sent him crashing back to the ground. Gaz woke up some time later to the sound of loud, muffled, yelling coming from somewhere in the building. He tried to move his arm into view again but yanked himself up with a start, as he was immediately aware of a feeling of wetness in his clothes. The tap was open, spilling water out over the edge of the sink, and water had begun to pool on the floor. " Shit! " He slowly got up, groaning as he felt the remnants of the crippling headache lurking right behind his temples. He carefully sloshed a few steps forward and reached over to shut off the tap when his bloodied arm came into view. RUN Whatever Future-Self had wanted to communicate, Gaz wished he would have done so on paper. Maybe with some additional details as to what he was meant to be running from and where to? Let alone when. Timing is everything they say, right? As he strained his memory to try and remember anything else from the night before, the yelling became much louder, most definitely emanating from somewhere on his floor. He heard a loud series of bangs down the hallway followed by the instantly recognizable, deep digitized voice of a New TriCity Enforcer. " OPEN THE DOOR NOW CITIZEN! " What was going on out there? Gaz briefly considered opening the door to see what the commotion was about but very quickly decided that would probably be just the latest in a series of terrible decisions. His mind unfocused again as he tried to make sense of the Message. Everyone was taught early on that each Awakening was meant to bring a sense of illumination, purpose, direction. Gaz felt nothing but confusion, distress, and anxiety. No one would never know what their Future-Self's exact Message was meant to be, as that was not passed to them. Rather, similar to a dream you've just woken up from where everything seems so clear just moments before, it all whisks away within moments, and very little- if anything- is retained. It is said that certain people, the Gifted, are able to retain the quasi-entirety of their Message on Awakening. Except no one had seen a Gifted in the past few centuries. Gaz wasn't asking to be Gifted, he didn't need to remember everything from his Future-Self's Message, but maybe a few extra words or context wouldn't have hurt either. Three loud BANGs on his door in rapid succession jolted him out of his stream of consciousness. Clearly the Enforcers hadn't found whatever or whoever they were looking for. " OPEN THE DOOR CITIZEN! " bellowed the ominous voice. " Ehrmm, sure just one second, I just need to get some pan- " " OPEN IT IMMEDIATELY OR WE WILL BE FORCED TO BREAK IT DOWN " As he pondered how rude it was of the Enforcer to interrupt him, Gaz's eye caught sight of a half-open metal suitcase laying on the floor at the foot of his bunk. " CITIZEN THIS IS YOUR FINAL WARNING, OPEN THE DOOR OR FACE IMMEDIATE CONSEQUENCES " Gaz barely registered what the Enforcer was saying. Time seemed to slow down to where he was suddenly acutely aware of his heart beat, breathing, and the perspiration gliding down the side of his face. The suitcase was full to the brim of brand new, shiny credits. He had never seen the suitcase in his life. Let alone that amount of credits. " PER MANDATE 6474-2 OF TRI-CITY ENFORCEMENT, ENTRY AUTHORIZED " At the edges of his peripheral, Gaz once again saw the cryptic message on his arm: RUN Synapses fired. Suddenly it connected. Gaz grasped the side of the railing of his bunk and vaulted over to where the suitcase lay, just as the door gave way with a sickening crunch. Without giving it a second thought, he grabbed the suitcase and crashed through the blinds and glass window onto the fire escape. " STOP YOUR FLIGHT CITIZEN OR LETHAL FORCE WILL BE USED PER MANDATE 8373-2 OF TRI-CITY ENFORCEMENT " Thank the Mandates. In the time it took for the Enforcer to rattle off the Mandate number, Gaz had managed to slide down the ladder to the dark street below, just as the first bullet ricocheted off the rung above his head. Suitcase in hand, sirens wailing, the caustic smell of the nearby sewer exacerbating the already suffocating thickness of the city air, he glanced once more down at his arm as he took a leaping step down the side alleyway. RUN He'd have to figure out why he had forsaken his arm over using paper at a later time, but in his head Gaz gave his Future-Self a well-deserved high-five. Gaz may not be Gifted but quite suddenly he sure felt a surge of enlightenment. Now he just needed to figure out how to get out of the City alive....

On an international level the German DIN 4512 system has been effectively superseded in the 1980s by ISO 6:1974, ISO 2240:1982, and ISO 5800:1979 where the same sensitivity is written in linear and logarithmic form as "ISO 10021" (now again with degree symbol). These ISO standards were subsequently adopted by DIN as well. Finally, the latest DIN 4512 revisions were replaced by corresponding ISO standards, DIN 4512-1:1993-05 by DIN ISO 6:1996-02 in September 2000, DIN 4512-4:1985-08 by DIN ISO 2240:1998-06 and DIN 4512-5:1990-11 by DIN ISO 5800:1998-06 both in July 2002.

As an experienced sushi chef, I want to clarify that while there may be a possibility of finding parasites in wild-caught fish, this issue is typically addressed by the fisheries through flash freezing upon capture. Consequently, the fish delivered to sushi establishments, including top-tier ones, pose minimal risks of contamination provided they aren't exposed to fluctuating temperatures or extended periods outside the cooler environment. 

Regarding bacterial or viral dangers associated with consuming fresh fish, such instances are uncommon since hazardous bacteria usually emerge when the fish comes ashore or resides in polluted waters. Nevertheless, these fish are promptly chilled after surfacing, limiting bacterial growth opportunities. Moreover, fish intended for raw consumption undergoes freezing procedures. Water quality monitoring processes are also implemented to ensure safety standards. It's worth mentioning that certain fish species harbor parasites or their eggs, but these can be neutralized via freezing methods mentioned earlier. In cases like herring popular in the Netherlands, gutting becomes necessary to eliminate parasites swiftly. Furthermore, visible parasite eggs present during preparation can be discarded easily.

However, specific fish varieties known for having parasites resistant to freezing or those inherently dangerous due to natural toxins are avoided entirely in both Western and Japanese culinary practices. Squid, for instance, is always cooked before eating, whereas numerous freshwater fish are excluded altogether. Lastly, some fish accumulate toxins from their diet or environment, particularly reef fishes and those dwelling in areas affected by mercury contamination, though they might still feature in Southeast Asian cuisines as the main source of foodborne illnesses.

Amy had taken her sister Ali with to a friends house. Ali had gotten into a fight with the friends little sister. Amy chased Ali as she stomped down the stairs of their friend's home and over to his mom on the front porch, pinning him up against it. Her foot was crushing his chest and he couldn't breathe. "Run!" yelled his mother, "Go get help!" Ali ran from the terror that was about to happen inside the house and out onto the street. He was lucky because there were no cars going by at the time or any people walking around. It also wasn't raining; so if someone would have walked past they wouldn't be able to see what all happened anyway."He okay?" asked Amy She nodded in response to which Amy replied, "Yeah I think so..." They both turned back towards where Ali had been standing moments earlier. The whole left side of his face was gone! She nearly fainted seeing this horrific sight. His lifeless body fell to the ground like he had just collapsed after being shot. But when Amy looked closer...nothing but skin remained above the cheekbone. There was nothing more than meat hanging off bones on Ali's head. A small pool of blood could still seep out from under the fleshy parts on top of his skull. Stunned, Amy felt light headed and as faint as cotton candy. Everything in the world slowed down for just seconds, then sped back up again. If Amy hadn't reached around his neck to try and find a pulse she would not be telling you now. After several deep breaths, while trying to calm herself, Amy bent forward and placed two fingertips on his carotid artery....just to make sure. No heartbeat. Only the tiniest flutter of breath came out between her lips as she thought about how much pain poor person must've went through for the rest of his life before meeting such an unfortunate end.

A hedge fund in its most basic form is a paid group of investors who take people's money and invest it to make a profit. The difference between a hedge fund, and say a typical mutual fund is that a mutual fund is generally restricted to buying a very specific type of investment- like stocks of large companies, or stocks for foreign companies based in Asia. A hedge fund can pretty much do whatever it wants with your money. It can buy gold, speculate on corn, sell real estate, invest in complex derivatives, or even buy a load of jelly beans if its that's what the head of the fund thinks will increase in value. The managers will often give you a very broad overview of how it tries to make money, but it is not bound by them, and will rarely give you specific details of its positions. To protect the average guy from having their money taken by some scam artist, or having an elderly person turn over their retirement fund to a company that is investing in things they don't understand, there are regulations in place that state that you have to have a million dollars in order to invest in a hedge fund, and that a hedge fund can have no more than 100 investors. The intent is that if you have that much money, you know what you are doing- whether that is true, could be debated. Lawyers have found clever ways to get around that by forming shell companies that pool money and then are the "investor" in a fund, but in general, hedge funds want relatively few clients that invest large amounts of money. The "hedge" part of the name hedge fund is derived from the fact that hedge funds try to make money regardless of whether the market moves up or down. If the market goes down, the hedge fund should have short positions that will increase in value. Complex investment strategies are employed to try to achieve this, but it doesn't always work. Again, you can contrast this with a typical mutual fund or pension fund that only buys stocks or bonds and never bets against them going down in value.

This proposal holds Internet Service Providers (ISPs) accountable for their clients' online activities, much like parents are liable for underage drinking occurrences within their homes. Both simple and strong induction consist of two components: a foundation case and an inductive assumption. Simple induction includes the following elements: Foundation case: Hypothesis 1 holds true. Inductive assumption: Assuming Hypothesis n is accurate implies Hypothesis n+1 is also valid. In contrast, strong induction comprises these aspects: Foundation case: Hypothesis sinces true. Inductive assumption: The truth of Hypotheses from 1 to n guarantees the accuracy of Hypothesis n+1. Strong induction might be required if the proof of Hypothesis n+1 relies on more than just Hypothesis n. As an example, consider verifying the effectiveness of merge sort with n items. Foundation case: Merge sort functions correctly for a single item, which is straightforward to demonstrate. Inductive assumption: Merge sort operates accurately for n items, assuming its efficiency for all preceding items (from 1 to n). Since the initial step of merge sort involves dividing the set into two nearly equal subsets and sorting them separately, ensuring the algorithm's correctness for both floor(n/2) and ceiling(n/2) values becomes essential. It should be noted that if one intends to validate correctness solely for powers of 2, then simple induction suffices by defining Hypothesis n as "merge sort being precise when dealing with 2^n items." A ninja edit suggests that demonstrating the reliability of quicksort using a randomly chosen pivot would better highlight the need for strong induction.

Our model is based on a bidirectional transformer encoder (i.e., BERT) and produces extremely high semantic-level accuracy, especially for highly structured documents or timelines among corpora as well as documents with multiple document types. Furthermore our method has an application in the context of image search systems where we show that it can be used to extract legends from images using text vocabularies extracted from image matching data. We introduce this approach in order to study its potential applications not only in relation to image classification but also for other domains involving unstructured data such as video surveillance, call logs, social media content analysis etc. Additionally, we investigate how our method can be improved through different modifications which include avoiding the use of sparse representations while increasing their number by using sigmoid functions and adding a matrix-vector product rule to generate the best possible nodes. This allows us to obtain a better depth representation of associations between labeled terms within any class. In addition to these improvements, we introduce several novel semantic models specific to ED. For example, we consider three different approaches for categorizing time series: firstly, an approach based on temporal regularization which makes sense when dealing with historical events of interest; secondly, different type of clustering which handles temporal dependencies combining two structural categories into one; thirdly, linear segmentation which allows extracting related features easily from hierarchical structures containing many labels. Smooth pursuit eye movements provide meaningful insights and information on subject's behavior and health and may, in particular situations, disturb the performance of typical fixationsaccade classification algorithms. Thus, an automatic and efficient algorithm to identify these eye movements is paramount for eye-tracking research involving dynamic stimuli. In this paper, we propose the Bayesian Decision Theory Identification (I-BDT) algorithm, a novel algorithm for ternary classification of eye movements that is able to reliably separate fixations, saccades, and smooth pursuits in an online fashion, even for low-resolution eye trackers. The proposed algorithm is evaluated on four datasets with distinct mixtures of eye movements, including fixations, saccades, as well as straight and circular smooth pursuits; data was collected with a sample rate of 30 Hz from six subjects, totaling 24 evaluation datasets. The algorithm exhibits high and consistent performance across all datasets and movements relative to a manual annotation by a domain expert (recall: 91.42 , 9.52; precision: 95.60 , 5.29; specificity 95.41 , 7.02) and displays a significant improvement when compared to I-VDT, an state-of-the-art algorithm (recall: 87.67 , 14.73; precision: 89.57 , 8.05; specificity 92.10 , 11.21). My two year tour didn't start too great. Recruits don't get to have good stories from their first week, even if they do get promoted to squad lead leaving the institute. Fresh from graduating in August 2018, they gave me a four-man room, five techs to cram it with, and command of the Techolite's Alpha Division, 4th Squad. One of the techs was four years my senior and formerly a network administrator with some big bank company. However he found out his squad lead was a restaurant manager before my induction into the institute. He may have taken some exception to that during orientation. Blood boiled on day one in that small room and we hadn't begun engaging the enemy. I was lucky he didn't try and overthrow me there and then. Techolite recruits were an angry, repressed branch of the army. We were new. There was a lot your lowest tech could get away with that a marine could only dream of doing to their drill sergeants. When a nation rested on young shoulders, bitching about your back came with the job. And boy, they let us bitch. Sudden orders from the top paused the admin from making any further rebellion. Division command ordered a recon of the enemy defense. Aggressive tactics were Alpha Division, and they asked for 4th Squad specifically to scoop some data. We'd bring back the mess. Intelligence would make sense of it. Our tiny room became a hot zone. Four techs jumped on their consoles booting up hardware. I sent the fifth to get us coffee. Your Uncle Buttons still gives me shit for that in his Christmas cards. Twenty minutes later, we launched our operation with nothing but the latest and greatest extens for Alpha Division. The room would die every time we threw them on, and trails of blue light screamed over us. Extens let you see the coding and blocking zap above you in lines like bullet trails. The love taps and initial hack attempts were higher above us, way into a space looming like a chandelier. Harder stuff would try to hit deeper, sunk lower. Sometimes zipping inches above you. For recon ops, we had to be on some fine wire to see deeper. Beyond what a monitor could tell you. It was not just coding at that point. Techneurology hooked us into the war itself, first row seats and popcorn banging on both sides. I witnessed the firing of a virus for the first time in that first op. Those large yellow blots always zipped in a blur. God forbid any of them would get smashed over us. You wouldn't want those things in your head after unplugging. We took our time pushing through trenches of corroded data, staying low to avoid a zip smashing through our little group. Finally found ourselves gaping at a large, blood mesh wall. There was no seeing through or over it, the damned thing was too tightly woven. I remember the patterns too. How they made no sense. It wasn't for us to do, but if at any time you ever see'random' in your life, I can bet your weekend pass I've seen chaos, and how nothing ever looked sane again. The op was simple. Just a literal scoop of that wall for intelligence to poke at. Our squad backup specialist whipped out a pole like he was going to beat it with the wife away, and thrust the damn thing like she just came back. Your Uncle Quaint was always a weird one. A couple seconds later he yanked it out, and I guess some logistics personnel forgot to cap the pole with a sealing agent. Our hole in the wall wasn't closing. I threw Quaint back, kicking the boys back into the trench. We had to make a haul for it. The wall was going to send out a detonation to clear the base before sealing the hole itself. Purges were nothing to let pool casually behind your back. We were warned at the institute that the enemy was more conscious of info leaks from random prods, and would blow out a server of any waste-data to ensure a leak wouldn't pile with the corrupted trench files for us to search later. The same ones we had to kick and push our way through to make our exit point. It was damned close. Your grandpa would have been a vegetable for a couple weeks if Buttons hadn't found another console to clear a few trench loads that'd have stood in our way. Boredom can save missions. And that's how your grandpa and your uncles helped crack the Turing Wall. We had many missions in the Great Cyberwar, but that first one told Alpha Division what 4th Squad was good for. Remember to ask your Uncle Quaint how we got some launch codes and accidentally blew up a town with them trying to order takeout later, I get a kick out of that every time.

For a phylum with relatively few species, ctenophores have a wide range of body plans. In addition oceanic species do not preserve well, and are known mainly from photographs and from observers' notes. Hence most attention has until recently concentrated on three coastal genera - Pleurobrachia, Beroe and Mnemiopsis. At least two textbooks base their descriptions of ctenophores on the cydippid Pleurobrachia.

A team from Glasgow University found there was a sharp fall in accidents from 5,901 in 1997 to 2,914 in 2014. The researchers said, however, there was "no evidence" the M74 had impacted on an "already decreasing trend." The five-mile (8km) route, which cost PS692m, links the M74 at Carmyle to the M8 southwest of the Kingston Bridge. Planning permission for the route was granted in October 1995 and immediately opposed by Joint Action Against the M74 (Jam74) - a coalition of community, environmental and sustainable transport groups. Construction began in 2008 after a last-ditch legal bid to halt the project was abandoned by Friends of the Earth Scotland and Jam74. Supporters claimed the road would bring economic benefits to the west of Scotland and help cut accidents, whereas critics argued it would cause more pollution, increase health problems and fragment communities. The Glasgow University study looked to evaluate the impact of the M74 extension on the number of road accidents on local roads during the construction period and following its opening. Lead author of the report, Dr Jonathan Olsen, said: "The building of the M74 extension in the south of Glasgow was controversial. There were strong arguments for and against its construction, but ultimately it went ahead. "One of the arguments in favour was that it could reduce road accidents on local streets. "In our study we examined police accident data from 1997 to 2014, three years after the new motorway was opened, and found that this predicted reduction in road accident numbers had not materialised." He added: "But on the other hand, we found no evidence that the M74 extension had led to an increase in accidents." Report co-author, Professor Rich Mitchell, added: "There is surprisingly little evidence about the impacts new motorways have. "This research will be useful for planners, politicians and residents elsewhere who are trying to decide whether to build or not." The study is published in the Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health.

In several combinatorial optimization problems arising in cryptography and design theory, the admissible solutions must often satisfy a balancedness constraint, such as being represented by bitstrings with a fixed number of states. In this paper we show that an efficient algorithm is given for computing the optimal balanced solutions to these problems. A new method is developed for finding weighted combinations (mixtures) of two or more bits that are uniformly likely to be produced by a random process having variable probability density functions over its space. The approach of using weights allows us to use small numbers of operations and to deal directly with the problem of finding the set of uniform probabilities used at each stage of the search. We present a series of examples where our algorithm finds well-defined mixtures. One example discusses applications to system identification within probabilistic databases. Another involves construction of decision trees from binary strings. A third example shows how to find all possible permutations which meet certain constraints on order andor size; it also features an application to the distribution of discrete logarithms. Finally, the notion introduced here is extended to general matrices containing any arbitrary group of real valued variables, giving rise to a very simple formula for calculating the likelihood of obtaining a desired output if it belongs to a mixture corresponding to a given input.

A firm hand grasped her arm and led them away as she escaped the bank with her mother and father none the wiser. Really it comes down to 2 reasons, neither of which have to do with people jumping off. 1. inconsistent snowfall throughout the years. (measured long term). Some places can easily get 250 inches (20 feet) of snow 1 year. And just 4 or 5 feet the next year. That's a huge differences. And having fixed cable support towers that are on the high side is a heck of a lot cheaper and safer than having some kind of fancy hydraulic cable support towers that go up and down. (although some mountains do have these) 2. Life expectancy and load. Installing a ski lift is very expensive. (millions) Replacing the steel cable that all of the chairs attach to is also very expensive. (hundreds of thousands, upwards to a million for a cable job). The main cable does stretch out over the course of a few years. As it stretches, the chairs will dip in between the support towers, which causes them to ride lower. If support towers were to low, that could cause a problem. Buy having them up higher you can run with the same cable longer as it stretches. If you look at most ski lifts, where you load on the bottom, the wheel that the cable wraps around is on a trolley. And that trolley slides back and forth. Attached to that trolley is a counter weight that pulls the wheel backwards in order to create tension on the cable. It's usually a large concrete block. On a busy day, when the ski lift is fully loaded, the counterweight will be up high, when it's slow, and the chairs are lightly loaded, the counterweight will be down low. The counterweight, and how it is all engineered determines how high the chairs are off of the ground. But on chair lifts that are fully loaded, and the counterweight is down low, then the cable is to stretched. Remember that chairs can easily dip a good 10 to 15 feet between the support towers depending on how loaded the lift is, and how stretched the cable is.

Thousands of elderly people in the UK are losing out on free personal care due to delays in assessments and care arrangements, a leading charity has claimed.
