We describe a simple approach to semantic parsing based on a tensor product kernel. We extract two feature vectors: one for the query and one for each candidate logical form. The features are weighted by their importance in determining an adequate representation of the clause, then combined using the tensor product kernel into a single label vector that is used to score all possible interpretations of the clause. Our implementation uses only a few parameters, can handle arbitrary complexity expressions, and does not require any information about the context in which the expression occurs. Unlike most previous approaches, we do not seek to identify positions within the clauses where different grammatical or orthographic structures might be expected; rather our goal is simply to detect whether there exists more than one interpretation of any given subexpression (which may correspond to multiple tokenizations).

In this paper, we investigate dynamic resource allocation (DRA) problems for Internet of Things (IoT) in real-time cloud radio access networks (C-RANs), by combining gradient boosting approximation and deep reinforcement learning to obtain a hybrid methodology for DRA in C-RAN. In a C-RAN, IoT devices can offload their computation tasks to the base station, which is connected to the cloud via high-speed backhaul. The base station schedules the computation tasks of IoT devices and optimizes the base station radio resource management (RRM) via a local controller. In the DRA, the base station tries to assign the computation tasks of IoT devices to the cloud via the local controller. For the sake of the real-time operation, the DRA is carried out in multiple rounds. In each round, the local controller selects the IoT devices with the most urgent tasks and allocates radio resources to the selected IoT devices. In the end, we propose a methodology based on the gradient boosting approximation and the deep reinforcement learning to solve the DRA problem. In the proposed methodology, the gradient boosting approximation is used to obtain the average reward function in the DRA problem and the deep reinforcement learning is used to obtain the optimal control policy in the DRA problem. Moreover, we obtain the upper and lower bounds of the average reward function and use the upper bound to train the deep reinforcement learning network. We conduct extensive simulations to verify that the proposed methodology outperforms other baseline schemes.

Networks are a natural way of thinking about many datasets. The data on which a network is based, however, is rarely collected in a form that suits the analysis process, making it necessary to create and reshape networks. Data wrangling is widely acknowledged to be a critical part of the data analysis pipeline, yet interactive network wrangling has received little attention in the visualization research community. In this paper, we discuss a set of operations that are important for wrangling network datasets and introduce a visual data wrangling tool, Origraph, that enables analysts to apply these operations to their datasets. Key operations include creating a network from source data such as tables, reshaping a network by introducing new node or edge classes, filtering nodes or edges, and deriving new node or edge attributes. Our tool, Origraph, enables analysts to execute these operations with little to no programming, and to immediately visualize the results. Origraph provides views to investigate the network model, a sample of the network, and node and edge attributes. In addition, we introduce interfaces designed to aid analysts in specifying arguments for sensible network wrangling operations. The present state of the art in analytics requires high upfront investment of human effort and computational resources to curate datasets, even before the first query is posed. So-called pay-as-you-go data curation techniques allow these high costs to be spread out, first by enabling queries over uncertain and incomplete data, and then by assessing the quality of the query results. We describe the design of a system, called Mimir, around a recently introduced class of probabilistic pay-as-you-go data cleaning operators called Lenses. Mimir wraps around any deterministic database engine using JDBC, extending it with support for probabilistic query processing. Queries processed through Mimir produce uncertainty-annotated result cursors that allow client applications to quickly assess result quality and provenance. We also present a GUI that provides analysts with an interactive tool for exploring the uncertainty exposed by the system. Finally, we present optimizations that make Lenses scalable, and validate this claim through experimental evidence.

Using visual data such as images or videos to discern if someone has interacted with an object or surface presents considerable challenges. We propose detecting interactions between stationary objects and surfaces by employing projections from dual vantage points and examining their intersections in 2D space—a concept known as cross-view projection consistency. In this paper, using the stochastic geometry theory, we present a framework for analyzing the performance of device-to-device (D2D) communications underlaid uplink (UL) cellular networks. In our analysis, we consider all L1 and L3 communication modes in the optical network pilot system as well as using time-frequency modulation algorithms to analyze the values of the L1 and L3 lome signals for each mode. We find that the power of the L1 and L3 modes is proportional to frequency used by the L1 and L3 modes compared with the time-frequency modulation algorithm. The power distribution of the L1 and L3 modes depend on the distance between L1 and L3 status codes. The relationships between L1 and L3 status codes are explained in terms of: (i) power distribution coefficient (Pc), (ii) polarization state (ppp), and (iii) phase stability (step Pst). Our results show that the time-frequency modulation algorithms can be applied across several modes in order to characterize the relationship between power and energy distribution coefficients. Moreover, they do not require special effects, since their use provides no additional information about the mode-destroying effect caused by the short wavelength propagation delays associated with the radio transmission modes.

In 200 BC, the nomadic Xiongnu group triumphed over the Han dynasty, compelling the latter to become subordinate partners while still perpetrating border incursions. Under the rule of Emperor Wu from 141 to 87 BC, multiple military offensives were initiated against the Xiongnu. Eventually, the Han achieved definitive success in these conflicts, leading to the Xiongnu accepting a subservient role as Han tribute states. This expansion facilitated the growth of Han authority into Central Asia's Tarim Basin, segmented the Xiongnu into dual factions, and contributed significantly to the establishment of the expansive Silk Road trading route that stretched up to the Mediterranean region. Moreover, regions beyond Han territory fell under the control of the nomadic Xianbei alliance. Additionally, Emperor Wu conducted fruitful military endeavors towards the southern direction, incorporating Nanyue in 109 BC and Dian in 111 BC, along with setting up the Xuantu and Lelang commanderies within the Korean Peninsula in 108 BC.

A collection of probabilistic forecasts achieves good calibration when predicted occurrences at a given probability 'p' manifest approximately 'p' times over time. Such accurate predictions hold significant value in decision analysis utilizing machine learning models. In this study, we introduce two novel non-parametric techniques aimed at refining the output of binary classifiers: one leveraging the Bayes optimal choice and another employing Bayesian model integration. These approaches boast independence from the underlying algorithmic learning process, allowing them to function as post-hoc adjustments regardless of the original model type. Their versatility extends across numerous machine learning frameworks. Both these methods, along with others, underwent evaluation using diverse datasets to assess their efficacy in both accuracy and calibration metrics. Findings indicate that these newly proposed techniques perform equally or even surpass existing leading calibration strategies.

Prior to the assault on Pearl Harbor, the sizable America First Committee with its 800,000 members strongly resisted any involvement by the US in the European war, despite providing military assistance to Britain and the USSR via the Lend-Lease initiative. However, the sentiment towards war shifted dramatically within the US post-attack. Following the events at Pearl Harbor, the US along with the UK, Canada, and the Netherlands, officially entered WWII against Japan on 8th December, with China and Australia joining shortly thereafter. Subsequently, just four days later, Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy also declared war on the US, plunging them into an extensive two-front battle. Many historians consider this move a significant strategic error because it negated the advantage that Germany derived from diverting the attention of the US away from Europe – a scenario foreseen several months earlier by Commander Arthur McCollum in his memorandum [note 12]. Additionally, it led to reduced support for Britain, something both Congress and Hitler had skillfully avoided throughout a year filled with provocations.

The larger the fan, the higher the thrust at the same RPM (rotation speed). The slower the fan spins, the quieter it is. So a larger fan that spins slower would produce the same power as a smaller one that spins faster. Efficiency of the engine also depends on the size of the fan compared to the size of the core (known as bypass ratio), since the fan is more efficient as a propulsion at airliner cruise speed that the jet exhaust.', "The jet engine compresses the air, inject fuels, compresses mixture, ignites it and exhausts the gas at an accelerated speed through an exit nozzle. Cell nuclei segmentation is one of the most important tasks in the analysis of biomedical images. With ever-growing sizes and amounts of three-dimensional images to be processed, there is a need for better and faster segmentation methods. Graph-based image segmentation has seen a rise in popularity in recent years, but is seen as very costly with regard to computational demand. We propose a new segmentation algorithm which overcomes these limitations. Our method uses recursive balanced graph partitioning to segment foreground components of a fast and efficient binarization. We construct a model for the cell nuclei to guide the partitioning process. Our algorithm is compared to other state-of-the-art segmentation algorithms in an experimental evaluation on two sets of realistically simulated inputs. Our method is faster, has similar or better quality and an acceptable memory overhead.

Synthetic crude oil, also known as syncrude, is the output from a bitumen upgrader facility used in connection with oil sand production in Canada. Bituminous sands are mined using enormous (100 ton capacity) power shovels and loaded into even larger (400 ton capacity) dump trucks for movement to an upgrading facility. The process used to extract the bitumen from the sand is a hot water process originally developed by Dr. Karl Clark of the University of Alberta during the 1920s. After extraction from the sand, the bitumen is fed into a bitumen upgrader which converts it into a light crude oil equivalent. This synthetic substance is fluid enough to be transferred through conventional oil pipelines and can be fed into conventional oil refineries without any further treatment. By 2015 Canadian bitumen upgraders were producing over 1 million barrels (160103 m3) per day of synthetic crude oil, of which 75 was exported to oil refineries in the United States.

The Amoy dialect (Xiamen) is a hybrid of the Quanzhou and Zhangzhou dialects. Taiwanese is also a hybrid of these two dialects. Taiwanese in northern Taiwan tends to be based on the Quanzhou variety, whereas the Taiwanese spoken in southern Taiwan tends to be based on Zhangzhou speech. There are minor variations in pronunciation and vocabulary between Quanzhou and Zhangzhou dialects. The grammar is generally the same. Additionally, extensive contact with the Japanese language has left a legacy of Japanese loanwords in Taiwanese Hokkien. On the other hand, the variants spoken in Singapore and Malaysia have a substantial number of loanwords from Malay and to a lesser extent, from English and other Chinese varieties, such as the closely related Teochew and some Cantonese.

A high-quality temporal-state quantized symbolic representation of a previously quantized control system must meet three criteria: closeness, validity, and comprehensiveness. Current methods for symbolic representation of unstable systems only achieve closeness and validity, leaving out comprehensiveness. System instability poses challenges in developing entirely comprehensive temporal-state quantized symbolic representations for bounded and quantized inputs from unstable systems, even when employing supervisory feedback mechanisms. Hence, in this study, we propose a method of defining the degree of completeness within the symbolic model via the essential concept of "Trimmed-Input Approximate Bisimulation," as discussed in our work. This degree is determined by a variable known as the "trimming" factor associated with the set of input paths. Furthermore, we present a technique for creating nearly complete, valid, and close temporal-state quantized symbolic models that align closely with time quantized models.

Using self-consistent field theory (SCFT) in spherical unit cells of various dimensionalities, D , a phase diagram of a diblock, A -b- B , is calculated in 5 dimensional space, d 5. This is an extension of a previuos work for d 4. The phase diagram is parameterized by the chain composition, f , and incompatibility between A and B , quantified by the product N . We predict 5 stable nanophases: layers, cylinders, 3 D spherical cells, 4 D spherical cells, and 5 D spherical cells. In the strong segregation limit, that is for large N , the order-order transition compositions are determined by the strong segregation theory (SST) in its simplest form. While the predictions of the SST theory are close to the corresponding SCFT extrapolations for d 4 , the extrapolations for d 5 significantly differ from them. This article describes a vulnerability within iCloud Sharing and Safari 15 that allowed hackers to gain unauthorized camera access on Macs. It details how the vulnerability was discovered and how users can protect themselves from this type of attack. In September 2020, a new vulnerability was discovered in iCloud Sharing and Safari 15 that allowed hackers to gain unauthorized camera access on Macs. The vulnerability, which is present in both macOS 10.15.5 and earlier versions, was discovered by researchers at Google's Project Zero. It allows an attacker to remotely take control of a victim's webcam and microphone without their knowledge or consent. The researchers found that the vulnerability could be exploited by creating a malicious website that uses a specially crafted iFrame to load content from an iCloud-shared photo album. When the victim visits the website, the iFrame loads the shared photo album and automatically starts playing the video. The video is then recorded by the attacker's website and streamed back to the attacker. The researchers have not released any details about how the vulnerability can be exploited, but they say that it can be used to spy on victims and steal sensitive information. They also warn that the vulnerability could be used to launch more sophisticated attacks, such as ransomware. Apple has patched the vulnerability in macOS 10.15.6 and later versions. However, older versions of macOS are still vulnerable. Users of older versions can protect themselves by disabling iCloud Sharing or by using a web browser other than Safari.

Life is good and all, but to me, death is more interesting. Every time something died, she would always be there in the shadows, a girl in a black cloak covering her whole body. As a child, I always wondered who she was and why no one else saw her. I only saw her for brief moments, but she captured my fascination. I wondered who she was and why I would see her everywhere. I was only interested in who she was until the day I survived the start of the war and spoke to her for the first time. I was only 12 when the war began. I was riding the bus back home from school when it happened. I had barely survived by being cushioned with the bodies of others on the bus when the bombing began. I lost consciousness for several minutes and woke up among the bodies and surrounded by burning vehicles. Miraculously, I was only slightly burned with cuts and bruises all over my body although I hadn't gotten any serious injuries. However, I knew it wasn't safe there so I struggled to get out of the bodies. I had just left the broken bus when I saw her in the middle of the road, uninjured and just blankly watching the world burn. "Hey! Get out of there! Those planes might come back and the cars will probably blow up soon with all this fire!" I shouted to her. She merely looked at me and pointed to herself wondering if I was talking to her. "Yes, you! Why are you just standing there watching? It isn't safe to be here!" She walked to me slowly as if unsure of what was happening until she was right in front of me. "Can you see me?" "Of course I can. I've been wondering why you show up everywhere, but we really should move to somewhere else." I grabbed her hand and pulled her along with me before she could say anything else. We needed to get to a bunker soon before talking. Nowadays, every city had bunkers in case of bombings as people grew fearful of the wars they saw on the news. I searched for the signs leading to the nearest fallout shelter and followed them to a parking garage. It was a sturdy building so it had survived the bombs. We went to the entrance of the shelter where we could hear people talking deeper inside. "Let's get inside before things get any worse, the shelter should be safe." "No. I have to go do my job. This is the first time someone so healthy has been able to see me though... I think I'll speak to you later." She looked solemn as she knocked loudly on the door. As she spoke, she raised her hand in front of my face and the last thing I heard was her voice. "Just stay in the hospital when you wake up. I'll find you later."

Automatic charge prediction aims to predict appropriate final charges according to the fact descriptions for a given criminal case. Automatic charge prediction plays a critical role in assisting judges and prosecutors as they plan sentencing procedures, and it is also used by defense counsels when making motions asking for new trials or plea deals. The main purpose of automatic charge prediction is to assist a judge with deciding what is necessary for an offender's sentence based on various factual circumstances such as prior convictions and associated behavior (e.g., drug use). Therefore, accurate charging decisions depend upon proper knowledge about an individual and hisher history, which often cannot be known until heshe enters prison. This information can only come from obtaining records from jail registries, court-ordered evaluations, parole hearings, etc. Due to large amounts of data, it is very difficult for courts and lawyers to sift through all this material and identify relevant facts that would help them make good decisions regarding the disposition of each defendant during the course of their trial. Consequently, many offenders end up being convicted even though no evidence exists to prove their guilt. In practice, therefore, automatic charge predictions are not efficient at predicting future sentences due to its inability to account for some important aspects of a person's past. For example, it may be impossible to accurately determine whether an offender has been involved in any other crimes since entering prison (even if one were possible), while the criminal record itself implies little accuracy because offenders sometimes do commit additional offenses after serving time. Moreover, the justice system does not typically provide enough information concerning a particular individual in order to correctly assess the risk of recidivism once released into society. Accordingly, there is still room for improvement in automated processing techniques related to sentence determinations.

It was called " The Ark Project ." At least, that was the name that the news and social media had come up with, once they'd stuck their collective noses into the affairs of the World Government. The World Government - an evolution of the now defunct U.N. - wasn't really the world government, of course. Everyone knew that. While there were some countries that weren't around anymore - and almost all of them because they'd been either absorbed by larger countries, or had merged to become newer countries - there were still more than a dozen's dozen still around, and they were all still independent, sovereign nations. What the World Government was, was something akin to the world equivalent of what had once been the Congress in the United States, before its citizens, finally fed up with the political corruption that had run so rampant that it was openly talked about, even in the news media, had all but revolted, refusing to support their congressional appointees, and calling for its abolishment. Not that the media had cared at all about that tidbit of history. They were much more interested in the particulars of the Ark Project, and in trying to figure out just why it was that the World Government had been so secretive about it. To the media, secrets were meant to be exposed, especially if they were government secrets, and since they were World Government secrets, the media believed that there shouldn't be any secrets they weren't privy to. It didn't take too long before the major outlines of the Ark Project were brought to light; it wasn't a huge secret that prison over-crowding was becoming a problem the world ' round, that many of the prisons - even the low security ones - were seriously overcrowded, in some cases so much so that the prisoners slept in shifts, so that it could be said that each prisoner had a bed to sleep in. The Ark Project, the media managed to uncover, was an idea conceived during a number of meetings of the World Government, in order to discuss, and then come up with a solution, to the world's prison overcrowding situation. The solution, the outline identified, was two-fold: the first was to find a way to make productive assets of the prisoners, rather than keep them contained in prisons in almost inhumane conditions, and the second was to use the volunteer prisoners in a colonization project. There had been a few manned trips to Mars already, and there were still few moons orbiting Saturn and Jupiter that were candidates for remote stations to be put together, and so it was decided that the volunteer prisoners would be the ' test subjects'to build those stations. The news was met with a considerable amount of positive fanfare. Once the news of the Ark Project was leaked, the project - now unfettered - seemed to proceed at an almost frenetic pace, and inside of a year the last of the first wave of volunteer prisoners - totaling nearly a hundred thousand from just about every corner of the world - had been put into cryogenic sleep and shuttled up into high earth orbit to wait for the space engines, as they were known, to fire up and take the cargo pods on their way to their destinations. Briefly, it was wondered, ' why so many prisoner volunteers? ', but the matter had been explained away that the building of the remote space stations would take a considerable amount of time and there was no way to replace someone who was accidentally injured or killed. The truth of the matter - that the prisoners weren't really going to Jupiter- or Saturn- to build remote space stations - and that they were actually simply being fired off into the sun - wouldn't be discovered for nearly another century...

In this work we focus on the problem of colorization for image compression. Since color information occupies a large proportion of the total storage size of an image, a method that preserves color when compressing a compressed image is desirable. Color information can be preserved by several methods including discrete cosine transform (DCT), frequency-domain color separation, and multi-dimensional convolutional coding. One possible technique to preserve color using DCT is to use RGB as an input pixel value, then transform it into a subtractive or additive matrix representation with subsampling called scalar quantization (SQ). To perform inverse DCT or similar operations, the original RGB values must first be transformed in the opposite direction: from subspace to space. This operation requires complex hardware and requires controlling the number of samples. To obtain good results by making the sample rate equal to the data transfer rate, therefore, scalars are typically used at both ends of the transformation process. Scalars represent the original pixels, which are normalized relative to each other based on their color settings. However, scalars have disadvantages such as loss of detail since they are normalized to zero; they also cannot be easily made uniform across every pixel because they do not necessarily correspond directly from one pixel to another. For example, scalar scaling often causes artifacts due to aliasing effects associated with various types of scaling techniques that depend upon the spatial indexing schemes employed. Another disadvantage of scalars relates to the fact that they tend to introduce distortion since dimensions between neighboring scalars change depending on what scale factor is utilized. Finally, scalar quantizing involves significant processing overhead, especially where the amount of data being compressed is relatively small.

Most Huguenots were men who had left their families in France to make new lives for themselves. The Huguenots settled in the Cape Colony, the so-called Cape of Good Hope, and were later joined by others. They created farms and industries, and worked in commerce, medicine, and as teachers. In 1692, they established the first French Reformed Church in the Cape Colony. Huguenots in South Africa established a new colony, Franschhoek, which still bears the name today. The Huguenots who settled in Franschhoek and the Drakenstein Valley in the mid-1700s were successful farmers and viticulturists. Many clustering algorithms exist that estimate a cluster centroid, such as K -means, K -medoids or mean-shift, but no algorithm seems to exist that clusters data by returning exactly K nodes. K -centroids are found in many popular machine learning methods and they may be used for both supervised (scalable) and unsupervised (adaptive). In this talk we demonstrate how these types of algorithms can be directly applied to the problem of finding optimal path lengths between computers using classical computing techniques like linear programming. We will use examples from working with Algorithmic Optimization of Bluetooth HCI Environments to find an optimal number of hops among several Bluetooth devices without requiring any extra knowledge about network topology, routing protocols etc., which is not necessarily available on each individual node. The advantage of our approach over existing approaches lies mainly in being able to find one central point more quickly than other known methodologies; another important factor is that it does not require any additional specialized hardware, unlike some others out there.

Motion planning for autonomous vehicles requires spatio-temporal motion plans (i.e. state trajectories) to account for dynamic obstacles. This requires a trajectory tracking control process which faithfully tracks planned trajectories. In this paper, a control scheme is presented which first optimizes a planned trajectory and then tracks the optimized trajectory using a feedback-feedforward controller. The feedforward element is calculated in a model predictive manner with a cost function focusing on driving performance. Stability of the error dynamic is then guaranteed by the design of the feedback-feedforward controller. The tracking performance of the control system is tested in a realistic simulated scenario where the control system must track an evasive lateral maneuver. The proposed controller performs well in simulation and can be easily adapted to different dynamic vehicle models. The uniqueness of the solution to the control synthesis eliminates any nondeterminism that could arise with switching between numerical solvers for the underlying mathematical program.

No longer would he be the butt of jokes at his office, being known simply as "Lonesome Jack." He was going to make a name for himself, and take down everybody who lacked belief in him; all those that had stepped on him. His coworkers, boss, ex girlfriends, parents, everybody, would feel his wrath and be forced to take him seriously from this moment on. As Jack cruised across the silent, melancholy streets of downtown, he watched as civilians, potential witnesses ran for cover under haunting facades of hotels, shops, restaurants, a reminder of the history that still lived in this city. He quickly came to the realization that he would need a weapon, but simply walking into a gun shop and buying a gun would be too suspicious. So he came to the conclusion that he would hunt for them as an animal would, simply with his bare hands. The growling engine of the Mustang fell to a silent conclusion as Jack stopped the car and opened his door slightly, as if to let the cold air into the furnace of hate that was contained in the cabin of his vehicle. He looked up at the cement tower that lay before him; "The Roosevelt." Specifically, the residence of his boss, the one who made him an exile at the office, who declined any attempt at him moving up in the business; the one who stole his fiance from under him. As he jogged into the Art Deco themed lobby of the hotel, he found the elevator opened, as if giving him an invitation to fulfill his prophecy. The numbers on the golden wall read "1..... 2..... 3..." all the way until it stopped at "25...." The doors creaked to an open position and he found himself alone, in complete silence upon the crimson carpet of the penthouse. Jack paced towards room 1990, the "President's Suite." To his surprise, the door lay open as well, a small crack of light escaped into the candle lit hallway. Taking this as further proof of his divine right of vengeance, Jack lust forward into the room, throwing the door open with ferocious might and made two large bounds right into the suite's master bedroom. As he thrust the two ancient oak doors of the room open, he witnessed his fiance holding a knife to his bosses throat, as well as three bags filled to the brim with unmarked bills, gold china, and other priceless objects near the window to the balcony and ultimately, the fire escape. In moments that seemed to live in complete slow motion, Jack analyzed each detail of the event as if he were the late Sherlock Holmes himself, tracking down precisely what was happening. As the two struggled in death's embrace, Jack jumped over the side of the immaculate drapes lining the bed and threw the woman to the ground, where she found herself soon swimming in a pool of crimson. The knife lay, 4 inches deep in her chest, where she had fallen. In complete shock, his fiance, whom he had nothing but anger up until now for, looked at him in the eyes and whispered "thank you" as she faded into an everlasting slumber. And in this moment, Jack realized, as he looked at the knife lying on the floor, the faint words "Phantom" etched on the hilt, that his fiance, who would often be gone late nights into the early morning hours was working for the mob, specifically the "Phantom Mob." This group of barbarians were feared throughout the entire bay area, and to his complete dismay, his own fiance was a member. In complete disgust he turned away. Jack's shoulders heaved up and down in animalistic spirit as he struggled to catch his breath. As he slowly looked up, fiery cauldrons of lava glowing in his eyes, he met gaze with his boss. The man lie complete fear, not even the slightest whimper escaping his pale white face His boss, who was nothing more than an angry man in a business suit had come to realize that his life had just been saved, as this woman's mission was to end his life, and take all that he had. With shorter frame lengths commonly used in Ultra-Reliable Low-Latency and massive Machine Type Communications, there's a balance needed between enhancing frame synchronization (FS) performance and boosting information throughput. This study focuses on constant transmission across Additive White Gaussian Noise (AWGN) channels with the synchronization sequence integrated within the data symbols instead of appending it as a separate frame header. Integrating the sequence allows for a synchronization length equal to the frame length; however, its power must be carefully managed to avoid compromising the code quality. Initially, we analyze the FS error probability by approximating the entire signal's received probability distribution. Subsequard numerical assessments demonstrate the accuracy of our analytical findings. Following this, we determine the optimal power division between the superimposed synchronization sequence and data symbols to maximize both successful frame reception and accurate decoding. Comparisons of our theoretical models against actual implementations reveal remarkably similar optimal power distribution strategies.

The Count-Min sketch is an important and well-studied data summarization method. It allows one to estimate the count of any item in a stream using a small, fixed size data sketch. However, the accuracy of the sketch depends on characteristics of the underlying data. This has led to a number of count estimation procedures which work well in one scenario but perform poorly in others. A practitioner is faced with two basic, unanswered questions. Which variant should be chosen when the data is unknown? Given an estimate, is its error sufficiently small to be trustworthy? We provide answers to these questions. We derive new count estimators, including a provably optimal estimator, which best or match previous estimators in all scenarios. We also provide practical, tight error bounds at query time for both new and existing estimators. These error estimates also yield procedures to choose the sketch tuning parameters optimally, as they can extrapolate the error to different choices of sketch width and depth. The key observation is that the distribution of errors in each counter can be empirically estimated from the sketch itself. By first estimating this distribution, count estimation becomes a statistical estimation and inference problem with a known error distribution. This provides both a principled way to derive new and optimal estimators as well as a way to study the error and properties of existing estimators.

The intricacies of sleep remain somewhat mysterious, despite identifying five distinct stages known as I, II, III, IV, and REM. During REM sleep, brain activity closely mirrors that of wakefulness. Regarding energy levels, an individual doesn't experience deficiency unless they exhibit severe symptoms; rather, energy is acquired from food intake and gradually consumed throughout the day while maintaining reserve stores. It's plausible that sleep serves as a period for the brain to eliminate accumulated metabolic waste and perform maintenance functions, similar to tidying up a restaurant at the end of a busy day.

On 15th September 187right, the inauguration of Galicia's initial railway track took place, stretching between O Carril, near Vilagarcia de Arousa, and Cornes in Conxo, heading towards Santiago de Compostela. Following this, a new line was established in 1875, linking A Coruna with Lugo. By 1883, Galicia had its maiden connection to the Spanish mainland via rail through O Barco de Valdeorras. Presently, there exists approximately 1,100 kilometers (680 miles) of train tracks within Galicia. Key cities throughout Galicia are interconnected by standard Iberian gauge (1,668 mm or 5 ft 5 2132 inches), managed by Adif and Renfe Operadora. A separate meter-gauge line (1,000 mm or 3 ft 3 38 inches), run by FEVE, links Ferrol to Ribadeo and Oviedo. As for electricity, solely the line extending from Ponferrada to Monforte de Lemos, then onto Ourense and finally reaching Vigo, is equipped with it. High-speed rail projects are also ongoing, including the partial opening of the Olmedo-Zamora-Galicia line in 2011 as well as plans for an AVE Atlantic Axis route serving significant Galician Atlantic coastal cities such as A Coruna, Santiago de Compostela, Pontevedra, and Vigo. Additionally, a proposed AVE line would create a link between Ourense, Pontevedra, and Vigo.

Galicia is poetically known as the "country of the thousand rivers" o pais dos mil rios. The largest and most important of these rivers is the Minho, known as O Pai Mino (Father Minho), 307.5 km (191.1 mi) long and discharging 419 m3 (548 cu yd) per second, with its affluent the Sil, which has created a spectacular canyon. Most of the rivers in the inland are tributaries of this fluvial system, which drains some 17,027 km2 (6,574 sq mi). Other rivers run directly into the Atlantic Ocean as Lerez or the Cantabrian Sea, most of them having short courses. Only the Navia, Ulla, Tambre, and Limia have courses longer than 100 km (62 mi).

In this paper, we study the performance of a TCP connection over cognitive radio networks. In these networks, the network may not always be available for transmission. Also, the packets can be lost due to wireless channel impairments. We evaluate the throughput and packet retransmission timeout probability of a secondary TCP connection over an ONOFF channel. We first assume that the ON and OFF time durations are exponential and later extend it to more general distributions. We then consider multiple TCP connections over the ONOFF channel. We validate our theoretical models and the approximations made therein via ns2 simulations.

Contemporary studies focusing on reinforcement learning within pure-conflict and pure-interest games underscore the significance of varied agent characteristics within the population. On the other hand, investigations into reinforcement learning for mixed-motive games have mostly utilized uniform methodologies. Recognizing the hallmark trait of mixed-motive games —the incomplete alignment of objectives amongst participants—our research examines how diverse populations impact reinforcement learning outcomes. Leveraging concepts from social psychology's interdependence theory, we integrate an adaptable framework of preferences regarding group outcomes known as Social Value Orientation (SVO) into reinforcement learning algorithms. Subsequently, we analyze the influence of varying SVO traits across different groups using two distinct mixed-motive Markov games. Our findings reveal that disparate SVO levels result in substantial and intricate differences in agent behaviors, aligning with predictions made by interdependence theory. Moreover, empirical evidence indicates that agents nurtured within diverse environments exhibit superior, more versatile strategies compared to their counterparts raised in uniform settings.

Invisible Edinburgh seeks to showcase an alternative aspect of Scotland's capital through their unique tours. Beginning at locations such as the Grassmarket, Castle Terrace, and Middle Meadow Walk, these experiences come with distinctive themes that reflect the personal expertise of each tour leader. Financial support for this initiative comes from the Edinburgh Airport Community Fund. Among the various topics explored during the tours are influential women in Edinburgh, local criminal history, sports within the community, and culinary philanthropy. Zakia Moulaoui, aged 28, who hails from France, founded this endeavor inspired by similar projects she encountered in Greece involving itinerant merchants conducting walking excursions. Speaking to the BBC Scotland news outlet, she mentioned plans to expand her team of guides later in September. Each tour incorporates elements from the life of its guide, such as sharing amusing tales related to historical sites or personal encounters. Participants can expect a blend of traditional and contemporary narratives, like learning about both Maggie Dickson and J.K. Rowling in one session. These tours are available every Saturday, with ticket purchases required via the internet, priced at £8 per person.

Infection begins when an organism successfully enters the body, grows and multiplies. This is referred to as colonization. Most humans are not easily infected. Those who are weak, sick, malnourished, have cancer or are diabetic have increased susceptibility to chronic or persistent infections. Individuals who have a suppressed immune system are particularly susceptible to opportunistic infections. Entrance to the host at host-pathogen interface, generally occurs through the mucosa in orifices like the oral cavity, nose, eyes, genitalia, anus, or the microbe can enter through open wounds. While a few organisms can grow at the initial site of entry, many migrate and cause systemic infection in different organs. Some pathogens grow within the host cells (intracellular) whereas others grow freely in bodily fluids.

Ross County captain Andrew Davies headed the visitors level, only for Kevin Gomis to put Dundee back in front with a header. And County were denied by the woodwork twice in injury time, with Jason Naismith coming closest with a fine effort from distance. "It was a great spectacle," said Dundee manager Paul Hartley. We could have scored more goals, especially after going 2-0 up." Ross County co-manager Stuart Kettlewell was left ruing missed chances for his team, who are now unbeaten in their last four games. "We knew that Dundee would be a good side," he said. "They're a very strong group and they've got some top players. "But I thought we were excellent, we took our chances when they came along and had some good opportunities to get back into the game. "We probably should have had a point on another day." Dundee started sharply and went ahead inside two minutes when Greg Stewart's excellent pass found Gomis, who turned his man and crossed for Hemmings to tap home. The home side doubled their advantage within seven minutes. Former Aberdeen winger Stewart found space down the right hand side and picked out Gomis, who headed home from six yards. Ross County hit back immediately through Davies, whose powerful header from Rory McAllister's free-kick flew past Scott Bain in the Dundee goal. The visitors then had the ball in the net for a second time, but this time Michael Gardyne's header from Craig Curran's cross was ruled out for offside. Gomis had a chance to restore Dundee's two-goal advantage when his powerful header from El-Hadji Diouf's cross bounced back off the post. County then levelled the match on the half-hour mark when Boyce glanced McAllister's corner beyond Bain. But the home side retook the lead nine minutes later when Hemmings fired home from the spot after Sean Kelly had been adjudged to have handled in the box. Just before the break, Gomis completed his brace with a simple header from Hemmings' cross. County pulled one back within two minutes of the restart when Boyce slotted home from 10 yards after good work from Martin Woods. And the visitors were inches away from an equaliser when McAllister's shot from 18 yards took a deflection off Genseric Kusunga and flashed just wide of the post. Dundee were looking dangerous on the counter and substitute Faissal El Bakhtaoui almost added a fifth when his low drive from 20 yards forced Scott Fox into a smart save. County also pressed for an equaliser and Curran narrowly missed the target with a dipping volley from 25 yards. But Dundee held on to claim all three points and move into fourth place in the Scottish Premiership table.

Using measurements from an infrared telescope in Hawaii, a UK and US team found evidence for temperatures as high as 1,500C - hundreds of degrees warmer than anywhere else on the planet. They suggest the hotspot is created by thunderous soundwaves "breaking" in the thin upper reaches of the atmosphere. The research is published in Nature. It arguably solves what planetary scientists had dubbed an "energy crisis" for gas giants like Jupiter: temperatures in their upper atmospheres soar much higher than can be explained by solar energy - especially given their vast distances from the Sun. If the mysterious heat were generated by local sources, like Jupiter's famous storm, then the conundrum would be solved - and these measurements are the first direct evidence of any such activity. Study co-author Dr Tom Stallard, from the University of Leicester, said this was a major step forward in a "20-30 year odyssey" to try and understand heat flow on Jupiter. "Ever since Voyager, we've had measurements of the temperature at the top of Jupiter's atmosphere, and it's been hot across the whole globe - from the poles, all the way to the equator," he told the BBC. Jupiter's enormous, dramatic aurora can explain the heat in the polar regions, but for that warmth to reach the equator would require incredibly dramatic mixing, which modelling studies haven't been able to support. "There's no real excuse for it to be so hot," said Dr James O'Donoghue from Boston University, the paper's first author. The freshly discovered spike in temperature, detected using a spectrometer at the Nasa Infrared Telescope Facility (IRTF) in Mauna Kea, Hawaii, offers a solution. Several hundred km directly above the clouds of the Great Red Spot, the hotspot suggests that high-altitude heat is somehow created by the turmoil beneath. "Several people have argued that it's likely that the heat comes from below, but the observations have never backed them up," Dr Stallard said. He and his colleagues don't know exactly what is causing the heat, but they have some ideas. It could be driven by great Jovian thunderclaps, rumbling upwards from the churning red clouds of the Solar System's biggest storm. "You get some kind of acoustic event, probably thunder or something like that - or possibly other forms of sound energy - and that propagates directly upwards," Dr Stallard explained. "That wave will continue going upwards until it reaches a lower-density region at the top of the atmosphere, and then it breaks and deposits all that wave energy into the top of the atmosphere, just like waves break on the shore - as the water gets thinner, it's less able to carry that wave and so it breaks and you see lots of energy." There is a precedent for such sound-driven warming much closer to home, according to Dr O'Donoghue. "There is some evidence in Earth's atmosphere, above storms and above features such as mountains - the Andes mountains in fact - that there are acoustic waves emanating from them, and that they propagate up into the atmosphere and cause heating there," he said. The key to revealing the temperature spike was a tiny ion: H3, a hydrogen molecule (H2) with an added proton. It is incredibly reactive and consequently, short-lived and rare on Earth. But in the sparse fringe of Jupiter's outer atmosphere there is almost nothing else for it to react with. Crucially, this ion works like a glowing, long-range thermometer for scientists, if they have the right sort of telescope - such as the spectrometer at the IRTF, which gathered the relevant data in a single nine-hour window back in 2012. "Just by measuring its light, you can find out the temperature wherever it is," said Dr O'Donoghue. "And it's throughout all of the gas giant upper atmospheres - so it's essentially an in situ temperature probe." Further insights might come from Nasa's Juno spacecraft, now in orbit around Jupiter after its five-year trek. Dr Stallard said that telescopes around the world were trained on the gas giant to take parallel measurements - and his team had planned their observations with the mission in mind. "We thought, this is something that we haven't addressed, and it needed addressing. We've really ramped up our studies away from the aurora. "Juno's going to reveal magnificent levels of detail about.... what the aurora are and how they're generated. But it will be interesting to see how much it tells us about the non-auroral regions and the top of the atmosphere. "Obviously it's been designed to look deep, and to look at the aurora at the poles, but potentially Juno could reveal a lot more." Follow Jonathan on Twitter

There exists an observable imbalance in causality when examining a situation involving a person's hand accidentally knocking over a glass of water onto a solid surface, causing it to shatter and spill. In this scenario, the factors contribsin the final arrangement of broken glass and spilled water - like the glass's pathway, its imperfections, and the angle at which it collides with the ground - can all be logically linked. Yet, if we were to consider the exact opposite sequence, explaining how each fragment could magically return to the hand and reformulate into the original cup shape, or how the water would neatly settle back inside the cup, becomes challenging. Attributing the specific formation and containment of the cup and water to either the hand or the floor proves to be complex since these entities lack the ability to produce such outcomes. Visual Place Recognition (VPR) is the ability to correctly recall a previously visited place under changing viewpoints and appearances. A large number of handcrafted and deep-learning-based VPR techniques exist, where the former approach mostly considers VPR as a retrieval problem, while the latter approaches consider it as a learning problem [orlando2016deep]. In the latter case, the challenge is to learn discriminative features for representing places in an end-to-end fashion. Recently, several deep learning-based methods have been proposed for VPR. Most of them rely on a pre-trained CNN model for a fixed-size image input, and then learn the representations for places from scratch using Variational Auto-Encoders (VAEs) [kingma2013auto]. While the VAE model is a powerful tool to learn the latent representations, it is a sequential model, which limits its scalability. Moreover, the input image is required to be of a fixed size, and the output representation is fixed as well, which may not be suitable for different domains. Recently, Chen et al. [chen2017places] proposed a Hierarchical Convolutional Neural Network (HCNet) model for VPR, which learns place representations in an end-to-end fashion. However, HCNet uses hand-crafted features for building a fixed-size input and a fixed-size output, which are not suitable for different domains. A hybrid VAE-CNN model is proposed by Liu et al. [liu2017places], which can obtain more discriminative place representations than the VAE-based model, but the complexity of this model is high. In this paper, we propose a CNN-based model, named Variational Recurrent Network (VRN), to learn place representations in an end-to-end fashion. The main contributions of this paper are as follows: 1. We propose a novel CNN-based model, VRN, to learn place representations in an end-to-end fashion. This model consists of a Variational Recurrent Network (VRN) module, which uses a Variational Recurrent Recurrent Neural Network (VRRNN) to learn place representations. 2. We formulate the VPR problem as a reinforcement learning (RL) problem. The place representations of VRN are learned as the value function of the RL model. 3. We use a deep Q-learning algorithm to learn the place representations of VRN. 4. We propose a learning-to-learn model, which consists of a VAE and a CNN, to learn place representations. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed model on two real-world datasets. Related Work There has been a large number of handcrafted and deep-learning-based VPR methods proposed, where the former approach mostly considers VPR as a retrieval problem, while the latter approaches consider it as a learning problem [orlando2016deep]. Handcrafted methods Most handcrafted methods use a single CNN to extract feature representations of places [orlando2016deep]. For instance, Xu et al. [xu2016places] proposed a CNN model to learn place representations, and they use a fully-connected layer to obtain the place representations. These handcrafted methods usually use the hand-crafted features, such as HOG [dalal2005histograms], LBP [lowe2004distinctive], and SIFT [lowe2004distinctive], to represent places. However, these hand-crafted features are usually not suitable for different domains. Recently, Chen et al. [chen2017places] proposed a Hierarchical Convolutional Neural Network (HCNet) model for VPR, which uses the features extracted from the convolutional layers to represent places. However, the input image is required to be of a fixed size, and the output representation is fixed as well, which may not be suitable for different domains. Deep-learning-based methods A deep-learning-based method can obtain more discriminative place representations than the handcrafted method. A number of deep-learning-based methods have been proposed for VPR. For instance, Liu et al. The abomination is here in front of us. It has happened to one of us." "We can not know that for sure." "But we can know for sure..... if we investigate." The dissenting man frowned and looked into the bedroom once again. The body was still there, unmoving on the bed. At any moment, he expected the body to move..... but it did not. He had to admit, it was strange. "We must take this to the Council," he said finally. "Such a decision is beyond the two of us to make." "Dead? Impossible." "We can not know that for certain. Nothing like this has ever happened to any of us; it is a completely new phenomenon. Until we study what has happened here, we will be at a loss. We have the records with which to check his conditions..." "Absolutely not. Those records were sealed for a reason. And besides, you know the code. We all agreed upon it. We can not investigate. Even the act of observation, if done incorrectly, can change conditions. We must be careful." "If I am correct, none of that matters now. His condition will not change." "And if you are incorrect?" The Great Hall, full of murmurs a second before, grew suddenly quiet. The presiding Head Master of the Council looked upon the witness with sadness in his eyes. "You have been among us for a great time, but you were not here when we decided to become the Observers. You know what happened, but you did not experience it. I was there, those eons ago. I saw it. I experienced it. We can not risk it again. And if this man you bring before us is indeed alive, it would be foul of us to change that." The Great Hall was still silent. Many of the Members nodded their heads slowly in agreement. The witness frowned. "You are correct. I was not there. I did not observe The Great Experiment. But it has been my duty to observe that which we left behind on that planet. And I tell you, this man appears in almost every way to resemble one of their dead." "Almost every way?" "Yes. The bodies of their dead decay very quickly. This man has not decayed at all, despite being unmoving for several years." "Then, indeed, can we not deduce that he must be alive?" "We can not. We do not know what cause death might have upon our bodies." "That is because we do not die." "As far as we know. In all our time, have we not learned that anything is possible? Before we attempted to create life on Earth, we had no concept of death." "This conversation is pointless," the Head Master said with a scowl. "I will not argue with you any longer. This Council's decision is final." The Head Master waved his hand to dismiss the witness. The witness turned to leave, then hesitated. He turned and looked at the Members. They had already turned their attention away from the witness and were murmuring once again. The witness felt a strange emotion gather in his gut: anger. "You have grown weak!" he bellowed. The murmuring stopped. The Head Master looked at him, annoyed. "You have become pathetic. The whole lot of you sit in this Great Hall and deliberate endlessly, always deciding not to act. Well I say that is nonsense." The Head Master leaned forward. "Are you quite done, young man?" "I may be younger than you, but I have lived for several millennia, and I think that is long enough to have some wisdom. In fact, it seems likely to me that living much longer only puts you out of touch. You are all living proof of that." "How dare you...!" "I'm not done yet," the witness interrupted. Indignant murmurs swelled in the Great Hall, but the Members listened. "I was assigned to observe the humans of Earth. It was my job to watch as the abomination we created occurred every day. I have watched it for several thousands of years. The records on The Great Experiment have been sealed, but I have seen enough to know what happened. You attempted to create life, and you were almost successful. Life was indeed created, but so too was death. The humans of Earth life short lives and then pass away. You saw this..... you saw what you had created, and you were appalled. You had not wished to create something so abysmal." The witness paused. The Great Hall was completely silent. Many of the Members looked down in shame. "And things got even worse after you abandoned the Experiment. The humans of Earth do not just die, they sometimes purposely bring death upon one another. They desire the death of each other." The Hall remained silent. The witness looked upon the Members with sadness in his eyes. "But you missed something. When you abandoned the Experiment and left it to me to observe, you did not see the beauty you had created." The eyes of hundreds of Members rose to meet the eyes of the witness. "The humans of Earth lead short lives, it is true. Many of them die violently and without purpose. But I have also seen them learn to deal with death. Indeed, the very fact that they will die one day gives their lives meaning. Look at us. We go on for eons without end. What we do from day to day makes little difference. We have been around for so long, done so much, and seen so many things, that we have even enforced a code upon ourselves to make us..... well, meaningless. Our lives have no meaning. We just sit and observe. Somewhere along the way, we made a mistake and we gave up." The witness smiled as he continued. "The humans of Earth do not give up. They are not perfect, and many of them are actually quite vile. But there is great beauty in the brief nature of their lives. They live with passion. They strive to make change. And they improve remarkably quickly. Do you know they have mastered the beginnings of space flight? They have already landed on several of the celestial bodies in their system. At this rate they may discover us soon. I hope we will have learned something from them by that time." The witness looked down at the body on the table in front of him. "This man has been observing the humans of Earth with me for a long time. He was my friend. But we have become so complacent and slow to react that I didn't even worry when he "slept" for several years. I suppose that if I was not used to seeing death I may have left him for many more years before growing suspicious. Come to think of it, he said something strange to me right before he laid down." The Head Master looked intently at the witness. "What did he tell you?" The witness smiled. "He said that he and I still had a part to play. That we would be so much more than Observers. I think I see what he meant now." The Head Master nodded slowly. "I think I see it too."

Constructing sidewalks can be costly and may not always make sense in locations where foot traffic is minimal," states an Architecture student who is currently enrolled in an American housing history course. During the post-war II period, America experienced a significant transition towards suburban living which affected the necessity for sidewalks. Urban environments typically require more pedestrian pathways due to proximity to various facilities like stores, cinemas, recreational spaces, and others, along with limited parking availability. Additionally, urban residents tend to rely more heavily on public transportation, necessitating accessible paths to transit stops.

In contrast, several factors contributed to the scarcity of sidewalks in suburban neighborhoods:

1. Suburban developments often centered their design around residential properties while assuming automobiles would facilitate easy access to essential services through highways.
2. Private amenities became increasingly popular during this time, rendering communal resources less necessary; families began enjoying private pools, barbecues, and picnics within their own yards rather than visiting public venues.
3. The pervasive influence of car culture solidified in America post-World War II, leading to infrastructural priorities favoring vehicular mobility over pedestrians or mass transit options.
4. Low volumes of pedestrian activity in suburban settings meant that sidewalks weren't seen as crucial – instead, people simply walked alongside roads when desired.

Although human development and urbanization have led to the depletion of natural habitats, some creatures, including the Rhesus macaque, have successfully adjusted to city life. The availability of ample food supplies and lack of predators have caused a significant rise in macaque numbers within cities, resulting in recurring clashes with people. Such densely populated regions experience macaques plundering agricultural produce, consuming avian and reptilian eggs, damaging nests, thereby negatively impacting various organisms within the ecological system. To alleright these detrimental outcomes, sterilization has been introduced as a compassionate and practical method of regulating macaque populations. Sterilization necessitates capturing individual or group members physically; hence, it's crucial to accurately distinguish them. This study presents the Macaque Face Identification (MFID), an innovative, image-based, non-intrusive solution utilizing facial recognition technology to recognize macaque faces for confirmation of sterilization status. Our main achievement involves creating a sturdy facial recognition and verification algorithm specifically tailored for Rhesus macaques while being applicable to other primate species. By testing MFID using a database comprising 93 monkeys through diverse assessment methods, we demonstrate its effectiveness. Additionally, we showcase impressive outcomes by applying our model to critically threatened primate types.

Embedded in the thylakoid membranes are important protein complexes which carry out the light reactions of photosynthesis. Photosystem II and photosystem I contain light-harvesting complexes with chlorophyll and carotenoids that form a network to draw gas molecules from the cell membrane via the channels associated with photosynthetic pathways, such as acidification or oxidizing activity (VPP). Thus, when the formation of these complexes is accomplished by other photoreceptor cells, this is known as microarrays. Typically, at least one photoresist layer containing titanium oxide compounds as well as aliphatic, aromatic, hydrophilic, and alkali metal components is provided on each cell surface for deposition into an appropriate photolithographic process after depositing onto the substrate. The coating can be deposited simultaneously with photomultiplier films of ALT (Aluminum Oxide Film), PMO (Polymerized Aluminium Oxide), or with any suitable polymer or polymeric material prior to coating onto the substrate. For further details concerning the use of CMOS technology in thin film deposition, see F et al., "Optical Coating of Alveolar Films," Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. U.S.A., Vol. 34, No. 5 (1988) and Dr. B Johnson's "Photochemical Polymerization of Alive Cured Alribution," Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA, Vol. 33, No. 4 (1993) pp. 283-283 (which are incorporated herein by reference). These layers, however, do not provide enough plateaus to enable the photochemical synthesis in large volumes sufficient to allow for physical deposition of the layers. Furthermore, these layers have a limited storage capability due to their high melting point. Because of this, it has been difficult to obtain a satisfactory film thickness in order to directly coat photoresists within the desired wavelength range. Further, photoresist layers, comprising higher temperature materials, may require additional processing steps to avoid loss of the underlying layer structure by isolation andor recovery. These limitations, coupled with increased costs, have reduced the ability of the photochemical synthesis necessary to achieve the desired coating properties.

Individuals opt to pay the set amount since they perceive value in doing so; therefore, altering the pricing doesn't seem justified. This decision stems from basic economic principles—supply and demand. A company's net earnings result from multiplying the quantity sold by the unit price. Setting prices excessively high may deter customers, whereas overly low prices might boost sales volume without significantly increasing overall revenue. Consequently, companies aim to find an equilibrium within market dynamics to maximize potential income. 

The relatively affordable nature of certain goods raises questions regarding production costs versus consumer expectations. While it could be assumed that minimal expenses associated with product provision would warrant reduced prices, actual pricing reflects customer willingness to spend more rather than direct correlation to manufacturing costs. Indeed, decreasing the price typically increases sales volumes; however, increased sales do not necessarily equate to elevated profits due to factors such as production and distribution expenditures. Movie producers have effectively capitalized on this concept by establishing multiple pricing tiers based on the timing of content availability. These tiers range from premium-priced theatrical releases to progressively cheaper alternatives available via various media platforms. As movies age, they transition across different channels, enabling audiences to access them at gradually declining rates while continuously generating revenue for the studio throughout its lifecycle.

After much contemplation, the heightened attention on media coverage recently highlighted the concept of resisting arrest for me once again. Currently, "resisting arrest" is considered a serious crime across various US states, although informal reports suggest it is often used to exaggerate minor infractions committed by individuals. It remains a criminal act against the law to oppose an unwarranted arrest; thus, even if you, as a law-abiding citizen, find yourself in a situation where the police have no legitimate basis for your arrest, they can still detain you without any resistance on your part. This legislation negatively impacts our society. From both psychological and physical standpoints, humans naturally react defensively to hostile behavior. Consequently, resisting arrest laws penalize innocent civilians simply for acting according to their inherent reflexes. However, I am not advocating for civilians to resist using lethal or disproportionate force – rather, there must exist some safeguards in place to allow citizens to resist in a measured manner. Although this might not be the ideal terminology or remedy, it stems from someone outside the field of expertise. To further clarify, making resisting arrest illegal serves to shield civilians during apprehension processes. A simple example could involve a police officer grasping your arm and you pulling away, potentially causing the officer to perceive an imminent threat and respond with force such as deploying a Taser, engaging in physical restraint, or mistakenly applying life-ending pressure due to concern over personal safety. The issue at hand extends beyond policies alone and delves into the underlying psychological factors present throughout the arrest process. In conclusion, while I firmly believe that American law enforcement practices contain elements of misconduct, the core issue lies within the personnel and ingrained customs themselves. Despite recognizing the need for increased protections for ordinary citizens, allowing them to resist arrest likely isn't the most effective approach. Instead, perhaps future generations of judges will demonstrate greater understanding toward such cases, signifying another direction altogether. Lastly, one must consider whether challenging an authority figure verbally—such as stating, "You cannot make me leave," upon hearing, "Get back here!"—is truly a course of action anyone would endorse.

In this paper we present various distributed algorithms for LP-type problems in the well-known gossip model. LP-type problems include many important classes of problems such as (integer) linear programming, geometric problems like smallest enclosing ball and polytope distance, and set problems like hitting set and set cover. In the gossip model, a node can only push information to or pull information from nodes chosen uniformly at random. Protocols for the gossip model are usually very practical due to their fast convergence, their simplicity, and their stability under stress and disruptions. Our algorithms are very efficient (logarithmic rounds or better with just polylogarithmic communication work per node per round) whenever the combinatorial dimension of the given LP-type problem is constant, even if the size of the given LP-type problem is polynomially large in the number of nodes.

In this paper, we propose an efficient and reproducible deep learning model for musical onset detection (MOD). We first review the state-of-the-art deep learning models for MOD, and identify their shortcomings and challenges: (i) the lack of hyper-parameter tuning details, (ii) the non-availability of code for training models on other datasets, and (iii) ignoring the network capability when comparing different architectures. Taking the above issues into account, we experiment with seven deep learning architectures. The most efficient one achieves equivalent performance to our implementation of the state-of-the-art architecture. However, it has only 28.3 of the total number of trainable parameters compared to the state-of-the-art. Our experiments are conducted using two different datasets: one mainly consists of instrumental music excerpts, and another developed by ourselves includes only solo singing voice excerpts. Further, inter-dataset transfer learning experiments are conducted. The results show that the model pre-trained on one dataset fails to detect onsets on another dataset, which denotes the importance of providing the implementation code to enable re-training the model for a different dataset. Datasets, code and a Jupyter notebook running on Google Colab are publicly available to make this research understandable and easy to reproduce.

Religious humanism is an integration of humanist ethical philosophy with religious rituals and beliefs that centre on human needs, interests, and abilities. Though practitioners of religious humanism did not officially organise under the name of "humanism" until the late 19th and early 20th centuries, non-theistic religions paired with human-centred ethical philosophy have a long history. The Cult of Reason (French: Culte de la Raison) was a religion based on deism devised during the French Revolution by Jacques Hebert, Pierre Gaspard Chaumette and their supporters. In 1793 during the French Revolution, the cathedral Notre Dame de Paris was turned into a "Temple to Reason" and for a time Lady Liberty replaced the Virgin Mary on several altars. In the 1850s, Auguste Comte, the Father of Sociology, founded Positivism, a "religion of humanity." One of the earliest forerunners of contemporary chartered humanist organisations was the Humanistic Religious Association formed in 1853 in London. This early group was democratically organised, with male and female members participating in the election of the leadership and promoted knowledge of the sciences, philosophy, and the arts. The Ethical Culture movement was founded in 1876. The movement's founder, Felix Adler, a former member of the Free Religious Association, conceived of Ethical Culture as a new religion that would retain the ethical message at the heart of all religions. Ethical Culture was religious in the sense of playing a defining role in people's lives and addressing issues of ultimate concern.

Soundboards manage two primary aspects - inputs such as microphones and effectors, and outputs including speakers, headphones, and recording devices. Basic soundboards provide independent volume and tone adjustments for both inputs and outputs. Advanced models offer additional features like distinct volume and tone settings for various frequency bands, along with diverse filtering options for every channel. Additionally, there exists a universal master volume setting for overall sound balance. Some soundboards even include modulation effects like reverberation, echo, and distortion. Every channel comes equipped with numerous individualized controls, allowing comprehensive manipulation. The dimensions and complexity of a soundboard typically correlate with its capacity for inputs and outputs; smaller units might support up to 24 channels, while mid-range ones could handle between 32 and PDH, whereas some professional equipment supports over 72 channels. This information hopefully clarifies any confusion regarding soundboards. Please note, however, that due to their highly adaptable nature, understanding the functionality of a particular soundboard requires knowledge about its unique configuration. Consider visualizing a soundboard as comprising rows and columns, where each row represents an input corresponding to an element within the musical composition, e.g., an individual instrument. In a basic scenario involving a vocalist accompanied by guitar, one would require inputs for the singer's microphone and guitar. Should the guitar possess stereo connectivity, dual inputs may be necessary. To configure the sound levels, begin from the upper section of the soundboard, commonly designated for 'gain.' This parameter functions similarly to a faucet's tap valve, controlling the intensity of the incoming signals. Higher gain sensitivity accommodates louder instruments, ensuming other elements don't become excessively dominated by the amplified source.
