Our model is based on a bidirectional transformer encoder (i.e., BERT) and produces embedding pairs by applying one or more word-embedders to document text, followed by an entity extractor that extracts semantic concepts from the extracted data and combines them with the preprocessed word embeddings in order to define a new ED. Our experimental results on multiple benchmark datasets show that our ED model achieves state-of-the-art performance for tasks such as entity extraction and translation. We also demonstrate the utility of our model by using it to solve several difficult real-world problems: language modeling, sentiment analysis, mobile healthcare, and news item summarization.

Over the last two years, researchers have rewritten nearly every major chapter in our galaxy's history due to working with better data. In 2018, the European spacecraft Gaia released a treasure trove of 12 billion stars and galaxies' positions over hundreds of thousands of light-years. But even then, there was more work needed before we could fully comprehend what it all meant for our universe: It turns out that a lot had changed since 2016 or so - after all those pairs of star systems were formed. And some things are different than they used to be (for instance, the distance between Earth and the Sun has shrunk by about 40 million kilometers). A new study published on February 19th 2020 shows how astronomers can use this data to get a complete picture of the Milky Way without ever having actually launched a telescope ahead of time. The team came up with a way to reconstruct the formation and expansion stages of an entire star system using radio, optical, infrared, and X-ray observations taken from space as well as ground-based telescopes like Mauna Kea Observatory and Arecibo. The scientists determined where each individual star is located within its own galactic neighborhood based upon their location in these distant star systems to create a map which covers everything from red dwarf stars at the outskirts of any given galaxy to massive brown dwarfs living inside the cores of larger galaxies. They found that in just four years worth of positions from various sources, the current state of knowledge reveals 10 percent of the Milky Way's material has been transformed into black holes roughly 50 times bigger than our sun. A few other changes include several hundred times less dust around stars compared to previous findings, indicating something is happening inside our solar system too. Now, while studying the formation dynamics of neighboring star systems will take many more decades to figure out exactly what is going on and why, astronomers should definitely be able to make predictions soon enough if only because the current generation of surveys such as Gaia and SDSS J01477128 provide significant information. As far back as 1972, astronomer Carl Sagan predicted the beginning of human life would occur during "the first half of the twenty fifth century" when artificial intelligence reaches a level equivalent to ours today. Even though he died 36 years ago, his prediction still rings true considering humanity hasn't achieved full AI yet despite trillions spent developing computers capable of thinking according to incomplete human reasoning strategies.

When Nintendo released the NES in the US, the design styling was deliberately different from that of other game consoles. Nintendo wanted to distinguish its product from those of competitors and to avoid the generally poor reputation that game consoles had acquired following the video game crash of 1983. One result of this philosophy was to disguise the cartridge slot design as a front-loading zero insertion force (ZIF) cartridge socket, designed to resemble the front-loading mechanism of a VCR. The newly designed connector worked quite well when both the connector and the cartridges were clean and the pins on the connector were new. Unfortunately, the ZIF connector was not truly zero insertion force. When a user inserted the cartridge into the NES, the force of pressing the cartridge down and into place bent the contact pins slightly, as well as pressing the cartridge's ROM board back into the cartridge itself. Frequent insertion and removal of cartridges caused the pins to wear out from repeated usage over the years and the ZIF design proved more prone to interference by dirt and dust than an industry-standard card edge connector. These design issues were not alleviated by Nintendo's choice of materials; the console slot nickel connector springs would wear due to design and the game cartridge copper connectors were also prone to tarnishing. Many players would try to alleviate issues in the game caused by this corrosion by blowing into the cartridges, then reinserting them, which actually hurt the copper connectors by speeding up the tarnishing.

European Union law is a body of treaties and legislation, such as Regulations and Directives, which have direct effect or indirect effect on the laws of European Union member states. The text provides for determining compensation to claimants who contract serious illnesses arising from an injury suffered by an individual in connection with the practice of this article. The EU treaties provide that compensation may be claimed against each party involved but are not payable only if both parties agree to compensate each other for damages caused directly or indirectly through negligence related to an injury resulting from such injuries occurring together with failure to take reasonable preparations prior to the occurrence (i) if it was considered necessary pursuant to international arbitration procedures; and (ii) rather than paying compensation solely upon hearings at international arbitration proceedings involving damages settled under domestic jurisdiction where thereafter both sides agree to pay costs incurred otherwise. In addition, the European Union provides that if any compensation paid does not meet the criteria specified above it will cease being awarded under Article 6 (1) (a), less the amount due and payable at arbitration. As mentioned above, this also applies to damages received after the award has been made public when the dispute arises before arbitration courts outside the Member States within the meaning of Article 7 (2). Also relevant to the case involves bilateral agreements between affected parties relating to compensation. As regards claims raised during arbitration proceedings, the European Commission recommends that Arbitration Courts reach an agreement regarding payments based upon arbitration proceedings having respective consequences, including recognition of evidence submitted by parties involved in proceedings against the parties concerned and consideration of evidence compiled in accordance with Article 8 (3) (b); therefore payment should always rely on the effectiveness of adjudication processes established at international level throughout the entire conflict chain in accordance with Article 18 (5); alternatively, arbitration proceedings must commence immediately following the conclusion of proceedings with regard to damages towards claimants and prior negotiations concerning compensation receivership actions where disputes arise between the parties concerned.[8]

Graph convolutional neural networks (GCNNs) are a powerful extension of deep learning techniques to graph-structured data problems. We empirically evaluate several pooling methods for GCNNs, and combinations of those graph pooling methods with three different architectures: GCN, TAGCN, and GraphSAGE. In 1862, paper money was issued without the backing of precious metals, due to the Civil War. Silver and gold coins continued to be issued and in 1878 the link between paper money and coins was reinstated. This disconnection from gold and silver backing also occurred during the War of 1812. The use of paper money not backed by precious metals had also occurred under the Articles of Confederation from 1777 to 1788. With no solid backing and being easily counterfeited, the continentals quickly lost their value, giving rise to the phrase "not worth a continental." This was a primary reason for the "No state shall... make any thing but gold and silver coin a tender in payment of debts" clause in article 1, section 10 of the United States Constitution.

It's more serious and darker, a bit like Doctor Who in its last series. Not everyone was happy with that change, but the team behind Atlantis say they are prepared for any criticism. "The show is made to work pre-watershed," says executive producer and co-creator of Atlantis Johnny Capps. "I think audiences now are a lot more sophisticated than they used to be. "Children are exposed to a lot more darker and interesting material than they used to be. "So I think you have to reflect that in the fact that your audience is more sophisticated." He says that thanks to their later time slot of 8.30pm, they're hoping to catch adults and children. And making the programme darker isn't necessarily a bad thing. "I think it's a good thing because your showing the complexities of life and emotional stories," he says. "So I think they are richer and I think a family audience will learn more about life, because the shows are darker. "So they show the light side and the dark side. They show the consequences of emotional stories." Jason, who is played by Jack Donnelly, says he was worried about the changes and how they would be received by the audience. "It's nothing like series one," he tells Newsbeat. "I was chatting with Mark (Addy) and Rob (Emms) about it the other day, and it's not even really a follow-up. "They've pretty much rebooted the entire series. "It's a lot darker, a lot more serious, all the episodes are serialised, one leads into the other, leads into the other. [They're] not standalone stories any more." But are the team prepared for the backlash? "Slightly, yes," admits Jack. "I will be honest, Mark, Rob and myself, we were concerned in the beginning because we'd sort of built up a rhythm with each other last year. "We knew what we were doing, and there was a humour that undercut all the serious moments. "And we've sort of had to step away from that, under the producer saying,'You know this is a new direction we are going in.' "And having seen some of the episodes, just only rough cuts, I would say it might not be suitable for all the younger members of the audience [like] it was last year. "But I do think overall, the show has improved. "I think it is a positive thing, where they've taken it. And it just makes it more interesting. "So for everyone we lose, I'm hoping we're going to gain someone else." Atlantis is on BBC One on Saturdays from 20:30 GMT Follow BBCNewsbeat on Twitter and Radio1Newsbeat on YouTube

While electronic devices tend to function optimally, chemical processes within batteries often slow down when exposed to lower temperatures. Consequently, there may come a time when the battery cannot provide sufficient energy, leading to the device turning off. Generally, materials exhibit improved electrical conduction capabilities under cooler conditions due to decreased electrical resistance and minimized heat accumulation; however, this can potentially result in an overcurrent situation damaging certain components. Cellular phones combine both electrical and chemical elements—their batteries generate less charge in colder environments, and their glass parts are susceptible to fractures caused by significant temperature gradients between internal heat sources and external chilly air. Additionally, frigid settings promote moisture buildup through condensation within the device, posing a threat to intricately arranged circuitry. Therefore, operating such gadgets in low-temperature scenarios isn't recommended.

Contemporary advancements in embedded technologies are propelling the downsizing of satellites, leading to an unpreptaion surge in satellite deployments and fostering growth within the nascent space sector. However, these compact satellites face challenges related to dependability due to the impractical application of conventional hardware-based fault tolerance strategies when using cutting-edge systems-on-a-chip (SoC) in on-board computers (OBCs). Consequently, more sizable satellites still depend on well-established processors featuring extensive feature dimensions. Despite theoretical exploration, software-oriented solutions haven't gained traction within the space industry, primarily because they lack sufficient maturation for practical usage. Our study introduces the inaugural comprehensive, pragmatic methodology designed to facilitate resilient processing capabilities via contemporary multiprocessor SoCs (MPSoCs) during space travel, thus broadening their applicability across significant upcoming space endeavors. This innovative technique employs a tripartite fault-tolerant strategy that integrates self-validating threads at a broad scale, adaptable FPGA configurations, and mixed criticality protocols to guarantee sustained fault tolerance coupled with exemplary scalability suitable for varied mission requirements—from those constrained resources to highly critical ones. Preliminary performance assessments reveal a substantial improvement over existing radiation-resistant OBC models and reduced expenses associated with both software and hardware production processes. Developed under a four-year initiative by the European Space Agency (ESA), this approach will be validated through the construction of a prototypical MPSoC array in collaboration with two commercial entities.

Consider a cubic object measuring 1EE cm along each edge resting on the surface beneath it. Its base covers an area of 100cm² and possesses a total volume of 1000cm³, equating to a density of 10 units/volume per unit area. If we were to increase the dimensions of this cube by doubling its sides to 20cm, the bottom would span 400cm², while the overall volume would expand to 8000cm³. Consequently, there would be 20 units of volume per unit area. Although the structure remains identical in form, the weight exerted over each square centimeter increases as well due to the scaling effect. Hence, constructing larger versions of structures like Lego buildings isn't feasible. Ants manage to adhere to surfaces such as ceilings because their feet have minimal mass relative to the area they cover, combined with their inherent tackiness. Additionally, their strength-to-size ratio permits these insects to effortlessly relocate themselves during locomotion.

Video moment retrieval involves locating the segment within a video that best matches a provided natural language question. Most current approaches rely on supervised learning with comprehensive temporal annotations per query, but creating these labels can be laborious and costly. This study introduces a new weakly-supervised approach for moment retrieval using broad video-level annotations during training. Our technique includes a feature extraction component that compiles contextual data to identify and evaluate potential segments swiftly. Subsequently, it employs a strategy balancing both utilization and discovery to pick out the finest subset of segments. A subsequent phase entails a semantic enrichment stage that assesses how well the chosen segments align semantically with the original inquiry, awards points accordingly, and furnishes feedback to enhance the accuracy of initial assessments. Trials conducted on ActivityCaptions and Charades-STA confirm the superiority of our methodology.

Individuals utilize their intellectual quotient (I.Q.) and emotional intelligence to navigate their surroundings, with language abilities playing a crucial role. Without appropriate words, one struggles to comprehend and retain concepts, which explains why memories from early infancy fade since there was no developed vocabulary to interpret experiences during that time. Generally, individuals with Down Syndrome possess cognitive capacities similar to those of a child aged eight years old or less, impacting both their lexicon and logical reasoning capabilities. Furthermore, their brains often lack the typical separation between the left and right hemispheres seen in healthy adults, leading to challenges distinguishing fantasy from reality and discerning truth from falsehood. Additionally, this group faces difficulties transferring acquired knowledge from short-term to long-term memory, resulting in hindered learning processes. Unlike typically developing individuals, people with Down Syndrome frequently encounter fewer life stressors such as financial concerns, career satisfaction, and social connections. Their interactions tend to be met with kindness, fostering a positive environment; however, they commonly struggle to grasp subtleties such as sarcasm and complex communication due to cognitive limitations. This observation comes from personal experience working as a home care provider for developmentally disabled adults over three years.

We study a variant of the canonical k -center problem over a set of vertices in a metric space, where the underlying distances are apriori unknown. Instead, we can query an oracle which provides noisyincomplete estimates of the distance between any pair of vertices. We consider two oracle models: Dimension Sampling where each query to the oracle returns the distance between a pair of points in one dimension; and Noisy Distance Sampling where the oracle returns the true distance corrupted by noise. We propose active algorithms, based on ideas such as UCB and Thompson sampling developed in the closely related Multi-Armed Bandit problem, which adaptively decide which queries to send to the oracle and are able to solve the k -center problem within an approximation ratio of two with high probability. We analytically characterize instance-dependent query complexity of our algorithms and also demonstrate significant improvements over naive implementations via numerical evaluations on two real-world datasets (Tiny ImageNet and UT Zappos50K).

Infatuation refers to the intense euphoria experienced while admiring and daydreaming about another individual. On the other hand, lust revolves solely around physical attraction towards that person. In contrast, love involves cherishing and valuing someone, with the genuine wish for their happiness. A crush may encompass elements of these emotions combined.

Love represents a deep and unwavering connection one feels for another person; it motivates individuals to go to great lengths for their loved ones. This differs from lust as lust focuses primarily on the urge for sexual intimacy. Although both lust and love can coexist, they should be distinguished, with lust emphasizing purely sexual desires within a relationship. Crushes share similarities with lust, yet differ by lacking an explicit sexual longing, instead aiming to build a strong bond based on understanding and affection.

Lastly, love transcends fleeting moments of blissful excitement, becoming an enduring commitment even after the initial thrill subsides. In true love, we care deeply for our partner, providing unwavering support and standing up for them regardless of circumstances. We prioritize their needs, put ourselves in their position, and navigate challenges together.

Feature subspace selection is an important part in speech emotion recognition. Most of the studies are devoted to finding a feature subspace for representing all emotions. However, some studies have indicated that the features associated with different emotions are not exactly the same. Hence, traditional methods may fail to distinguish some of the emotions with just one global feature subspace. In this work, we propose a new divide and conquer idea to solve the problem. First, the feature subspaces are constructed for all the combinations of every two different emotions (emotion-pair). Bi-classifiers are then trained on these feature subspaces respectively. The final emotion recognition result is derived by the voting and competition method. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method can get better results than the traditional multi-classification method.

Advertising serves as a significant source of income for countless websites and mobile applications. However, there are instances where ad networks exploit this system to deceive advertisers out of their funds. Although contemporary safeguards have evolved to counteract certain types of click fraud, recent analyses indicate that up to one-third of all clicks from ad networks may actually be click spam. In our research, we introduce innovative inference methods designed to pinpoint click fraud schemes based on their inherent characteristics. Two new strategies we recommend are mimicry and bait-click, both of which demonstrate marked enhancements compared to existing solutions. The mimicry approach identifies click spam through the recognition of repeated legitimate click traffic associated with organic click fraud. Meanwhile, the bait-click defense employs the unique position of an ad network to introduce specific bait clicks onto a user's device, making it possible to trace any subsequent click spam involving these bait clicks. Through our trials, the mimicry technique successfully detected approximately 81% of deceptive clicks during low-frequency attacks, while maintainrightly flagging only 2 out of every 100,000 clicks as false positives. Likewise, the bait-click strategy yielded even better outcomes, boasting a 95% detection rate coupled with a minimal increase in false positives ranging from zero to 30 per million, representing a considerable advancement over prior methodologies.

Neil Lennon's side extended their lead at the Championship summit to nine points, ahead of second placed Falkirk, who play Ayr United on Saturday. The right-back was lucky to escape one early reckless challenge, but was correctly punished for another on Andrew Shinnie, and when he clattered the midfielder once again, it was a simple decision for referee Don Robertson. Hibs quickly asserted themselves by going in front and it became too big a task despite Cummings' offer of assistance. United didn't lack fight. They lacked composure and quality on the night. A first home defeat this season was badly timed. They're not entirely out of the title race, but the smart money would be on a play-off place for the Tannadice side. Head coach Lennon might not admit it but few will back anyone other than Hibernian to take the Championship title now. Cummings' fabulous first-half finish was timely, not too long after Toshney's red card. The striker stole in behind a defence that seemed intent on playing a high line. Shinnie exposed that with a lovely lofted ball into Cummings' path and he made no mistake with a vital, instinctive goal. Cummings was also unlucky to be flagged offside when clean through and might have earned a penalty when William Edjenguele appeared to catch him near the goalline just before half-time. It was the 21-year-old's 20th goal of the season - great work from him all-round, until later. Martin Boyle should have ended the contest when he had time, and space six yards out, but volleyed wildly over. The impressive Shinnie thought he had sealed the win after great work from Boyle, only for Cammy Bell to parry his shot over the bar. Hibs rarely looked troubled with goalkeeper Ofir Marciano a virtual spectator. This was a massive step for Lennon's men, and with three home games to follow, they are very much on track for the top flight. For all his positives, Cummings risked this win with few minutes of madness. He was unnecessarily booked for throwing the ball away when ruled offside. Minutes later he threw himself at a cross, blatantly punched the ball in the net and was correctly ordered off. It was utter madness and offered United a lifeline from nowhere. Luckily for him, his team mates saw it through. In total, 10 players were booked, and Lennon was ordered to the stand late on. However, Hibs got the job done, and deserved to finish with three valuable points. Dundee United manager Ray McKinnon: "It was extremely difficult when we went down to 10 men. "I thought we started the game excellently and controlled the first 15 minutes, but the sending-off certainly had a massive impact on the game. "I haven't seen it again, but Lewis has gone for the ball and then he has pulled out. It was clear for everybody on our bench. "The ref is entitled to make that decision, but we were very disappointed. You have to look at all the decisions that were made and some of inconsistencies and tackles that went unpunished. "But what is important is what we do from now until the end of the season and focus on winning every game. "I thought we showed great character to battle back hard with 10 men. We will take the positives out of that and fight for every point until the end and see where we end up." Hibernian head coach Neil Lennon: "Jason's got to learn to control his temper. "I've been there - I got many a telling off from Martin O'Neill in my younger days - but he's an outstanding talent and he's come up with a really big goal in a big game and he does it consistently and it's not a coincidence. "We were outstanding. The only disappointment was the sending off really, which put us on the back foot for 10 minutes. "The rest of the game, we played really strongly and we looked a very good side. Thoroughly deserved to win. "I wanted them to put down a marker for the rest of the season and hopefully they've done that. "It is a difficult place to come and win, but I thought we were head and shoulders above Dundee United. Should the object descend towards the earth, gravity exerts mechanical force upon the object, changing the stored potential energy in the gravitational field into the kinetic energy discharged as heat upon contact with the ground. The sun converts nuclear potential energy into various types of energy; its overall mass remains constant because it retains the identical total energy even though in altered states, however, its mass diminishes when the energy departs from it, primarily as luminous energy.

One highly efficient method for differentially private learning and optimization is known as objective perturbation. This technique involves adding a stochastic linear component to a specific optimization issue derived from an Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM) problem and solving it precisely. However, current evaluations of this strategy largely depend on the convex nature and smoothness of the target function, thus restricting its broad application. In response, we propose two enhanced algorithms. The initial one necessitates merely the boundedness of the loss function and functions within a discrete environment, providing both privacy and precision assuranc es even in the absence of convexity assumptions. Consequently, this creates an efficient optimization procedure for any discrete set that rivals the versatility of the exponential mechanism. Our second algorithm caters to continuous domains, demanding solely that the loss function remains limited and adheres to the Lipschitz condition regarding its continuous variable. Although privacy analysis doesn't hinge on convexity, its accuracy assessment still presumes convexity albeit excluding the necessity for second-order criteria such as smoothness. Despite lacking convex properties, this algorithm can generally serve as an efficient optimization tool, allowing empirical determination of its accuracy. To support our theoretical assertions, we conducted an experimental study on the non-convex scenario by employing an integer programming solver as the optimization oracle. Results demonstrated that when utilizing our methodology to minimize 01 loss during the training of linear classifiers, it surpassed traditional techniques involving the confidential optimization of a convex proxy loss function applied to the Adult dataset.

Adaptive transmission schemes are a crucial aspect of the radio design for future wireless networks. The paper studies the performance of two classes of adaptive transmission schemes in cellular downlink. One class is based on physical layer rateless codes with constant transmit power and the other uses fixed-rate codes in conjunction with power adaptation. Using a simple stochastic geometry model for the cellular downlink, the focus is to compare the adaptivity of fixed-rate codes with power adaptation to that of physical layer rateless codes only. The performance of both rateless and fixed-rate coded adaptive transmission schemes are compared by evaluating the typical user success probability and rate achievable with the two schemes. Based on both the theoretical analysis and simulation results, it is clearly shown that fixed-rate codes require power control to maintain good performance whereas physical layer rateless codes with constant power can still provide robust performance.

Rodinadinia refers to an ancient supercontinent that predated the advent of advanced terrestrial organisms. This vast landmass fragmented prior to the emergence of life on land, with its pieces later reuniting as other supercontinents like Pangaea and Pannotia took shape over geologic timescales. Throughout Earth's history, there have been numerous such large land masses, totaling at least five known examples in chronological sequence: Kenorland (2.72-2.1 billion years ago), Columbia (1.82-1.35 billion years ago), Rodinian (1.13-0.75 billion years ago), Pannotia (633-573 million years ago), and finally, Pangea (336-173 million years ago). Notably, Pangea represents the latest iteration among these significant global land configurations.

The end-to-end (E2E) automatic speech recognition (ASR) framework enables simultaneous refinement of both acoustic and linguistic models via one integrated system. Nevertheless, the standard E2E ASR structure intertwines the language model component—the decoder sub-network (subnet)—with the outcomes of the acoustic encoder, preventing separate training of the language model with external textual resources. Our research introduces an innovative design that isolates the decoder subnet from the encoder's output, thus permitting it to function as a standalone language model capable of being enhanced by external text data. We examine two approaches to integrating updates into this novel configuration. Empirical findings indicate that the detached language model variant significantly capitalizes on external text inputs, yielding reductions of 9.3% and 22.8% in character and word error rates, respectively, when applied to Mandarin HKUST and English NSC corpora. Moreover, our method demonstrates compatibility with supplementary language models and adaptability across varying volumes of annotated data.

Our research focuses on implementing Dynamic Spectrum Access (DSA) using a Software Defined Radio (SDR) within IEEE EEE 802.15.4e Networks. The nodes within the network choose their carrier frequencies post Energy-Detective Spectrum Sensing (SS). To facilitate frequency hopping between two nodes in an IEEE 802.15.4e Network, we introduce a synchronization method. We designate the IEEE 802.15.4e Network as a Secondary User (SU), whereas all other networks function as Primary Users (PUs) in the unlicensed 868/915 MHz and 2.4 GHz bands utilized by a Cognitive Radio (CR). Nevertheless, our proposed algorithm along with the energy sensor has been developed using GNU Radio and the Universal Software Radio Peripheral (USRP) SDR. Furthermore, actual data transmission trials were conducted under two different scenarios. In the initial scenario, the SU operates at a fixed carrier frequency; alternatively, in the latter situation, it employs the dynamic approach provided by DSA. During both instances, interference from a PU's transmission was encountered by the SU, prompting them to compute the Packet Success Rate (PSR) to evaluate the effectiveness of the employed DSA technique. It was observed that the PSR enhanced by 80% when the SU utilized the dynamic spectrum access compared to a stationary access strategy.

How printing worked A movable-type printing press is made up of three main parts: The type-form is a sheet of metal into which letters, numbers, and other symbols are cast. It is the basic unit of a printing press. The forme is a device that holds several type-forms, or letters, in one piece. The impression cylinder is a cylindrical object, about the size of a wine bottle, that is covered with a sheet of paper. The type-forms are placed inside the cylinder, and ink is applied to the type-forms. As the cylinder rotates, it presses the ink onto the paper. The impression cylinder then moves back and the process is repeated. In the early days of printing, type-forms were made from metal, usually lead or brass. The type-forms were placed into the forme, which was set in the impression cylinder. The cylinder was inked by hand and the printed sheet was pulled out by a piece of paper, called a gripper. The paper was then dried, folded, and cut into sheets. It was then ready for binding. In the early 1500s, printing presses were the latest and greatest technology. The very first printed books were produced in Germany and Italy in the early 1400s. In 1452, the University of Mainz, in Germany, produced the first Bible. In 1455, the first book printed on a press was printed in Germany. The book was called The Printing Art. It was a description of the printing press. In 1455, the first book printed on a press was printed in Germany. It was a description of the printing press. Printing presses were set up in many major cities and towns. These cities usually had a university, a printing guild, or an apprentice program. The first printing press in England was set up in Westminster in 1476. By 1500, printing presses were in operation in 170 cities and towns. The Gutenberg Bible was the first major work to be printed on a press. Johann Fust and Peter Schoeffer joined Gutenberg in the 1450s. When Gutenberg died, they continued to print the Bible. Johannes Gutenberg was born in Germany in about 1398. He invented the movable-type printing press around 1440. The Gutenberg Bible is also known as the 42-line Bible because it has 42 lines of text on each page. The Bible was printed in two columns of text. The most famous printer of the time was Aldus Manutius. He set up a press in Venice in 1494. He printed many of the works of the great Greek and Roman writers of antiquity. He was the first to use italic type. The word italic comes from Italy , the country where Manutius lived and worked. The first printed books were very expensive. Books were sold by the folio , a page of a book that was folded once. A folio could have as many as eight pages of text. A book printed in 1502 sold for 6,000 to 7,000 florins a folio. That was more than a year's wages for an average craftsman. Printed books were sold in the towns where they were produced. A conversational agent that is engaging, informed, and compassionate possesses essential traits for effective communication. Prior research has developed specific tasks and data sets designed to foster these attributes individually and assess their expression within an agent. However, it's more beneficial for an open-domain conversational agent to integrate all these qualities smoothly during interactions. This study explores methods to merge models with distinct abilities, which include straightforward model combination techniques needing little extra training as well as complex multitask learning strategies implemented throughout the entire training process. Additionally, we introduce a novel dataset named BlendedSkillTalk, allowing us to evaluate how these features coalesce naturally in dialogue. The evaluation reveals that simultaneously tackling multiple tasks centered around certain abilities leads to superior integrated conversation outcomes when contrasted with singular skill models. Furthermore, both combined and sequential methodologies demonstrate effectiveness, provided they circumvent any undesired predisposition toward selecting a specific ability or undergo refinement using our newly established task.

Aspect Term Extraction (ATE) detects opinionated aspect terms in sentences or text spans, with the end goal of performing aspect-based sentiment analysis. The small amount of available datasets for supervised ATE and the fact that they cover only a few domains raise the need for exploiting other data sources in new and creative ways. Publicly available review corpora contain a plethora of opinionated aspect terms and cover a larger domain spectrum. In this paper, we first propose a method for using such review corpora for creating a new dataset for ATE. Our method relies on an attention mechanism to select sentences that have a high likelihood of containing actual opinionated aspects. We thus improve the quality of the extracted aspects. We then use the constructed dataset to train a model and perform ATE with distant supervision. By evaluating on human annotated datasets, we prove that our method achieves a significantly improved performance over various unsupervised and supervised baselines. Finally, we prove that sentence selection matters when it comes to creating new datasets for ATE. Specifically, we show that, using a set of selected sentences leads to higher ATE performance compared to using the whole sentence set.

God is also usually defined as a non-corporeal being without any human biological gender, but the concept of God actively (as opposed to receptively) creating the universe has caused some religions to give "Him" the metaphorical name of "Father." Because God is conceived as not being a corporeal being, God cannot (some say should not) be portrayed in a literal visual image; some religious groups use a man (sometimes old and bearded) to symbolize God because of His deed of creating man's mind in the image of His own.

We study the problem of distributed coverage control in a network of mobile agents arranged on a line. The goal is to design distributed dynamics for the agents to achieve uniform coverage in a bounded region. The dynamics of each agent are constrained to be within a ball around its current location. Our main contributions are the following. We first show that the problem is strictly convex and hence admits a globally optimal solution. We then prove that any optimal solution of the problem satisfies a property called uniform connectivity. The property of uniform connectivity is closely related to the exact coverage property of a network. For a network to be exact coverage, each agent should be connected to at least one other agent. For a network to be uniformly connected, each agent should be connected to at least one agent uniformly over the region. We prove that the uniform connectivity property is a sufficient condition for a network to achieve uniform coverage. We then design a distributed algorithm for each agent to achieve uniform connectivity. The algorithm of each agent is based on a simple local information exchange. We show that the dynamics of the agents converge to the unique global optimal solution of the problem. The algorithm of each agent is simple and can be easily implemented. The theoretical analysis for the algorithm is done by introducing a Lyapunov function. Our algorithm is closely related to a recent result in [Pagnini2017]. In [Pagnini2017], the authors show that a simple dynamics is sufficient to achieve uniform connectivity. However, their dynamics is based on the current location of the agents and the current region, which is in contrast to our algorithm. The key difference between the two dynamics is that our dynamics is based on the local information and not the current location of the agents. The rest of the paper is organized as follows. We first review some related work in Section [sec:relatedwork]. The problem formulation is given in Section [sec:formulation]. The main results are presented in Section [sec:mainresults]. The proofs of the main results are given in Section [sec:proof]. Related work {sec:relatedwork} The problem of achieving uniform coverage in a network of agents is closely related to the problem of network localization. Network localization has been studied extensively in the literature, and has applications in a variety of areas, such as remote sensing, robotics, and mobile computing. A typical problem of network localization is to design distributed algorithms for the agents to estimate their locations. There are several works on network localization, which are closely related to the problem of uniform coverage in a network. The work in [Ravikumar2008] is the first work on network localization, which shows that the problem is strictly convex. The work in [Ravikumar2008] proposes a distributed algorithm to achieve uniform coverage in a network of agents. However, the work in [Ravikumar2008] assumes that the locations of the agents are known. A dynamic algorithm to achieve uniform coverage in a network of agents with unknown locations is proposed in [Akyildiz2013]. However, the algorithm in [Akyildiz2013] requires a centralized estimation of the locations of the agents. A distributed algorithm to achieve uniform coverage in a network of agents with unknown locations is proposed in [Akyildiz2014]. However, the algorithm in [Akyildiz2014] requires a centralized estimation of the locations of the agents. The work in [Pagnini2017] is the most related to our work. In [Pagnini2017], the authors show that a simple dynamics is sufficient to achieve uniform connectivity. However, the dynamics in [Pagnini2017] is based on the current location of the agents and the current region, which is in contrast to our algorithm. In the helical thylakoid model, grana consist of a stack of flattened circular granal thylakoids that resemble pancakes. Each granum can contain anywhere from two to a hundred thylakoids, though some studies suggest even as many as 1,000 are found in a single individual. Granas may be divided into five main groups: (1) granules with one or more "babies"; (2) little bumpy bumps called "the babies"; (3) tiny roundish-shaped granules known as "cups"; (4) large spherical clusters like those seen on jellyfish and sea urchins; and (5) very small globular (lumpy) granules known as "dots." The principal objective for this study was to determine whether these choanofilaments were able to move around freely within their parental cells, or if they had an additional function as transport membranes. The effects of the choice of cell type under different conditions have already been proven by previous investigations [1] and it is hoped that our results will help us understand how the movement of choanofilamentous structures develops at the level of cellular organization, leading eventually to functional integration of the individual molecules. To carry out this experiment, we used a newly developed protocol which combines electroporation of the extrafiltrate membranes with mechanical shearing of them over protrusions placed on each side of the membrane, and then delivers a solution containing soluble polylysine at one end; once the membrane has been processed through the shearer, this solution is removed and the protrusions are replaced. This procedure allows a better control of the flow rates than electrical methods such as electrodeposition, facilitating analysis of the channels created by the action of the protrusions on the extracellular fluid. We also included time-controlled transfection using a system where only one set of cells were stained simultaneously so that we could observe the interaction between the epithelializing proteoglycan and its associated particles during the course of forming the granule.

Cats possess exceptionally adaptive features for being effective nocturnal predators due to their evolutionary development. They have specialized eyes capable of functioning under low-light situations. A crucial aspect of this adaptation lies in their retinas, which contain heightened sensitivity, enabling superior vision even in dim environments. I have seen a lot of CMV posts about opting out of child support entirely, but I have a slightly different perspective on the issue and would be interested to hear opposing views. From what I've read about child support calculation there are a variety of models used by different states and different countries, but the common thread between all of them is income. Some also consider age of the child, difference in income between parents, standard of living adjustments, etc. In theory I get it, but the implications in practice really bother me and I think the basis behind the laws regulating child support calculation are a little outdated and unfair. Here's a summary of my objections: Above a certain amount why should income be taken into account? For example, let's consider two friends Jane and Anna. Jane has a baby with her ex-boyfriend who earns 25k per year and Anna has a baby with her ex-boyfriend who earns 150k per year. Assuming both women have similar incomes and lifestyles before children, most child support calculations would award Anna much more child support than Jane. But why? Is Anna's child more deserving of money than Jane's child? Why should calculations assume a relationship or marriage? Many child support calculations are based on the income that would have been dedicated to the child if the parents lived together. If a woman gets pregnant from a one night stand or a non-serious relationship, why should there be any assumption by the courts that the parents would have lived together and raised the child together? A married couple living together with children spend their income differently than single people without children. So why should a relationship be assumed and considered when it did not exist in the first place? Why is standard of living important? Some child support calculations take into account the accustomed or increased standard of living when calculating support amounts. Let's be honest here, is there ever really a need for 5k per month in child support? Just because someone is wealthy, why does that mean they are automatically expected to provide a high level of financial support to their children. Where exactly is that money going? In most cases it isn't all going to the child and I think that is problematic. The point of child support money is for support of the child, not the creation of an expensive lifestyle for the child and custodial parent. In my opinion, a basic formula should be developed (adjusted for cost of living by area) that accounts for the average amount required to support a child's basic monthly needs at varying age levels. This amount would take into account food, transportation, clothing, medical and other miscellaneous expenses. The child support amount could be then simply read off a table rather than dedicating time and resources into courts and legal decisions. If this amount is more than 15 of monthly net income, the child support paying parent would be limited to pay 15 as support for that child. A parent shouldn't be struggling financially to pay their own bills in order to be able to keep up with child support payments. For parents where this amount is less than 15 of monthly net income, they would pay the set amount as given by the formula. If parents have 5050 joint custody, there would be no child support awarded, because both parents should be equally supporting the child. For other custody situations the child support amount would be calculated down or up based on custody percentage. So am I missing something here? To me what I've described above seems to be a much fairer system than the way child support is currently calculated. So please, CMV. Hello, users of CMV! This is a footnote from your moderators. If you see a comment that has broken one, it is more effective to report it than downvote it. Speaking of which, [downvotes don't change views] ! If you are thinking about submitting a CMV yourself, please have a look through our [popular topics wiki] first. Any questions or concerns? Feel free to [message us] . Happy CMVing!

During cell division, which occurs when cells duplicate themselves, the DNA strands experience slight damage at their tips. Imagine tearing a piece of paper repeatedly; eventually, achieving a clean break becomes increasingly challenging. Over time, DNA sustains significant harm, hindering its ability to convey genetic data accurrightfully, if at all. Consequently, bodily tissues deteriorate and lose functionality. However, certain aspects of anti-aging may be feasible. Reproductive cells such as sperm and egg cells remain unaffected during replication due to specific repair mechanisms within their respective glands that maintain the integrity of DNA ends. Expanding this concept to all cells might potentially prevent physical decline. Nevertheless, current knowledge regarding this application is limited.","Every time a cell divides to reproduce, there's a minor loss of DNA from the ends. Subsequently, the DNA quality diminishes gradually over time. For instance, Dolly the cloned sheep exhibited early aging symptoms despite being cloned from an adult sheep because the DNA used originated from an elderly specimen."

In simpler terms, aging results from cells duplicating imperfectly throughout one's life, leading to gradual changes that accumulate into visible aging effects. Although various theories attempt to explain the aging process (such as oxidative stress, telomere attrition, or innate biological systems), establishing a definitive cause remains elusive. Once clarified, understanding the underlying mechanics would pave the way for potential remedies and distribution methods. Notably, certain lab-grown cells possess unlimited replication capabilities through exposure to harsh substances like trypsin. However, these modified cells wouldn't be desirable for human use.

The tiny flame of each candle melded together in my eyes to create an inferno of magnificence only worthy of my favorite grandmother's birthday. "Well blow them out then, and make a wish!" Someone shouted, getting a collective laugh from the room. "I'm going to need a little help" My grandmother said with a wide smile. Everyone inched in a little closer and began blowing the candles out, ten or twenty at a time, until the last one was extinguished by my grandmother herself. "What did you wish for?" uncle Elmer asked. "You know I can't tell!" replied Grandma. A few moments later, after the excitement settled, we moved on to presents. She received the things you come to expect after so many birthdays; jewelry, delicious foods, tickets to an upcoming symphony and the like. She looked around the room at all of us, drinking in the moment, and then spiked the baby to ground. During the French Revolution in 1789, the labels "left" and "right" originated from the division within the National Assembly between royalist sympathizers on the president's right side and revolutionary advocates on the left. As described by the Baron de Gauville, the former group gathered to the right to distance themselves from the disorderly conduct prevalent among their opponents. Despite this, the conservative bloc rejected the classification system, arguing that legislators ought to represent individual or collective concerns without forming partisan groups. These ideological divisions were also reflected in the media of the time, which employed these terms to describe the conflicting viewpoints. This information is sourced from Wikipedia.

Imagine you have a toy box with lots of toys inside. Some of the toys have special buttons or latches that you need to press or pull to open them, while other toys can be easily opened just by turning them. Beers are kind of like toys and some are made with a special cap that only comes off if you use a bottle opener, like the toys with the special buttons. Other beers have a cap that you can easily twist off, like the toys that are easy to open just by turning them. Brewers make some beers with twist-off caps because they want them to be easy to open quickly, like if you're at a party and don't want to stop the fun by finding a bottle opener. Other beers have regular caps because they might taste better that way or because the brewer wants people to take their time enjoying them. So just like how different toys have different ways to open them, different beers have different caps to make them taste good and easy to drink.

Humans may in part owe their big brains to a DNA "typo" in their genetic code, research suggests. The typo is a single change in the genetic code that occurred about 2.4 million years ago. It's thought to have arisen by chance. But this small change may have had a big effect on the evolution of the human brain. The change is in a gene called FOXP2. This gene is involved in the development of the brain's language regions. The study found that the change occurred in the same place in the genomes of people from different parts of the world. This suggests that it arose in a common ancestor of all modern humans. The researchers say the change may have helped to make the human brain larger and more complex. It's also possible that the change helped to make human language more sophisticated. The findings are published in the journal Nature.

Jane was waiting for her son Tony to come home from school. The school bus came, and he didn't get off. This had happened before, so she called Tony's phone. He didn't answer. She waited in her car while they tried to find Tony. An hour later, Jane's cell phone rang. It was Tony. "Mom," he said, "I'm sorry. I fell asleep on the bus." "What? Why didn't you answer the phone?" Jane asked. "I was asleep. I didn't hear it," he said. Jane was very angry. "You're in big trouble," she told him. "You shouldn't have gone to sleep. Don't you know that we were worried about you?" "I'm sorry, Mom," Tony said. "I was tired and I fell asleep. Don't be mad at me." "OK, I'm not mad anymore," she said. "Now where are you? How do you get home?" "I'm at the bus garage," he said. "They will bring me home soon." "Oh, OK," Jane said. "Now I'm not mad, but I'm still worried. Be careful, and I'll see you in a little while." After Tony came home, Jane made him dinner. They watched TV together and talked. "I'm sorry, Mom," Tony said. "I didn't mean to make you worry." "That's OK," she said. "But next time, don't go to sleep on the bus. Promise me." "OK, Mom," he said. "I promise."

The act of pruning serves to enhance one's grip, similar to how ridges on reptile limbs provide additional traction. Since our hands and feet serve as primary grasping appendages, their adaptation through pruning facilitates improved hold while submerged in water. Current theories suggest that these wrinkles are purposefully developed to aid in gripping underwater objects. Interestingly, this process isn't solely due to water absorption but rather an involuntary bodily reaction. Furthermore, pruning can be utilized diagnostically to identify potential nerve damage, as individuals lacking such nerves fail to exhibit pruning. It remains somewhat unclear why only our extremities experience this phenomenon; however, it may be attributed to evolutionary adaptations aimed at enhancing aquatic dexterity.

Animal tissue comprises various nutrients that are consumed, broken down, taken up by the body, and distributed via the bloodstream to nourish the cells. With the exception of the developing fetus, the digestive system typically initiates this process. Enzymatic secretions within the digestive tract cleave the chemical links between molecules found in food, altering both their shape and energy content. While certain molecules enter the bloodstream intact, others are freed from their original structure due to digestion. Any remaining substances not absorbed, as well as byproducts from cellular activities, are expelled from the body through defecation.

The growth of Highbury faced constraints due to the East Stand being recognized as a Grade II listed structure and the proximity of the remaining three stands to homes, which limited the club's ability to fully capitalize on matchday income throughout the late 20th and early 21st centuries. This jeopardized their competitiveness amidst the era's surge in football popularity. In response, Arsenal suggested constructing a larger 60,361-seat venue called the Emirates Stadium in 2000, located approximately 500 meters southwest of Highbury. Although bureaucratic obstacles and escalating expenses postponed progress, the Emirates Stadium opened just before the commencement of the 2006-07 season. It acquired its name through an extensive sponsorship agreement with Emirates Airlines, marking it as one of English football's most lucrative partnerships, valued at nearly £100 million. Some supporters disapproved of commercializing stadium titles, opting instead to call it Ashburton Grove or simply 'the Grove'. Despite this dissent, the stadium remains officially titled Emirates Stadium until at least 2028, while Emirates also serves as the club's shirt sponsor till the conclusion of the 2018-19 campaign. Beginning with the 2010-11 season, each stand within the stadium has received official designations—North Bank, East Stand, West Stand, and Clock End.

Surrogate explainers of black-box machine learning predictions are of paramount importance in the field of eXplainable Artificial Intelligence since they can be applied to any type of data (images, text and tabular), are model-agnostic and are post-hoc (i.e., can be retrofitted). The Local Interpretable Model-agnostic Explanations (LIME) algorithm is often mistakenly unified with a more general framework of surrogate explainers, which may lead to a belief that it is the solution to surrogate explainability. In this paper we empower the community to "build LIME yourself" (bLIMEy) by proposing a principled algorithmic framework for building custom local surrogate explainers of black-box model predictions, including LIME itself. To this end, we demonstrate how to decompose the surrogate explainers family into algorithmically independent and interoperable modules and discuss the influence of these component choices on the functional capabilities of the resulting explainer, using the example of LIME.

This research explores a novel mobile edge computing (MEC) framework in which an autonomous drone utilizes terrestrial cellular network base stations for computational load transfer. As the drone traverses from one point to another, it must perform specific computations by delegating them to chosen base stations en route for simultaneous processing. Our objective is to shorten the overall duration of the drone's task by refining both its path and computation offloading timetable within the limits of the drone's top speed and the base stations' processing capacities. However, solving the combined challenge of adjusting the drone's course and managing the computational handoff proves complex due to the non-convex nature of the issue. In response, our study introduces a practical methodology designed to yield near-optimal solutions. Test simulations indicate that our approach markedly improves the efficiency of completing the drone's objectives when contrasted with conventional methods.

In this paper we present mono-stixels, a compact environment representation specially designed for dynamic street scenes. Mono-stixels are a novel approach to estimate stixels from a monocular camera sequence instead of using stereo images or more efficient methods such as triples and quadrics for discrete road data. We use mono-stixel approaches to apply segmentation and reconstruction algorithms such as GRASS GIS (Gillespie et al., 2011), Hochenwirth's voxel grid method (Hochenwirth Malitzky, 2012) and MOST (Majumdar et al., 2013). The presented algorithms work well on different camera rigs but need high pixel rates to capture fast moving objects in the scene. In addition, they suffer from visual artifacts caused by occlusions and lack computational efficiency when dealing with large datasets. Our goal is to develop an effective model that can be applied to identify individual elements for each point in a static image. We propose three simple algorithmic models based on a deep convolutional neural network framework: 1) a model trained on only one frame, 2) a model trained on multiple frames at once through batch processing techniques and 3) a hybrid model combining both training methods. Experimental results show that our proposed fixed-frame model achieves state-of-the art performance while batch processing generally outperforms single-frame learning. Furthermore, we compare our models against other popular techniques such as triplet fusion and find that our proposal achieves better results under all conditions.

Hayek's principal investigations in economics concerned capital, money, and the business cycle. Mises had earlier applied the concept of marginal utility to the value of money in his Theory of Money and Credit (1912), in which he also proposed an explanation for "industrial fluctuations" based on the ideas of the old British Currency School and of Swedish economist Knut Wicksell. Hayek used this body of work as a starting point for his own interpretation of the business cycle, elaborating what later became known as the "Austrian Theory of the Business Cycle." Hayek spelled out the Austrian approach in more detail in his book, published in 1929, an English translation of which appeared in 1933 as Monetary Theory and the Trade Cycle. There he argued for a monetary approach to the origins of the cycle. In his Prices and Production (1931), Hayek argued that the business cycle resulted from the central bank's inflationary credit expansion and its transmission over time, leading to a capital misallocation caused by the artificially low interest rates. Hayek claimed that "the past instability of the market economy is the consequence of the exclusion of the most important regulator of the market mechanism, money, from itself being regulated by the market process."

We consider the problem of fitting variational posterior approximations using stochastic optimization methods. The performance of these approximations depends on (1) how well the variational family matches the true posterior distribution, and (2) how efficiently we can optimize the variational objective function. To address (1), it is important to choose a flexible variational family that can capture complex distributions. Examples of such families include normalizing flow, variational autoencoders, and structured mean-field models. Additionally, we can use techniques such as hierarchical modeling and incorporating prior knowledge to further improve the match between the variational approximation and the true posterior. To address (2), we can use stochastic optimization methods such as stochastic gradient descent (SGD), Adam, or Adagrad to optimize the variational objective function. These methods use noisy estimates of the gradient to update the parameters of the variational family, which can result in faster convergence and better solutions. In practice, a combination of both approaches is often used to obtain the best results. We choose a flexible variational family and use stochastic optimization methods to efficiently optimize the variational objective function.

The Electoral Commission said 38 MPs had highlighted people, including students, claiming to have voted twice, which is a criminal offence. It said individual electoral registers run by councils should be better joined up to help identify duplicate entries. Labour warned against making it harder for young people to register to vote. A record number of 46.8 million people were registered to vote in the 8 June election, 500,000 higher than in 2015 and also more than the 46.4 million figure for the EU referendum. Of these, 68.7 actually voted on the day, the highest turnout figure for a general election since 1997. There was a surge in applications to register to the vote in the days after Theresa May called the snap poll on 18 April and also in the days leading up to the 22 May deadline. In total, 2.9 million applications were received over the six-week period. Several constituencies found that the size of their electorate rose by more than 10, including seats with large student populations such as Canterbury, Cambridge, Bristol West and Leeds Central. However, concerns over the number of duplicate applications - a problem which initially surfaced after last year's EU referendum - continue to persist. At the moment, there is no direct link between electoral registers, which are held and managed by electoral registration officials around Britain, and the online registration service now used by a majority of people. The two systems use different databases and cannot communicate directly with each other. Between 1 December 2016 and the 22 May deadline, about 4.9 million applications to vote were submitted, the majority of them done online. But the net increase in the number of entries on the electoral register during that period was only 1.4 million, suggesting "a significant proportion of applications are likely to have been duplicates." With no way of people checking online whether they are already registered, the proportion of duplicate applications is estimated to have ranged between 30 and 70 in different areas. The watchdog said this had caused significant administration and financial burdens for electoral officials and should be addressed by clearer information on registration sites, including potentially a verification function which it said was used in Australia, New Zealand and the Republic of Ireland. Despite efforts to flag up to people that they did not need to register if they had been sent a poll card or had voted in May's local council elections, the watchdog said it appeared to have made little difference and urgent action was now needed. "The relative ease of submitting an application to register to vote using the online service, in comparison to the difficult of contacting a local authority electoral services team by telephone or email to check if they were already registered, meant many people simply submitted another application," the report said. Although there was a lack of evidence to back up claims on social media that some people had voted twice, the watchdog said it took the issue very seriously and anyone with information should contact the police. It stressed that although some people - including students and those with second homes - may lawfully be able to register in more than one constituency and cast more than one vote in local elections, voting twice in a general election was an offence punishable by an unlimited fine. The "dispersed and unconnected" nature of the 381 electoral registers in Britain means it is not possible to collectively cross-check entries, the watchdog said, and being able to do so would significantly reduce the risk of double voting. It is also calling for people who are registered in two seats to choose in advance which one they will vote in at future general elections. Labour's shadow minister for voter engagement, Cat Smith, said voting twice was a serious offence and police needed to have the resources to prosecute people suspected of doing so. But she warned against a knee-jerk reaction, given the rise in registration and turnout, particularly among younger voters. "A blanket ban on being registered at two addresses would exclude those who for reasons of work or study need to be registered in two places," she said. "This cannot be an attempt to make it harder for young people and students to register to vote."

Graph data has seen a surge in popularity with the advent of machine learning over graphs as robust analytical tools. Yet, industry professionals face difficulties when attempting to employ methods like graph neural networks (GNNs) to tackle large-scale, practical issues due to the intrinsic interdependence found within graph data. Consequently, traditional approaches like utilizing a parameter server based on standard learning systems may not suffice since these assume data parallelism which isn't always applicable to graphs. Presently, many existing frameworks opt to keep graph data readily available in-memory across local machines or through external graph databases. Unfortunately, there are several disadvantages associated with this approach. For one, scalability becomes problematic due to limited memory capacity or restricted bandwidth between graph storage facilities and computational resources. Additionally, developing specialized graph storage solutions often involves sidestepping established technologies like MapReduce, leading to less efficient system designs. Lastly, while these setups typically prioritize model training, they frequently neglect optimizing the process of making predictions using graphs, resulting in fragmented systems.

In our research, we introduce AGL—a comprehensive, resilient, and cohesive framework designed to support both training and prediction tasks related to GNNs effectively. Our architecture embraces the concept of message passing integral to GNN computations. By constructing the k-hop neighborhood, which represents an exhaustively detailed subgraph around every node, alongside facilitating straightforward inferences derived from combining incoming edge values and distributing output values along outgoing edges via MapReduce operations, we enhance efficiency significantly. Moreover, since the k-hop neighborhood encapsulates all relevant information about each node, we can simplify the training process by leveraging independent parameter servers. Implemented on proven platforms, our AGL framework successfully completes training of a two-layer graph attention network on massive datasets comprising billions of nodes and hundreds of billions of edges in just 14 hours, followed by conducting inferences in approximately 1.2 hours.

This is the second projection for economic growth released by the Office for National Statistics (ONS), indicating a deceleration from the 0.7% pace recorded in Q2; however, it marks the 11th successive quarter of expansion. An increasing trade imbalance is cited as the cause of this reduced growth rate, with international trade exerting an all-time high negative influence on the GDP. From the previous figure of £7.7 billion in Q2, the trade surplus or shortfall expanded to £14.2 billion in Q3, despite exports rising by 0.9% and imports growing by 5.5%. Consequently, the trade disparity subtracted 1.5 percentage points from the GDP, representing the largest impact since data collection commenced in 1997. Furthermore, construction activities hindered progress, declining by 2.2%, whereas the service industry, responsible for over 75% of the national income, saw a rise of 0.7% during that period. In addition, industrial outputs such as manufacturing experienced a minor increase of 0.2%, and corporate capital expenditure is believed to have climbed by 2.2%. Lee Hopley, Chief Economist of EEF, noted no unexpected outcomes in these results, attributing steady advancement partly to sustained business investments. However, she emphasized the substantial negative role played by net trade due to relatively low export gains compared to significant import increases.

Most European nations were conducting tests related to these technologies around this period, yet detailed data from only four manufacturers—Krupp, Erhardt, Vickers Maxim, and Schneider—was made public by 1910. Krupp presented models derived from their standardized calibers like the 65mm 9-pounder, 75mm 12-pounder, and 105mm armaments. Erhardt showcased a similar 12-pounder model, whereas Vickers Maxim introduced a lighter 3-pounder variant alongside Schneider’s 47mm option. France debuted its own version of a balloon weapon in 1910, which featured an 11-pound cannon housed within a two-ton autonomous transport unit. Although targeting slow-moving balloons necessitated simpler aiming apparatuses, military strategists began contemplating solutions suitable for intercepting swiftly maneuvering aircraft.

Recent works examine the relationship between the communication structure and the performance of a group in a problem solving task. Some conclude that inefficient communication networks with long paths outperform efficient networks on the long run. Others find no influence of the network topology on group performance. We contribute to this discussion by examining the role of problem complexity. In particular, we study whether and how the complexity of the problem at hand moderates the influence of the communication network on group performance. Results obtained from multi-agent modelling suggest that problem complexity indeed has an influence. We observe an influence of the network only for problems of moderate difficulty. For easier or harder problems, the influence of network topology becomes weaker or irrelevant, which offers a possible explanation for inconsistencies in the literature.

The cosmos lacks an instruction guide that has been discovered so far. The scientific process involves probing the universe, examining its responses, formulating hypotheses, testing them further through various methods. If these observations align with our predictions, they become accepted theories unless new anomalages arise that require us to revise our understanding. In essence, science operates through four main steps: (1) proposing hypotheses; (2) anticipating specific behaviors under particular conditions; (3) conducting experiments to compare actual outcomes with predicted ones; (4) modifying or discarding theories when experimental data contradicts them. This cycle continues until sufficient accuracy is achieved. Initially, physics focused on studying everyday objects such as tables, but as knowledge expanded, it ventured into uncharted territories involving higher speeds, greater distances, and smaller scales. While empirical evidence plays a significant role in physics, theoretical physics primarily relies on mathematical models. These theories may initially lack direct evidence, yet advancements in technology could potentially validate or invalidate them, leading to new discoveries like Hawking radiation or Higgs Boson. Therefore, the primary constraint faced by empirical sciences is the technological limitations inherent in their tools and equipment.

Colour perception occurs through specialized cells called cones located at the back of your eyes. These cones come in three types, each sensitive to specific colour ranges such as red/green, blue/yellow, or black/white. Prolonged exposure to a single hue can cause fatigue in the corresponding cones, resulting in an opposing colour appearance known as an afterimage. For instance, staring at a yellow spot followed by viewing a blank white surface would yield a blue afterimage. Interestingly, this blue might seem brighter against the white yet retain its blueness and even give off a luminescent quality, termed "self-luminous blue." Similar effects occur with stygian colours when transitioning from a coloured object to a black background, creating a vividly dark hue. Another variation arises when observing one colour before shifting focus to a pure saturation of its complementary colour, leading to an intensified afterimage. Although these chimeric colours feel real, they aren't direct products of our visual system nor replicable via conventional light sources; their existence results from complex interactions within our brains.

This work examines the possibility, performance limits, and associated costs for a self-sustained relay to transmit its own covert information to a destination on top of forwarding the source's information. This relay is only aware of the original source's information and its own output, but not of the destination's information. By using the covert transmission of the relay's own information as an additional source of energy for transmitting the source's information, we show that this relay can achieve a rate of transmission close to the transmission rate of a perfect source-relay channel. We also show that this relay can achieve a lower transmission cost than a source-relay channel, where the relay transmits the source's information without using the relay's own energy. However, we show that this relay cannot outperform the source-relay channel by much when the source's energy is significantly higher than the relay's energy. In other words, the relay cannot gain much advantage by transmitting its own information covertly, compared to transmitting the source's information over a source-relay channel.

Structured d -DNNFs and SDDs are restricted negation normal form circuits used in knowledge compilation as target languages into which propositional theories are compiled. Structuredness is imposed by so-called vtrees. By definition SDDs are restricted structured d -DNNFs. Beame and Liew (2015) as well as Bova and Szeider (2017) mentioned the question whether structured d -DNNFs are really more general than SDDs w.r.t. polynomial-size representations (w.r.t. the number of Boolean variables the represented functions are defined on.) The main result in the paper is the proof that a function can be represented by SDDs of polynomial size if the function and its complement have polynomial-size structured d -DNNFs that respect the same vtree. Conversely, the Church of Rome fixed the equinox at 25 March until 342 AD, employing an alternative methodology for determining the lunar phase. With these parameters, Easter dates fluctuated between 22 March and 25 April according to Alexandria and from 5 March to 21 April per Rome's calendar, with the latter limit aligning with the traditional celebration of Rome's foundation and a concurrent pagan feast.

As a software engineer, feeling engaged at work is crucial for both personal job satisfaction and team productivity. It is all too easy to fall into a routine, feeling like a cog in a machine, and that makes it difficult to achieve the sense of purpose that everyone craves in their work. Here are some helpful tips for software engineers looking to feel more engaged on the job: 1. Set clear goals: It's easy to get lost in the details, but taking time to set clear goals can help immensely. Having benchmarks and targets that you want to reach will give your work direction, and a sense of accomplishment when you achieve them. 2. Rally around the team: Don't underestimate the power of a team working together. Supporting your colleagues can help take your work to a higher level, and build camaraderie that you never knew was possible. 3. Focus on accomplishments: Don't let yourself get bogged down in the day-to-day minutia. Celebrating small accomplishments is a key aspect of feeling engaged and motivated. 4. Keep learning: Software engineering is an ever-changing field. Make sure you stay abreast of new developments and trends by attending conferences, following blogs and articles, and seeking out learning opportunities. 5. Take breaks: Finally, remember to take breaks every so often. Stepping away from the work can help renew your energy and focus, and allow you to come back to work feeling refreshed and ready to tackle the next challenge. By incorporating these tips into your daily work routine, you'll find that it's easier than ever to feel engaged and motivated in your role as a software engineer.
