I think that not eating meat is cruel.. specifically NOT eating lamb, chicken, pork, etc. Further, they must be killed in a humane manner (as humane as possible). The one point I want to bring up ahead of time is that the animals MUST be respected and not abused and given a good life. This specifically excludes factory farming which I don't support. There are basically three choices for an animal: - the animal can not be born - the animal could live in the wild - the animal could be raised on a farm I think it's better for the animal to exist. Further, I think it's MORE ethical for these animals to exist. And the money to pay for them has to come from somewhere which is from the market ... The alternative is to live wild. If you have objections to killing an animal in captivity, how do you feel about them dying in the wild? Starvation, predation, disease. These aren't fun ways to die. So in conclusion. It's far better for everyone involved to eat

Upon examining a bacterium closely, one would find it to be a simple structure composed primarily of various chemicals enclosed within a protective outer layer, along with additional components such as appendages for mobility. This concoction consists mainly of water mixed with electrolytes and intricate carbon-based compounds. Subjecting the bacterium to high temperatures causes internal pressure buildup leading to the breakage of its exterior barrier. Consequently, the contents leak out and disperse into surrounding liquid, undergoing transformation similar to food during cooking processes. However, due to the minuscule quantity involved and thorough dispersion within vast amounts of water, it remains inconspicuous and harmless. Similarly, when exposed to dry heat via baking or frying, the bacterium's membrane ruptures but lacks sufficient moisture for efficient removal; hence, once all fluids evaporate, a barely visible residue remains.

Boiling water to eliminate bacteria results in their demise, yet remnants persist within the water. Steam distillation effectively separates water from impurities, including deceased bacteria, leaving them behind upon condensation. Furthermore, filtration systems efficiently eradicate viruses and nonviable bacteria from water sources. Even though bacteria perish, they might release potentially hazardous substances resistant to boiling. Therefore, depyrogenation involves eliminating or nullifying these harmful agents present in solutions.

In essence, the decomposition of bacteria resembles the softening of vegetables or meats albeit on a significantly smaller scale. Despite the destruction of bacteria, traces remain unless specific procedures are employed, particularly when sterile equipment necessitates rigorous cleansing prior to usage to expedite recovery. These organisms either rupture or are consumed by immune cells (macrophages), ultimately becoming sustenance for other life forms or decomposing entirely.

Heat treatment, such as autoclaving, ensures the elimination of pathogens, leaving nothing behind. The resulting fragments serve as nourishment for other microbes or degrade completely over time.

I used to fear death, like most people do. But when Death spared my life and granted me immortality, it changed my perspective entirely. Death became my friend, my only companion, the only one who had been with me through centuries. As time passed, Death grew more occupied with his work, and our chance encounters became fewer and farther between. I couldn't help feeling a sense of loneliness, even though I had watched the rise and fall of kingdoms, witnessed the birth and death of entire civilizations. So I decided to spend my immortality in a noble pursuit - the quest for world peace, the end of war, and the cure for diseases that had troubled humanity for centuries. I knew these were lofty goals, but I had centuries of time at my disposal. I started with small steps, working with local communities and gradually building up momentum towards a larger scale. Centuries turned into millennia as I devoted myself to this cause. Wars broke out; diseases spread, empires rose and fell, but my determination never waned. I traveled the world, seeking out the knowledge and insights that would help me achieve my goals. Then one fine day, I had finally succeeded. The world was at peace, and diseases had been eradicated. It was as if a great weight had been lifted off my shoulders. For centuries, I had been working towards this momentous point in history, and at last, I had achieved it. But the greatest joy was still to come. For as I journeyed onwards, I knew that Death would be waiting for me at the end of my road. I knew that we would be reunited at last, and I would have my friend back. The thought of spending eternity with my old friend kept me going through all these years of toil and struggle. And when my journey ended, and I met Death once again, it was as if we had never been apart. We picked up our friendship where we had left off centuries ago, and I knew that I had spent my immortality wisely. For I had created a better world not just for humanity, but for my old friend as well.

Weakly-supervised learning based on, e.g., partially labelled images or image-tags, is currently attracting significant attention in CNN segmentation as it can mitigate the need for full and laborious pixelvoxel annotations. Enforcing high-order (global) inequality constraints on the network output (for instance, to constrain the size of the target region) can leverage unlabeled data, guiding the training process with domain-specific knowledge. Inequality constraints are very flexible because they do not assume exact prior knowledge. However, constrained Lagrangian dual optimization has been largely avoided in deep networks, mainly for computational tractability reasons. To the best of our knowledge, the method of Pathak et al. is the only prior work that addresses deep CNNs with linear constraints in weakly supervised segmentation. It uses the constraints to synthesize fully-labeled training masks (proposals) from weak labels, mimicking full supervision and facilitating dual optimization. We propose to introduce a differentiable penalty, which enforces inequality constraints directly in the loss function, avoiding expensive Lagrangian dual iterates and proposal generation. From constrained-optimization perspective, our simple penalty-based approach is not optimal as there is no guarantee that the constraints are satisfied. However, surprisingly, it yields substantially better results than the Lagrangian-based constrained CNNs in , while reducing the computational demand for training. By annotating only a small fraction of the pixels, the proposed approach can reach a level of segmentation performance that is comparable to full supervision on three separate tasks. While our experiments focused on basic linear constraints such as the target-region size and image tags, our framework can be easily extended to other non-linear constraints, e.g., invariant shape moments and other region statistics . Therefore, it has the potential to close the gap between weakly and fully supervised learning in semantic medical image segmentation. Our code is publicly available.

Functional programming operates under the principle that invoking a function with identical inputs yields consistent outputs. To achieve this, functional languages abstain from utilizing any form of mutable state. For instance, a function like `add(a, b)` that computes the sum of two numbers is acceptable within this paradigm. Conversely, a function such as `addToAccount(a, accountNo)`, which modifies the balance of an account based on its current state, does not align with functional programming principles due to its variable output. The benefit of this approach lies in enhancing code reliability through improved testability and predictability. Although functional programming supports immutable objects without internal state changes, object-oriented programming revolves around encapsulation by grouping related data and behavior into cohesive units known as classes and objects. Unlike functional programming, object-oriented programming retains state information within the object's properties. While object-oriented code allows for the inclusion of functions, these do not necessarily need to adhere to functional purity. Consider an account class; while you can define a method to retrieve the account balance, it might yield varying results upon successive calls if the balance fluctuates—an action prohibited in functional programming languages. In some countries, formal education can take place through home schooling. Informal learning may be assisted by a teacher occupying a transient or ongoing role, such as a family member, friend of the child, neighbour and so on. The informal status of these teachers means that their qualifications are not subject to institutional recognition; furthermore they lack any formal training in teaching. However there is no reason why it would necessarily follow that this means all schools should have equal professional standards for teachers. A number of factors influence whether an individual will consider taking up the job of giving one form of instruction over another (Green Jacobs 2004). In many cases it comes down to practicality -the quality of the infanttoddler's environment, the proximity of other children who could act as model peers, adequate accommodation etc. These issues usually do not apply equally across different social groups within society. This paper argues that although parents' use of informal educational arrangements varies considerably between nations, state policies towards private provision tend to reflect similar underlying values about how best to nurture children's success. This has implications both when analysing what constitutes effective parenting practices which promote early literacy development and also considering the implications of changing patterns of employment at young ages. It is important to keep in mind that people's attitudes about the appropriateness of accessing alternative forms of formal schooling vary according to where people live, age, gender and level of income. Evidence from India suggests that mothers with higher levels of schooling have significantly larger children, even after controlling for wealth effects (Grossman 2002). The findings in studies like these raise questions about the extent to which characteristics associated with high socio-economic status affect fertility decisions independently of women's choices regarding labour supply andor co-operation within couples. An extensive body of international literature examines the relationship between mothers' participation in paid work and various aspects of children's cognitive and non-cognitive outcomes. We introduce Cluster Pruning (CP), a technique aimed at reducing and speeding up the performance of deep neural networks. CP eliminates redundant filters through clustering, utilizing characteristics extracted from both input and output weight links. Compared to previous methodologies, our strategy addresses two main challenges: (1) uneven filter removal: CP effectively identifies the optimal quantity of filters to eliminate across different layers of a neural network, unlike earlier techniques which apply uniform pruning or rely on complex procedures like manual sensitivity assessment or reinforcement learning to figure it out; (2) one-time execution: By incorporating CUP into the initial training stage, we've developed CUP-Single Shot (CUP-SS), resulting in substantial reductions in overall training duration when juxtaposed against conventional pruning processes. Upon thorough testing using various data sets (such as MNIST, CIFAR-10, and ImageNet) and architectures (like VGG-16, Resnets-183456), we demonstrate that CUP surpasses current cutting-edge solutions. Particularly, CUP-SS delivers a 2.2 flops decrease for an Imagenet-trained Resnet-50 model whilst maintaining a maximum deviation of only 0.9 in top-5 precision. Additionally, it cuts down training times by more than 14 hours relative to standard Resnet-50 configurations. For replication purposes, our code is accessible via this link.

Video moment retrieval is to search the moment that is most relevant to the given natural language query. Existing methods are mostly trained in a fully-supervised setting, which requires the video moment annotation for each query, which is very expensive and time-consuming. To tackle this problem, we propose a semi-supervised video moment retrieval (SMR) approach to exploit the semantic information in the video moment caption, which is less expensive and readily available. Our SMR approach consists of two components: a) a cross-modal semantic attention model that exploits the cross-modal semantic consistency between the video moment caption and the query to align the video moment with the query, and b) a self-supervised video moment pre-training (VMP) model that aims to exploit the consistency between the video moment caption and the video moment to generate the semantic representation of video moment caption, in order to train a video moment encoder for moment retrieval. In addition, we also propose a novel end-to-end SMR framework to jointly train these two components, which is able to mutually promote each other. Extensive experiments conducted on THUMOS14 show that our method achieves the state-of-the-art performance.

LTE in the unlicensed band (LTE-U) is a promising solution to overcome the scarcity of the wireless spectrum. However, to reap the benefits of LTE-U, it is essential to maintain its effective coexistence with WiFi systems. Such a coexistence, hence, constitutes a major challenge for LTE-U deployment. In this paper, the problem of unlicensed spectrum sharing among WiFi and LTE-U system is studied. In particular, a fair time sharing model based on ruin theory is proposed to share redundant spectral resources from the unlicensed band with LTE-U without jeopardizing the performance of the WiFi system. Fairness among both WiFi and LTE-U is maintained by applying the concept of probability of ruin. In particular, the probability of ruin is used to perform efficient duty-cycle allocation in LTE-U, so as to provide fairness to the WiFi system and maintain certain WiFi performance. Simulation results show that the proposed ruin-based algorithm provides better fairness to the WiFi system as compared to equal duty-cycle sharing among WiFi and LTE-U.

Recently, there has been significant online debate concerning the DC Circuit rulings on Net Neutrality. Initially, like many others, I believed that the court should not differentiate between telecommunications carriers and information service providers, thus excluding ISPs from net neutrality regulations. However, upon reflection, it seems that forcing ISPs into compliance with Net Neutrality laws could do more harm than good by stifling innovation, enabling monopolies, and burdening the industry with excessive legal challenges. For instance, if we look at how Comcast operates without Net Neutrality, imagine them charging extra fees to Netflix for bandwidth usage. As a result, Netflix would have to pass these costs onto its customers, leading to dissatisfaction among consumers and potentially losing business. Therefore, despite concerns about monopolization, it's essential to recognize that neither the internet was ever truly neutral nor completely dominated by one entity. Enforcing strict Net Neutrality might inadright unintentionally lead to negative consequences for both the industry and consumers alike.

Christopher Tate, who also runs Donington Park circuit, said most of the British industry was in "Motorsport Valley," in central England counties. The Heads of the Valleys Development Company, which runs the Circuit of Wales, has said up to 6,000 jobs could be created by the project. Mr Tate, a director of the Association of Motor Racing Circuit Owners, told the BBC's Good Morning Wales programme there had always been "an eyebrow raised" about some of the claims made about the size of the proposed Circuit of Wales. He stressed it was not a question of not wanting more competition, but being "surprised and concerned" about the figures involved. "When it came to the point that it was apparent that private investment felt it needed to be underwritten by the government of Wales, more eyebrows were raised, as you can imagine, among the members of our association - 17 of them, including circuits of course in Wales at Pembrey and on Anglesey - that said'really? Wouldn't be nice if all our private investors got underwritten by our government?'." He said the recent announcement by First Minister Carwyn Jones that the TVR car company would establish a new factory in the Ebbw Vale enterprise zone and bring about 150 jobs, was still "a long way short of the much-vaunted 6,000." "That number depends on the building of hotels and restaurants and other factory units and industrial units and so on," he said. "Right across the UK - not just in Wales - there is not a shortage of empty industrial space at the moment. "The second [point] is, the British motor sport industry is very much focused on what they call'Motorsport Valley' - running approximately from Oxford up in a loop through Northamptonshire towards Leicestershire and Derbyshire. "So it doesn't matter if someone had suggested that a new motor racing track be built in Cornwall or in Aberdeen or in Ebbw Vale or, for that matter, in Norwich. Machine learning models are shown to be vulnerable to adversarial examples. While most of the existing methods for adversarial attack and defense work on 2D image domains, a few recent methods have been proposed for 3D shape domains. The underlying assumptions, design principles, and limitations of these methods are not well-understood, leaving the 3D domain vulnerable to adversarial attacks. We propose a new attack method that is more efficient and easier to apply than existing methods, as it requires neither specialized 3D shape editing tools nor advanced knowledge of 3D shape representation. We validate the attack method on four common deep neural networks using the ModelNet40 dataset and demonstrate that 3D shapes are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. We further investigate the robustness of adversarially attacked 3D shape models and show that attacking a 3D shape model is as effective as attacking its 2D projection counterpart. 3D shape models are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. We propose a simple method for adversarial attack and show that the 3D shape models are as vulnerable as their 2D projection counterparts.

Research conducted by scientists from the Stanford University School of Medicine, which was featured in the American Journal of Human Genetics under the title "Genetic Structure, Self-Identified Race/Ethnicity, and Confounding in Case-Control Association Studies," disputes the notion that race is solely a societal concept. According to one of the study's authors, Neil Rish, they examined the relationship between genetic makeup (determined through microsatellite markers) and how individuals perceive their own race. The results showed an almost perfect alignment, with a 99.9% agreement between both aspects. Interestingly, the data revealed more inconsistency when comparing self-reported gender against genetic information from the X chromosome. This suggests that even categories like sex can present issues and that distinctions exist between sex and gender, potentially leading to discrepancies between personal identification and biological factors. Furthermore, this highlights the presence of sexism within society.

This study introduces a comprehensive framework designed to tackle various stochastic optimal control issues related to robot navigation and management within intricate settings. To address challenges stemming from extensive choice spaces and elaborate surroundings, we implement two pivotal strategies: (a) applying a diffusion wavelet methodology for constructing a layered state space representation via a Markov chain; and (b) employing a desirabilibity function-oriented depiction of the Markov decision process (MDP), which facilitates the efficient derivation of the best course of action. Within our suggested model, initially, a broad strategy encompassing far-reaching temporal transitions between states is developed through a rough approximation of an MDP characterized by basic scales in the abstract hierarchy. Subsequently, a more granular regional plan is devised by resolving another MDP centered around specific portions of the state spectrum, informed by the preceding overview. This multi-level scheme subsequently enables us to derive a flawless time-optimal control directive under a diminishing horizon regimen. Finally, illustrative simulations showcase the effectiveness and soundness of this novel technique.

Luther's disappearance during his return trip back to Wittenberg was planned. Frederick III had him intercepted on his way home in the forest near Wittenberg by masked horsemen who were ordered not to kill Luther but only capture him and take him into custody for a while, then release him once they were sure he was safe from further trouble. After this incident, there was still high tension between Waldgrave of Hesse-Kassel and Martin Luther; more than ever before because of their respective roles as rulers within the Holy Roman Empire. For example, when Hahnenburg transferred to Hesse-Cassel after Hahnenberg died at age 50 in 1541, the new Elector John George I (died 1552) initially did not allow Luther open access through the Electoral territories immediately upon taking office. This led to tensions that culminated in the War of the League of Augsburg which lasted until 1548. In addition, the dispute over money that resulted in the death sentence against Johann Tetzel, one of Luther's chief opponents among German clergy whom Luther wanted executed, sparked what became known as the "Tetzel war" or the "Money controversy," involving many other Catholic officials throughout Germany whose financial interests would be adversely affected if the Church began accepting funds collected outside its own structures rather than just tithes paid directly to church coffers. This event also contributed significantly to the ongoing religious reformation within the State of Bavaria where it became evident that a break with Rome might eventually have serious economic consequences for the Imperial city-state. With tensions increasing along these lines, Pope Leo XII decided early in 1543 to send an envoy named Cardinal Cajetan to try to resolve some outstanding issues between himself, Emperor Charles V and Archduke Ferdinand II (the future King of Bohemia). Unfortunately, Cajetan arrived too late: Luther was already preparing his controversial Theses responses to all those he felt had criticized him unfairly just prior to Cajetans arrival and the turmoil arising out of them ensured that he managed to escape once again from the clutches of the Papacy long enough to provoke another round of violence in the so-called "Thirty Years' War," ultimately resulting in the Reformation being accepted in part of the empire about 25 years later rather than fully creating a schism within the Catholic faith itself like happened in France due largely to French support for anti-Catholic reformers such as John Calvin.

Abstract: The vision of Organic Computing addresses challenges that arise in the design of future information systems that are comprised of numerous, heterogeneous, resource-constrained and error-prone components or devices. Here, the notion organic particularly highlights the idea that, in order to be manageable, such systems should exhibit self-organization, self-adaptation and self-healing characteristics similar to those of biological systems. In recent years, the principles underlying many of the interesting characteristics of natural systems have been investigated from the perspective of complex systems science, particularly using the conceptual framework of statistical physics and statistical mechanics. In this article, we review some of the interesting relations between statistical physics and networked systems and discuss applications in the engineering of organic networked computing systems with predictable, quantifiable and controllable self- properties.

In an era when big data are becoming the norm, there is less concern with the quantity but more with the quality and completeness of the data. In many disciplines, data are collected from heterogeneous sources, resulting in multi-view or multi-modal datasets. The missing data problem has been challenging to address in multi-view data analysis. Especially, when certain samples miss an entire view of data, it creates the missing view problem. Classic multiple imputations or matrix completion methods are hardly effective here when no information can be based on in the specific view to impute data for such samples. The commonly-used simple method of removing samples with a missing view can dramatically reduce sample size, thus diminishing the statistical power of a subsequent analysis. In this paper, we propose a novel approach for view imputation via generative adversarial networks (GANs), which we name by VIGAN. This approach first treats each view as a separate domain and identifies domain-to-domain mappings via a GAN using randomly-sampled data from each view, and then employs a multi-modal denoising autoencoder (DAE) to reconstruct the missing view from the GAN outputs based on paired data across the views. Then, by optimizing the GAN and DAE jointly, our model enables the knowledge integration for domain mappings and view correspondences to effectively recover the missing view. Empirical results on benchmark datasets validate the VIGAN approach by comparing against the state of the art. The evaluation of VIGAN in a genetic study of substance use disorders further proves the effectiveness and usability of this approach in life science.

In the autonomous regions of Bavaria, Saxony, and Thuringia, it is known as the State Government (Staatsregierung), whereas in the other seven areas, they use the term Land Government (Landesregierung). Prior to January 1, 2000, Bavaria operated under a two-chamber legislature comprising an electorally chosen Landtag and a Senate representing significant social and economic entities within the state. However, this structure was discarded after a public vote in 199 rightfully so. Governance in Berlin, Bremen, and Hamburg differs somewhat from that in other territories. Here, the administrative arm includes a Senate composed of around eight individuals appointed by the local assembly; these officials fulfill responsibilities similar to those held by ministers elsewhere. Corresponding to the role of Minister-President found in the greater provinces, we see the titles of Senatspräsident (Senate President) in Bremen, Erster Bürgermeister (First Mayor) in Hamburg, and Regierender Bürgermeister (Governing Mayor) in Berlin. Additionally, the legislative body in Berlin is named the Abgeordnetenhaus (Representative House), while Bremen and Hamburg feature a Burgerschaft. Meanwhile, the governing councils in the remaining 13 locations are identified as Landtags (Provincial Assemblies).

Britain's imperialist ambitions can be seen as early as the sixteenth century. In 1599 the British East India Company was established and was chartered by Queen Elizabeth in the following year to explore the New World, set up a settlement at Jamestown (Virginia), establish trade links with America and create an army of indentured labour for the growing colonies. The expansionist policy encouraged England to send troops to fight against the Spanish, who had captured Montserrat from Portugal on 4 May 1602 - followed two years later by Guadeloupe - but it was not until 1703 that Edward VI launched the Royal Navy's first expedition across the Atlantic ocean. The king spent almost four months travelling through the Caribbean before he turned his attentions towards the continent of North America. He arrived in Quebec City in September 1704, after which Edward VII embarked on a grand tour of Canada, spending time on Lake Superior and visiting Ottawa. After delivering a speech at Fort Frontenac, near Montreal, he returned home in July 1705 only to embark again on his second voyage around the world. This trip saw him completing the first circumnavigation of the globe when he sailed round South America back into Europe. On this occasion also, however, he could find no support among those residing in France. So, in November 1707 he paid another visit to Ireland where he met with some success. The French King Louis XIV responded enthusiastically to his invitation to come to Paris; so Edward travelled south-eastwards in order to gain his favour while Louis XVI observed developments in England. As part of preparations for the ensuing Treaty of Fontainebleau held in December 1708, Louis XIII gave permission for the king of Great Britain to sell arms and ammunition to the Irish Parliamentary Army. While there were still protests over the sale of arms to England as well as concerns about the effects of the Napoleonic Wars on the fledgling nation, many devout Catholics welcomed the opportunity to obtain British weapons. The treaty proved successful: Edward sent 50,000 worth of munitions and armed mercenaries to Ireland during 1709 while Louis XV appointed Edward VII's brother Cecil Lord High Admiral of the English Channel. Meanwhile a new British presence began to swell north of the border. The Duke of York led more than 3,500 men to Scotland in July 1710 while Charles I made good use of his position as Prince Regent to launch several military expeditions in Ireland. His successes included capturing Dublin Castle on 13 March 1712 when he briefly occupied the city with 1,200 soldiers but eventually retreated after the Marquis de Lafayette defeated the garrison. By then, however, the attitudes toward Great Britain changed significantly in Northern Ireland and the realm became involved once more in the Seven Years' War between England and France. After the Treaty of Utrecht in 1713, Anglo-Irish relations took their worst turn since James II left office in 1688. It is estimated that the war cost thousands of lives on both sides at a cost of over 1 billion. The royal family remained close to France throughout the conflict although young Anne Boleyn, Princess Charlotte, King George III and the Earl of St Albans all visited Paris in pursuit of peace. During the troubles, Parliament passed a series of laws restricting the power of the Church of England, specifically in relation to intermarriage between Anglicans and Protestants. However, disagreements over how much control over religious matters should remain within the church itself resulted in considerable public animosity arising between the clergy and the wider population. Although popular support for the Catholic cause continued to grow, many people saw themselves as being divided into sections of loyalists and anti-loyalists. Ultimately, the civil wars and subsequent riots destroyed much parts of Belfast and created further divisions along sectarian lines.

In 1935, the Mutual Radio Network became the first commercial radio network to broadcast in color. In 1937, CBS's parent company, the National Broadcasting Company, Inc., (NBC), purchased the Mutual Broadcasting System, Inc., (MBS) for 3.5 million, becoming the nation's largest radio network. In 1939, Mutual debuted a new, new look for the network, which included its first color kinescope broadcast, from the Griffith Stadium in Los Angeles. Mutual also hired Hollywood's most famous disc jockey, Jack Martin, to host the network's flagship morning program, "Jack and Joe." This was followed by the premiere of the "All-Star Big Band," in 1941. 1940s-1960s Mutual's "Big Band" was an American radio program that aired from 1941 to 1961. Hosted by Jack Martin, the program featured a combination of musical talent and comedy sketches, and was Mutual's most popular show. On October 10, 1947, Mutual debuted "Your Music Is Heard," a 15-minute program that was heard on 56 stations across the United States. The program was sponsored by Colgate-Palmolive, and featured jazz music, comedians, and musical performances. "Your Music Is Heard" was discontinued after two seasons. In 1950, Mutual began using the "Mutual Broadcasting System" name, which was abbreviated to "Mutual" in most markets. The same year, Mutual introduced a new color logo and a new theme song, "The Light of Day," composed by Bennie Benjamin and Milton Goetz. In 1952, Mutual premiered a 15-minute series, "The Bob Hope Show." Hope was one of Mutual's most popular performers, and the program was carried by nearly every Mutual affiliate in the United States. Mutual also aired "The John Charles Daly Show," a popular comedy series that ran from 1951 to 1954. Mutual's "Big Band" show was heard on radio and television in the United States, the United Kingdom, and Australia. In 1953, Mutual began using color television, with the introduction of "Mutual's Big Band in Color." In 1956, Mutual premiered "The Garry Moore Show." My sister and her family visited us recently from Connecticut. Her kids are really into horseback riding, and it was blizzard conditions at their house, so they wanted to take advantage of our nice weather to get on some horses. She found a Groupon for this place and purchased them for the whole family. Now, she lived in Arizona until she was thirty, so I'm surprised she wanted to do a western trail ride. It seemed a little gimmicky. I was expecting the owners and trail guides to be hamming it up for the tourists, calling us greenhorns and such. When we got there we had to fill out the insurance waivers, and everything seemed really disorganized. We had indicated that we were all going to wear helmets on the ride (I'd rather look stupid than have some dumb horse put me in a wheelchair) and they seemed irritated that we were trying to find helmets that actually fit, especially for the kids. The helmets were all stored on shelves inside and were dusty as heck. I got the idea that they just threw them up there after the previous trail ride without doing anything to sanitize them. Luckily, my head hasn't been itchy, so no lice. They could have an air compressor and some Lysol, at least, to blow the dust off and disinfect them. When we got out to the stables, they gave us a curt speech about safety and following the trail guide. They told us to always follow the horse in front of us, too, and never stray off the path. They then assigned us horses, based on our riding skills (indicated on the waiver). There was an older gentleman that seemed like he actually might have cared about the customers, but the younger guys definitely didn't. I was told to go to a horse toward the end of the stable. When I got there he was tied up, so I proceeded to climb on. One of the employees yelled at me to stop and came over with the stairs. Fair enough...they want people to be safe, I guess. There's no reason to yell, though. When I was getting on the horse he told me I smelled like sunscreen. I told him I didn't want skin cancer, and we were going to be baking in the sun for 1.5 hours, so yes, I did smell like sunscreen. He mockingly laughed and told me that he hasn't worn sunscreen since he was a teenager. Wow! That's impressive! You must be immune to ultraviolet rays. Well, if that chew in your lip doesn't give you cancer, you can rely on the sun as a back-up plan! When we finally got on the trail, the demeanor of the guides didn't get any better. I had a stubborn horse that was always trying to nibble on grass and weeds. They constantly yelled at me to get him moving so I wasn't holding up the line. Luckily my daughter's horse was obedient and didn't cause problems. I don't think I could handle them yelling at her. The ride itself was half-nice. I say this because it was hot and dusty for half of it, and somewhat shady and cool for the other half. The ride starts at the stable and progresses across flat scrubland for about ten minutes. You end up on a bluff overlooking the river, then go down a gully to get to the water. There were probably many good photo opportunities, but we weren't allowed to stop and take advantage, lest we get yelled at. Most of my pictures are of the backs of the riders in front of me. Those will look great on the Apple TV slideshow, for sure! We rode across the river a few times, saw some wild mustangs and looked for eagles. They said that the area is a protected eagle breeding ground, but unfortunately we didn't see any. My sister saw a good photo op when we were in the middle of the river, scooted her horse about three feet to the side and slowed it down. Of course, she was yelled at. We were hoping to have the guides give us some history of the area, maybe some info about the flora and fauna. Anything to make it an interesting ride. Our guide said one thing during the ride, and I don't even remember what it was, so it must have been really awe-inspiring and important. Oh, I almost forgot about one of the worst things! About halfway through the ride we were getting parched and asked about the water situation. The deal that we bought said that water was included. It may have been our fault for not asking about it at the beginning, but we were preoccupied with all of the insurance and helmet stuff. Anyway, the guide told us that the water was in a cooler by the stables. We told him that nobody informed us where the cooler was, or that we would need to grab a bottle before we left. We figured that they would have some in a saddle bag or at a stop on the trail. He said, well, you should have grabbed a bottle before you left the stables. Thanks, genius! When we finally got back to the stables, the water bottles were there, as promised. They were sitting outside in an ice-free cooler, baking in the sun. Ahhhh! Nice, hot water to quench the thirst! Thanks for the experience, Fort Mcdowell Adventures! I won't be back!

Combustion is a high-temperature exothermic redox (reduction-oxidation) chemical reaction. Oxygen is a very common, and fairly strong, oxidizing agent. It is not, however, strictly required for a fire. Some very severe fires can occur in dry wood without oxygen, such as soot blazes; these fire types are known as flashover type fires because they usually appear suddenly with an intense "flash" or explosion of flame at the surface. One of the most common causes of combustion is carbon monoxide poisoning from incomplete burning starting material that may contain relatively large amounts of carbon. Under normal conditions, the gas produced by incomplete combustion is used to heat the air entering an engine's cylinder. When there is insufficient fuel available to completely combust all of the gases emitted during burning andor when the composition of this mixture changes due to erosion of the carburetor components, then a rapid buildup of pressure occurs within the cylinder which will cause the piston to move upward rapidly, producing a powerful force on the crankshaft. This effect is called detonation. The phenomenon differs depending upon whether the operating point of the internal combustion engine is at peak power, near its compression top dead center (TDC), or just prior to TDC. In either case, if the condition continues for some time, the effects of excessive exhaust gases will be accompanied by a build up of thermal energy within the cylinders resulting in potentially catastrophic damage to the engine and its associated drive train. For instance, the engine pistons could become hot enough to ignite the adjacent oil or coolant. If the ignition source were a spark plug positioned directly across the gap between two piston rings during engine operation, rapid expansion of the ignited gas would result in extreme heating of the main bearings supporting the connecting shaft of the crankshaft causing them to burn out. If the ignition source was a coil end spark plug located adjacent one of the sides of the spark plug electrode (s), it would likely catch fire, and possibly explode forcing parts of the crankcase and transmission housing into contact with the side wall of the engine block. Using conventional spark plugs with current attempts to control engine knock from detonation is difficult and requires frequent replacement of spark plugs and modification of existing engines. More recently, attempts have been made to prevent detonation based on the idea of using relatively low levels of anti-knock agents instead of conventional spark plugs to provide adequate charge conditioning. Numerous patents describe various methods and devices for injecting substances into the intake air stream to add balance to the well-known rich (i.e., excess air) system used to produce maximum engine horsepower and torque during steady state running. Such systems generally aim to enhance the efficiency of the EGR process by increasing the amount of fresh air provided to the cylinders under certain circumstances. However, these systems are less effective than desired in preventing undesirable events like blow-by gasses escaping from the combustion chamber through the intake passages toward the turbocharger compressor, and thereby increasing the risk of turbocharger failure. These escape lines must typically be carefully designed to minimize the flow from each passage, but even small losses make it more difficult to maintain optimal turbocharging performance, particularly in cold climates where boost pressures drop significantly after engine warmup. Other attempts to prevent detonation include the addition of silicon dioxide or zinc oxide particles in the fuel charge by use of a particle accelerator device (pump). See U.S. Pat. Nos. 4,178,824, 5,106,993 and 6,245,944, the entire disclosures of which are hereby incorporated herein by reference. See also WO 0103700 A1, the entire disclosure of which is hereby incorporated herein by reference. While these technologies do reduce knocking to varying degrees, the increased cost remains prohibitive compared with other means for achieving comparable results. Additionally, these inventions require careful maintenance procedures to detect the presence of any accumulation of sludge deposits or other unwanted materials on the wall surfaces of the injectors themselves.

In many physical systems, inputs related by intrinsic system symmetries are mapped to the same output. When inverting such systems, i.e., solving the associated inverse problems, there is no unique solution. This causes fundamental difficulties for deploying the emerging end-to-end deep learning approach. Using the generalized phase retrieval problem as an illustrative example, we show that careful symmetry breaking on the training data can help get rid of the difficulties and significantly improve the learning performance. We also extract and highlight the underlying mathematical principle of the proposed solution, which is directly applicable to other inverse problems.

Something Wicked this Way Comes, shown on a Sunday morning, featured the illusionist putting a plastic bag over his head and walking on broken glass. Broadcasting watchdog Ofcom said children could have imitated Brown's "clearly dangerous behaviour." It received five complaints about the show, which aired on UKTV's Watch channel on 6 December. UKTV said the programme was broadcast in error and was unsuitable for a pre-watershed transmission. In the 14-minute segment, Brown had sought to demonstrate a technique to limit pain and bleeding. He placed a transparent bag over his head and sealed it while a member of the audience tapped out his pulse rate on a drum. Once his pulse rate had slowed to a stop, Brown - who appeared to be in a state of semi-consciousness - removed the bag from his head and walked barefoot on a path of broken glass. At the end of the sequence, the camera zoomed on his feet to show that they had not bled as a result of contact with the glass. Ofcom said: "Plastic bags are a common household item that children frequently have access to without parental supervision. They also present a widely acknowledged risk of harm to young children. "Therefore, Ofcom took the view that Derren Brown's use of a plastic bag to asphyxiate himself was likely to be easily imitable by children in a manner that was harmful. "This was particularly because self-asphyxiation was presented as a way to carry out acts which would not normally be possible because of the bleeding and pain that resulted. "Further in this programme no negative consequences of self-asphyxiation were identified." Ofcom also found that Brown's use of swear words during the segment breached the code on offensive language before the watershed. UKTV said an internal investigation had revealed that "due to human error" the programme was "erroneously labelled" as being suitable for broadcast before the watershed. It said it had implemented additional safeguards to prevent the same mistake happening again.

TimeML is an XML-based schema for annotating temporal information over discourse. The standard has been used to annotate a variety of resources and is followed by a number of tools, the creation of which constitute hundreds of thousands of man-hours of research work. However, the current state of resources is such that many are not valid, or do not produce valid output, or contain ambiguous or custom additions and removals. Difficulties arising from these variances were highlighted in the TempEval-3 exercise, which included its own extra stipulations over conventional TimeML as a response. To unify the state of current resources, and to make progress toward easy adoption of its current incarnation ISO-TimeML, this paper introduces TimeML-strict: a valid, unambiguous, and easy-to-process subset of TimeML. We also introduce three resources - a schema for TimeML-strict; a validator tool for TimeML-strict, so that one may ensure documents are in the correct form; and a repair tool that corrects common invalidating errors and adds disambiguating markup in order to convert documents from the laxer TimeML standard to TimeML-strict.

Ann Jarvis first held a "Mother's Friendship Day" and tried popularizing it in 1868, but died in 1905 before it really caught on outside of a few locales. In 1877, because of a dispute between temperance and anti-temperance groups where some anti-temperance goons forced some prohibitionists to get publicly drunk, which caused a Reverend to get all verclempt, as his sons were among those involuntarily intoxicated, and become unable to finish his sermon, a woman jumped to his defense to finish his sermon for him, and called on mothers to join the temperance movement. In gratitude, the sons began a campaign to return to the town and pay tribute to her every year on the second Sunday in May, and urged their business contacts to do likewise. In 1910, Ann Jarvis's daughter, Anna Jarvis, got West Virginia to recognize Mother's Day as a holiday, and other states quickly followed suit. In 1914, Congress passed a resolution declaring the second Sunday in May as Mother's Day, and requested a proclamation, and the next day, President Wilson proclaimed the first national Mother's Day.

In machine learning, error back-propagation in multi-layer neural networks (deep learning) has been impressively successful in supervised and reinforcement learning tasks. As a model for learning in the brain, however, deep learning has long been regarded as implausible, since it relies in its basic form on a non-local plasticity rule. To overcome this problem, energy-based models with local contrastive Hebbian learning were proposed and tested on a classification task with networks of rate neurons. We extended this work by implementing and testing such a model with networks of leaky integrate-and-fire neurons. Preliminary results indicate that it is possible to learn a non-linear regression task with hidden layers, spiking neurons and a local synaptic plasticity rule.

Much of the work of the Scottish Parliament is done in committee. The role of committees is stronger in the Scottish Parliament than in other parliamentary systems, partly as a result of the Parliament's relatively small size. Committees are used to investigate issues in more detail than possible in plenary sessions. Committees can consider and report on any matter, but this will normally be done on the basis of a specific topic. Committees have an advisory role in relation to Scottish law and the work of the Scottish Government, but have no power to make laws. The Law Society of Scotland, for example, submits to the Justice Committee evidence on all Bills affecting Scots law. Most parliamentary committees in the Scottish Parliament are "statutory" committees. This means that they are established and run by the Parliament under section 30 of the Scotland Act 1998. The full list of statutory committees is given in the Scottish Parliament Standing Orders. The most important statutory committee is the Public Audit and Post-legislative Scrutiny Committee, which was created in 1999. Deep learning frameworks have achieved significant advancements across numerous practical scenarios. Recent research has attempted to construct intricate network structures through iterative unfolding of specific optimization processes that incorporate elements related to the tasks at hand. Regrettably, because network parameters fluctuate dynamically during this process, the resulting deep propagation networks fail to exhibit the same favorable convergence characteristics inherent to the initial optimization procedures. In response, this study introduces an innovative proximal unrolling approach aimed at creating deep learning models by merging empirically validated network designs with abundant insights drawn from the tasks involved. Significantly, it has been theoretically demonstrated that (1) the iterations produced by our unrolled deep models will consistently reach a critical point within a defined variational energy landscape, and (2) our methodology remains capable of extracting prior knowledge from training datasets to produce stable propagation outcomes, even if complete task details are absent. A wide array of tests conducted on diverse real-life applications affirms both the theoretical convergence properties and the efficacy of the developed deep models.

We study black-box reductions from mechanism design to algorithm design for welfare maximization in settings of incomplete information. Given oracle access to an algorithm for an underlying optimization problem, the goal is to design a mechanism that maximizes social welfare. We consider the setting where agents have different underlying types, and the algorithm designer has no knowledge of these types. We show that any such problem can be reduced to an algorithmic problem in which the algorithm designer is given access to a black-box optimization oracle. Specifically, we prove a general result showing that for any welfare-maximizing mechanism, there exists an equivalent algorithm that maximizes social welfare when given access to a black-box optimization oracle. We then provide several examples which demonstrate the generality of this result. Our results suggest that black-box reductions from mechanism design to algorithm design may be more widely applicable than previously thought. Additionally, our work provides new insight into the connections between mechanism design and algorithms for welfare maximization.

During the Cambrian period, Gondwana had a mild climate. West Antarctica was partially in the Northern Hemisphere, and during this period large amounts of sandstones, limestones and shales were deposited. East Antarctica was at the equator, where sea floor invertebrates and trilobites flourished in the tropical seas. By the start of the Devonian period (416 Ma), Gondwana was in more southern latitudes and the climate was cooler, though fossils of land plants are known from this time. Sand and silts were laid down in what is now the Ellsworth, Horlick and Pensacola Mountains. Glaciation began at the end of the Devonian period (360 Ma), as Gondwana became centered on the South Pole and the climate cooled, though flora remained. During the Permian period, the land became dominated by seed plants such as Glossopteris, a pteridosperm which grew in swamps. Over time these swamps became deposits of coal in the Transantarctic Mountains. Towards the end of the Permian period, continued warming led to a dry, hot climate over much of Gondwana.

Similarly, acquiring the exact same assortment of goods in 2015 would necessitate nearly fifteen times the amount spent using 1971 currency. This trend arises because individuals tend to transition towards utilizing more effective commodities with advancing technology over time. A compelling example can be found in Agatha Christie's life story, which states, "At no point did I imagine myself affluent enough to possess a vehicle; yet paradoxically, I was destitute enough not to hire any assistance." Comparable circumstances existed during the 1970s era, where certain millionaires lacked access to personal computers, although many other essentials such as education, clerical aid, and accommodation remained relatively affordable.

Moreover, inflation metrics do not primarily aim to assess alterations in living costs. Instead, these indices gauge 'core inflation,' which signifies the escalation in overall prices attributable solely to fluctuations in monetary demand and supply, excluding factors related to resource availability and productivity enhancements. Consequently, discrepancies may arise between actual cost-of-living changes, shifts in currency exchange rates, and calculated inflation data. Despite seemingly impractical comparisons between consumer goodsets spanning four decades, economists persistently compute inflation statistics due to their relevance in analyzing economic conditions. While successful predation results in a gain of energy, hunting invariably involves energetic costs as well. When hunger is not an issue, in general most predators will not seek to attack prey since the costs outweigh the benefits. For instance, a large predatory fish like a shark that is well fed in an aquarium will typically ignore the smaller fish swimming around it (while the prey fish take advantage of the fact that the apex predator is apparently uninterested). Surplus killing represents a deviation from this type of behaviour. The treatment of consumption in terms of cost-benefit analysis is known as optimal foraging theory, and has been quite successful in the study of animal behavior. In general, costs and benefits are considered in energy gain per unit time, though other factors are also important, such as essential nutrients that have no caloric value but are necessary for survival and health.

What you hear is the scream of sirens. In Bangladesh, the England team bus travels with a phalanx of motorcycle outriders and a fleet of police cars jammed full of heavily armed officers. The ECB's security team gave Bangladesh the all clear but the authorities here don't want to take any chances. An incident-free England tour will be evidence to the world that Bangladesh isn't as dangerous as many fear. Any attack would be a disaster for the reputation of the country. But there is a risk that the small army guarding the cricket - not to mention the elaborate drills the Bangladeshis carried out inside a cricket stadium, complete with helicopters and a litter of pretend corpses - exaggerates the dangers to foreign visitors. This is not a country in the grip of fear. Out on the streets of Dhaka the atmosphere is just as friendly and welcoming as I've always found it. That said, earlier in the week I stopped for a cup of strong sweet tea at a stall in a busy market. "Aren't you worried?," asked the chaiwala - the tea man. "Why?," I asked. "Because you are the only white man here." I looked around. He was right. Synthesizing physiologically-accurate human movement in a variety of conditions can help practitioners plan surgeries, design experiments, or prototype assistive devices in simulated environments, reducing time and costs and improving treatment outcomes. Because of the large and complex solution spaces of biomechanical models, current methods are constrained to specific movements and models, requiring careful design of a controller and hindering many possible applications. We sought to discover if modern optimization methods efficiently explore these complex spaces. To do this, we posed the problem as a competition in which participants were tasked with developing a controller to enable a physiologically-based human model to navigate a complex obstacle course as quickly as possible, without using any experimental data. They were provided with a human musculoskeletal model and a physics-based simulation environment. In this paper, we discuss the design of the competition, technical difficulties, results, and analysis of the top controllers. The challenge proved that deep reinforcement learning techniques, despite their high computational cost, can be successfully employed as an optimization method for synthesizing physiologically feasible motion in high-dimensional biomechanical systems.

This can help inform future decisions regarding policy changes; knowing which side your neighbors sit on may allow them to give better feedback when discussing ideas due to being able to speak their minds without fear of retribution. For example, someone who isn't afraid to call out racism will have fewer qualms doing so among those whose views would punish such statements as disloyalty. In this paper, we want to study the informative value of negative links in signed complex networks. For this purpose, we extract and analyze a collection of signed networks representing voting sessions of the European Parliament (EP). We first process some data collected by the VoteWatch Europe Website for the whole 7 t h term (2009-2014), by considering voting similarities between Members of the EP to define weighted signed links. We then apply a selection of community detection algorithms, designed to process only positive links, to these data. We also apply Parallel Iterative Local Search (Parallel ILS), an algorithm recently proposed to identify balanced partitions in signed networks. Our results show that, contrary to the conclusions of a previous study focusing on other data, the partitions detected by ignoring or considering the negative links are indeed remarkably different for these networks. The relevance of negative links for graph partitioning therefore is an open question which should be further explored.

Boolean functional synthesis involves creating a Boolean function based on a specified relationship between input and output variables. Although there have been considerable advancements in synthesis algorithms recently, boolean functional synthesis still presents difficulties, even with advanced decomposition methods. Our study introduces a novel method of decomposition that differs from current approaches, focusing on separating input and output elements within the specification. This technique utilizes an input-output division of a CNF formula through sequential examination of each component. By leveraging distinctive attributes of these parts, we successfully create a complete solution for the whole specification. Initially, we establish a theoretical finding indicating that certain structured input components allow for more efficient synthesis using this model compared to generic cases. Additionally, our experiments demonstrate that our algorithm outperforms other top-tier tools in practical scenarios where they typically struggle, thereby enhancing contemporary synthesis practices.

Religious humanism merges humanist moral principles with traditional religious practices focused on fulfilling human requirements, interests, and capabilities. Although it wasn't formally recognized as "humanism" until the turn of the 19th century, combining secular values with human-centered ethics has historical roots. An example includes the Deistic Cult of Reason established amidst the French Revolution by notable figures like Jacques Hebert and Pierre Gaspard Chaumette, which led to transforming the Notre Dame de Paris into a "Temple of Reason," where liberty symbols temporarily took over religious iconography. Furthermore, sociologist Auguste Comte initiated Positivism in the mid-19th century, dubbing it a "religion of humanity." Another precursor to modern humanist organizations was the Humanistic Religious Association created in London in 1853, promoting equality among its members while emphasizing science, philosophy, and art education. Lastly, the Ethical Culture movement emerged in 187ptailed by Felix Adler, who envisioned it as a faith-based yet ethically driven lifestyle, aiming to sustain core values found across various religions.

Our study examines two distinct kinds of summation-by-packages finite difference methods utilized to approximate the second derivative with a variable coefficient. One approach incorporates ghost points, whereas the other does not require any ghost points. We explore an unknown correlation between these two categories of summation-by-packages operators. Merging them yields a novel fourth-order precise finite difference discretization featuring hanging nodes at the mesh refinement interface. For our model problem, we employ the two-dimensional acoustic wave equation expressed in its second-order form concerning acoustic pressure, proving the energy stability of the suggested technique. When compared to existing techniques relying on ghost points, this method results in a more compact system of linear equations necessary to solve for the ghost point values. Moreover, it allows maintaining the same explicit time step without reduction, unlike the parallel problem. Additionally, we provide a comprehensive assessment comparing the accuracy and time-step limitations against the simultaneous approximation term penalty method.

Attributed network embedding has attracted plenty of interest in recent years. It aims to learn task-independent, low-dimensional, and continuous vectors for nodes preserving both topology and attribute information. Most of the existing methods, such as random-walk based methods and GCNs, mainly focus on the local information, i.e., the attributes of the neighbours. Thus, they have been well studied for assortative networks (i.e., networks with communities) but ignored disassortative networks (i.e., networks with multipartite, hubs, and hybrid structures), which are common in the real world. To enable model both assortative and disassortative networks, we propose a block-based generative model for attributed network embedding from a probability perspective. Specifically, the nodes are assigned to several blocks wherein the nodes in the same block share the similar linkage patterns. These patterns can define assortative networks containing communities or disassortative networks with the multipartite, hub, or any hybrid structures. To preserve the attribute information, we assume that each node has a hidden embedding related to its assigned block. We use a neural network to characterize the nonlinearity between node embeddings and node attributes. We perform extensive experiments on real-world and synthetic attributed networks. The results show that our proposed method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art embedding methods for both clustering and classification tasks, especially on disassortative networks.

The ability to determine what parts of objects and surfaces people touch as they go about their daily lives would be useful in understanding how the COVID-19 virus spreads. To determine whether a person has touched an object or surface using visual data, images, or videos, is a hard problem. Computer vision 3D reconstruction approaches project objects and the human body from the 2D image domain to 3D and perform 3D space intersection directly. However, this solution would not meet the accuracy requirement in applications due to projection error. Another standard approach is to train a neural network to infer touch actions from the collected visual data. This strategy would require significant amounts of training data to generalize over scale and viewpoint variations. A different approach to this problem is to identify whether a person has touched a defined object. In this work, we show that the solution to this problem can be straightforward. Specifically, we show that the contact between an object and a static surface can be identified by projecting the object onto the static surface through two different viewpoints and analyzing their 2D intersection. The object contacts the surface when the projected points are close to each other; we call this cross view projection consistency. Instead of doing 3D scene reconstruction or transfer learning from deep networks, a mapping from the surface in the two camera views to the surface space is the only requirement. For planar space, this mapping is the Homography transformation. This simple method can be easily adapted to real-life applications. In this paper, we apply our method to do office occupancy detection for studying the COVID-19 transmission pattern from an office desk in a meeting room using the contact information.

Written Japanese also includes a pair of syllabaries known as kana, derived by simplifying Chinese characters selected to represent syllables of Japanese. The syllabaries differ because they sometimes selected different characters for a syllable, and because they used different strategies to reduce these characters for easy writing: the angular katakana were obtained by selecting a part of each character, while hiragana were derived from the cursive forms of whole characters. Modern Japanese writing uses a composite system, using kanji for word stems, hiragana for inflexional endings and grammatical words, and katakana to transcribe non-Chinese loanwords as well as serve as a method to emphasize native words (similar to how italics are used in Romance languages).

The simplicity lies in the fact that the U.S. President is chosen through an Electoral College system, which represents the states rather than directly reflecting the popular vote among the general populace. Each state's allocation of votes corresponds to its total representation in both the Senate and House of Representatives. In most cases, when a candidate secures victory within a particular state, they receive all the electoral votes designated for that state. Consequently, winning becomes about claiming victories across multiple states as opposed to garnering individual votes on a national scale. Without this system, there exists a theoretical scenario whereby only ten or eleven heavily populated states might determine the election outcome, effectively silencing the remaining thirty-nine forty states. Furthermore, candidates may prioritize focusing their efforts solely on these densely populated areas at the expense of others. However, the Electoral College ensures that candidates must appeal nationwide, considering even less populated regions during their campaigns. It parallels the concept of providing every state with a minimum level of congressional representation. As such, it preserves the political significance of smaller states against potential domination by more populous ones. Ultimately, this means a president could emerge victorious despite losing the overall popular vote if they achieve narrow margins in enough states to secure the majority of electoral votes. Thus, the system places greater emphasis on balancing state power over sheer numbers of individuals residing in any given region.

Search engines rely on this thing called a crawler that documents the existence of websites and also some metadata about it. Crawlers prowl the internet trying to access any and every website and page that they come across. If a website mentions a link, the crawler sees that link and puts it into its queue of things to crawl. Programmers who follow good etiquette will make their crawler check for this file called "robot.txt" before allowing it to search the website. This file says to the crawler "hey! I don't want you to index me!" or "hey! Don't read any of my contents!" Webmasters who choose the former usually won't have their website indexed at all (that is, if the crawler's programmer is kind enough to follow their request) and those who choose the latter will be indexed but won't have any of the information about their website read and thus the message that you see about "this site's robot.txt file." Webmasters do this for any number of reason. Some want their websites to remain private, some don't want the extra traffic crawlers bring. Some just simply only want their main domain address indexed and not the millions of sub-pages within their website.

I stacked them up and felt euphoria, followed by a slow burning sensation in my chest, and I started crying, and then cooling down. This cycle repeated many times, following many events, and I slowly stopped getting happy. I made the connection. I stopped doing things, I stopped cheering, I just stopped. My parents thought I was a bit slow, or maybe traumatized, but it was none of those. I just didn't want to feel the burning. I realized it was radioactive when I grew up some more. We were doing an experiment in class with rad sensors, to see what was more radioactive; water, or coal. I was with a girl I liked, and every time I looked at her, the rad sensor would spike a little. Every time she spoke, it spiked a little. Almost every little thing she did raised it up some more. They never found out. How would they know? I only knew because I just kept getting hotter and hotter, having to go to the bathroom to cool down. Keeping sad was pretty easy after the 9th grade, my mother got into an accident and was sent to the hospital. I saw her once, and wanted to stay for as long as possible, only because it kept me sad. I had to leave, but it gave me something to lean back to when I got a bit too nuclear. I thought to her, how she will die, and how I will never get to feel her hug after that point. What's better was that I was close to my mother, she raised me, and now I was sent to my father. Though I didn't acknowledge it much, I did love my mother, which made the accident all the better for me and the rest of humanity. But, good things come to an end, or even bad things, in this case. I really wish I didn't have some luck. I wish it went to someone else for a change. I stopped visiting my mother early on in order to imagine the worst case scenario for her. It made living a bit easier, though I still couldn't do anything too fun, or else I might blow the world sky high. On that fateful day, I got a call from my dad. I answered, and he told me to come home. I was out walking around, because staying in my house was depressing, but it was also boring. I came home slowly, to try and pique my dad's temper. What I didn't expect was my mother, sitting in our living room. She was there, with a smile on her face. The smile of someone who didn't know me for the whole time I lived after that accident. The smile of someone I just couldn't ignore.

The Silkworm by JK Rowling's pseudonym Robert Galbraith and Ian McEwan's The Children Act are among 25 British novels in the running for the world's richest literary prize. The DSC Prize for South Asian Literature, worth 50,000, is open to any novel published in English with an Asian connection. This year's shortlist includes five novels set in India, four from Pakistan, three from Bangladesh, two from Sri Lanka and one each from Nepal and Singapore. The winner will be announced at a ceremony in New Delhi on 17 November. The shortlisted novels are: The Silkworm by Robert Galbraith (UK) The Children Act by Ian McEwan (UK) Jasmine Days by Benyamin (India) In Other Rooms, Other Wonders by Daniyal Mueenuddin (Pakistan) A Golden Age by Tahmima Anam (Bangladesh) The Good Muslim by Tahmima Anam (Bangladesh) Nights of the Rainbow by Shehan Karunatilaka (Sri Lanka) The Black Coat by Neel Mukherjee (India) The Story of a Brief Marriage by Anuk Arudpragasam (Sri Lanka) Sleeping on Jupiter by Anuradha Roy (India) River of Smoke by Amitav Ghosh (India) The Lowland by Jhumpa Lahiri (USA) Chauranga by Bishwanath Saikia (India) The Book of Gold Leaves by Mirza Waheed (India) Cooling Time by Anjali Joseph (India) The Story of My Assassins by Tarun J. Tejpal (India) The In-Between World of Vikram Lall by Moses Isegawa (Uganda) The God of Small Things by Arundhati Roy (India) The Karachi Debutante by Sabyn Javeri (Pakistan) The Last Gift by Shamsur Rahman Faruqi (India) Souvenir by Rahul Bhattacharya (India) The Patience Stone by Atiq Rahimi (Afghanistan) The DSC Prize for South Asian Literature was established in 2010 and is open to any novel published in English with an Asian connection. It is named after the late Indian publisher Deepak Sharma Chauhan, who was passionate about promoting South Asian writing. The prize is awarded annually by a jury of international literary figures. Previous winners include Hashi Mohamed (UK) for his debut novel, The Boy Who Followed His Father into Auschwitz; Jeet Thayil (India) for Narcopolis; and Anosh Irani (IndiaCanada) for The Parcel.

He was blonde. Not dirty blonde, not hay colored with a tint of orange; no, he was perfectly yellow haired. Long and flowing, those blonde strands fell in front of two pools, freshly cleaned and never contaminated. His nose fell into a French point that reminded her of the Eiffel Tower, and was curved by a grand staircase that made his nostrils. His cheeks were sandy and rough, as if he'd been sun-burnt and salt swept a thousand times over by the coast just outside her house. He flashed his teeth in a thieve's smile, and a lone cigarette hung tight in his smirk. He wore an attire of a messenger of the military. A brown felt shirt with brass buttons and pockets all over it. His sleeves were rolled up and held into place with two straps, buttoned. His pants were grey khaki. His belt matched his shirt, his boots matched his pants. She was stricken, and she hated it. He was too perfect. He was exactly what she wanted him to be and everything else more. He even spoke with an accent. She stomped her feet and told him very politely to exit the premises. He simply smiled and patted her on the head as if she was a simple little school girl. His laugh was the same one her first love had, that reassuring, boyish giggle. She hated him. Because he wasn't real. He sounded too much like her first love, looked too much like the men she saw in her magazines, and he was military. God she loved men in uniform. She could've looked past that though. She could've let it go, and begged him to stay right there on the spot. If he didn't smoke that damn cigarette. That cigarette held no brand, had no markings, had no line to show that it was hand rolled. Most obviously though, it had no smell. None at all. When he rubbed his hand through her hair, and when the cigarette nearly poked her in the face, she could feel no heat, and could smell no tobacco. He never exhaled either. No smoke ever made its way out of his lungs and down that great staircase. She thanked him for the letter she received, and he left, closing the door himself. "Who was that?" her cat asked. "Oh no one," she said, "Just a postman." "Oh, good," he said, jumping up into her lap as she sat at her desk, "Did you remember to take your pills this morning?"

The poet stayed at Moat Brae in Dumfries as a child, and it is where he learnt to read and write. Now it has been restored by a community project to celebrate the man who made 'Scotland's national bard'. The house, which is owned by the National Trust for Scotland, has been empty since 2005, when it was put on the market and was about to be demolished. The situation was saved after the National Trust and the Scottish Government provided a 2.6million grant. On Monday, local dignitaries will gather for a special ceremony to celebrate the start of a refurbishment project which will turn Moat Brae into a centre for Burns's work. The house will open its doors to the public in 2019, and will have an exhibition on the life and work of Burns. It will also be used for events and performances to celebrate the Bard. It will be called Burns Birthplace Museum, and the National Trust is in the process of recruiting a curator to oversee the collection. The museum will include the first edition of Burns's poetry, A Select Collection of Original Scottish Airs, which was published in Edinburgh in 1787. It is one of only two known copies in existence. It was originally part of a collection of 500 poems and songs, but was shortened to 200 when the poet's brother Gilbert published the first volume. The work was first published in 1786, and the edition held by Moat Brae was given to the poet by his father in 1787. The edition is said to be the most valuable Burns book in the world. The house will also have a replica of a plaster cast bust of Burns, which is on display at the National Portrait Gallery in Edinburgh. The original bust, which was sculpted by John Graham Gilbert in 1821, was stolen from the gallery in 2014. The most efficient known QSC is an n,1 code based on Calderbank and Shor's construction [CS], which uses only three local error correcting operations: Hadamard (H), CNOT gates between neighboring particles and a pi2 rotation around one axis. This protocol yields an efficiently correctable system for any number of involved spin- rac{12} objects interacting via Ising interactions under decoherence conditions typical for experiments. Calderbank et al. showed how to add logical single qubit rotations at fixed time intervals to their decoding procedure without changing its efficiency. This study introduces a method for calculating the necessary storage capacity within an electrical grid to meet a specified level of risk tolerance. Inputs include categorized events based on maximum unmet power demand and the acceptable probability of failing to supply energy, resulting in the required overall storage capacity.
