Measuring uncertainty is a promising technique for detecting adversarial examples, crafted inputs on which the model predicts an incorrect class with high confidence. But many measures of uncertainty exist, including predictive entropy and mutual information, each capturing different types of uncertainty. We study these measures, and shed light on why mutual information seems to be effective at the task of adversarial example detection. We highlight failure modes for MC dropout, a widely used approach for estimating uncertainty in deep models. This leads to an improved understanding of the drawbacks of current methods, and a proposal to improve the quality of uncertainty estimates using probabilistic model ensembles. We give illustrative experiments using MNIST to demonstrate the intuition underlying the different measures of uncertainty, as well as experiments on a real-world Kaggle dogs vs cats classification dataset.

The topmost brick will eventually reach the end without hitting another object, causing the subsequent brick to be unsupported and fall freely. The finalized trade price represents the most recent completed exchange. Essentially, when purchasing, there is always room to negotiate by proposing a specific purchase or sale price. Reflecting back on the significant stock market downturn, an article highlighted instances where businesses were valued below their asset value, prompting strategic acquisitions. Brokerages facilitate transactions between buyers and sellers, often holding stakes in multiple firms, enabling them to process orders internally rather than externally—a practice that incurs commissions. Major exchanges like NASDAQ and the NYSE prioritize cybersecurity, implementing robust mechanisms resistant to intrusion. Algorithm-driven automated trading platforms aim to capitalize on rapid transactions based on predefined algorithms. However, occasional system failures leading to sudden price drops do not constitute hacking; savvy investors might exploit such opportunities to place profitable purchase requests during these periods.

Alissa received an invitation to her class reunion. She reluctantly decided that she would attend it. The night of the reunion, she saw many people she used to know. A few hours later, she was introduced to a friend who said she could not fit in and had no place else for her at the reunion due to an illness. "I thought I'd be fine," she told me. "But then I found out my father died two days earlier." The next day, she invited me over for dinner while sitting alone on the patio with her mother. They enjoyed each other's company as they waited outside their apartments. She thanked me and hugged me before leaving to go home. In the course of the week, I visited her family members, relatives and friends - including her parents - who were also attending the reunion. My sister mentioned that she had been thinking about returning home since her uncle died when she first arrived. She asked me if I wanted to join them too but I confessed I wasn't able to come because of work commitments already scheduled for that afternoon and couldn't stay longer than ten minutes without moving things around. Then she asked if she could join us afterward so we could have a picnic together after dinner. After the reunion, I returned home to New York City to visit my husband and his family; he lived nearby. His parents agreed to let me accompany him there which meant traveling all the way back to where I grew up from Manhattan. Thereafter, I stayed over three nights to catch up with my friends until I left to visit my aunt and cousins again during the holiday season. It didn't matter how long we spent visiting - the memories I felt helped keep my spirits high despite being away from my father's funeral service, as well as being home with my children every Friday evening for Thanksgiving dinner with them-my brother described it differently: "We ate a lot more meals together!" While my feelings toward my dad are distant now just one year removed from his death, his love and kindness still grip me deeply. I miss hearing his voice sometimes even though he hasn't spoken much lately. He probably wouldn't approve or condone being lonely anymore unless you attended a funeral too often like I did. But what he missed most is the unconditional warmth and support he offered throughout my childhood thanks to his patience, understanding, generosity and love. My father was an amazing man whose heart never wavered nor changed. He loved unconditionally and always spoke lovingly to anyone who faced hardship along the way. His spirit will remain and his legacy will live forever in our hearts today. Agile methodology encompasses various approaches such as Scrum, XP, and Lean within its vast landscape. These differing approaches offer unique interpretations of Agile principles. While I won't delve into specific methodologies, it's common for organizations to incorporate elements from multiple Agile schools into their processes. Before Agile emerged, the predominant approach was known as the Waterfall model, which is still utilized by certain companies.

The Waterfall model segments the software development lifecycle into sequential phases where each phase must be completed before moving onto the next one. Starting from conceptualization to delivery, this process may span extended periods, sometimes upwards of a year. Traditional Waterfall stages include Requirement Gathering, System Design, Coding, Testing, and Maintenership.

Although the Waterfall model has faced criticism recently, some firms continue to find success using it due to factors like high transition costs and potential disruptions in operations. Agile development entered the scene as a response to the rigidity of the Waterfall model. It posits that making decisions about requirements and design months in advance could lead to missed opportunities given the rapidly changing nature of markets. Thus, Agile offers more flexibility to adapt to evolving circumstances.

I unfastened my necktie, taking a small sip of tepid, bland liquid masquerading as coffee. A droplet landed on the tie's somber striped design, though there was no remedy available. I pushed up the crisp white cuffs of my shirt before settling over my aged wooden workstation. Resting my head against my hands, I gazed vacantly downwards. This desk was marred by dirt and marks; when was the last time someone tidied up here? Casting an eye towards the unevenly patterned rug beneath me, which shared the same lackluster appeal as the desk, I recoiled slightly due to concerns regarding personal hygiene. Raising myself away from the tabletop, I idly propped my limbs over the edge and peered upward through yawns at the mundane ceiling, counting imperfections along the way. Observing a spider crawl into a ventilation grille prompted me to spin the modest rotating seat underfoot. The monotonous hum emanating from the surroundings persisted, instilling a sense of indifference within me. Breathing this stale atmosphere seemed almost unhygienical compared to touching the desk directly. Perhaps being conscious of these poor conditions heightened my apprehensions. After a short while, I picked up a pen lying close by, fiddling with it absentmindedly. Eventually, my desk telephone interrupted my listlessness. Halfheartedly attempting to raise my head, I offered only a perfunctory glance as it continued ringing briefly. Exerting minimal energy, I struggled to hoist one hand high enough to reach the device, finally managing to bring it to bear upon the receiver.

With its AI-powered Smart Camera, you won't have to worry about staying in frame during your video chats. But on the other hand, there are serious privacy concerns. For starters, Facebook is notorious for data collection, so many people don't trust them with their personal information. Then there's the fact that Facebook will be able to collect data on what you're saying and doing while using Portal. This raises questions about how secure and private the device really is. Finally, people may feel uneasy about the idea of having a camera in their home that's connected to Facebook. It's hard to know just how much access Facebook will have to your life if you use this device. At the end of the day, only you can decide whether or not Facebook Portal is right for you. It certainly offers some interesting features, but the potential privacy implications should definitely give you pause.
